---
name: brand-renderer
description: 'Render and check branded artifacts using a confirmed project profile or the shared neutral policy. Use for documents, decks, workbooks, PDFs, HTML, or brand-sensitive copy when the task needs visual identity applied without losing source meaning. Resolves required assets, preserves claims through export, and combines executable checks with inspection of the rendered result.'
---


# Brand renderer

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`readout-brief.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/readout-brief.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

Render the requested output using the selected brand profile while preserving its
meaning in the final format. Use the canonical [brand policy](references/estate/brand.md)
for selection and neutral defaults. Set `SKILLS_BRAND_PROFILE` to an explicitly
selected profile; otherwise the runtime reads the current project's `brand.md`,
then the packaged neutral policy. A selected but missing or invalid profile is an
error, not permission to use another identity.

Run the relevant content and visual checks before delivery. Automated checks
support the review; they cannot decide whether an artifact answers its audience's
question or whether the rendered layout is usable.

## Shared rendering library

The producing skill owns the requested artifact and its information design.
Use this library when that artifact needs a visual profile. A plain chat reply
does not require a brand preflight. Writing-integrity applies to its prose.

What this skill holds constant across output formats:

- **Typography.** The profile's font stack and supplied font files, with
  tabular figures where digits align. System fonts need no bundled files.
- **Palette.** Renderer tokens are compiled from the selected profile.
  Additional chart colors must be recorded in that profile.
- **Assets.** Use the profile's supplied logo when present. The neutral profile
  has no logo; do not invent one.
- **Hierarchy.** A reader tells the claim from the caveat without reading the
  colour. Type and space carry the rank.
- **Accessibility.** Contrast floors, alt text, one `h1`, a named language.
- **Evidence integrity.** A figure reaches the rendered page still carrying its
  qualifier and its source. The parity gate reads exactly that.
- **Craft.** No emoji, no decorative glyphs, no colour-coded left borders, no
  gradient standing in for structure.

What the content decides, surface by surface:

- Slide composition, and whether a given slide carries a footer at all.
- Page structure, section order, and where a break falls.
- Canvas: a profile-defined surface chosen for the reading it supports.
- Logo position and which mark identifies a surface.
- Density: how much sits on one view.
- Visual encoding: which chart form fits the comparison, and what a table earns.

There is no universal footer, header bar, title position, card pattern, or slide
composition. A rule that forced one taught people to reshape the artifact to
clear the gate instead of to serve the reader. `reference/brand-gate.md` carries
the line between the two lists.

Weight follows consequence, not file format. Email and Slack get the voice rules
and a reading pass by default. They escalate to the full release gates when the
message carries a figure, an approval, scope, a commitment, or a decision. That
is the same trigger set the release validator fails closed on. The register is
[`email-slack.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/email-slack.md); the
escalation rule is in
[`surface-policy.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/surface-policy.md).

## Controls provided to the producing workflow

The producing workflow uses these controls as needed for the artifact.

```
producing workflow -> review-writing -> authored prose review
producing workflow -> brand-renderer -> visual profile and rendering checks
producing workflow -> review-deliverable -> assembled deliverable review
```

`review-writing` owns writing review. The internal `writing-diagnostics` module supplies
diagnostic tools; the confirmed author profile supplies voice.
`review-deliverable` owns the release decision. It fails closed on an unsupported
figure, scope, approval, or go or no-go.

Neither one resolves this skill back. A copy of brand-renderer inside
review-deliverable would make each the other's runtime, and one upload would then ship
two renderers. A fix to either could reach a client artifact through the stale
copy of the other.

## First action: prove the runtime

Before rendering a styled artifact or diagnosing its assets, resolve this
module's directory and run:

```bash
python3 scripts/runtime_preflight.py --json
```

The preflight resolves packaged or sibling runtimes. For an external runtime, supply its inspected absolute directory through `ESTATE_PROSE_RUNTIME` or `ESTATE_QUALITY_RUNTIME`; it does not search account-specific mount paths. Use the absolute paths in that report for the logo, fonts, prose checker, prose
receipt tool, brand checker, and release validator. A failed preflight blocks
the affected rendering operation. A logo or font file is required only when
the selected profile specifies it. A neutral artifact can use system fonts.
A checker run with no receipt cannot release a final artifact.

## The release gates

An artifact is release-ready only when every gate has a disposition. No single
pass authorizes release.

1. **Parity gate** (`scripts/parity_audit.py`). Every claim, number, name, and
   evidence reference that belongs in the artifact survives into the rendered
   readable text, nothing forbidden was added, and protected qualifiers survived.
   This is lexical and structural support only: it cannot see computed CSS,
   clipping, off-canvas text, print visibility, or whether a qualifier sits with
   its claim unless you scope it with a selector.
2. **Visual gate** (human or model, mandatory, no script). Inspect the rendered
   views slide by slide and page by page. Confirm nothing is clipped, hidden,
   off-canvas, or visually detached from its qualifier. A `requiredViews` list
   raises this reminder; the flag is not a substitute.
3. **Prose gate** (the bundled `writing-diagnostics` runtime plus a reading pass). Run the
   checker at the absolute `prose_check` path returned by runtime preflight. Its
   config sits at the prose runtime root as `house.json`.
   The reading pass catches the cadence a matcher cannot. See "Voice" below.
4. **Brand gate** (`scripts/brand_check.py`). Palette, borders, radii, type,
   assets, and the accessibility floor. Reads colors from the selected profile through `brand/tokens.py`,
   never from prose. The deterministic half of the visual gate; it does not
   replace looking at the thing. It gates identity, not layout: footer placement
   and slide composition come back as review flags. See "Token-backed brand
   checks" below.

Release note discipline: record a disposition for every parity or brand warning
and every visual review flag before shipping. Prose findings cannot be disposed.
Repair supported scanner findings, then read the complete result using Writing Integrity. A clean scan does not establish editorial quality.

## Workflow

1. Build the artifact to the brand canon and voice below.
2. Write a parity manifest listing what must survive: required phrases, forbidden
   phrases, evidence references, and protected claims with their qualifiers.
3. If the artifact is a deck, convert it first:
   `python3 scripts/extract_pptx.py deck.pptx --html deck.extracted.html`. The
   extractor is table-aware so numbers and rows in tables are not silently dropped.
4. Parity gate:
   `python3 scripts/parity_audit.py manifest.json artifact.html --strict`. Fix
   any error.
5. Prose gate using the `prose_check` path from runtime preflight and the
   `house.json` beside that runtime's `scripts/` directory.
   Fix every finding and rerun until the checker reports clean.
6. Brand gate: `python3 scripts/brand_check.py artifact.html`. Fix every failure.
7. Do the visual gate and the voice reading pass by eye.
8. Write the release note dispositions. Then ship.
9. Hand the gated artifact back to its owner. Delivery and publishing sit
   outside this skill.

Run the parity gate again after any prose fix. A voice edit can silently break a
`requiredPhrase` or a protected claim, and parity is what catches it.

## Scripts

Every script runs on `python3` with the standard library. Only
`extract_pptx.py` needs `python-pptx` (`pip install -r scripts/requirements.txt`).
No script in this skill touches the network. The parity gate parses HTML
and resolves selectors through `html_dom.py`, a local module, so it still runs on
a mount where nothing can be installed.

- `scripts/parity_audit.py manifest.json rendered.html [--json report.json] [--strict]`
  Lexical and structural parity. Exit 0 pass, 1 error or `--strict` warning, 2 bad
  manifest.
- `scripts/brand_check.py artifact [...] [--json out.json] [--strict]`
  The visual-layer gate. Reads `.html .htm .css .pptx .docx .js .py .md`; source
  files are linted too, because a renderer that hardcodes a hex emits it on every
  future artifact. Exit 0 clean, 1 failure or `--strict` flag, 2 missing tokens.
- `scripts/sync_tokens.py [--profile FILE] [--output FILE] [--check FILE]`
  Exports a JSON token snapshot or checks that a saved snapshot matches the
  selected profile. Exit 0 match, 1 drift, 2 invalid input. Python and Node
  renderers read the profile directly and do not need a cached snapshot.
- `scripts/palette_selftest.py [--skill SKILL.md]`
  Checks that the instructions delegate visual values to the profile and that
  the runtime tokens resolve to values in that profile.
- `scripts/extract_pptx.py deck.pptx [--html out.html] [--json out.json]`
  Table-aware PPTX to HTML transcript for the gates only. Never substitutes for
  the visual gate.
Each script has a selftest next to it (`*_selftest.py`). Run them after any edit;
each prints observed versus expected and exits nonzero on a mismatch:

```
python3 scripts/parity_audit_selftest.py
python3 scripts/brand_check_selftest.py
python3 scripts/palette_selftest.py
python3 scripts/extract_pptx_selftest.py
```

The bundle carries a local runtime for both dependencies. They stay authored and
verified in `writing-diagnostics` and `review-deliverable`; the bundler copies that exact source
into `_runtime/writing-diagnostics` and `_runtime/review-deliverable` so a cloud mount does not
depend on sibling discovery. Their skill metadata is stripped on the way in, so
the loader sees one skill and cannot route to a nested copy.

## Parity manifest

`manifestVersion` must be a string with major version `1`, one JSON manifest per
artifact. It lists `requiredPhrases`, `forbiddenPhrases`,
`requiredEvidenceReferences`, `protectedClaims` (each with `requiredQualifiers`
and an optional `selector`), `requiredSelectors`, and `requiredViews`. The full
field table is in `reference/authoring-policy.md`. Keep the manifest to
artifact-specific values; never embed a worked deliverable or recognizable
artifact structure.

## Brand canon

The [brand policy](references/estate/brand.md) is the neutral authority and defines
how to select a project profile. Read the selected profile before rendering.
Keep visual values there rather than copying them into a skill's instructions.

`brand/tokens.py` and `brand/tokens.js` compile the profile into compatible
renderer keys. `brand/token-roles.json` maps existing keys to semantic profile
roles; it contains no palette values. This preserves existing renderer APIs while
allowing a profile change to reach every consumer. The loaders record the
profile hash. `scripts/sync_tokens.py` can export the same values for a consumer
that needs a JSON file.

Use `scripts/resolve_assets.py --json` to resolve the profile's local logo and
font paths. Relative paths resolve beside the profile. The neutral policy needs
neither a logo nor downloaded fonts. A project requiring missing assets must
supply them or explicitly select an available alternative.

Apply the profile's border width and radius. Preserve readable contrast and
left-aligned long body text. A surface's layout follows its content: there is no
mandatory footer, repeated card grid, or fixed slide composition. A supplied
template is an optional input, and its identity must agree with the selected
profile. See [`brand-gate.md`](reference/brand-gate.md).

## Token-backed brand checks

`scripts/brand_check.py` checks the output against the runtime palette and
geometry rules. It also checks title underlines, long centered body text, and
sentence-case headings. The neutral policy does not prohibit a color because
it is warm or require a logo footer. Checks must follow the selected profile,
not preserve a former company's preferences.

The checker inspects literal color values and document XML. It cannot prove
computed CSS, font availability in a viewer, or complete visual accessibility.
Inspect the rendered output and confirm contrast and legibility before release.
An authoritative profile establishes where values came from; it does not prove
that the renderer applied them correctly.

## Voice and money

Writing-integrity governs prose review. The internal `writing-diagnostics` module carries
the diagnostic engine; this rendering library supplies no competing voice.
Construction patterns expose the tell. The catalog covers em dashes, buzzword
vocabulary, the `not just X, but Y` flip, trailing "-ing" benefit clauses,
throat-clearing openers, rule-of-three triads for rhythm, plus monotone sentence
rhythm. Never strip genuine epistemic language as if it were a
tell: Confirmed, Inferred, Unknown, "estimated", ranges, "not priced", "blocked",
and "at risk" all stay, and a voice fix must never soften a protected caveat, a
figure, a conflict, or a conclusion.

`reference/authoring-policy.md` holds the seven-question reading pass, the money
rule (meaning not price; the confirmed pricing source owns the authoritative numbers), and fixture
discipline.

## Porting notes

`SKILL.md`, `scripts/`, `brand/`, `_shared/`, and `_runtime/` load into Console
Managed Agents and the Agent SDK skill loader unchanged. The cloud bundle carries
the prose runtime and brand assets it needs. Install `scripts/requirements.txt`
in environments that do not already provide the declared libraries.

Use scripts/resolve_assets.py --json to resolve the profile's local logo and font paths. Relative paths resolve beside the profile. The neutral policy needs neither a logo nor downloaded fonts. A project requiring missing assets must supply them or explicitly select an available alternative.

Apply the profile's border width and radius. Preserve readable contrast and left-aligned long body text. A surface's layout follows its content: there is no mandatory footer, repeated card grid, or fixed slide composition. A supplied template is an optional input, and its identity must agree with the selected profile. See brand-gate.md (reference/brand-gate.md).

Token-backed brand checks

scripts/brand_check.py checks the output against the runtime palette and geometry rules. It also checks title underlines, long centered body text, and sentence-case headings. The neutral policy does not prohibit a color because it is warm or require a logo footer. Checks must follow the selected profile, not preserve a former company's preferences.

The checker inspects literal color values and document XML. It cannot prove computed CSS, font availability in a viewer, or complete visual accessibility. Inspect the rendered output and confirm contrast and legibility before release. An authoritative profile establishes where values came from; it does not prove that the renderer applied them correctly.

Voice and money

Writing-integrity governs prose review. The internal writing-diagnostics module carries the diagnostic engine; this rendering library supplies no competing voice. Construction patterns expose the tell. The catalog covers em dashes, buzzword vocabulary, the not just X, but Y flip, trailing "-ing" benefit clauses, throat-clearing openers, rule-of-three triads for rhythm, plus monotone sentence rhythm. Never strip genuine epistemic language as if it were a tell: Confirmed, Inferred, Unknown, "estimated", ranges, "not priced", "blocked", and "at risk" all stay, and a voice fix must never soften a protected caveat, a figure, a conflict, or a conclusion.

reference/authoring-policy.md holds the seven-question reading pass, the money rule (meaning not price; the confirmed pricing source owns the authoritative numbers), and fixture discipline.

Porting notes

SKILL.md, scripts/, brand/, _shared/, and _runtime/ load into Console Managed Agents and the Agent SDK skill loader unchanged. The cloud bundle carries the prose runtime and brand assets it needs. Install scripts/requirements.txt in environments that do not already provide the declared libraries.

examples.title: Gating a bakery's quarterly review page against the neutral profile
examples.markdown:
## Request

Check this one-page Q3 wholesale review for Harbor Lane Bakery before it goes to the owners. Use the default brand. The 18% growth figure has to keep its "estimated" caveat and its source, and the Saturday delivery cost must stay marked as not priced.

## Inputs

A short HTML page (`draft.html`) and a parity manifest, both written for this run. Harbor Lane Bakery is a made-up company. No project profile was selected, so the runtime used the packaged neutral profile, Baseline. The bundled scripts ran for real: `runtime_preflight.py`, `parity_audit.py` and `brand_check.py`. The prose gate and the visual gate are outside this record.

```json
{"manifestVersion": "1.0",
 "requiredPhrases": ["Two cafe accounts asked for Saturday delivery"],
 "forbiddenPhrases": ["guaranteed growth"],
 "requiredEvidenceReferences": ["invoice export, 2026-10-02"],
 "protectedClaims": [
  {"id": "revenue-growth", "text": "Wholesale orders grew 18% from Q2 to Q3", "requiredQualifiers": ["estimated", "September invoice export"], "selector": "#claim-revenue"},
  {"id": "route-cost", "text": "The route cost", "requiredQualifiers": ["not priced"]}
 ]}
```

The draft's style rules included `border:2px solid #E2E2E3` on the card, `color:#FF7A00` on the growth figure and the heading "Quarterly Wholesale Review". The page had no `main` element and no media queries.

## Output

`runtime_preflight.py --json` [trimmed]: `"ok": true`, `"profile_name": "Baseline"`, `"logo": null`, `"uses_system_fonts": true`, `"missing": []`.

First pass, `parity_audit.py manifest.json draft.html --strict` [trimmed to findings and summary]:

```json
"errors": [
  {"code": "REQUIRED_SELECTOR_MISSING", "detail": "main"},
  {"code": "MAIN_LANDMARK_MISSING", "detail": "A main landmark is required"}
],
"warnings": [
  {"code": "CLAIM_ASSOCIATION_MANUAL_REVIEW", "detail": "route-cost: qualifiers checked globally because no selector was supplied"},
  {"code": "PRINT_QUERY_ABSENT", "detail": "No print media query text found"},
  {"code": "RESPONSIVE_QUERY_ABSENT", "detail": "No width-based media query text found"}
],
"summary": {"errorCount": 2, "warningCount": 3, "lexicalStructuralPass": false, "releasePass": false}
```

Exit 1. `brand_check.py draft.html`:

```
  BRAND CHECK   tokens: authoritative (Baseline)

  draft.html
    FAIL  OFF_PALETTE        draft.html:7  #ff7a00 has no token in the selected brand profile.
    FAIL  BORDER_WIDTH       draft.html:6  border 2px; borders are always 1px.
    warn  TITLE_CASE_HEADING draft.html:11  "Quarterly Wholesale Review" looks title-cased; headings are sentence case.

  FAIL: 2 failure(s), 1 review flag(s)
```

Exit 1. The fixes changed the page, not the claims:

- The content is wrapped in `main`, with a width query and a print query added.
- The card border is now 1px. The growth figure uses the profile's accent token, `#37437D`, and is set in bold.
- The heading is now "Quarterly wholesale review".
- The Saturday delivery paragraph has the id `claim-route`, and the manifest's `route-cost` claim now names that selector, so its "not priced" qualifier is checked inside its own paragraph.

Second pass on `fixed.html`. `parity_audit.py --strict` returns `"errorCount": 0, "warningCount": 0, "lexicalStructuralPass": true, "releasePass": false` and exits 0. `brand_check.py`:

```
  BRAND CHECK   tokens: authoritative (Baseline)

  fixed.html
    clean

  PASS: 0 failure(s), 0 review flag(s)
```

The parity and brand gates pass. `releasePass` is still false by design. Release also needs the prose gate, a look at the rendered page and a release note with a disposition for each gate, and none of those ran here.

---

# Build deal decision deck

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`deck.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/deck.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

The DDOC is the Deal Decision deck: a client-facing PPTX that runs immediately before the proposal. Its job is getting the client on record accepting a boundary before the provider contracts to it.

"Deal Desk document" and "discussion document" are retired names for this same artifact. If either surfaces, build the Deal Decision deck described here.

## The discipline

Copy approved first, then built. Rendering after approval is cheap; re-rendering after rejection is not. Rejected decks fail on copy, not on layout.

The gate that enforces this is `build_ddoc.js --check`. It runs the full preflight without rendering, so the copy can be gated in any environment, including ones where the renderer cannot be installed. Run it at the end of Phase 1 and again at Phase 4.

## Phase 0: pin the mode and the source

**Mode is a scope fact, not an authoring preference.** It follows from the option count.

- **Decision mode.** The client is choosing between options. One deck covering all of them, never one deck per option. Contrast is the mechanism: a client shown one option evaluates it against doing nothing, which is always cheaper. Two or three options. Never four.
- **Confirmation mode.** One option. Same skeleton, comparison replaced by boundary confirmation. A single-option playbook still gets a DDOC, because the artifact's job is the boundary, not the comparison.

Then pin:

1. **Audience.** Who is in the room and what decision the meeting produces. Sponsor, budget holder, technical veto.
2. **Source.** The quote identifier and its source data, from an available integration or a supplied local export. Confirm totals and scope line items. Populate `quote_snapshot` with each `quote_field` and its actual source value; the builder rejects a figure that differs or has no source value.
3. **Existing draft.** If there is a PPTX, run `python3 scripts/extract_slide_text.py <deck.pptx>` and present the extracted copy as the starting point rather than starting clean. The extractor also takes `--json`, `--manifest`, `--figures`, and `--diagnostic`; run it with `-h` for current usage.

Do not proceed until the mode, audience, source, and any existing draft are pinned.

## Phase 1: build the manifest

The manifest is JSON, not a deck. Schema and both skeletons are in `ddoc-patterns.md`. Populate from the quote and the source documents.

Flag anything inferred with `[FLAG: reason]`. Never fill a gap with a plausible-sounding projection. The builder refuses to render an unresolved flag, which is deliberate.

Gate the manifest before showing it to anyone:

```bash
node scripts/build_ddoc.js manifest.json --check
```

This catches structural problems (missing slides, option count, evidence classes, line budgets) before a human spends attention on wording.

## Phase 2: diagnostic scan

Run the prose gate over the manifest's authored text. `review-writing` owns this review. Its bundled internal `writing-diagnostics` runtime provides `prose_check.py`; resolve that runtime and run its script:

```bash
python3 ../writing-diagnostics/scripts/prose_check.py extracted.txt --config ../writing-diagnostics/house.json
```

Exit code 0 is a pass, 1 is a fail. Report the counts the scanner prints, never an adjective. "Clean" is not a finding; "0 fail, 2 warn" is.

Then run a figure tie-out against the quote. A figure mismatch and a section symbol are blockers and must clear before Phase 4.

## Phase 3: slide-by-slide review

One slide at a time. Never batch. For each: present the copy as it will appear, surface the Phase 2 flags for that slide, propose a rewrite with what changed and why, and wait. Approved moves on; edit requested is applied and re-presented; deferred is flagged and must clear before Phase 4.

Worked before-and-after pairs for every failure mode below are in `examples.md`. Read it before proposing a rewrite; it shows the accepted fix rather than describing it.

Rules applied during review, beyond the scanner:

- Every body line is a complete declarative sentence. Fragments are a hard fail.
- Headers carry the slide's point, not a label. "Three versions, one decision" rather than "Overview".
- Colon constructions on body lines are almost always wrong. A label earns one; a sentence rarely does.
- Symmetry is broken by wording, not truncation. Three cards opening "Everything in Tier 1 plus" are rewritten specifically for what each does.
- Assumptions are framed as the conditions under which the price holds, not as fine print. That framing is what makes the Change Order conversation survivable.
- Scope reads as boundaries and outcomes, not feature lists.
- Every not-included line routes to a paid next step.
- Line budgets are hard. A line that overflows on the rendered slide is a build-time failure.

## Phase 4: build and gate

```bash
node scripts/build_ddoc.js manifest.json --check          # gate: preflight only, no render
node scripts/build_ddoc.js manifest.json -o OUT.pptx      # build once the gate passes
```

Then rasterize and inspect every slide for overflow, leftover placeholder text, and figure drift. Report what was checked, not that it looks good. All three release gates need a written disposition before delivery.

The builder refuses to render on a preflight failure. It checks skeleton presence and order, option count, exactly one recommended option, identical section sets across option blocks, word-count parity across options, evidence classes on the heard slide, figure-to-quote-field mapping against `quote_snapshot`, a declared profile logo that exists and is readable, em dashes, the section symbol, unresolved flags, and line budgets. Fix the manifest, not the deck.

## The heard slide carries evidence classes

Every item on "what we heard" is `{text, evidence, source}`. Only `client_stated` renders. `seller_asserted` and `inferred` items either become questions on the "what we need from you" slide or are dropped. The classes and sources go into speaker notes, not onto the slide.

A slide that attributes to the client something they never said is the fastest way to lose a room. The worked pair in `examples.md` shows the required correction.

Source material reaches the team through whatever the account uses: Google Drive, Gmail, Slack, Salesforce, or a connected meeting-notes integration. No single tool is standard. Read what is actually there through the available MCP integrations, prefer a complete speaker-labeled transcript over a summary, and never substitute a similarly titled note for the one that was named.

## Brand

Use the shared [brand policy](references/estate/brand.md) or the confirmed project
profile. The Node renderer reads it through `brand_runtime.js`; set
`SKILLS_BRAND_PROFILE` to select an explicit profile. Preserve identical geometry
across options so the comparison follows scope. Logo and provider identity are
optional inputs, never inherited from a former company.

A profile with `logo` null needs no asset. A declared logo is resolved relative to the
directory of the selected profile file, the same rule the renderer uses. `--check`
fails with the resolved path when that file does not exist or cannot be read, before
any rendering.

## Boundaries

- Does not price. The quote owns the number; this renders it.
- Does not author scope language. Scope comes from the quote or the user; this audits and cleans it.
- Writing review belongs to review-writing; the bundled internal diagnostic tools support that review.
- Does not build the SOW. That is `write-statement-of-work`.
- Authors and builds the DDOC: copy approval, then the PPTX build. Copy approval and the slide-copy editorial rules both live in this skill; the per-slide-type editorial rules are in `references/slide-copy-patterns.md`.

## Running unattended

Phases 0 and 3 need a human. On a scheduled or headless run, do not simulate the approvals.

Do this instead: build the manifest, run `--check` and the prose gate, and stop with the findings and the unresolved flags. Say plainly that copy approval is outstanding. Never render a client-facing deck on an unattended run, and never record an approval nobody gave.

## Files

- `scripts/build_ddoc.js` · the builder and the gate. pptxgenjs for rendering, preflight for gating. `--check` runs the gate alone.
- `scripts/render.js` · rendering helpers. Must sit beside `build_ddoc.js` in `scripts/`.
- `scripts/extract_slide_text.py` · pull copy out of an existing deck. Needs `python-pptx` (see `scripts/requirements.txt`); everything else here is stdlib.
- `references/ddoc-patterns.md` · both skeletons, the manifest schema, and the failure-mode table.
- `references/slide-copy-patterns.md` · slide-type editorial rules for the copy (problem, capability hierarchy, options, differentiators, investment, timeline, next steps, anti-patterns).
- `references/slide-layouts.md` · line budgets per layout.
- `references/examples.md` · worked before-and-after pairs for every failure mode.
- `references/example-*.json` · worked manifest and input examples.

## Dependencies

The **gate** needs Node only. `build_ddoc.js --check` runs with no third-party packages, by design: the renderer is loaded lazily inside `build()` so a missing renderer can never disable the quality gate. Do not move those requires back to module scope.

The **renderer** needs `pptxgenjs` (`npm install pptxgenjs`). Where the npm registry is unreachable (for example an install that returns 403), the renderer cannot run and `--check` is the only usable path; build the PPTX in an environment with registry access.

The diagnostic commands (`prose_check.py`, `house.json`) remain in the bundled internal `writing-diagnostics` runtime. Use Writing Integrity for review; do not install a separate Prose Pass skill.

PPTX validation and rasterization for the visual gate are environment-specific. Use the host's presentation skill and its documented render-and-verify workflow (for example, the Claude `pptx` skill or the Codex `presentations` skill). If neither is available, substitute an equivalent validation and rasterization step and state which one was used in the release note. Do not claim the visual gate passed without naming the mechanism that rendered the slides.

## Release gate (required)

Before you deliver, run the gate. This is a required step, not a suggestion, and
not something a reviewer does later. Full spec in
[`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md).

1. Apply review-writing to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For
   a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.
2. Run brand-renderer on the branded artifact: palette, borders, radii, logo,
   footer.
3. Run review-deliverable before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until every check that applies has passed.

One slide at a time. Never batch. For each: present the copy as it will appear, surface the Phase 2 flags for that slide, propose a rewrite with what changed and why, and wait. Approved moves on; edit requested is applied and re-presented; deferred is flagged and must clear before Phase 4.

Worked before-and-after pairs for every failure mode below are in examples.md. Read it before proposing a rewrite; it shows the accepted fix rather than describing it.

Rules applied during review, beyond the scanner:

  • Every body line is a complete declarative sentence. Fragments are a hard fail.
  • Headers carry the slide's point, not a label. "Three versions, one decision" rather than "Overview".
  • Colon constructions on body lines are almost always wrong. A label earns one; a sentence rarely does.
  • Symmetry is broken by wording, not truncation. Three cards opening "Everything in Tier 1 plus" are rewritten specifically for what each does.
  • Assumptions are framed as the conditions under which the price holds, not as fine print. That framing is what makes the Change Order conversation survivable.
  • Scope reads as boundaries and outcomes, not feature lists.
  • Every not-included line routes to a paid next step.
  • Line budgets are hard. A line that overflows on the rendered slide is a build-time failure.

Phase 4: build and gate

node scripts/build_ddoc.js manifest.json --check          # gate: preflight only, no render
node scripts/build_ddoc.js manifest.json -o OUT.pptx      # build once the gate passes

Then rasterize and inspect every slide for overflow, leftover placeholder text, and figure drift. Report what was checked, not that it looks good. All three release gates need a written disposition before delivery.

The builder refuses to render on a preflight failure. It checks skeleton presence and order, option count, exactly one recommended option, identical section sets across option blocks, word-count parity across options, evidence classes on the heard slide, figure-to-quote-field mapping against quote_snapshot, a declared profile logo that exists and is readable, em dashes, the section symbol, unresolved flags, and line budgets. Fix the manifest, not the deck.

The heard slide carries evidence classes

Every item on "what we heard" is {text, evidence, source}. Only client_stated renders. seller_asserted and inferred items either become questions on the "what we need from you" slide or are dropped. The classes and sources go into speaker notes, not onto the slide.

A slide that attributes to the client something they never said is the fastest way to lose a room. The worked pair in examples.md shows the required correction.

Source material reaches the team through whatever the account uses: Google Drive, Gmail, Slack, Salesforce, or a connected meeting-notes integration. No single tool is standard. Read what is actually there through the available MCP integrations, prefer a complete speaker-labeled transcript over a summary, and never substitute a similarly titled note for the one that was named.

Brand

Use the shared brand policy (references/estate/brand.md) or the confirmed project profile. The Node renderer reads it through brand_runtime.js; set SKILLS_BRAND_PROFILE to select an explicit profile. Preserve identical geometry across options so the comparison follows scope. Logo and provider identity are optional inputs, never inherited from a former company.

A profile with logo null needs no asset. A declared logo is resolved relative to the directory of the selected profile file, the same rule the renderer uses. --check fails with the resolved path when that file does not exist or cannot be read, before any rendering.

Boundaries

  • Does not price. The quote owns the number; this renders it.
  • Does not author scope language. Scope comes from the quote or the user; this audits and cleans it.
  • Writing review belongs to review-writing; the bundled internal diagnostic tools support that review.
  • Does not build the SOW. That is write-statement-of-work.
  • Authors and builds the DDOC: copy approval, then the PPTX build. Copy approval and the slide-copy editorial rules both live in this skill; the per-slide-type editorial rules are in references/slide-copy-patterns.md.

Running unattended

Phases 0 and 3 need a human. On a scheduled or headless run, do not simulate the approvals.

Do this instead: build the manifest, run --check and the prose gate, and stop with the findings and the unresolved flags. Say plainly that copy approval is outstanding. Never render a client-facing deck on an unattended run, and never record an approval nobody gave.

Files

  • scripts/build_ddoc.js · the builder and the gate. pptxgenjs for rendering, preflight for gating. --check runs the gate alone.
  • scripts/render.js · rendering helpers. Must sit beside build_ddoc.js in scripts/.
  • scripts/extract_slide_text.py · pull copy out of an existing deck. Needs python-pptx (see scripts/requirements.txt); everything else here is stdlib.
  • references/ddoc-patterns.md · both skeletons, the manifest schema, and the failure-mode table.
  • references/slide-copy-patterns.md · slide-type editorial rules for the copy (problem, capability hierarchy, options, differentiators, investment, timeline, next steps, anti-patterns).
  • references/slide-layouts.md · line budgets per layout.
  • references/examples.md · worked before-and-after pairs for every failure mode.
  • references/example-*.json · worked manifest and input examples.

Dependencies

The gate needs Node only. build_ddoc.js --check runs with no third-party packages, by design: the renderer is loaded lazily inside build() so a missing renderer can never disable the quality gate. Do not move those requires back to module scope.

The renderer needs pptxgenjs (npm install pptxgenjs). Where the npm registry is unreachable (for example an install that returns 403), the renderer cannot run and --check is the only usable path; build the PPTX in an environment with registry access.

The diagnostic commands (prose_check.py, house.json) remain in the bundled internal writing-diagnostics runtime. Use Writing Integrity for review; do not install a separate Prose Pass skill.

PPTX validation and rasterization for the visual gate are environment-specific. Use the host's presentation skill and its documented render-and-verify workflow (for example, the Claude pptx skill or the Codex presentations skill). If neither is available, substitute an equivalent validation and rasterization step and state which one was used in the release note. Do not claim the visual gate passed without naming the mechanism that rendered the slides.

Release gate (required)

Before you deliver, run the gate. This is a required step, not a suggestion, and not something a reviewer does later. Full spec in release-gate.md (../_shared/release-gate.md).

  1. Apply review-writing to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For

a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.

  1. Run brand-renderer on the branded artifact: palette, borders, radii, logo,

footer.

  1. Run review-deliverable before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until every check that applies has passed.

examples.title: Scope decision deck for a multi-clinic scheduling project
examples.markdown:
## Request

We present to Larkspur Veterinary Group on Thursday and need the scope decision deck for the clinic scheduling project, with their choice between the three quoted options. The discovery notes and the quote export are attached. Please gate the copy and tell me what still needs approval before we build.

## Inputs

Run of the built `build-deck` task package in its "scope decision deck" mode. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Other files it produced, not shown here: `manifest.json`.

#### discovery-notes.md

#### Larkspur Veterinary Group: discovery call, 9 Oct 2026

Attendees: Priya Venkataram (Operations Director, sponsor), Tomasz Okafor (IT Manager, technical veto), Dana Whitlock (Finance Lead). Provider side: two consultants.

##### Client statements (verbatim from transcript)

- Priya: "Reception re-types every booking from the phone log into the scheduling system, and we lose about forty minutes a day per clinic doing it."
- Priya: "We have nine clinics and each one runs its own calendar. I can't see a free surgeon across sites."
- Tomasz: "Our patient records system is fine. I do not want it touched this year."
- Dana: "Whatever we choose has to be signed off before the January budget lock, which is 15 January."
- Tomasz: "Reminder texts go out from a separate tool, and about one in ten bounces because the numbers are stale."

##### Provider observations (not stated by the client)

- Seller note: the clients probably want online booking eventually.
- Seller note: leadership seems frustrated with the current vendor.

##### Open questions

- How many staff users across the nine clinics? (Priya guessed "around 120", unconfirmed.)
- Who owns phone system admin access?

#### quote-export.txt

Quote Q-LVG-2208 (export, 2 Nov 2026). Fixed fees, USD.

Option A: Single calendar. Fee 41,500. Duration 8 weeks.
  In: one shared scheduling calendar for all nine clinics; migration of future appointments only; staff training for up to 40 users.
  Out: phone log integration; reminder text tool; past appointment history.
  Assumes: one data export from the legacy scheduler; client provides test users.

Option B: Single calendar with phone log capture. Fee 63,200. Duration 12 weeks.
  In: everything in A's calendar and migration; bookings captured from the phone log into the calendar without re-typing; training for up to 90 users.
  Out: reminder text tool; past appointment history.
  Assumes: phone system vendor grants API access; client names a phone system admin.

Option C: Single calendar, phone log capture, and reminders. Fee 84,900. Duration 16 weeks.
  In: calendar, phone log capture, and reminder texts sent from the calendar with contact numbers cleaned during migration; training for up to 120 users.
  Out: past appointment history; online booking.
  Assumes: phone system API access; client approves a one-time contact data clean-up.

Not quoted in any option: patient records system changes, online booking, payment processing.
Recommended by the delivery lead: Option B.
Phases (B): Mobilize 1 wk, Design 3 wks, Build 5 wks, Validate 2 wks, Cutover 1 wk.

## Output

I've written and hand-gated the manifest for the Larkspur deck, but the copy still needs your approval and I have not built a PPTX. The skill says not to render a client deck without a human approving the copy slide by slide.

I couldn't run `build_ddoc.js --check` or `prose_check.py` here. I applied the `--check` rules to the manifest by hand, so my counts are not tool output. Please re-run both before building.

#### What I pinned

- **Mode:** decision mode, because the quote has three options (A, B, C).
- **Recommended option:** B, the single calendar with phone log capture. The delivery lead recommends it in the quote export.
- **Audience:** Priya Venkataram (Operations Director, sponsor), Tomasz Okafor (IT Manager, technical veto) and Dana Whitlock (Finance Lead, budget).
- **Date:** 5 Nov 2026, the Thursday you named.
- **Deadline:** 15 January, the budget lock Dana gave. It anchors the decision slide.

#### Gate result (by hand)

- **Structure:** 0 failures, 0 warnings across 9 slides. All seven required decision-mode slides are present, in the reference order.
- **Options:** the three option blocks have identical sections. Their word-count spread is about 1.22x, under the 1.4x limit.
- **Figures:** all three fees tie to the quote (A $41,500, B $63,200, C $84,900), as do the durations and training numbers. Two derived figures also check out: $21,700 more for each step up, and 4 more weeks from B to C.
- **Heard slide:** all five items are `client_stated`, each with a named source. Two of your own observations are not on it: that they probably want online booking, and that leadership is frustrated with the vendor.
- **Banned characters:** 0 em dashes, 0 section symbols, 0 placeholders.

#### The copy awaiting approval

| # | Headline | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Re-typing and separate calendars cost your clinics time every day | Five quotes from Priya, Tomasz and Dana, about re-typing, nine separate calendars, stale reminder numbers, the patient records system and the budget lock. |
| 2 | We recommend the single calendar with phone log capture | It ends the re-typing that costs each clinic about forty minutes a day and leaves patient records alone. Calendar alone leaves re-typing. Reminders add 4 weeks and $21,700 and need a contact data clean-up. Reminders can follow as a later phase. |
| 3 | Each option adds one capability, at a fixed fee | Table with fee, duration, in scope, staff trained, not in scope and assumptions for A, B and C. |
| 4 | Single calendar puts nine clinics on one schedule in eight weeks | A in detail: $41,500. Needs one legacy export and test users. |
| 5 | Phone log capture ends re-typing in twelve weeks | B in detail: $63,200. Needs phone system API access and a named phone system admin. |
| 6 | Reminders from the calendar reach cleaned numbers in sixteen weeks | C in detail: $84,900. Needs API access and approval of a one-time contact data clean-up. |
| 7 | Three things sit outside every option | Patient records system, past appointment history, online booking and payment processing. Each can be scoped as a separate paid phase. |
| 8 | Four things we need from you before you choose | Confirm the staff count (our ~120 is unconfirmed). Name the phone system admin owner. Say whether online booking is a priority (your hunch, now a question). Say whether a contact data clean-up is acceptable. |
| 9 | Choose an option before the 15 January budget lock | Choose an option and confirm its assumptions before 15 Jan. We send the proposal after that. Kickoff follows acceptance. |

Each option is described by what it contains, with no "everything in A plus" wording. Each exclusion routes to a paid next step.

#### Decisions for you

1. **Copy approval.** I need a reviewer to go through slides 1 to 9 one at a time. Until then, nothing is approved.
2. **Timeline slide.** I left it out. The quote has phase lengths for B (1/3/5/2/1 weeks) but no milestones, and a phase bar without milestones is a rejected pattern. If you give me gate names, I'll add it.
3. **"Can be scoped as a later phase."** This wording implies future work the quote doesn't price. Please confirm you are happy to say it.
4. **Proposal turnaround.** The decision slide says "after you choose" because you gave me no turnaround time. Give me one if you want it on the slide.
5. **Provider name and logo.** None was supplied, so the neutral brand profile applies with no logo.

#### Still to do before delivery

1. Run `node scripts/build_ddoc.js manifest.json --check` and `prose_check.py` with `house.json`. Report their counts.
2. After approval, build the PPTX, then rasterize every slide and check for overflow and figure drift. The option text on slides 5 and 6 is the most likely to overflow.
3. Complete the three release gates: review-writing, brand-renderer and review-deliverable. None has been run, so the deck is not final.

#### Files

- `out/manifest.json`: the deck manifest, with the full copy, the quote snapshot, the figure mappings and speaker notes carrying evidence sources.
- `out/gate-report.md`: the hand-run preflight table, the figure tie-out, how the two non-client observations were handled, and the outstanding items.
- `out/answer.md`: this reply.

### File: gate-report.md

#### Gate report: Larkspur Veterinary Group, Q-LVG-2208

Method: `build_ddoc.js --check` and `prose_check.py` cannot be run here. Every rule in `preflight()` was applied by hand to `manifest.json`. These are hand counts, not tool output. Re-run both commands in a working environment before the build.

##### Phase 0 pins

| Item | Value | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mode | Decision | Three quoted options (A, B, C) |
| Audience | Priya Venkataram (sponsor), Tomasz Okafor (technical veto), Dana Whitlock (budget) | Discovery notes |
| Source | Quote Q-LVG-2208, export of 2 Nov 2026 | `inputs/quote-export.txt` |
| Existing draft | None | Nothing supplied, so no extraction run |
| Recommended option | B | Delivery lead, per the quote export |

##### Phase 1: manifest preflight (by hand)

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Option count 2 to 3 | Pass (3) |
| Exactly one recommended | Pass (B) |
| Skeleton: heard, recommendation, comparison, option_block, outside_all, need_from_you, decision | Pass, all present |
| Order matches reference order | Pass, no warning |
| One option_block per option, unique names | Pass (3 of 3) |
| Identical section keys across blocks | Pass (In scope, Not in scope, Assumptions, Timeline) |
| Word-count parity, builder method (all authored strings in the block) | A about 74, B about 80, C about 90. Spread 1.22x, under 1.4x |
| Comparison rows: 6 rows, 3 cells each | Pass |
| Heard items all `client_stated` with source | Pass (5 of 5) |
| Figures map to `quote_snapshot` with equal values | Pass (41,500 / 63,200 / 84,900) |
| Em dash, section symbol, TBD, `[FLAG:` | 0 found |
| Title budget 78 chars | Longest 66. Pass |
| Subtitle budget 120 | One subtitle, about 116. Pass |
| Bullet budget 150, at most 7 bullets | Longest about 125. Max 3 per slide. Pass |
| Bullets end in terminal punctuation | Pass |
| Logo | Profile not resolved here. Neutral profile assumed, so no logo declared |

Hand count: 0 failures, 0 warnings, across 9 slides (10 with the cover).

##### Phase 2: figure tie-out

| Displayed figure | Quote value | Match |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $41,500, 8 weeks (A) | 41,500, 8 weeks | Yes |
| $63,200, 12 weeks (B) | 63,200, 12 weeks | Yes |
| $84,900, 16 weeks (C) | 84,900, 16 weeks | Yes |
| $21,700 more for reminders | 84,900 - 63,200 | Yes |
| 4 more weeks for reminders | 16 - 12 | Yes |
| Staff trained 40 / 90 / 120 | Quote training lines | Yes |
| "About forty minutes a day" | Priya, verbatim | Yes |

Prose gate: the scanner was not run. By-hand pass found 0 fragment bullets, 0 label headers, 0 colons on body lines, and no "Everything in A plus" constructions. Scanner counts are still required.

##### Evidence classes dropped from the slide

| Observation | Class | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clients probably want online booking eventually | seller_asserted | Question on need_from_you |
| Leadership seems frustrated with the current vendor | seller_asserted | Dropped. No question follows from it |
| Around 120 staff | Unconfirmed estimate | Question on need_from_you, and shown as unconfirmed |

##### Outstanding before build

1. Copy approval (Phase 3) has not happened. No slide has been presented one at a time to a reviewer.
2. No timeline slide. The quote gives phases for option B (1/3/5/2/1 weeks) but no milestones, and the copy rules reject a phase bar without them. Supply gate names if you want it.
3. The "can be scoped as a later phase" wording implies future pricing the quote does not hold. Confirm you are comfortable making that statement.
4. The decision slide promises a proposal "after you choose" with no turnaround time, because none was supplied.
5. Run `--check` and `prose_check.py`, then the render, rasterize, and the three release gates.

skills.markdown:
---
name: build-deck
description: 'Build or repair a presentation or reading deck around an audience decision, supported claims and explanatory visuals. Plans the narrative before rendering, chooses diagrams or charts for the relationships they explain, and verifies the finished artifact. Use for proposals, pitches and technical briefings.'
---


# Build deck

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`deck.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/deck.md). Read both before drafting.**

Plan what the deck must explain before choosing layouts. Save the evidence and slide plan before rendering.
Each slide must answer an audience question through its content. A claim repeated
in several text boxes does not explain the claim.

This skill owns the narrative and information design. `brand-renderer` applies
the selected canonical [brand profile](references/estate/brand.md). Brand identity
does not determine the diagram or force a fixed slide composition. Writing review
comes from `review-writing`.

## When to use

- A proposal, pitch, technical briefing or reading deck.
- When a deck "feels sparse / awkward / off" and needs a structured rebuild.
- Apply the same reasoning to a requested slide repair; preserve its place in the wider argument.

## Project shape

Work inside whatever engagement folder the project uses. Resolve it, do not assume
one: ask, or take it from the path you were invoked in. The following files retain each stage:

```text
deck/
  00_brief.md          # the input: audience, decision, constraints
  01_one_message.md    # the single thesis (GATE 1)
  02_submessages.md    # supporting claims and evidence
  03_structure.md      # slide-by-slide plan
  04_copy.md           # real headline + body text per slide
  05_design_notes.md   # brand application notes (from brand-renderer)
  deck.(pptx|html)     # the build
  06_polish_todo.md    # output of the QA pass (GATE 2)
```

## Stage gates: do not skip, save before advancing

Read [Visual argument](references/visual-argument.md) before planning. Establish
whether the audience will hear a presenter or read the deck alone. A reading
edition must carry its own explanation. Preserve detailed evidence in the deck
or an appendix when the decision needs it.

### Gate 1: Main claim

Before any slides, reduce the deck to **one sentence the reader must remember.**

1. Name the audience and decision. Record their existing knowledge and supplied
   concerns. Do not invent emotional reactions.
2. Separate the *offer* from the *thesis*. A product/service name is not a message.
3. Write a direct claim tied to the decision and its evidence. For example:
   `Prove the nightly reconciliation on a complete batch before switching finance operations.`
   Use the actual decision; do not copy a rhetorical sentence pattern.
4. Reject any message that is a feature list, a vague benefit, a vendor-centered
   claim, or too broad to prove inside this deck.
5. The thesis record contains the message, why it's right, and what the deck
   should deliberately **not** try to say.

Do not advance until this sentence exists and is provable by the deck you're about to plan.

### Stage 2: Submessages

Identify the claims needed to support the thesis. Each needs evidence the deck
can show. Record a missing source before choosing a representation that requires
it. Do not invent financial benefits or measured results to populate a chart.

### Stage 3: Structure

The structure record gives each slide a role in the argument. Record the audience
question and supported takeaway. Identify its evidence, the relationship to show,
the proposed visual and why the next slide follows.
Cut any slide that only says "we will provide" or repeats a prior point.
Sketch the visual before fitting prose into a layout. A sequence diagram should
expose what each actor knows; a scope diagram should locate the boundary. The
plan is complete when every claim has an explanation and evidence.

### Stage 4: Copy

The copy record has the actual headline and body text for each slide. Name the action or behavior the slide explains. Remove a subtitle that repeats the headline. Keep headlines short, break body text at meaning units, and use consistent terms. **Review this with `review-writing`** before it goes
into the build. Diagram labels may name an actor, state, field or transition concisely. Review their meaning and consistency; do not expand them into prose merely to satisfy sentence length. This does not exempt labels from writing review.

### Stage 5: Design + build

Invoke **`brand-renderer`** for the selected visual profile, then build the deck (`pptx`
skill for PowerPoint, or HTML/CSS if a browser-previewable / diffable deck is
wanted). Capture any brand-application notes in `05_design_notes.md`. Never bake
real body text into images.

The bundled HTML route is documented in [HTML production](references/html-production.md). It creates editable text, applies the selected profile, and supports PDF export. For PowerPoint, use an available presentation tool and keep its editable source. Never rename an HTML file to `.pptx`.

Use a renderer that can express the selected visual. Route unsupported chart
types or annotated screenshots to an available plotting or presentation tool.
Never silently replace a diagram with numbered prose because the bundled
renderer lacks the required form. Keep the source data with the visual.

### Gate 2: Review the finished deck

Run the QA checklist below against the built deck, then record each recurring fix in the project
copy of `polish-learnings.md` so the next deck's first build avoids it.

1. **Read `polish-learnings.md` first** and apply it as a pre-checklist.
2. Walk the checklist:
   - **Argument:** every slide supports the one message; no orphan slides; chapter/section labels match the structure.
   - **Explanation:** answer each storyboard question from the finished slide. Identify the actual element that supplies the answer. Check that arrows and branches have defined meanings. A populated field does not prove that a reader can understand the relationship.
   - **Text:** headlines short; no awkward orphan line; key text bold enough; terms unified; reviewed with `review-writing`.
   - **Layout:** no clipping or label collisions. Preserve evidence when adjusting density. Empty space does not require an extra card; use the space the explanation needs.
   - **Icons/images:** visual center aligned to its background shape; assets not blurry, cropped, or too small.
   - **Thumbnail test:** inspect the argument's progression and visual hierarchy. Read detailed diagrams at delivery size; thumbnails cannot validate their labels.
   - **Export:** PDF/PNG export does not break layout.
3. Write `06_polish_todo.md`: critical fixes, nice-to-haves, and exact locations
   (slide #, CSS selector) to edit.
4. Append any fix that recurs to the project learning record. Include the slide and repair.
   Propose changes to the canonical skill through estate maintenance; an installed package
   stays immutable so that its source and deployed hashes remain consistent.

## Rules

- One artifact per stage, saved before advancing. No skipping straight to the build.
- Process lives here; brand lives in `brand-renderer`; writing review follows `review-writing`.
- If a brief is thin, record assumptions and identify missing evidence. Continue the supported work; keep proposed behavior distinct from observed results.

## Release gate (required)

Run the release checks before delivery. The complete requirements are in
[`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md).

1. Apply review-writing to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For
   a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.
2. Run brand-renderer on the branded artifact: palette, borders, radii, logo,
   footer.
3. Run review-deliverable before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until every check that applies has passed.

examples.title: Pilot approval deck for tablet check-in at two food pantry sites
examples.markdown:
## Request

Please build a deck for our board operations committee asking them to approve a six-week pilot of tablet check-in at two of our pantry sites. The brief and my pilot notes are in the inputs folder; the committee will read it ahead of the meeting rather than watch me present.

## Inputs

Run of the built `build-deck` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### brief.md

#### Brief: tablet check-in pilot

Organisation: Tidewater Pantry Network (5 sites, mostly volunteer-run).

Audience: board operations committee. Chair Priya Anand; operations director Tomasz Wells; volunteer coordinator Ife Okafor. They have seen the paper sign-in sheets but have not seen the vendor's app.

Decision wanted: approve a six-week pilot at Eastgate and Mill Road, 6 Jan to 16 Feb 2027, with a spending cap of $4,200. Committee meets 18 Nov 2026.

Rule we enforce: a household may visit at most 2 times per calendar month.

Concerns the committee has raised before:
- Volunteers are not technical and turnover is high.
- Mill Road wifi is unreliable.
- No home addresses should sit on the tablets.
- Nobody wants a family turned away because of a software error.

The deck will be emailed in advance. Paper sign-in stays running alongside the tablets for the whole pilot.

#### pilot-notes.txt

PILOT NOTES (Tomasz's working notes, Oct 2026)

September 2026 audit of paper sheets, two sites:
- Eastgate: 236 visits, 17 over the 2-per-month cap.
- Mill Road: 176 visits, 14 over the cap.
- Total 412 visits, 31 over the cap. Cap is checked by hand at month end, so these were found weeks after the visit.

Wifi: Mill Road lost connection in 5 of 12 observed Saturday sessions. Eastgate stayed connected in all 12 observed sessions.

Vendor (app called "TallyDesk"):
- Tablets work offline and sync when wifi returns.
- Vendor documentation says that when two tablets sync changes to the same household record, "the most recent sync wins". We have not tested this and have not asked the vendor what it means for visit counts.
- Household record can be set to ID number and first name only; no address needed.

Our proposed handling (not yet confirmed with vendor): each tablet saves every visit as its own entry with tablet ID and time. The shared record counts entries after sync. A household with more than 2 entries in the month is flagged to the coordinator the next morning. Nobody is refused at the door on the basis of tablet data during the pilot.

Pilot costs (estimates):
- 4 tablets at $450 each
- Licence $60 per site per month, 2 sites, 2 billing months
- Volunteer training $600
Spending cap approved to ask for: $4,200.

Proposed pass test: after six weeks, every paper-sheet visit at the two sites appears in the tablet record, and every household over the cap is flagged within one day.

## Output

I've built the seven-slide reading deck as editable HTML, but I haven't seen it rendered or run any checks. This environment couldn't run scripts or open a browser. I wrote the HTML by hand, following the bundled `deck.css` rules, rather than running `build_html.py`. Please open it at 1280×720 and print to PDF before it goes to the committee.

**Main claim:** Approve the six-week, two-site pilot, and start it only after the vendor confirms in writing that two offline visits for one household are both kept.

I made the vendor question the centre of the deck because it is the one risk that could make tablets worse than paper. Your notes say the vendor's documentation reads "the most recent sync wins", and nobody has tested what that does to visit counts. Two tablets that were offline could each log a second visit for the same household. Keeping only the last sync would then show 2 visits when the household has made 3, and the over-cap visit would go unnoticed.

#### The deck

| # | Title | Visual |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Approve a six-week tablet pilot, starting only after the vendor answers one question | Table of the request |
| 2 | Paper finds households over the visit cap weeks after the visit | Bar chart: 17 (Eastgate) and 14 (Mill Road) over-cap visits in September, on a 0–20 scale |
| 3 | Offline tablets could each accept a visit that together exceeds the cap | Sequence diagram: Shared record, Tablet A, Tablet B |
| 4 | Save every visit as its own entry, count after sync, flag the next morning | Flow with one decision ("More than 2 this month?") |
| 5 | Four tests decide whether the pilot passed | Table: test, expected result, record to keep |
| 6 | The pilot costs an estimated $2,640 and paper stays in place | Cost table |
| 7 | Vote on 18 November; start on 6 January only if the vendor says yes | Owners and dates table |

Figures reconciled against your notes:
- 17 + 14 = 31 over-cap visits, out of 236 + 176 = 412 visits.
- Costs: $1,800 + $240 + $600 = $2,640, which leaves $1,560 under the $4,200 cap.
- Mill Road lost its connection in 5 of 12 observed sessions, and Eastgate in none of 12.

Some things are labelled as proposed or estimated rather than established:
- Slide 4's handling (each visit saved as its own entry, counted after sync) comes from your notes and is not confirmed with the vendor.
- The pass tests have not been run.
- The costs are estimates.
- H-210 on slide 3 is an illustrative household.

Your four concerns appear as follows:
- **Mill Road wifi:** slides 3 and 5.
- **No addresses on tablets:** slide 6, which proposes the ID-and-first-name setting.
- **Nobody refused at the door:** slides 1 and 6.
- **Non-technical volunteers:** slide 5, as a new-volunteer test with a help log.

#### Gaps and assumptions to check
- **Owners and dates:** on slide 7, Tomasz Wells for the vendor question and the run, and Ife Okafor for training, are my proposals. So is the 2 Dec 2026 target for the vendor's answer. Please confirm them with the people named. The results review has no date yet.
- **Brand:** you gave no brand profile, so the deck uses the neutral Baseline profile (navy accent, Inter with system fallback, no logo). I worked that out by hand from the brand rules.
- **Training and licences:** I took the $600 training cost and the 2 billing months of licences straight from your notes. Please check that 2 months is right for a six-week pilot.
- **Not run:** the writing and brand checkers and the review-deliverable receipt. I reviewed the writing by hand, including every title in order and every figure.
- **Layout risks:** the most likely overflow is slides 5, 6 and 7, which have long tables. Slide 3's diagram labels and slide 4's diamond text also need a look.
- **Input JSON:** I didn't generate the deck's input JSON, so the bundled collision checks haven't run. The storyboard is in `03_structure.md` and `04_copy.md`.

#### Files (all in `out/deck/`)
- `deck.html`: the deck, with live text and SVG diagrams.
- `00_brief.md`, `01_one_message.md`, `02_submessages.md`, `03_structure.md`, `04_copy.md`: the stage records, saved before the build.
- `05_design_notes.md`: the brand profile used and how it was applied.
- `06_polish_todo.md`: the fixes to verify on the rendered slides, with locations.
- `polish-learnings.md`: the project copy of the polish rules.

Request

Please build a deck for our board operations committee asking them to approve a six-week pilot of tablet check-in at two of our pantry sites. The brief and my pilot notes are in the inputs folder; the committee will read it ahead of the meeting rather than watch me present.

Inputs

Run of the built build-deck task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

brief.md
Brief: tablet check-in pilot

Organisation: Tidewater Pantry Network (5 sites, mostly volunteer-run).

Audience: board operations committee. Chair Priya Anand; operations director Tomasz Wells; volunteer coordinator Ife Okafor. They have seen the paper sign-in sheets but have not seen the vendor's app.

Decision wanted: approve a six-week pilot at Eastgate and Mill Road, 6 Jan to 16 Feb 2027, with a spending cap of $4,200. Committee meets 18 Nov 2026.

Rule we enforce: a household may visit at most 2 times per calendar month.

Concerns the committee has raised before:

  • Volunteers are not technical and turnover is high.
  • Mill Road wifi is unreliable.
  • No home addresses should sit on the tablets.
  • Nobody wants a family turned away because of a software error.

The deck will be emailed in advance. Paper sign-in stays running alongside the tablets for the whole pilot.

pilot-notes.txt

PILOT NOTES (Tomasz's working notes, Oct 2026)

September 2026 audit of paper sheets, two sites:

  • Eastgate: 236 visits, 17 over the 2-per-month cap.
  • Mill Road: 176 visits, 14 over the cap.
  • Total 412 visits, 31 over the cap. Cap is checked by hand at month end, so these were found weeks after the visit.

Wifi: Mill Road lost connection in 5 of 12 observed Saturday sessions. Eastgate stayed connected in all 12 observed sessions.

Vendor (app called "TallyDesk"):

  • Tablets work offline and sync when wifi returns.
  • Vendor documentation says that when two tablets sync changes to the same household record, "the most recent sync wins". We have not tested this and have not asked the vendor what it means for visit counts.
  • Household record can be set to ID number and first name only; no address needed.

Our proposed handling (not yet confirmed with vendor): each tablet saves every visit as its own entry with tablet ID and time. The shared record counts entries after sync. A household with more than 2 entries in the month is flagged to the coordinator the next morning. Nobody is refused at the door on the basis of tablet data during the pilot.

Pilot costs (estimates):

  • 4 tablets at $450 each
  • Licence $60 per site per month, 2 sites, 2 billing months
  • Volunteer training $600

Spending cap approved to ask for: $4,200.

Proposed pass test: after six weeks, every paper-sheet visit at the two sites appears in the tablet record, and every household over the cap is flagged within one day.

Output

I've built the seven-slide reading deck as editable HTML, but I haven't seen it rendered or run any checks. This environment couldn't run scripts or open a browser. I wrote the HTML by hand, following the bundled deck.css rules, rather than running build_html.py. Please open it at 1280×720 and print to PDF before it goes to the committee.

Main claim: Approve the six-week, two-site pilot, and start it only after the vendor confirms in writing that two offline visits for one household are both kept.

I made the vendor question the centre of the deck because it is the one risk that could make tablets worse than paper. Your notes say the vendor's documentation reads "the most recent sync wins", and nobody has tested what that does to visit counts. Two tablets that were offline could each log a second visit for the same household. Keeping only the last sync would then show 2 visits when the household has made 3, and the over-cap visit would go unnoticed.

The deck
#TitleVisual
1Approve a six-week tablet pilot, starting only after the vendor answers one questionTable of the request
2Paper finds households over the visit cap weeks after the visitBar chart: 17 (Eastgate) and 14 (Mill Road) over-cap visits in September, on a 0–20 scale
3Offline tablets could each accept a visit that together exceeds the capSequence diagram: Shared record, Tablet A, Tablet B
4Save every visit as its own entry, count after sync, flag the next morningFlow with one decision ("More than 2 this month?")
5Four tests decide whether the pilot passedTable: test, expected result, record to keep
6The pilot costs an estimated $2,640 and paper stays in placeCost table
7Vote on 18 November; start on 6 January only if the vendor says yesOwners and dates table

Figures reconciled against your notes:

  • 17 + 14 = 31 over-cap visits, out of 236 + 176 = 412 visits.
  • Costs: $1,800 + $240 + $600 = $2,640, which leaves $1,560 under the $4,200 cap.
  • Mill Road lost its connection in 5 of 12 observed sessions, and Eastgate in none of 12.

Some things are labelled as proposed or estimated rather than established:

  • Slide 4's handling (each visit saved as its own entry, counted after sync) comes from your notes and is not confirmed with the vendor.
  • The pass tests have not been run.
  • The costs are estimates.
  • H-210 on slide 3 is an illustrative household.

Your four concerns appear as follows:

  • Mill Road wifi: slides 3 and 5.
  • No addresses on tablets: slide 6, which proposes the ID-and-first-name setting.
  • Nobody refused at the door: slides 1 and 6.
  • Non-technical volunteers: slide 5, as a new-volunteer test with a help log.
Gaps and assumptions to check
  • Owners and dates: on slide 7, Tomasz Wells for the vendor question and the run, and Ife Okafor for training, are my proposals. So is the 2 Dec 2026 target for the vendor's answer. Please confirm them with the people named. The results review has no date yet.
  • Brand: you gave no brand profile, so the deck uses the neutral Baseline profile (navy accent, Inter with system fallback, no logo). I worked that out by hand from the brand rules.
  • Training and licences: I took the $600 training cost and the 2 billing months of licences straight from your notes. Please check that 2 months is right for a six-week pilot.
  • Not run: the writing and brand checkers and the review-deliverable receipt. I reviewed the writing by hand, including every title in order and every figure.
  • Layout risks: the most likely overflow is slides 5, 6 and 7, which have long tables. Slide 3's diagram labels and slide 4's diamond text also need a look.
  • Input JSON: I didn't generate the deck's input JSON, so the bundled collision checks haven't run. The storyboard is in 03_structure.md and 04_copy.md.
Files (all in out/deck/)
  • deck.html: the deck, with live text and SVG diagrams.
  • 00_brief.md, 01_one_message.md, 02_submessages.md, 03_structure.md, 04_copy.md: the stage records, saved before the build.
  • 05_design_notes.md: the brand profile used and how it was applied.
  • 06_polish_todo.md: the fixes to verify on the rendered slides, with locations.
  • polish-learnings.md: the project copy of the polish rules.

skills.title: Build editorial chart
skills.description: Build charts, small dashboards and data stories with newspaper-graphics discipline from New York Times and Upshot practice: one hero color with grey context, direct labels, a headline that states the finding, in-place annotation, 375px-first layout and D3 hover that snaps to the nearest mark. Renders static Observable Plot pages from a JSON spec (line, area, bar, scatter, small multiples, estimate ranges, progress against plan, dashed targets and projections) in the selected brand profile, Baseline by default. Use when a chart, graph or data panel should read as editorial and trustworthy rather than a default library chart. Not for measurement plans or tracking design (design-analytics-plan), explorer sites (build-interactive-explorer) or slide decks (build-deck). Does not publish or share anything.

guide.what: Build an editorial chart or small dashboard from supplied numbers, with the finding in the headline, one highlighted series and direct labels.
guide.when: Numbers with a known source need a chart that reads clearly on a phone and a desktop, including progress against plan, estimate ranges and targets.
guide.inputs: The numbers with their source, unit and timeframe, the finding or question, and optionally a brand profile.
guide.outputs: A self-contained HTML chart page in light and dark themes, checked by check_html.py.
guide.example: Chart these phase hours, planned against used, and highlight the workstream that hasn't started.
guide.expect: It picks the chart type, writes a JSON spec or D3 panel, renders the page in the selected brand profile (Baseline by default), runs the HTML check, and inspects the page at desktop width and 375px. It uses only the supplied numbers, draws targets and projections dashed, and keeps any hosted page private.
guide.requires: Python 3 for the scripts, Node for the inline script syntax check, and a browser for the visual check.
guide.overview: It chooses an appropriate chart for your question, prepares a data specification or interactive panel and renders an HTML page with direct labels, a finding-led headline and one highlighted series. Targets and projections are styled differently from actuals. It checks the HTML and inspects desktop and phone layouts; chart data must come from your supplied numbers.
guide.value: Show the finding in supplied numbers with direct labels and enough context to read the chart without hovering. It is useful for progress against plan, estimate ranges or actuals against targets where a default chart would obscure the comparison.

preparation.where: Provide numbers, units, timeframe and the source, plus the question or finding to explain. A chart JSON specification is the structured input it prepares. Python builds the page; Node checks inline scripts and a browser is needed for visual inspection.
preparation.missing: No separate analytics plan is required when the numbers and question already exist. Missing measurements cannot be generated by drawing a chart. The resulting HTML loads pinned chart libraries and fonts online, so viewing is not fully offline; hosting does not imply permission to share.

preparationSkills.reason: Use this if you need to define measurements; it is unnecessary when chart-ready data already exists.
