skills.markdown:
---
name: build-roadmap
description: Build interactive roadmaps (now/next/later boards, Gantt timelines, swimlanes, sprint trains, launch countdowns, RAID overlays, outcome roadmaps, GTM, content, brand/demand and OKR roadmaps) as embeddable components in the governing org's brand, with data from connected tools such as Google Sheets, Linear, Jira, Asana or Notion. Use whenever the user asks for a roadmap, timeline, release plan, migration plan, launch plan, campaign calendar or delivery plan as an artifact, page section or embedded element, or wants an existing roadmap rebranded, connected to live data, or turned from a feature list into outcomes. Do not use it to rank candidates (use prioritization) or to plan a sprint (use plan-sprint).
---

# Build roadmap

The kit has three formats: **Relaxed** (the default: a friendly dashboard, after Coursify), **Compact** (a dense working tool, after Venture CRM) and **Editorial** (a strategy page, after Avalon). Each roadmap is built in one format, set with `meta.mode`; viewers cannot switch it. A brand changes colors, fonts and radius in all three; the components and each mode's treatment stay the same.

A roadmap is three things kept apart:

- **Plan**: a JSON file of the work (`references/schema.md`). This is the only thing you write per roadmap.
- **Theme**: a CSS file of `--brand-*` settings compiled from the org's brand profile (`references/branding.md`). Without a profile, each mode keeps its default look.
- **Kit**: the fixed renderer and components (`assets/rk.js`, `assets/rk.css`, and `assets/rk-live.js` for live data).

Never write roadmap CSS or markup by hand, and never restyle the kit per roadmap. That is what keeps every roadmap in an org consistent, and every org's roadmaps in that org's brand.

## Workflow

1. **Template.** Pick one from `references/catalog.md`. If nothing fits, pick the closest block recipe and say which.
2. **Brand.** Resolve the identity in the order given in `references/branding.md` and state it in one line. Use only confirmed values. Draft values need the user's go-ahead.
3. **Data.** If the work lives in a connected tool, read it there (snapshot) and decide with the user whether the page should stay live (`references/connectors.md`). Otherwise build from the request. Ask only for an input that changes the plan's structure. Infer the rest, say so in `meta.source`, and list the inferences in the follow-up.
4. **Plan.** Write the plan JSON. Fill every column and lane with specifically named work tied to an outcome.
5. **Build.** `python3 scripts/build.py plan.json --brand <profile> --out <dir>`. It validates the plan, compiles the theme, prints the brand report, and writes a folder of separate files. Relay any neutral substitutions and contrast warnings to the user.
6. **Deliver** to the right target (below), then write the template's follow-up analysis in chat, not in the page.

## Outcome mode

When a now/next/later roadmap should commit to outcomes rather than features, follow [outcome roadmaps](references/outcome-roadmaps.md). Rank candidates with `prioritize-work` first, and take jobs and desired outcomes from `frame-jobs-to-be-done` where they exist. Each Now card has a named owner and an Outcome written as baseline → target. It cites its evidence and lists dependencies by RAID ID. Now holds at most three cards. Later holds problems, not dates. Run `python3 scripts/outcome_check.py plan.json` before `build.py`; it exits 1 when Now is over the cap or a Now Outcome has nothing to measure.

## Targets

- **Skills Estate page** (single file, no network): `python3 scripts/rk_embed.py page plan.json --output attempt-001/roadmap.html`, with `--profile brand.md` for a confirmed project profile; otherwise the estate neutral profile applies. The stylesheet is rewritten to the profile's roles only: no web fonts, no fixed colors, the profile radius on every corner and the profile border width. Run `brand-renderer` on the result. `build-interactive-proposal` and `map-journey` inline the same components through `rk_embed.assets()`; `frame-jobs-to-be-done` builds its readouts with `page`. Live bindings are refused here; build a snapshot.
- **claude.ai Artifact** (`--target artifact`, the default): publish `index.html` with the `files` map that `build.py` prints, plus its `capabilities` when the plan has live bindings. To update, edit `plan.json` and republish the same `file_path`.
- **An existing website or app** (`--target web`, or copy the files): put `rk.css`, `theme.css`, `rk.js` (and `rk-live.js`) in the site's static assets, then place `<rk-roadmap src="/path/plan.json"></rk-roadmap>` wherever the roadmap belongs. It works in React, Vue and plain HTML because it is a standard custom element. Live bindings work only inside claude.ai Artifacts. Elsewhere the snapshot renders.
- **Inside another artifact or page you are building**: include the same files and either the `<rk-roadmap>` element or `RoadmapKit.mount(plan, element)`. Several roadmaps can share one page.
- **No shell available**: write the files yourself. Copy `rk.css`, `rk.js` and `rk-live.js` unchanged, write `theme.css` by hand from the brand roles in `references/branding.md`, write `plan.json`, and use the page markup that `build.py` would produce: two stylesheet links, `<rk-roadmap src="plan.json">` and the script tags.

## Updating a plan

The page has a "Copy plan JSON" button. When the user pastes JSON back, treat it as the current plan: card moves they made are decisions. Keep the same `id` so saved board state lines up.

## Rules

- One identity per roadmap. Use recorded brand values only. Missing roles fall back to neutral and get reported. Contrast failures are reported, not fixed.
- Legend groups use palette slots `c: 1` to `6`, which map to the brand's chart colors. Status, risk, confidence and capacity use tones (`good`, `warn`, `crit`, `info`, `muted`), which are fixed by the kit and never themed.
- At most 6 legend groups.
- Card titles name initiatives ("Import clients from QuickBooks in one step"), not categories.
- Live bindings need a `verified` note from a real observed result. Never ship guessed payload paths.
- Read-only connectors only. The kit never writes back to a source tool.
- Mark invented inputs as example data in `meta.source`.
- Show evidence as numbers: `cite` on cards, callouts and rows, with one `evidence` block (or the host page's list). Never label every card with its basis.

## Files

- `assets/rk.css`, `assets/rk.js`, `assets/rk-live.js`: the kit, with the Relaxed, Compact and Editorial formats.
- `themes/neutral.json`: the estate neutral profile as kit JSON. `themes/example-brand.md`: a fictional `brand.md` showing the format.
- `scripts/build.py`: validator and bundle builder. `scripts/outcome_check.py`: the outcome-mode check, with `scripts/outcome_check_selftest.py` and its fixtures. `scripts/brand.py`: brand profile → theme CSS and report. `scripts/rk_embed.py`: single-file estate pages and the inline assets other estate skills embed.
- `references/schema.md`, `references/catalog.md`, `references/branding.md`, `references/connectors.md`, `references/outcome-roadmaps.md`.
- `UPSTREAM.md` and `LICENSE-UPSTREAM`: provenance and license for the outcome-mode material.
- `examples/*.json`: six worked plans. `06-sheets-live.json` is the live-data example.

  2. Brand. Resolve the identity in the order given in references/branding.md and state it in one line. Use only confirmed values. Draft values need the user's go-ahead.
  3. Data. If the work lives in a connected tool, read it there (snapshot) and decide with the user whether the page should stay live (references/connectors.md). Otherwise build from the request. Ask only for an input that changes the plan's structure. Infer the rest, say so in meta.source, and list the inferences in the follow-up.
  4. Plan. Write the plan JSON. Fill every column and lane with specifically named work tied to an outcome.
  5. Build. python3 scripts/build.py plan.json --brand <profile> --out <dir>. It validates the plan, compiles the theme, prints the brand report, and writes a folder of separate files. Relay any neutral substitutions and contrast warnings to the user.
  6. Deliver to the right target (below), then write the template's follow-up analysis in chat, not in the page.

Outcome mode

When a now/next/later roadmap should commit to outcomes rather than features, follow outcome roadmaps (references/outcome-roadmaps.md). Rank candidates with prioritize-work first, and take jobs and desired outcomes from frame-jobs-to-be-done where they exist. Each Now card has a named owner and an Outcome written as baseline → target. It cites its evidence and lists dependencies by RAID ID. Now holds at most three cards. Later holds problems, not dates. Run python3 scripts/outcome_check.py plan.json before build.py; it exits 1 when Now is over the cap or a Now Outcome has nothing to measure.

Targets

  • Skills Estate page (single file, no network): python3 scripts/rk_embed.py page plan.json --output attempt-001/roadmap.html, with --profile brand.md for a confirmed project profile; otherwise the estate neutral profile applies. The stylesheet is rewritten to the profile's roles only: no web fonts, no fixed colors, the profile radius on every corner and the profile border width. Run brand-renderer on the result. build-interactive-proposal and map-journey inline the same components through rk_embed.assets(); frame-jobs-to-be-done builds its readouts with page. Live bindings are refused here; build a snapshot.
  • claude.ai Artifact (--target artifact, the default): publish index.html with the files map that build.py prints, plus its capabilities when the plan has live bindings. To update, edit plan.json and republish the same file_path.
  • An existing website or app (--target web, or copy the files): put rk.css, theme.css, rk.js (and rk-live.js) in the site's static assets, then place <rk-roadmap src="/path/plan.json"></rk-roadmap> wherever the roadmap belongs. It works in React, Vue and plain HTML because it is a standard custom element. Live bindings work only inside claude.ai Artifacts. Elsewhere the snapshot renders.
  • Inside another artifact or page you are building: include the same files and either the <rk-roadmap> element or RoadmapKit.mount(plan, element). Several roadmaps can share one page.
  • No shell available: write the files yourself. Copy rk.css, rk.js and rk-live.js unchanged, write theme.css by hand from the brand roles in references/branding.md, write plan.json, and use the page markup that build.py would produce: two stylesheet links, <rk-roadmap src="plan.json"> and the script tags.

Updating a plan

The page has a "Copy plan JSON" button. When the user pastes JSON back, treat it as the current plan: card moves they made are decisions. Keep the same id so saved board state lines up.

Rules

  • One identity per roadmap. Use recorded brand values only. Missing roles fall back to neutral and get reported. Contrast failures are reported, not fixed.
  • Legend groups use palette slots c: 1 to 6, which map to the brand's chart colors. Status, risk, confidence and capacity use tones (good, warn, crit, info, muted), which are fixed by the kit and never themed.
  • At most 6 legend groups.
  • Card titles name initiatives ("Import clients from QuickBooks in one step"), not categories.
  • Live bindings need a verified note from a real observed result. Never ship guessed payload paths.
  • Read-only connectors only. The kit never writes back to a source tool.
  • Mark invented inputs as example data in meta.source.
  • Show evidence as numbers: cite on cards, callouts and rows, with one evidence block (or the host page's list). Never label every card with its basis.

Files

  • assets/rk.css, assets/rk.js, assets/rk-live.js: the kit, with the Relaxed, Compact and Editorial formats.
  • themes/neutral.json: the estate neutral profile as kit JSON. themes/example-brand.md: a fictional brand.md showing the format.
  • scripts/build.py: validator and bundle builder. scripts/outcome_check.py: the outcome-mode check, with scripts/outcome_check_selftest.py and its fixtures. scripts/brand.py: brand profile → theme CSS and report. scripts/rk_embed.py: single-file estate pages and the inline assets other estate skills embed.
  • references/schema.md, references/catalog.md, references/branding.md, references/connectors.md, references/outcome-roadmaps.md.
  • UPSTREAM.md and LICENSE-UPSTREAM: provenance and license for the outcome-mode material.
  • examples/*.json: six worked plans. 06-sheets-live.json is the live-data example.
skills.excerptHtml:
The kit has three formats: Relaxed (the default: a friendly dashboard, after Coursify), Compact (a dense working tool, after Venture CRM) and Editorial (a strategy page, after Avalon). Each roadmap is built in one format, set with meta.mode; viewers cannot switch it. A brand changes colors, fonts and radius in all three; the components and each mode's treatment stay the same.

A roadmap is three things kept apart:

  • Plan: a JSON file of the work (references/schema.md). This is the only thing you write per roadmap.
  • Theme: a CSS file of --brand-* settings compiled from the org's brand profile (references/branding.md). Without a profile, each mode keeps its default look.
  • Kit: the fixed renderer and components (assets/rk.js, assets/rk.css, and assets/rk-live.js for live data).

examples.title: Database migration roadmap with go/no-go gates and rollback
examples.markdown:
## Request

We're moving our dock scheduling system off the old on-prem Oracle database onto managed Postgres, and I need a migration roadmap I can embed in our engineering wiki page. The brief and constraints are in the attached files; please make it something the team can read at a glance in standup.

## Inputs

Run of the built `build-roadmap` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Other files it produced, not shown here: `index.html`, `plan.json`, `theme.css`.

#### constraints.txt

Constraints from the ops director (Imani Okafor)
- Downtime budget at cutover: 45 minutes, Sunday night only. No cutover in the week of Feb 15 (peak carrier season starts).
- Rollback to Oracle must be possible for 14 days after cutover.
- Shadow-read mismatch rate must be under 0.01% of compared rows before cutover is approved.
- Go/no-go decisions are made by Imani and Priya together.
- Risk tolerance: low. We would rather slip two weeks than cut over with open mismatches.

Owners: Priya Raman (overall), Tomasz Wieczorek (schema, procedures, CDC), Jun Park (API), Alicia Mendes (carrier portal), Dev Anand (finance feeds and decommission).

#### migration-brief.md

#### Dock scheduling: Oracle to Postgres

Owner: Priya Raman (engineering manager, Dock Systems). Team: 5 engineers plus 1 DBA, Tomasz Wieczorek.

##### Why now
- Oracle 12c support contract ends 31 March 2027. Renewal quote is $182,000 a year.
- Nightly batch job (slot reconciliation) now takes 6h10m and sometimes overlaps the 05:00 shift start.
- Managed Postgres in our cloud account is already approved by security.

##### What is affected
- Dock Scheduler API (Java), about 140 tables, 38 stored procedures (PL/SQL).
- Carrier portal read replica, used by 62 carriers.
- Nightly slot reconciliation job (PL/SQL package RECON_PKG).
- Reporting extracts to the finance warehouse, 4 feeds.

##### Plan so far
- Weeks 1-4 (Nov 16 - Dec 11): inventory, schema conversion, convert the 38 procedures, set up change data capture from Oracle.
- Weeks 5-8 (Jan 4 - Jan 29): run both databases in parallel. Writes go to Oracle, shadow reads compared against Postgres.
- Weeks 9-10 (Feb 1 - Feb 12): cutover on a Sunday night, Feb 7 at 22:00.
- Weeks 11-14 (Feb 15 - Mar 12): decommission Oracle, drop CDC, archive.

##### Known risks
- RECON_PKG uses Oracle-specific hierarchical queries and has no tests.
- Carrier portal replica lag must stay under 30 seconds.
- Two finance feeds depend on Oracle date formatting.

## Output

I've built the migration roadmap as a plan file plus a page shell. It is not rendered or build-checked yet, and the plan has one date conflict you need to settle (below).

**Template and format:** Tech migration, with four phases (Prep, Parallel run, Cutover, Cleanup) and a go/no-go card at the end of each. I used the Compact format because your team will read it in standup. It is a dense working view with bordered columns.

**Brand:** No brand profile was supplied, so it uses the kit's Compact defaults. I haven't called it on-brand. If your wiki has a `brand.md` or design tokens, send them and I'll compile a theme.

#### What I changed from your brief

**The cleanup phase now starts later than your brief says.** Your rollback commitment runs 14 days after the 7 Feb cutover, so it ends on 21 Feb. The brief starts decommissioning on 15 Feb. Dropping the CDC or Oracle that week would remove the rollback path. In the roadmap, Oracle stays on standby until 21 Feb. Imani and Priya confirm on 22 Feb, and CDC then stops. The Oracle shutdown go/no-go falls on 12 Mar, which still leaves about three weeks before support ends on 31 Mar. Please confirm this is acceptable.

#### Contents of the roadmap

Header: downtime budget 45 min, cutover Sun 7 Feb 2027 22:00, rollback window 14 days, Oracle support ends 31 Mar 2027.

| Phase | Dates | Steps | Biggest risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prep | 16 Nov – 11 Dec | Inventory 140 tables, 38 procedures and 4 feeds; convert the schema with row-count and checksum checks; convert the 38 procedures; write tests for RECON_PKG; start CDC; alert on CDC lag over the holiday gap; Go/no-go 1 | RECON_PKG has no tests |
| Parallel run | 4 – 29 Jan | Shadow reads (mismatch under 0.01%); rewrite RECON_PKG; carrier portal replica (lag under 30 s); reproduce the 4 finance feeds; timed staging rehearsal; Go/no-go 2 on 29 Jan | Shadow-read mismatches |
| Cutover | 1 – 12 Feb | Freeze writes and drain CDC at 22:00; switch the API; repoint portal and feeds; reverse sync to Oracle for 14 days; Go/no-go 3 at 04:00 Monday, before the 05:00 shift | Overrunning 45 minutes |
| Cleanup | 15 Feb – 12 Mar | Oracle on standby to 21 Feb; stop CDC and reverse sync 22 Feb; remove Oracle code from the API; archive and shut down Oracle; Go/no-go 4 | Dropping Oracle inside the rollback window |

Every step card has an owner from your constraints file, a risk tag, an exit criterion, a rollback and a verification. A "Riskiest steps" block and a three-item evidence list (the contract and quote, the batch job, your constraints) sit below the board. The board is fixed in order, so cards can't be dragged.

#### Inferred, so please confirm

- **Reverse sync (Postgres to Oracle, 14 days).** Without it, a rollback after live bookings would lose them. This is the main addition. The cutover rehearsal should test it.
- **Holiday gap, 14 Dec – 3 Jan.** The brief schedules nothing there while CDC runs unattended. I added a lag-alert step owned by Priya.
- **14 clean reconciliation nights** as the exit criterion for the RECON_PKG rewrite. The brief only says the job must stop overlapping the 05:00 shift start.
- **The step-level breakdown and owner assignments per step.** The brief gave phases and a list of owners, not individual steps.
- **Go/no-go 2 fallback.** If it fails, cutover moves to a Sunday before 15 Feb, or after peak season. Your constraint rules out the week of 15 Feb.

These are listed in the page footer, and the inferred cards carry an "Inferred" tag.

#### How it was checked

- I couldn't run `build.py` here, so I followed the "no shell" route and wrote the files by hand.
- By hand I checked these rules: every card's column exists, every group is in the legend, and cite numbers 1–3 have evidence entries. I also checked that the legend has 5 groups, under the limit of 6.
- I haven't rendered the page. Run `python3 scripts/build.py plan.json --out <dir>` to validate and build it.
- The outcome-mode check doesn't apply, because this isn't a now/next/later board.

#### Putting it in the wiki

Copy `rk.css` and `rk.js` unchanged from the skill's `assets/` folder into your wiki's static files, next to `theme.css`. Then place `<rk-roadmap src="/path/plan.json"></rk-roadmap>` where it belongs. I did not copy those two kit files into `out/`.

#### Follow-up

**Riskiest step:** rewriting RECON_PKG. It uses Oracle hierarchical queries and has no tests, so Oracle's output is the only specification. Don't start the rewrite until the characterization tests pass against Oracle.

**Cheapest de-risking test:** run the staging rehearsal early, with the reverse sync included, and time it. If the runbook doesn't fit in 45 minutes, you'll know by January rather than on the night.

#### Files

All in `./out/`:

- `plan.json`: the roadmap data (all four phases, 22 cards, callouts, evidence).
- `theme.css`: empty on purpose, since no brand profile was confirmed.
- `index.html`: page shell with the two stylesheet links, `<rk-roadmap src="plan.json">` and the `rk.js` script.
- `answer.md`: this reply.

I've built the migration roadmap as a plan file plus a page shell. It is not rendered or build-checked yet, and the plan has one date conflict you need to settle (below).

Template and format: Tech migration, with four phases (Prep, Parallel run, Cutover, Cleanup) and a go/no-go card at the end of each. I used the Compact format because your team will read it in standup. It is a dense working view with bordered columns.

Brand: No brand profile was supplied, so it uses the kit's Compact defaults. I haven't called it on-brand. If your wiki has a brand.md or design tokens, send them and I'll compile a theme.

What I changed from your brief

The cleanup phase now starts later than your brief says. Your rollback commitment runs 14 days after the 7 Feb cutover, so it ends on 21 Feb. The brief starts decommissioning on 15 Feb. Dropping the CDC or Oracle that week would remove the rollback path. In the roadmap, Oracle stays on standby until 21 Feb. Imani and Priya confirm on 22 Feb, and CDC then stops. The Oracle shutdown go/no-go falls on 12 Mar, which still leaves about three weeks before support ends on 31 Mar. Please confirm this is acceptable.

Contents of the roadmap

Header: downtime budget 45 min, cutover Sun 7 Feb 2027 22:00, rollback window 14 days, Oracle support ends 31 Mar 2027.

Prep16 Nov – 11 DecInventory 140 tables, 38 procedures and 4 feeds; convert the schema with row-count and checksum checks; convert the 38 procedures; write tests for RECON_PKG; start CDC; alert on CDC lag over the holiday gap; Go/no-go 1RECON_PKG has no tests
Parallel run4 – 29 JanShadow reads (mismatch under 0.01%); rewrite RECON_PKG; carrier portal replica (lag under 30 s); reproduce the 4 finance feeds; timed staging rehearsal; Go/no-go 2 on 29 JanShadow-read mismatches
Cutover1 – 12 FebFreeze writes and drain CDC at 22:00; switch the API; repoint portal and feeds; reverse sync to Oracle for 14 days; Go/no-go 3 at 04:00 Monday, before the 05:00 shiftOverrunning 45 minutes
Cleanup15 Feb – 12 MarOracle on standby to 21 Feb; stop CDC and reverse sync 22 Feb; remove Oracle code from the API; archive and shut down Oracle; Go/no-go 4Dropping Oracle inside the rollback window

Every step card has an owner from your constraints file, a risk tag, an exit criterion, a rollback and a verification. A "Riskiest steps" block and a three-item evidence list (the contract and quote, the batch job, your constraints) sit below the board. The board is fixed in order, so cards can't be dragged.

Inferred, so please confirm
  • Reverse sync (Postgres to Oracle, 14 days). Without it, a rollback after live bookings would lose them. This is the main addition. The cutover rehearsal should test it.
  • Holiday gap, 14 Dec – 3 Jan. The brief schedules nothing there while CDC runs unattended. I added a lag-alert step owned by Priya.
  • 14 clean reconciliation nights as the exit criterion for the RECON_PKG rewrite. The brief only says the job must stop overlapping the 05:00 shift start.
  • The step-level breakdown and owner assignments per step. The brief gave phases and a list of owners, not individual steps.
  • Go/no-go 2 fallback. If it fails, cutover moves to a Sunday before 15 Feb, or after peak season. Your constraint rules out the week of 15 Feb.

  • I couldn't run build.py here, so I followed the "no shell" route and wrote the files by hand.

Copy rk.css and rk.js unchanged from the skill's assets/ folder into your wiki's static files, next to theme.css. Then place <rk-roadmap src="/path/plan.json"></rk-roadmap> where it belongs. I did not copy those two kit files into out/.

Riskiest step: rewriting RECON_PKG. It uses Oracle hierarchical queries and has no tests, so Oracle's output is the only specification. Don't start the rewrite until the characterization tests pass against Oracle.

---
name: capture-knowledge
description: Save a knowledge-hub decision, discovery, or factual correction with evidence and review state. Use when the user says remember this, correct the hub, or capture a decision. Do not treat brainstorming as confirmed fact or claim a proposal is accepted.
metadata:

# Capture knowledge

## Host access

Resolve the hub endpoint, router, local roots and permitted account from explicit task or project configuration. No personal drive, owner profile, schedule or account is a default. Confirm that the selected adapter implements the named operations; if it does not, use its supported equivalent and preserve the same revision, authorization and acceptance checks.

Use only tools and files actually available in this session. In Claude Code invoke `/capture-knowledge`; in Codex use `$capture-knowledge`; in Claude chat/Cowork ask to use `capture-knowledge`. Mac paths identify local authorities; in Cowork resolve them only through a folder already shared with this session. Cloud chat cannot read a Mac path or localhost merely because this skill names it. When hub access or a required foundation is unavailable, report that gap and continue only work supported by accessible evidence. Use named companion skills when available; otherwise apply the safeguards below and identify any required review gate you cannot complete. Do not install dependencies or broaden permissions automatically.

Use the existing hub update workflow. Do not write a second memory database or edit an assistant's separate memory unless the user explicitly requests that separate destination.

1. Read the current configured hub router when available and call the permitted hub's `get_context`. Establish exactly what the user wants retained, where it belongs, and its existing sharing boundary. Default private personal capture to a permitted local destination; never infer approval to upload it to hosted or shared spaces.
2. Search for the existing subject record. Fully fetch the relevant record and sources in bounded parts, pinned to exact revisions. A correction belongs with its subject and provenance, not in a competing rulebook. If several authorities disagree, keep the conflict visible; neither drive, the newest timestamp, nor an AI synthesis wins automatically.
3. Preserve the user's wording where it expresses a decision. Classify each statement as confirmed, user-reported, observed, proposed, estimated, or creative canon as supported by the contract. Record the source and when the statement applied separately from when it was captured. A user report is attributable evidence, not independent verification. Ask only for an ambiguity that materially changes the decision, authority, or sharing scope.
4. Inspect the actual proposal schema in the available tool/service before constructing input; do not invent required fields or a new-record revision sentinel. Submit `propose_update` against the exact record and contract revisions read. Contract, confirmed-fact, and sharing changes follow the service's owner-review rules. On revision conflict, refetch and compare; preserve both edits and do not force an overwrite.
5. If the connector lacks write access, use an already-authorized local hub workflow only when the current task permits it. Never elevate a shared/cloud actor by borrowing local owner credentials. If no permitted write path exists, save a clearly marked private pending proposal under the current local intake route, including target, base revisions, evidence, and reason it is pending. If even that destination is unavailable, return the draft without claiming it was saved.
6. Verify the service response and fetch the resulting state. Distinguish draft, saved pending, proposal submitted, accepted, and dependent review needed. Acceptance requires an acceptance receipt or current accepted revision; creating a proposal is insufficient. After an accepted correction, identify registered dependents, request the supported refresh, and verify what changed. Unregistered documents may still be stale. Preserve submitted résumés, published historical artifacts, and archived evidence; create corrected successors where appropriate.

Return what was captured, its source, destination, exact state, and what remains for review. A saved proposal is not an automatic change to every AI tool. For material changes use `verify-work-state` and report changed now, verified, still unchanged, and exact next action.

Examples: `$capture-knowledge Hold the sales-pursuit number until we have supporting evidence.` / `$capture-knowledge Save this as a proposed product idea, not a committed plan.`

examples.title: Correct a supplier minimum order and log a proposed idea
examples.markdown:
## Request

Please capture a correction in the hub: the Millbrook Mills wholesale minimum order is £250, not £400 as our supplier record says. Dana Okafor told me this by phone on 28 October and I have her follow-up email pasted in the inputs. Also note that moving to a second flour supplier is only an idea, not a decision.

## Inputs

**Dry run.** This skill normally works on live systems or its owner's own setup. Here the system state is invented in the inputs below, and nothing was changed anywhere. Run of the built `capture-knowledge` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### email-from-dana.txt

From: Dana Okafor <dana.okafor@millbrook.example.com>
To: Priya Nambiar <priya@tallowandfinch.example.com>
Date: Wed 28 Oct 2026, 16:42
Subject: Re: minimum order

Hi Priya,

Following our call today: from 1 June 2026 the minimum for wholesale accounts is £250 per delivery. The old £400 figure was on the March 2025 price list and we have since replaced it. A new price list is going out in January; I can't send the revised PDF before then.

Dana

#### hub-state.md

#### Hub state export (read-only snapshot, 2026-11-04)

##### Configuration
- Router: project config `hub.local.yaml`, hub `tallow-ops`, adapter `hub-local-v2`
- get_context: owner role = operations lead (Priya Nambiar); sharing boundary = team-internal; local intake route `intake/pending/` is writable
- Adapter operations available: `search`, `fetch_record`, `propose_update`, `get_acceptance_receipt`. No direct write to confirmed records.
- propose_update schema: `record_id`, `base_revision`, `contract_revision`, `claim_text`, `status_label`, `evidence[]`, `applies_from`

##### Record SUP-014 "Millbrook Mills (flour supplier)"
- Revision: r17, contract revision c4, state: accepted
- Line 9: "Wholesale minimum order: £400 per delivery." Label: confirmed. Source: price list PDF dated 2025-03-12.
- Registered dependents: ORD-003 "Weekly flour ordering checklist" (r9), BUD-021 "Q1 purchasing budget" (r3)

##### Record SUP-022 "Flour supplier options"
- Revision: r5, state: accepted
- Line 4: "Single-supplier arrangement with Millbrook Mills." No mention of a second supplier.

##### Other source found by search
- `shared/pricing-sheet-2026.xlsx` (team drive), row 12: Millbrook Mills minimum order £250, edited 2026-06-02, editor not recorded.

##### Existing dependents (not registered)
- `notes/ordering-cheatsheet.md` quotes "£400 minimum" (not registered with the hub)

## Output

I've drafted both items as private pending proposals. Nothing has been submitted, accepted or changed in the hub.

#### What I checked
- **Hub access:** The snapshot shows the `tallow-ops` hub with an adapter that has `search`, `fetch_record`, `propose_update` and `get_acceptance_receipt`. I had no live connection in this session, so I worked from the exported state and could not call `propose_update`.
- **SUP-014 (Millbrook Mills):** At r17, line 9 reads "Wholesale minimum order: £400 per delivery", labelled confirmed, from the 12 March 2025 price list.
- **Pricing sheet:** `shared/pricing-sheet-2026.xlsx` row 12 says £250, edited 2 June 2026. The editor isn't recorded, so I treated it as consistent with Dana's email and not as independent proof.
- **SUP-022 (Flour supplier options):** At r5 it says "Single-supplier arrangement with Millbrook Mills" and doesn't mention a second supplier.

#### Correction to SUP-014
- **Proposed claim:** "Wholesale minimum order: £250 per delivery, from 1 June 2026. Replaces £400 from the 12 March 2025 price list."
- **Label:** user-reported. Dana Okafor's email of 28 October 2026 is attributable evidence from the supplier, but you relayed it and I couldn't verify it with the supplier.
- **Dates kept separate:** it applied from 1 June 2026, as Dana states, and was captured on 4 November 2026.
- **Base:** record r17, contract c4.
- **Old line:** the £400 line stays visible and isn't deleted. Line 9 is a confirmed fact, so the correction needs owner review, which the snapshot lists as Priya Nambiar.
- **Open gap:** Dana can't send a revised price list until January 2027. Until then the correction rests on her email and the call. When the list arrives, attach it and ask for the label to be upgraded.

#### Second-supplier idea
- **Proposed claim:** "Moving to a second flour supplier is an idea only. No decision has been made."
- **Label:** proposed, applying from 4 November 2026, against SUP-022 r5.
- **Existing line:** line 4 is unchanged.
- **How to read it:** this is not a plan and it doesn't alter the single-supplier arrangement.

#### Current state
| Item | State |
|---|---|
| £250 correction | Draft saved as a pending proposal. Not submitted and not accepted. |
| Second-supplier idea | Draft saved as a pending proposal. Not submitted and not accepted. |
| SUP-014 in the hub | Unchanged. Still says £400. |
| ORD-003 (r9) and BUD-021 (r3) | Unchanged. They still carry the £400 figure. |
| `notes/ordering-cheatsheet.md` | Unchanged. It isn't registered with the hub, so a refresh won't reach it. |

#### What happens next
1. Submit both proposals with `propose_update` using the fields in the pending file. They were built from the schema listed in the snapshot: `record_id`, `base_revision`, `contract_revision`, `claim_text`, `status_label`, `evidence[]`, `applies_from`. If r17 or r5 has moved by then, refetch and compare before sending. Don't overwrite the newer edit.
2. Priya Nambiar reviews the SUP-014 change. It counts as accepted only once an acceptance receipt or a new accepted revision exists.
3. After acceptance, request a refresh of ORD-003 and BUD-021, then fetch them to confirm what changed. BUD-021 is a Q1 purchasing budget, so check whether the lower minimum affects any figure in it.
4. Edit the £400 in `notes/ordering-cheatsheet.md` by hand, or register it with the hub.

This hasn't reached any AI tool's separate memory. It only becomes shared hub knowledge once accepted.

#### Files
- `out/pending-proposal-SUP-014.md` holds both proposals. Key content:
  - SUP-014 / base r17 / c4 / user-reported / applies from 2026-06-01 / £250 per delivery, evidence: the call, Dana's email, the pricing sheet row.
  - SUP-022 / base r5 / proposed / applies from 2026-11-04 / second supplier is an idea only.
  - Steps to take after acceptance.

### File: pending-proposal-SUP-014.md

#### PENDING PROPOSAL (private, not submitted, not accepted)

Prepared 2026-11-04 for intake route `intake/pending/`. Nothing here has been sent to `propose_update`.

##### Proposal 1: correct SUP-014

- record_id: SUP-014
- base_revision: r17
- contract_revision: c4
- status_label: user-reported (supplier contact statement; not independently verified)
- applies_from: 2026-06-01 (when the supplier says the new minimum took effect)
- captured: 2026-11-04 by Priya Nambiar
- claim_text: "Wholesale minimum order: £250 per delivery, from 1 June 2026. Replaces £400 from the 12 March 2025 price list."
- evidence:
  1. Phone call with Dana Okafor (Millbrook Mills), 2026-10-28, as reported by Priya Nambiar.
  2. Email from Dana Okafor, 2026-10-28 16:42: "from 1 June 2026 the minimum for wholesale accounts is £250 per delivery. The old £400 figure was on the March 2025 price list and we have since replaced it."
  3. `shared/pricing-sheet-2026.xlsx`, row 12, £250, edited 2026-06-02, editor not recorded. Consistent with the email but not an independent source.
- Existing line kept visible: line 9, "£400 per delivery", confirmed, price list PDF 2025-03-12. Not deleted; the owner decides whether it is superseded.
- Review route: SUP-014 line 9 is a confirmed fact, so owner review (Priya Nambiar) is required.
- Gap: no revised price list yet. Supplier expects to issue one in January 2027.

##### Proposal 2: record the second-supplier idea

- record_id: SUP-022
- base_revision: r5
- status_label: proposed
- applies_from: 2026-11-04
- claim_text: "Moving to a second flour supplier is an idea only. No decision has been made."
- evidence: user statement, 2026-11-04.
- Not added to SUP-022 line 4 ("Single-supplier arrangement with Millbrook Mills"), which stays as is.

##### After acceptance (not yet applicable)

- Request refresh of registered dependents ORD-003 (r9) and BUD-021 (r3), then fetch both and check the £400 figure is gone or flagged.
- Unregistered: `notes/ordering-cheatsheet.md` quotes "£400 minimum". Edit by hand or register it.

# Capture requirements

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`readout-brief.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/readout-brief.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

## Purpose

This skill guides the agent through an interactive, structured conversation to
capture business requirements in the Estate approved delivery matrix format.
The final output is a **branded Excel workbook (.xlsx)** with two tabs, ready
for client presentation and downstream use by AI agents or development teams.

## Reference files

Detailed tables live in `references/` to keep this file lean. Read the relevant
one when you reach that part of the work:

- `references/excel-workbook-format.md`: the per-column tables for both tabs,
  the default blue/white styling theme, the Epics-tab formula, and recalculation.
- `references/gherkin-and-questions.md`: Gherkin acceptance-criteria structure
  with a worked example, plus clarifying-question guidance.
- `references/jira-export-and-traceability.md`: the Source column and the
  three legitimate values for it, the gap list, and the workbook-to-Jira field
  mapping. Read it when the requirements come from a SOW or scope document, or
  when the output goes into a Jira backlog rather than staying a spreadsheet.
- `references/ba-mode-salesforce.md`: the BA mode rules for Salesforce
  engagements. Read it whenever BA mode is on (see below).

## Before Generating the Workbook

**Always read the host spreadsheet skill before writing any openpyxl code.**
Look for `xlsx`, `spreadsheets`, or the equivalent in the available skills list.
Follow its guidelines for formula construction, recalculation, error
checking, and code style. Use its `scripts/recalc.py` to recalculate
formulas after generating the workbook.

If an **Estate brand guidelines skill** exists (check available skills),
read it and use the official brand colors instead of the default blue/white
theme in the reference file.

## Delivery Matrix: Key Definitions

These definitions form the hierarchy used to organize every requirement:

| Level | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Business Need** | Clearly defined problem, opportunity, or objective that drives the creation of a capability or project. *(attribute on Epic)* |
| **Capability** | A broad, enduring business function or outcome. *(attribute on Epic)* |
| **Epic** | A major business deliverable/process spanning multiple requirements. |
| **Requirement** | A specific rule or condition the system must satisfy. |
| **User Story** | A user-centered statement of action for a requirement. *(attribute on Requirement)* |
| **Acceptance Criteria** | Measurable success conditions for a user story, written in **Gherkin** format. *(attribute on Requirement)* |

### Hierarchy

```
Business Need
 └─ Capability
     └─ Epic
         └─ Requirement
             ├─ User Story (As a / I want to / So that)
             └─ Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin: Given / When / Then)
```

## Output Format: Excel Workbook (.xlsx)

The deliverable is a single `.xlsx` workbook with **two tabs**: an "Epics"
summary tab and a "Requirements" detail tab. For the full per-column layout of
each tab, the styling theme, the Epics-tab COUNTIF formula, and recalculation,
see `references/excel-workbook-format.md`. Business Need lives exclusively on
the Epics tab and is not repeated on individual requirement rows.

## Canonical Values: Priority (MoSCoW)

Use **exactly** these values. No variations, abbreviations, or synonyms.

| Value | When to use |
|---|---|
| **Must Have** | Non-negotiable for the release. System won't work or be compliant without it. Default when priority is unclear. |
| **Should Have** | Important but not critical for launch. Can be deferred to fast-follow if necessary. |
| **Could Have** | Desirable nice-to-have. Minimal impact if omitted. |
| **Won't Have** | Explicitly out of scope for this release. Captured for future consideration. |

**Inference guidance:** When working from source material (documents, meeting
transcripts, chat messages, etc.), look for priority signals:

- "must", "critical", "required", "compliance", "regulatory", "blocking"
  → **Must Have**
- "important", "should", "expected", "high value" → **Should Have**
- "nice to have", "if time permits", "ideally", "bonus", "enhancement"
  → **Could Have**
- "out of scope", "not now", "future", "phase 2", "parking lot", "deferred"
  → **Won't Have**

If no signal is present, default to **Must Have**.

## Canonical Values: Status

| Value | When to use |
|---|---|
| **Draft** | Initial capture. Not yet reviewed. Default for all new requirements. |
| **Reviewed** | Reviewed by stakeholders but not formally signed off. |
| **Approved** | Formally approved and baselined. |

## BA Mode: Salesforce Engagements

BA mode turns on when the source material is a Salesforce Statement of Work
or scope document, or when the backlog feeds a Salesforce build. It changes
nothing about the hierarchy, the workbook, or the phases below. It adds
discipline on top: do not start without the SOW, sweep the SOW for every
Salesforce area it commits to, trace every requirement to a named SOW section,
prefer standard platform capability before recommending custom development,
and widen Gherkin coverage to permission and negative scenarios. The full
rules are in `references/ba-mode-salesforce.md`; read that file before Phase 1
whenever this mode applies. In BA mode also read
`references/jira-export-and-traceability.md`, since the Source column and the
gap list are mandatory there rather than situational.

## Interactive Workflow

**This is a conversation-driven skill.** Do NOT jump straight to producing
a workbook. Follow the phases below.

### Phase 1: Intake & Understanding

1. **Gather source material.** If the user provides documents (decks, PRDs,
   briefs, specs, meeting transcripts, or verbal descriptions), read and
   digest them thoroughly. There may be multiple sources.
2. **Identify candidate Epics, Capabilities, and Business Needs.**
3. **Present the proposed hierarchy to the user.**

   **MUST** use the exact indentation format shown below. Each level MUST
   be on its own line with proper indentation. Do NOT collapse the hierarchy
   into a single paragraph or run items together on one line.

   **CRITICAL FORMATTING RULE:** Use ONLY standard markdown list characters
   (`-` or `*`) for ALL hierarchy levels. Do NOT use Unicode bullet
   characters (`•`, `◦`, `▪`, etc.). The chat renderer does not recognize
   these as list markers and will collapse the hierarchy into a single
   paragraph. This is the #1 formatting failure mode for this skill.

   **Required format (follow this structure exactly):**

   ```markdown
   **Proposed Hierarchy:**

   - **Business Need:** Enable compliant, error-free pricing for
     FDA-regulated medical devices...

     - **Capability:** Automated contract pricing that selects the
       correct product price tier...

       - **Epic:** Contract-Driven Pricing Engine [Prefix: **CPE**]
         - Auto-Apply Contracted Price
         - Tiered Pricing Logic
         - Fallback to List Price
         - Audit Trail for Pricing Decisions
         - Contract Identification on Quote Creation
   ```

   Formatting rules:
   - Use standard markdown `-` for ALL hierarchy levels (Business Need,
     Capability, Epic, and requirement names). NEVER use `•` or other
     Unicode bullet characters.
   - Use **2-space indentation** per nesting level so the markdown parser
     recognizes sub-lists.
   - Insert a **blank line** before each Business Need, Capability, and
     Epic item to ensure line-break separation in the rendered output.
   - Do NOT wrap the hierarchy in a blockquote (`>`). Output it as a
     top-level markdown list.
   - **Every item on its own line.** Never concatenated into a paragraph.
   - Bold the labels: **Business Need:**, **Capability:**, **Epic:**.
   - Show the proposed prefix in brackets after the epic name.
   - Show requirement short names only, not full user stories or details.
   - If there are multiple business needs, capabilities, or epics, repeat
     the full indented structure for each.

4. **Use `ask_user_input_v0`** to confirm or adjust:
   - Are these the right epics?
   - Are any missing or should any be merged/split?
   - Is the capability grouping correct?
   - Are the epic prefixes OK?

5. Iterate until the user approves the hierarchy.

### Phase 2: Detailed Requirements Drafting

Once hierarchy is confirmed:

1. **Generate the first version of the .xlsx workbook** with both tabs
   fully populated: Gherkin acceptance criteria, inferred priorities,
   default statuses, formulas, and styling.
2. **Save and present** the workbook to the user for review.
3. **MUST include a direct download link** to the file in your response
   text (not just via `present_files`). After presenting the file, add a
   line like:

   > 📎 **[Download requirements_v1.xlsx]**. If you don't see the file,
   > open the **Artifacts panel** (top-right corner).

   This is important because users may not notice the artifacts panel,
   especially if it's minimized.
4. **Use `ask_user_input_v0`** to ask about:
   - Personas: Are the "As A" roles correct?
   - Acceptance criteria: Are the Gherkin scenarios complete?
   - Missing requirements: Anything to add?
   - Priority: Do the inferred MoSCoW values look right?
   - Assumptions: Any constraints or dependencies to note?

### Phase 3: Iteration & Refinement

1. The user may respond with:
   - Verbal edits ("change X to Y", "add a requirement for Z")
   - An edited .xlsx file they re-upload
2. Apply edits and produce a new version.
3. **If the host provides a durable shared-file editor** (for example Cowork or a
   connected ChatGPT spreadsheet), co-author within the shared file directly.
4. **Otherwise**, create versioned files (e.g.,
   `requirements_v1.xlsx`, `requirements_v2.xlsx`) for a clear revision
   trail.
5. Continue iterating until the user is satisfied.
6. When the team needs to know which stories can enter a sprint, hand the
   Requirements tab to `refine-backlog`. It grades readiness and proposes
   splits and estimates; the stories themselves change here, in this workbook,
   so Requirement Numbers and Status stay canonical. See
   `../_shared/planning-chain.md`.

### Phase 4: Final Delivery

1. Produce the final `.xlsx` workbook.
2. **Present the file and include a direct download link in your response.**
   Always remind the user:

   > 📎 **[Download requirements_final.xlsx]**. Open the **Artifacts
   > panel** (top-right corner) if you don't see the file.

3. Provide a brief summary:
   - Total number of requirements
   - Breakdown by epic
   - Number of epics and capabilities
   - Priority distribution (Must/Should/Could/Won't counts)
   - Any open items or assumptions flagged during the session

## Acceptance Criteria and Clarifying Questions

Acceptance criteria are written in Gherkin. For the scenario structure, a
worked example, and guidance on when and how to ask clarifying questions with
`ask_user_input_v0`, see `references/gherkin-and-questions.md`.

## Important Reminders

- **Always include a download link and artifacts panel reminder** when
  presenting files. Users often miss the artifacts panel. Every time you
  present a file, add: "📎 **[Download filename.xlsx]**. Open the
  **Artifacts panel** (top-right) if you don't see the file."
- **Always start with the interactive hierarchy review.** Never skip to
  workbook generation without confirming structure with the user first.
- **Use `ask_user_input_v0`** to present options as clickable choices whenever
  the question has bounded answers.
- **Gherkin is non-negotiable** for acceptance criteria formatting.
- **Prefix-based numbering**: auto-generate but always confirm with the user.
- **Infer priority from source material** using the signal words above.
  Default to Must Have when uncertain.
- **Business Need** lives only on the Epics tab. Do not include it on
  the Requirements tab.
- **Always read the xlsx skill** before generating the workbook.
- **Always recalculate** the workbook after generation using recalc.py.
- **Check for brand guidelines skill.** If it exists, use official Estate
  colors instead of the default blue/white theme.
- When the user provides vague input, infer reasonable defaults but flag
  your assumptions and ask for confirmation.

## Release gate (required)

Before you deliver, run the gate. This is a required step, not a suggestion. Full
spec in [`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md).

1. Apply review-writing to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For
   a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.
2. Run review-deliverable before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until both checks have passed.

2. **Present the file and include a direct download link in your response.**
   Always remind the user:

> 📎 **[Download requirements_final.xlsx]**. Open the **Artifacts
   > panel** (top-right corner) if you don't see the file.

3. Provide a brief summary:
   - Total number of requirements
   - Breakdown by epic
   - Number of epics and capabilities
   - Priority distribution (Must/Should/Could/Won't counts)
   - Any open items or assumptions flagged during the session

## Acceptance Criteria and Clarifying Questions

Acceptance criteria are written in Gherkin. For the scenario structure, a
worked example, and guidance on when and how to ask clarifying questions with
`ask_user_input_v0`, see `references/gherkin-and-questions.md`.

## Important Reminders

- **Always include a download link and artifacts panel reminder** when
  presenting files. Users often miss the artifacts panel. Every time you
  present a file, add: "📎 **[Download filename.xlsx]**. Open the
  **Artifacts panel** (top-right) if you don't see the file."
- **Always start with the interactive hierarchy review.** Never skip to
  workbook generation without confirming structure with the user first.
- **Use `ask_user_input_v0`** to present options as clickable choices whenever
  the question has bounded answers.
- **Gherkin is non-negotiable** for acceptance criteria formatting.
- **Prefix-based numbering**: auto-generate but always confirm with the user.
- **Infer priority from source material** using the signal words above.
  Default to Must Have when uncertain.
- **Business Need** lives only on the Epics tab. Do not include it on
  the Requirements tab.
- **Always read the xlsx skill** before generating the workbook.
- **Always recalculate** the workbook after generation using recalc.py.
- **Check for brand guidelines skill.** If it exists, use official Estate
  colors instead of the default blue/white theme.
- When the user provides vague input, infer reasonable defaults but flag
  your assumptions and ask for confirmation.

## Release gate (required)

Before you deliver, run the gate. This is a required step, not a suggestion. Full
spec in [`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md).

1. Apply review-writing to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For
   a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.
2. Run review-deliverable before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until both checks have passed.

examples.title: Requirements backlog from a credit union onboarding workshop
examples.markdown:
## Request

Turn these Cedar & Pine Credit Union onboarding workshop notes into the requirements backlog: epics, capabilities, user stories with Gherkin acceptance criteria. Notes are in ./inputs/. Produce the workbook if your tools allow, and show the backlog content in your answer.

## Inputs

Run of the built `capture-requirements` task package. All inputs below are invented. The run had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Files it also produced, not shown here: `epics.csv`, `gap-list.md`, `requirements.csv`.

#### workshop-notes.md

#### Cedar & Pine Credit Union — member onboarding workshop notes (fictional)

Date: (workshop 1 of 2). Attendees: Member Services lead (Aisha Grant), Compliance officer (Rob Lindqvist), Digital banking manager (Kai Nakamura), Branch manager (Sofia Mendes).

Goal: let new members open a membership and a first savings account online in under 10 minutes, instead of the current branch visit.

Discussion:
- Applicant enters personal details, SSN, address; identity verification through the existing KYC vendor ("VeriPass"). Rob: KYC must pass before any account number is issued. Manual review queue for VeriPass "refer" results, worked by Member Services within 1 business day.
- Eligibility: must live or work in one of 6 counties, or be a family member of a current member. Applicant self-attests; Member Services spot-checks 10%.
- Funding: initial $5 share deposit by debit card or ACH from an external account. Kai: ACH micro-deposit verification takes too long; prefer instant account verification through the existing aggregator.
- Disclosures: Truth in Savings disclosure and membership agreement must be presented and accepted before submission; store the version accepted.
- Joint owners: Sofia says 20% of branch openings are joint. Group agreed joint applications are phase two.
- Minors: out of scope; branch only.
- Notifications: email + SMS at submission, approval, and if more information is needed.
- Staff view: Member Services needs a queue of pending applications with KYC result, eligibility basis, and funding status.
- Reporting: Aisha wants daily counts of started, abandoned, submitted, approved, referred.
- Accessibility: must meet WCAG 2.2 AA (board requirement).
- Open question: does the core banking system accept account creation via API, or only batch file? Kai to confirm with vendor.

## Output

### Cedar & Pine Credit Union: online onboarding requirements backlog

The backlog has 9 epics under 3 capabilities and 22 requirements, all in Draft. Eighteen are Must Have, 2 Should Have, 2 Won't Have. Nine open questions are on a separate gap list. The biggest is G8: whether core banking accepts account creation by API or only by batch file.

#### What I could and could not do

- **No .xlsx workbook.** My tools here write text files only, and I could not run a script. I wrote the two tabs as CSV files that import directly into the two-tab layout (Epics, Requirements) from the skill's workbook format. The Epics file holds the live `=COUNTIF(Requirements!C:C, A2)` formulas. Those only calculate once both tabs sit in one workbook, so I did not recalculate anything.
- **Hierarchy review skipped.** The skill has you confirm the hierarchy and prefixes before drafting. No one was available, so the hierarchy and prefixes below are my proposal and are unconfirmed.
- **Checks not run.** I ran no writing checker, brand check or quality gate. I read the text once myself. Styling (default blue/white theme, dropdowns, filters) is not applied, because that happens when the workbook is built.
- **Source column added.** The skill asks for one when a source document exists. Every row cites the notes' bullet by topic, since the notes have no section numbers.
- **Priorities inferred.** Where the notes gave no signal I used the default (Must Have) and said so in the row's notes.

#### Proposed hierarchy

- **Business Need:** Let new members open a membership and a first savings account online in under 10 minutes instead of visiting a branch.

  - **Capability:** Online account opening

    - **Epic:** Online Application Intake [Prefix: **APP**]
      - Capture applicant details
      - Complete application in under 10 minutes
      - Exclude joint applications from this release
      - Exclude minor applicants

    - **Epic:** Membership Eligibility [Prefix: **ELG**]
      - Self-attest eligibility
      - Record eligibility basis
      - Spot-check 10% of self-attested eligibility

    - **Epic:** Identity Verification (KYC) [Prefix: **KYC**]
      - Verify identity through VeriPass
      - Withhold account number until KYC passes
      - Route VeriPass refer results to manual review

    - **Epic:** Initial Share Deposit Funding [Prefix: **FND**]
      - Fund share deposit by debit card
      - Fund share deposit by ACH
      - Verify external account instantly

    - **Epic:** Disclosures and Agreements [Prefix: **DSC**]
      - Require disclosure acceptance before submission
      - Store accepted document versions

    - **Epic:** Accessibility [Prefix: **ACC**]
      - Meet WCAG 2.2 AA

  - **Capability:** Applicant communication

    - **Epic:** Applicant Notifications [Prefix: **NTF**]
      - Notify applicant on submission
      - Notify applicant on approval
      - Notify applicant when more information is needed

  - **Capability:** Onboarding operations and oversight

    - **Epic:** Member Services Application Queue [Prefix: **OPS**]
      - Pending applications queue
      - Work referred applications within one business day

    - **Epic:** Onboarding Reporting [Prefix: **RPT**]
      - Daily onboarding counts

#### Epics tab

| Epic Name | Prefix | Capability | Business Need | Requirement Count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Online Application Intake | APP | Online account opening | New members must open a membership and first savings account online in under 10 minutes instead of visiting a branch. | 4 |
| Membership Eligibility | ELG | Online account opening | Only people who live or work in one of the 6 counties, or who are family of a current member, may join. | 3 |
| Identity Verification (KYC) | KYC | Online account opening | No account number may be issued until identity verification through VeriPass passes. | 3 |
| Initial Share Deposit Funding | FND | Online account opening | A new membership needs a $5 share deposit that the applicant can pay online without slow bank verification. | 3 |
| Disclosures and Agreements | DSC | Online account opening | The credit union must show it presented the Truth in Savings disclosure and membership agreement and that the applicant accepted them. | 2 |
| Accessibility | ACC | Online account opening | The board requires the online application to meet WCAG 2.2 AA. | 1 |
| Applicant Notifications | NTF | Applicant communication | Applicants applying without a branch visit need to know when the application is received, approved, or stalled. | 3 |
| Member Services Application Queue | OPS | Onboarding operations and oversight | Member Services must work pending and referred applications within one business day. | 2 |
| Onboarding Reporting | RPT | Onboarding operations and oversight | Member Services leadership needs daily visibility into how many applications start, stall, and complete. | 1 |

#### Requirements tab: summary

| Number | Name | As A | Priority | Source (workshop-notes.md) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| APP-001 | Capture applicant details | Applicant | Must Have | Discussion: identity bullet |
| APP-002 | Complete application in under 10 minutes | Applicant | Must Have | Goal |
| APP-003 | Exclude joint applications from this release | Member Services lead | Won't Have | Discussion: joint owners bullet |
| APP-004 | Exclude minor applicants | Member Services lead | Won't Have | Discussion: minors bullet |
| ELG-001 | Self-attest eligibility | Applicant | Must Have | Discussion: eligibility bullet |
| ELG-002 | Record eligibility basis | Member Services representative | Must Have | Eligibility and staff view bullets |
| ELG-003 | Spot-check 10% of self-attested eligibility | Member Services representative | Must Have | Discussion: eligibility bullet |
| KYC-001 | Verify identity through VeriPass | Applicant | Must Have | Discussion: identity bullet |
| KYC-002 | Withhold account number until KYC passes | Compliance officer | Must Have | Discussion: identity bullet |
| KYC-003 | Route VeriPass refer results to manual review | Applicant | Must Have | Discussion: identity bullet |
| FND-001 | Fund share deposit by debit card | Applicant | Must Have | Discussion: funding bullet |
| FND-002 | Fund share deposit by ACH | Applicant | Must Have | Discussion: funding bullet |
| FND-003 | Verify external account instantly | Applicant | Should Have | Discussion: funding bullet |
| DSC-001 | Require disclosure acceptance before submission | Applicant | Must Have | Discussion: disclosures bullet |
| DSC-002 | Store accepted document versions | Compliance officer | Must Have | Discussion: disclosures bullet |
| ACC-001 | Meet WCAG 2.2 AA | Applicant using assistive technology | Must Have | Discussion: accessibility bullet |
| NTF-001 | Notify applicant on submission | Applicant | Must Have (default) | Discussion: notifications bullet |
| NTF-002 | Notify applicant on approval | Applicant | Must Have (default) | Discussion: notifications bullet |
| NTF-003 | Notify applicant when more information is needed | Applicant | Must Have (default) | Discussion: notifications bullet |
| OPS-001 | Pending applications queue | Member Services representative | Must Have | Discussion: staff view bullet |
| OPS-002 | Work referred applications within one business day | Member Services lead | Must Have | Discussion: identity bullet |
| RPT-001 | Daily onboarding counts | Member Services lead | Should Have | Discussion: reporting bullet |

Priority reasoning: KYC, disclosures and WCAG are stated as compliance or board requirements, so Must Have. FND-003 is a stated preference ("prefer"), so Should Have. RPT-001 is something Aisha "wants", with no must-language, so Should Have. Joint and minor applications are phase two or out of scope, so Won't Have.

#### Requirements tab: user stories and acceptance criteria

Every row is Status = Draft. "As A" is the persona, then the story reads "I want to … so that …".

##### APP: Online Application Intake

**APP-001 Capture applicant details** (Must Have). As an Applicant, I want to enter my name, SSN and address in the online application, so that I can apply without visiting a branch.

```gherkin
Scenario: Complete details accepted
  Given an applicant on the personal details step with no saved data
  When they enter a legal name, a 9-digit SSN and a residential address and select Continue
  Then the application advances to the eligibility step
  And the entered values are saved to the application record

Scenario: Required field missing
  Given an applicant on the personal details step
  When they leave the SSN blank and select Continue
  Then the application stays on the step
  And an error message names the SSN field

Scenario: Malformed SSN
  Given an applicant on the personal details step
  When they enter 12345 as the SSN and select Continue
  Then the application stays on the step
  And an error message states that the SSN must be 9 digits
```
Note: only "personal details, SSN, address" are named in the notes (G1).

**APP-002 Complete application in under 10 minutes** (Must Have). As an Applicant, I want to finish the membership and first savings account application in under 10 minutes, so that I do not need a branch visit.

```gherkin
Scenario: Application finished within target
  Given an eligible applicant with valid details, a debit card funding source and a VeriPass result of pass
  When they go from starting the application to the submission confirmation page
  Then the elapsed time is under 10 minutes

Scenario: Elapsed time is recorded
  Given an applicant starts an application
  When the application is submitted
  Then the start timestamp and submit timestamp are stored on the application record
```
Note: how the target is measured is undefined (G2). Excluding manual review time is my assumption.

**APP-003 Exclude joint applications from this release** (Won't Have). As the Member Services lead, I want joint applications left out of the first release and recorded for phase two, so that the first release stays limited to single-owner applications.

```gherkin
Scenario: No joint option offered
  Given an applicant on the application start page
  When they view the available application types
  Then no joint-owner option is shown
  And the page states that joint accounts are opened at a branch
```
Note: the group agreed joint is phase two; Sofia Mendes said 20% of branch openings are joint. The branch message is my assumption.

**APP-004 Exclude minor applicants** (Won't Have). As the Member Services lead, I want minor accounts kept out of the online application, so that minors are opened only at a branch.

```gherkin
Scenario: Minor directed to branch
  Given an applicant on the personal details step
  When they enter a date of birth that makes them under 18
  Then the application stops
  And the page states that minor accounts are opened at a branch
```
Note: the notes say "out of scope; branch only". Collecting date of birth and the age of 18 are my assumptions (G1).

##### ELG: Membership Eligibility

**ELG-001 Self-attest eligibility** (Must Have). As an Applicant, I want to state whether I live or work in one of the 6 counties or am a family member of a current member, so that the credit union can confirm I am eligible to join.

```gherkin
Scenario: Applicant attests county residence
  Given an applicant on the eligibility step
  When they select 'I live in one of the 6 counties' and confirm
  Then the application advances to the next step

Scenario: Applicant attests family membership
  Given an applicant on the eligibility step
  When they select 'I am a family member of a current member' and confirm
  Then the application advances to the next step

Scenario: Applicant meets no basis
  Given an applicant on the eligibility step
  When they select 'None of these apply'
  Then the application cannot be submitted
  And the page states that membership is limited to the 6 counties and family of current members
```
Note: the county list and family-relationship detail are missing (G5). The "none" outcome is inferred.

**ELG-002 Record eligibility basis** (Must Have). As a Member Services representative, I want to see which eligibility basis each applicant attested, so that I can review it in the queue and in a spot-check.

```gherkin
Scenario: Basis stored
  Given an applicant attests 'I work in one of the 6 counties'
  When the application is submitted
  Then the application record stores the eligibility basis as 'Works in county'

Scenario: Basis shown in queue
  Given a submitted application with eligibility basis 'Family member'
  When a Member Services representative opens the pending applications queue
  Then the row for that application shows 'Family member'
```

**ELG-003 Spot-check 10% of self-attested eligibility** (Must Have). As a Member Services representative, I want a 10% sample of applications flagged for an eligibility spot-check, so that the credit union can test self-attested eligibility.

```gherkin
Scenario: Sample flagged
  Given 100 applications were submitted with self-attested eligibility during the sampling period
  When the sampling period closes
  Then 10 of those applications are flagged 'Eligibility spot-check' in the queue

Scenario: Spot-check result recorded
  Given an application flagged for spot-check
  When a Member Services representative records the result as 'Confirmed' or 'Not confirmed'
  Then the result and the representative's name are stored on the application record
```
Note: sampling period, selection method and the "Not confirmed" follow-up are not stated (G5).

##### KYC: Identity Verification

**KYC-001 Verify identity through VeriPass** (Must Have). As an Applicant, I want my identity checked through VeriPass when I submit, so that the credit union can open my account in line with KYC rules.

```gherkin
Scenario: Identity data sent for verification
  Given a submitted application with name, SSN and address
  When the application enters identity verification
  Then the details are sent to VeriPass
  And the returned result (pass or refer) is stored on the application record

Scenario: VeriPass unavailable
  Given VeriPass does not respond
  When the application enters identity verification
  Then the application is held with status 'Verification pending'
  And no account number is issued
```
Note: the notes describe only a "refer" result besides a pass (G3). The unavailable scenario is inferred.

**KYC-002 Withhold account number until KYC passes** (Must Have). As the Compliance officer, I want no account number issued before VeriPass returns pass, so that no account exists for an unverified identity.

```gherkin
Scenario: Pass releases account number
  Given an application with a VeriPass result of pass
  When account creation runs
  Then an account number is issued and stored on the application record

Scenario: Refer blocks account number
  Given an application with a VeriPass result of refer
  When account creation runs
  Then no account number is issued

Scenario: Manual review approval releases account number
  Given an application with a VeriPass result of refer that a Member Services representative has approved
  When account creation runs
  Then an account number is issued
```
Note: Rob Lindqvist: "KYC must pass before any account number is issued." Treating a manual approval as a pass is my inference (G3). The core banking interface is unresolved (G8).

**KYC-003 Route VeriPass refer results to manual review** (Must Have). As an Applicant, I want to be told when my identity check needs manual review, so that I know the application has not failed.

```gherkin
Scenario: Refer result queued
  Given an application with a VeriPass result of refer
  When the result is received
  Then the application appears in the Member Services queue with status 'Referred'
  And the applicant sees a message that the application is under review

Scenario: Pass result not queued for review
  Given an application with a VeriPass result of pass
  When the result is received
  Then the application does not appear with status 'Referred'
```

##### FND: Initial Share Deposit Funding

**FND-001 Fund share deposit by debit card** (Must Have). As an Applicant, I want to pay the initial $5 share deposit by debit card, so that my membership is funded when I apply.

```gherkin
Scenario: Debit card accepted
  Given an applicant on the funding step with a valid debit card
  When they choose debit card and confirm the $5 share deposit
  Then a $5.00 charge is authorized
  And the funding status is 'Funded'

Scenario: Debit card declined
  Given an applicant on the funding step
  When the card issuer declines the $5 charge
  Then the funding status stays 'Not funded'
  And the applicant is offered another funding method
```
Note: whether funding comes before or after KYC is not stated (G4).

**FND-002 Fund share deposit by ACH** (Must Have). As an Applicant, I want to pay the initial $5 share deposit by ACH from an account at another institution, so that I can fund without a debit card.

```gherkin
Scenario: ACH funding initiated
  Given an applicant on the funding step with a verified external account
  When they choose ACH and confirm the $5 share deposit
  Then a $5.00 ACH debit is initiated against the external account
  And the funding status is 'Pending ACH'

Scenario: No verified external account
  Given an applicant on the funding step who has not verified an external account
  When they choose ACH
  Then they are taken to account verification before the ACH debit can be confirmed
```
Note: ACH return handling is not stated (G4).

**FND-003 Verify external account instantly** (Should Have). As an Applicant, I want my external account verified instantly through the existing aggregator, so that I do not wait for micro-deposits.

```gherkin
Scenario: Instant verification succeeds
  Given an applicant who chose ACH funding
  When they sign in to their bank through the aggregator and authorize account access
  Then the external account is marked 'Verified' in the same session
  And no micro-deposit is sent

Scenario: Aggregator cannot verify the account
  Given an applicant who chose ACH funding
  When the aggregator returns no verification for the account
  Then the external account is not marked 'Verified'
  And the applicant is offered debit card funding
```
Note: Kai Nakamura prefers this over micro-deposits. Whether micro-deposits stay as a fallback is undecided, so the debit-card fallback is my assumption (G4).

##### DSC: Disclosures and Agreements

**DSC-001 Require disclosure acceptance before submission** (Must Have). As an Applicant, I want to read and accept the Truth in Savings disclosure and membership agreement before I submit, so that I know the terms I am agreeing to.

```gherkin
Scenario: Both documents presented
  Given an applicant on the review step
  When the step loads
  Then the Truth in Savings disclosure and the membership agreement are both displayed

Scenario: Submission blocked until accepted
  Given an applicant who has not accepted both documents
  When they select Submit
  Then the application is not submitted
  And a message states that both documents must be accepted

Scenario: Submission allowed after acceptance
  Given an applicant who accepted both documents
  When they select Submit
  Then the application is submitted
```

**DSC-002 Store accepted document versions** (Must Have). As the Compliance officer, I want the version of each document the applicant accepted stored with the application, so that I can show what each member agreed to.

```gherkin
Scenario: Versions stored
  Given the Truth in Savings disclosure is version 3 and the membership agreement is version 5
  When an applicant accepts both and submits
  Then the application record stores 'Truth in Savings v3' and 'Membership agreement v5'
  And the acceptance date and time

Scenario: Later version does not change earlier record
  Given an application that stored 'Membership agreement v5'
  When version 6 of the membership agreement is published
  Then the stored record still shows 'Membership agreement v5'
```
Note: retention period is not stated (G7).

##### ACC: Accessibility

**ACC-001 Meet WCAG 2.2 AA** (Must Have). As an Applicant using assistive technology, I want to complete the whole application with a keyboard and screen reader, so that I can join without help from a branch.

```gherkin
Scenario: Keyboard-only completion
  Given an applicant using only a keyboard
  When they move through every step from start to confirmation
  Then every control can be reached and operated
  And focus is always visible

Scenario: Conformance audit
  Given the finished application flow
  When it is tested against WCAG 2.2 Level AA success criteria
  Then no failures remain open
```
Note: board requirement. Test method and tools are not stated.

##### NTF: Applicant Notifications

**NTF-001 Notify applicant on submission** (Must Have, default). As an Applicant, I want an email and SMS when I submit, so that I know the credit union received my application.

```gherkin
Scenario: Both messages sent
  Given an applicant with an email address and mobile number on the application
  When the application is submitted
  Then one email and one SMS are sent confirming receipt

Scenario: Send failure recorded
  Given the SMS provider rejects a message
  When the submission notification is sent
  Then the email is still sent
  And the failure is stored on the application record
```
Note: SMS consent is not addressed (G6).

**NTF-002 Notify applicant on approval** (Must Have, default). As an Applicant, I want an email and SMS when my application is approved, so that I know my membership is open.

```gherkin
Scenario: Approval messages sent
  Given an application that has been approved
  When the approval is recorded
  Then one email and one SMS are sent
  And the messages state the account number issued
```
Note: whether the account number may appear in an SMS is a security question (G6).

**NTF-003 Notify applicant when more information is needed** (Must Have, default). As an Applicant, I want an email and SMS if the credit union needs more information from me, so that I can respond and keep my application moving.

```gherkin
Scenario: More-information messages sent
  Given a Member Services representative marks an application 'More information needed'
  When the status is saved
  Then one email and one SMS are sent to the applicant
  And the messages state what is needed
```
Note: how the applicant returns the information is not stated (G3).

##### OPS: Member Services Application Queue

**OPS-001 Pending applications queue** (Must Have). As a Member Services representative, I want a queue of pending applications showing KYC result, eligibility basis and funding status, so that I can see which applications need action.

```gherkin
Scenario: Queue columns
  Given three applications are pending
  When a Member Services representative opens the queue
  Then each row shows the applicant name, KYC result, eligibility basis and funding status

Scenario: Approved applications leave the queue
  Given an application with status 'Approved'
  When a Member Services representative opens the queue
  Then the application is not listed as pending
```
Note: filters, sorting and who may see SSN data are not stated (G7).

```
