Turn these Cedar & Pine Credit Union onboarding workshop notes into the requirements backlog: epics, capabilities, user stories with Gherkin acceptance criteria. Notes are in ./inputs/. Produce the workbook if your tools allow, and show the backlog content in your answer.

Cedar & Pine Credit Union — member onboarding workshop notes (fictional)

Date: (workshop 1 of 2). Attendees: Member Services lead (Aisha Grant), Compliance officer (Rob Lindqvist), Digital banking manager (Kai Nakamura), Branch manager (Sofia Mendes).

Goal: let new members open a membership and a first savings account online in under 10 minutes, instead of the current branch visit.

Discussion:

  • Applicant enters personal details, SSN, address; identity verification through the existing KYC vendor ("VeriPass"). Rob: KYC must pass before any account number is issued. Manual review queue for VeriPass "refer" results, worked by Member Services within 1 business day.
  • Eligibility: must live or work in one of 6 counties, or be a family member of a current member. Applicant self-attests; Member Services spot-checks 10%.
  • Funding: initial $5 share deposit by debit card or ACH from an external account. Kai: ACH micro-deposit verification takes too long; prefer instant account verification through the existing aggregator.
  • Disclosures: Truth in Savings disclosure and membership agreement must be presented and accepted before submission; store the version accepted.
  • Joint owners: Sofia says 20% of branch openings are joint. Group agreed joint applications are phase two.
  • Minors: out of scope; branch only.
  • Notifications: email + SMS at submission, approval, and if more information is needed.
  • Staff view: Member Services needs a queue of pending applications with KYC result, eligibility basis, and funding status.
  • Reporting: Aisha wants daily counts of started, abandoned, submitted, approved, referred.
  • Accessibility: must meet WCAG 2.2 AA (board requirement).
  • Open question: does the core banking system accept account creation via API, or only batch file? Kai to confirm with vendor.

APP: Online Application Intake

Scenario: Malformed SSN

Note: only "personal details, SSN, address" are named in the notes (G1).

APP-002 Complete application in under 10 minutes (Must Have). As an Applicant, I want to finish the membership and first savings account application in under 10 minutes, so that I do not need a branch visit.

Scenario: Elapsed time is recorded
  Given an applicant starts an application

Note: how the target is measured is undefined (G2). Excluding manual review time is my assumption.

skills.title: Capture salesforce screens

skills.markdown:
---
name: capture-salesforce-screens
description: 'Drive the sfqa CLI to capture headless screenshots and run clickpath assertions against a Salesforce org. No interactive login, no credential exposure. Trigger when you need to capture what a Salesforce page looks like without a human watching: after deploying UI-affecting metadata and needing verification evidence, when estate-ac-qa needs its browser driver, or when a ticket needs screenshot proof of a rendered page. Do not trigger for interactive browser exploration (use sf-browser-automation) or for non-Salesforce pages.'
---


# Capture salesforce screens

Captures real Lightning pages from a real headless Chromium, authenticated off
the SF CLI. No interactive login, no credential in the transcript.

**Tool:** set `SFQA_HOME` to the explicitly selected installation for this task.
Verify that its `sfqa.mjs` exists and inspect its current help before use. This
skill does not bundle that executable or establish that a cached installation is
approved. If no supported tool is available, report the browser check pending.

```bash
: "${SFQA_HOME:?Set SFQA_HOME to the selected tool installation}"
test -f "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs"
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" help
```

Use an explicitly confirmed org alias and page or record ID from the task.
The examples below are synthetic; replace their identifiers before invocation.
A write in a clickpath needs the user's authorization for that target.

## When to use this

Use this skill when you need a headless, unattended screenshot or clickpath
assertion against a Salesforce org. Typical callers:

- **`estate-ac-qa`** loads this as its Step 0 browser driver
- Any agent that needs visual evidence of a deployed change
- Manual requests for "show me the page" or "screenshot the record"

For interactive exploration in a visible Chrome the user is watching, use
`sf-browser-automation` instead. This skill is headless-only.

## First run

```bash
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" doctor            # checks SF CLI + Chromium
```

If Chromium is missing, report the dependency. Install a supported browser only when authorized. Do not launch installed macOS Chrome through Node or Playwright; use a permitted connected browser or supported isolated Chromium environment. Never retry the blocked launch path.

## Single screenshot

```bash
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" shot \
  --org CONFIRMED_ORG_ALIAS \
  --url /lightning/r/Account/ACCOUNT_RECORD_ID/view \
  --wait record \
  --out qa/GH-42/account.png --text
```

Writes `account.png`, `account.meta.json` (URL, title, readiness) and, with
`--text`, `account.txt` containing the page's visible text, which is what you
should grep to confirm a value rendered.

Prints a JSON receipt. **Check `ready`**: `false` means a readiness stage timed
out and the image may show a partly-loaded page.

## Many screenshots (one browser, one session)

```bash
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" batch --list shots.json
```

```json
{
  "org": "CONFIRMED_ORG_ALIAS",
  "outDir": "qa/GH-42",
  "viewport": "1600x1000",
  "text": true,
  "shots": [
    { "name": "quote",    "url": "/lightning/r/Quote/0Q0.../view", "wait": "record", "fullPage": true },
    { "name": "accounts", "url": "/lightning/o/Account/list",      "wait": "list" },
    { "name": "fields",   "url": "/lightning/setup/ObjectManager/Account/FieldsAndRelationships/view" }
  ]
}
```

## Clickpath + acceptance criteria (the QA workhorse)

```bash
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" flow --flow acceptance.json
```

```json
{
  "org": "CONFIRMED_ORG_ALIAS",
  "name": "GH-42 invoice summary fees",
  "outDir": "qa/GH-42",
  "text": true,
  "steps": [
    { "goto": "/lightning/r/Account/001.../view", "wait": "record" },
    { "expectText": ["Account Health Summary", "Annual Revenue"], "shot": "details" },
    { "click": "a[role=\"tab\"]:has-text(\"Related\")", "shot": "related" },
    { "expectText": "Contacts" },
    { "click": "button:has-text(\"Edit\")", "wait": "edit", "shot": "edit-modal" },
    { "fill": { "selector": "input[name=\"Name\"]", "value": "Acme Corp" } },
    { "click": "button[name=\"SaveEdit\"]", "wait": "record" },
    { "expectText": "Acme Corp", "shot": "saved", "critical": true }
  ]
}
```

Writes numbered PNGs plus `report.json` and `report.md` (inline screenshots,
per-step pass/fail) into `outDir`. Exit code 2 if any step failed, so it works as
a gate. `report.md` pastes straight into a GitHub issue or PR comment.

**Step keys:** `goto`, `wait`, `waitFor`, `settle`, `quiet`, `dismiss`, `click`,
`clickAt`, `hover`, `type`, `fill`, `press`, `scroll`, `scrollTo`, `expectText`,
`expectNoText`, `shot`, `critical`, `name`.

## When to trust the detector, and when to use your own eyes

`shot`/`batch`/`flow` use readiness heuristics. Verify them against representative pages in the selected org before relying on a bulk capture; prior measurements from another org do not establish current readiness.

Use `watch` when a heuristic shouldn't have the final say, for example an LWC doing
an external callout that legitimately takes 20s, a page that looks wrong, or
anything unfamiliar:

```bash
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" watch --org CONFIRMED_ORG_ALIAS \
  --url /lightning/r/Account/001.../view --every 2000 --for 20000 --out-dir qa/watch
```

It captures a frame every N ms and **decides nothing**. Read the frames, judge
visually, and re-run with a larger `--for` if `stillMoving` is true.

## Slowness is a finding, report it

Every capture reports `renderMs` (when the page actually stopped changing, the QA
signal) and `totalMs` (includes ~3.9s of our own confirmation window). `slow: true`
appears when `renderMs` exceeds `--slow-threshold` (default 5000).

Treat a slow page as a defect worth mentioning, not just a longer wait. Likely
causes: slow SOQL, an external callout, or a stale LWC needing recompile. Retry
with `--hard-refresh` to rule the last one out.

**Calibrate per org.** Measure representative pages in the authorized target and
record the samples before selecting `--slow-threshold`. A threshold from another
project is not a baseline for this one.

## How readiness works, and why you rarely need to tune it

Lightning boots async, keeps long-poll connections open forever (so `networkidle`
never fires), and renders into **shadow DOM** (so `document.querySelector` cannot
see its components). The tool therefore waits on a signal that needs no knowledge
of Salesforce internals: **the page stopped changing.**

Specifically: text length steady **and** no DOM mutation, across **all frames**, for
2500ms in the described implementation; confirm the selected tool's current
settings. Text can stabilize before all components arrive, an iframe can load
while the main frame is quiet, and persistent network connections can outlive
rendering. A quiet window is a heuristic, not proof that required content loaded.

Practical consequences:

- **Do not pass `settle` after a click.** Interaction steps auto-wait for quiet.
  Adding `settle` *disables* that and reverts you to guessing.
- `--wait <mode>` (`auto`, `record`, `list`, `edit`, `setup`, `none`) is only a
  speed hint. `auto` works on every page family, including Object Manager (which
  lives on a different domain and matches no standard content selector).
- Setup / Object Manager pages are a Lightning+Aura+Visualforce mix and are slower
  and uglier than anything you ship. Prefer testing real front-end pages.
- After deploying an LWC, add `--hard-refresh` to defeat a stale compiled bundle.
- Raise `--settle` only for genuinely animated content, e.g. dashboards.

## Clicking: selector vs coordinates

Both dispatch **real mouse/keyboard events via CDP**, never a JS `.click()`.

- `click: "<selector>"` -- Playwright hit-tests and enforces actionability. If a
  human could not click it (covered by an overlay, hidden, disabled), the step
  **fails** rather than silently passing. That is the QA-correct behaviour and the
  main reason not to use JS clicks.
- `clickAt: [x, y]` -- raw coordinates, zero DOM knowledge. Use this when you have
  just looked at a screenshot and want to click what you see. Coordinates are in
  CSS pixels of the viewport (`--viewport`), not the retina pixels of the PNG:
  with the default `--scale 2`, divide the pixel position in the image by 2.

## Useful flags

| Flag | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `--full-page` | Whole scrollable page, not just the viewport |
| `--selector <css>` | Crop to one component (e.g. a single LWC) |
| `--mask <css,css>` | Cover elements, redact PII before sharing |
| `--dismiss` | Close toasts / walkthrough tooltips / splash modals first |
| `--viewport 390x844` | Mobile-width rendering |
| `--headed` | Watch it run, for debugging |
| `--hard-refresh` | Reload bypassing HTTP cache, stale LWC after a deploy |
| `--slow-threshold <ms>` | Flag slow pages as a finding (calibrate per org) |
| `--text` | Write visible page text (grep this to verify values) |

## Sessions

Inspect the selected tool's session configuration before use. Reuse a cached
session only after verifying its org and account match the task. Keep cookies in
private storage outside packages and reports. A username or matching alias alone
does not authorize reuse in another account context.

When supported by the selected tool, `sfqa session --org CONFIRMED_ORG_ALIAS
--refresh` renews that session and `--clear` removes it. Authentication changes
remain separate authorized account actions. Do not silently choose a cached org.

## Credential safety (why this is safe to run unattended)

- **No bearer token is ever handled.** Auth redeems a **single-use** frontdoor URL
  from `sf org open --url-only`, consumed in-process by `page.goto()`. It is burned
  by that one navigation. The legacy `frontdoor.jsp?sid=<accessToken>` trick is
  *not* used and no longer works on current orgs anyway.
- The URL is never printed. Every byte the process writes passes through a
  redaction filter that scrubs `otp`/`cshc`/`sid`/token shapes, including from
  uncaught exceptions and Playwright errors that quote the URL.
- Playwright tracing and HAR recording are deliberately disabled; both would
  persist the session cookie to disk.
- **Never** run `sf org open --url-only` or `sf org display --json` yourself and
  paste the output. That puts a live credential in the transcript. Let the tool
  consume them internally.

## Gotchas

- Deploy succeeding is not verification, and neither is a green `ready`. Look at
  the PNG, and grep the `.txt`.
- On failure the tool writes `<out>.FAILED.png`. Check it first when diagnosing.
- Screenshots are retina (`--scale 2`), so a 1600x1000 viewport yields a 3200x2000
  PNG. Use `--scale 1` for smaller files.
- Inspect the actual browser path and supported launch policy before running. The tool configuration does not override the prohibition on direct installed macOS Chrome launches. Record any headless rendering limits.
- Each invocation uses a fresh browser profile, so the HTTP cache is always cold
  between runs. Stale LWC bundles only matter *within* one batch/flow run.

examples.title: Screenshot evidence for a new fee field on a wholesale account page
examples.markdown:
## Request

$capture-salesforce-screens We deployed the Delivery Fee field to the Account page layout in the uat-orchard sandbox for ticket GH-118. Get me screenshot proof that it renders on account 001UAT000000AbCDE and that the Related tab still loads. Don't edit anything.

## Inputs

**Dry run.** This skill normally works on live systems or its owner's own setup. Here the system state is invented in the inputs below, and nothing was changed anywhere. The recording session made up the org alias `uat-orchard`, the ticket and the record ID. It had no Salesforce org, no SF CLI session, no `sfqa` installation and no approved browser, so nothing below was captured. Following the skill, the answer prepares the run and reports the browser check as pending. It does not describe screenshots that don't exist.

The user confirmed the org alias and record ID in the request. The flow has no write steps, so it needs no write authorization.

## Output

I couldn't capture anything. `SFQA_HOME` isn't set in this environment, so there's no selected `sfqa` installation to run, and the skill doesn't bundle one. The browser check for GH-118 is **pending**.

Once a supported `sfqa` installation is selected, this is the run. First confirm the tool and its dependencies:

```bash
: "${SFQA_HOME:?Set SFQA_HOME to the selected tool installation}"
test -f "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs"
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" help
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" doctor
```

If `doctor` reports Chromium missing, stop and report it. Don't point the tool at the installed macOS Chrome.

Then run this flow as `qa/GH-118/acceptance.json`. It only reads: it opens the record, checks the field label, opens the Related tab and checks that it loaded.

```json
{
  "org": "uat-orchard",
  "name": "GH-118 delivery fee field on Account",
  "outDir": "qa/GH-118",
  "text": true,
  "steps": [
    { "goto": "/lightning/r/Account/001UAT000000AbCDE/view", "wait": "record" },
    { "expectText": "Delivery Fee", "shot": "details", "critical": true },
    { "click": "a[role=\"tab\"]:has-text(\"Related\")", "shot": "related" },
    { "expectText": "Contacts", "shot": "related-loaded" }
  ]
}
```

```bash
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" flow --flow qa/GH-118/acceptance.json --hard-refresh
```

`--hard-refresh` rules out a stale cached bundle right after the deploy. Exit code 2 means a step failed, and `<name>.FAILED.png` is the first file to open. A passing run isn't proof on its own: open `details.png` and confirm the Delivery Fee value is visible, then grep the `.txt` beside it for "Delivery Fee". Report any step with `slow: true` as a finding. This org has no measured baseline yet, so leave `--slow-threshold` at its default and record the `renderMs` values as the first samples.

`report.md` from that run can go straight into GH-118.

Then run this flow as qa/GH-118/acceptance.json. It only reads: it opens the record, checks the field label, opens the Related tab and checks that it loaded.

{
  "org": "uat-orchard",
  "name": "GH-118 delivery fee field on Account",
  "outDir": "qa/GH-118",
  "text": true,
  "steps": [
    { "goto": "/lightning/r/Account/001UAT000000AbCDE/view", "wait": "record" },
    { "expectText": "Delivery Fee", "shot": "details", "critical": true },
    { "click": "a[role=\"tab\"]:has-text(\"Related\")", "shot": "related" },
    { "expectText": "Contacts", "shot": "related-loaded" }
  ]
}
node "$SFQA_HOME/sfqa.mjs" flow --flow qa/GH-118/acceptance.json --hard-refresh

--hard-refresh rules out a stale cached bundle right after the deploy. Exit code 2 means a step failed, and <name>.FAILED.png is the first file to open. A passing run isn't proof on its own: open details.png and confirm the Delivery Fee value is visible, then grep the .txt beside it for "Delivery Fee". Report any step with slow: true as a finding. This org has no measured baseline yet, so leave --slow-threshold at its default and record the renderMs values as the first samples.

report.md from that run can go straight into GH-118.

# Check knowledge hub

## Host access

Resolve the hub endpoint, router, local roots and permitted account from explicit task or project configuration. No personal drive, owner profile, schedule or account is a default. Confirm that the selected adapter implements the named operations; if it does not, use its supported equivalent and preserve the same revision, authorization and acceptance checks.

Use only tools and files actually available in this session. In Claude Code invoke `/check-knowledge-hub`; in Codex use `$check-knowledge-hub`; in Claude chat/Cowork ask to use `check-knowledge-hub`. Mac paths identify local authorities; in Cowork resolve them only through a folder already shared with this session. Cloud chat cannot read a Mac path or localhost merely because this skill names it. When hub access or a required foundation is unavailable, report that gap and continue only work supported by accessible evidence. Use named companion skills when available; otherwise apply the safeguards below and identify any required review gate you cannot complete. Do not install dependencies or broaden permissions automatically.

1. Read the current configured hub router when available. Call `get_context`, then `check_health` on the existing permitted hub connection. Record the observation time, the route (the local service or the remote gateway that web assistants use), actor scope, and returned contract revision. Do not silently substitute a different account or endpoint.
2. Interpret the response within that scope. Null backup, budget, or bridge fields mean unavailable to this check, not absent or healthy. Zero visible findings in a common-contract-only view does not mean the private hub is healthy. “Verified connected” means retrieval was observed; it does not prove that the tool followed guidance, accessed private records, or completed a cloud connection.
3. For authorized Mac-local maintenance, run `python3 scripts/collect_evidence.py --index CONFIG.json` from this skill directory first. Require an explicitly selected, owner-authorized configuration outside the package; `references/evidence-index.json` is an unconfigured schema template, not a live destination. Read the configuration before executing and confirm its paths, selected skill entrypoints, optional launchd labels and expected heartbeat age. The script reads the hub’s existing writer-maintained SQLite receipt pointers in read-only mode, verifies the current backup file and skill links, and reports bridge and launchd state. It does not perform a restore or print raw private records, login keys, or recovery material. If this session cannot run local scripts or reach the runtime, label these areas `not-rechecked`; do not infer a current failure from an old receipt. Do not create a second Store/writer or reuse local owner authentication for a cloud caller. Then inspect current operator documentation or bounded logs only for gaps the script cannot cover.
4. Check the dimensions the task and access support: source mounts and registered coverage; source/retrieval revision parity; current adapters and actual account probes; failed/overdue jobs and backlog; unresolved freshness/dependency findings; monthly usage plus infrastructure reserve; backup age, isolated restoration evidence, off-service delivery, and separate key recovery. Verify timestamps and expected schedules from the current configuration. File presence does not prove installation, a schedule does not prove execution, and local restoration does not prove off-service recovery.
5. Use each script row as the starting status for its area. Its `verified-now` restore status means the latest recorded isolated restore covers the current generation and its encrypted backup hash still matches; it does not mean a restore ran during this health check. It reads receipt pointers by database key, not filename, so newer receipts in nested folders count when written by the hub. Classify remaining dimensions as verified now, needs attention, or not rechecked, with timestamp and evidence. Carry stable finding IDs across reviews. A narrower check leaves prior findings not rechecked; it does not resolve them. Mark resolution only after passing evidence and reopen on recurrence. Do not turn old field-guide counts or previous healthy receipts into present status.
6. For connection behavior, make a harmless read probe against a record the actor is allowed to see, fully fetch the pinned revision, and compare it with the expected revision. If two tools are being verified, test each actual account. Use synthetic nonprivate material for write-path tests, only within an authorized test scope; never mutate production merely to prove a check worked.
7. Prioritize findings by consequence: wrong authority/private leakage or data loss, failed capture/retrieval, recovery gaps, blocked jobs, then cosmetic drift. If repair was requested, fix reversible failures within that scope and recheck. Otherwise return the concrete repair needed. Changing account access, sharing, contracts, spending commitments, or destructive state requires the applicable user authorization. Do not create another maintenance scheduler by default.

Report a short, useful status with evidence and the most important next action. Explicitly separate local service availability from remote gateway access and ledger accounting from provider billing enforcement. Explain that the Hub runs only on the Mac, so Mac-local agents and every remote client lose access while the Mac is asleep or offline. Use `verify-work-state` for repairs and state changed now, verified, still unchanged, and exact next action.

Examples: `$check-knowledge-hub Check what is working and what needs attention.` / `$check-knowledge-hub Diagnose the stale context and repair reversible local failures.`

examples.title: Diagnosing missing phone notes and a stalled photo index
examples.markdown:
## Request

$check-knowledge-hub Notes I saved from my phone yesterday aren't showing up when I ask the assistant on my laptop, and the survey photos folder seems to have stopped indexing. Check what is working and what needs attention. I've pasted the health response and an export of the hub state; don't change anything.

## Inputs

**Dry run.** This skill normally works on live systems or its owner's own setup. Here the system state is invented in the inputs below, and nothing was changed anywhere. Run of the built `check-knowledge-hub` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### check_health-response.md

#### check_health response (pasted by user)

Observed: 2026-11-04T08:10:00Z
Route: remote gateway (web assistant)
Actor scope: priya-anand, common contract plus own private records
Contract revision (get_context): r212
Retrieval revision (pinned fetch of note "Site visit 3 Nov"): r209

```
status: ok
visible_findings: 0
backup: null
budget: null
bridge: null
jobs: null
```

Note from Priya: the phone save of "Site visit 3 Nov" returned "saved" on 2026-11-03 around 16:20Z.

#### hub-state-export.md

#### Hub state export (read-only, taken 2026-11-04T08:10:00Z)

Config used (owner-authorized, outside the package):
runtimeRoot /Users/priya/KnowledgeRuntime; offMacBackupDir /Volumes/OffsiteVault/hub-backups;
bridgeMaxAgeSeconds 900; mountRoots /Volumes/FieldData;
skillEntrypoints /Users/priya/skills/capture-knowledge/SKILL.md, /Volumes/FieldData/skills/photo-index/SKILL.md;
launchdJobs com.example.knowledge.maintenance

manifest.json generation: 418

settings.last_backup: at 2026-11-04T02:00:12Z, generation 418, offService false,
  destination /Users/priya/KnowledgeRuntime/backups/hub-418-20261104.enc, recorded sha256 matches file (recomputed)

settings.last_restore: at 2026-10-27T03:15:40Z, state passed, generation 391, records 5120,
  backupHash matches file hub-391-20261027.enc

Off-Mac folder listing: hub-412-20261101.enc, hub-415-20261102.enc (separate volume from runtime)

bridge (latest heartbeat): at 2026-11-04T07:41:05Z
  roots: /Users/priya/Notes mounted; /Volumes/FieldData not mounted
  sources: field-notes ok; survey-photos offline-or-missing

jobs (newest first):
  ingest        done    2026-11-04T07:30:00Z
  maintenance-cycle failed 2026-11-02T03:00:04Z
  maintenance-cycle done   2026-10-30T03:00:02Z

skill entrypoints: capture-knowledge/SKILL.md readable;
  /Volumes/FieldData/skills/photo-index/SKILL.md not found (FieldData not a mount point)

launchctl print com.example.knowledge.maintenance: state = waiting

## Output

**The hub is reachable, but retrieval is behind and the photo index is stopped. Nothing here was changed.**

The most important next action is to mount `/Volumes/FieldData` on the Mac. That fixes the photo indexing. Then rerun the maintenance cycle, which has been failing since 2 Nov.

#### Scope of this check

- Observed 2026-11-04T08:10Z.
- Route: remote gateway (web assistant), actor `priya-anand`, common contract plus your own private records.
- Local evidence: your hub-state export, read with the `collect_evidence.py` rules. I applied those rules by hand because I can't run scripts here. I did not probe the Mac or the launchd job live.
- The hub runs only on the Mac. While the Mac is asleep or offline, Mac-local agents and every remote client lose access.

#### Why the phone note is missing

The pinned fetch of "Site visit 3 Nov" returned revision **r209**. The contract revision is **r212**. Retrieval is three revisions behind, so the assistant on your laptop is reading older context. The phone's "saved" reply on 3 Nov (~16:20Z) shows the save was accepted. It doesn't show the note was indexed.

I can't name the cause from this evidence. The likely suspects are the failed maintenance cycle (F-02) and the stopped photo source (F-01). The export doesn't show which one blocks the note. The note's own record and the ingest log would show it. Ingest itself ran fine at 07:30Z.

#### Findings

| ID | Area | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 | Bridge / sources | Needs attention | Latest heartbeat 07:41:05Z is 29 min old, over the 15 min limit. `/Volumes/FieldData` is not mounted and `survey-photos` is offline-or-missing. `field-notes` is ok. |
| F-02 | Maintenance job | Needs attention | `maintenance-cycle` failed 2026-11-02T03:00Z. The last success was 30 Oct. Launchd shows the job as `waiting`. Waiting is normal between runs, so the failed run is the real signal. |
| F-03 | Restore evidence | Needs attention | The last isolated restore (27 Oct, generation 391, 5,120 records, passed) predates the failed cycle and covers an old generation. The current generation is 418. The restore is not evidence for the current data. |
| F-04 | Off-Mac backup | Needs attention | The latest backup (generation 418, 02:00Z today) is local only. Off-Mac holds generations 412 and 415, so the current generation has no off-Mac copy. |
| F-05 | Retrieval parity | Needs attention | r209 against r212, described above. |
| F-06 | Skill links | Partly not rechecked | `capture-knowledge` is readable. `photo-index` could not be checked because FieldData isn't mounted. This is a result of F-01, not a separate fault. |

Verified now:
- **Local backup.** The generation 418 file's hash matches its recorded value, and it covers the current generation. It was written at 02:00Z, about 8 hours ago.
- **Ingest.** The last ingest job finished at 07:30Z.
- **Notes root.** `/Users/priya/Notes` is mounted.

#### What this check could not see

- **Budget, backup, bridge and jobs from the gateway.** All came back null. Null means unavailable to this check, not healthy. I took those areas from your local export instead.
- **"Zero visible findings."** That is a common-contract view and says nothing about your private hub.
- **Key recovery.** Not rechecked. No key escrow evidence was supplied.
- **Monthly usage and infrastructure reserve.** Not rechecked, because the budget field was null. I have no ledger or provider billing figures.
- **Local service against remote gateway.** The gateway answered a read. The local service was not probed live, so its current state is known only from the 08:10Z export.

#### Next actions, in order

1. Mount `/Volumes/FieldData` on the Mac, then look for a new bridge heartbeat. It should be under 15 minutes old with `survey-photos` ok. (F-01, F-06)
2. Read the log for the 2 Nov `maintenance-cycle` failure and rerun the cycle once the source is mounted. Rerunning is a repair, so tell me if you want me to do it. (F-02)
3. After that, fetch "Site visit 3 Nov" again and compare it with the contract revision. It should return r212 or later. (F-05)
4. Let the nightly run copy generation 418 to the off-Mac volume. Check for a `*-418-*.enc` file in `/Volumes/OffsiteVault/hub-backups` tomorrow. (F-04)
5. Schedule a fresh isolated restore of the current generation. A restore changes state, so I haven't started one. (F-03)

If you reopen this later, findings F-01 to F-06 keep these IDs. A narrower check will leave the others marked not rechecked. I'll mark one resolved only after passing evidence.

#### Files

No files were produced. The only artefact is this report.

  1. Mount /Volumes/FieldData on the Mac, then look for a new bridge heartbeat. It should be under 15 minutes old with survey-photos ok. (F-01, F-06)
  2. Read the log for the 2 Nov maintenance-cycle failure and rerun the cycle once the source is mounted. Rerunning is a repair, so tell me if you want me to do it. (F-02)
  3. After that, fetch "Site visit 3 Nov" again and compare it with the contract revision. It should return r212 or later. (F-05)
  4. Let the nightly run copy generation 418 to the off-Mac volume. Check for a *-418-*.enc file in /Volumes/OffsiteVault/hub-backups tomorrow. (F-04)
  5. Schedule a fresh isolated restore of the current generation. A restore changes state, so I haven't started one. (F-03)

skills.markdown:
---
name: compare-scope-options
description: Build a static scope summary or side-by-side option comparison from current quotes or a dated quote export. Reconciles every scope item, per-option hour value, status and staffing-snapshot price before producing a complete HTML reference. Use for scope matrices, tier comparisons and client leave-behinds. Route selectable proposal experiences to build-interactive-proposal, deal decision decks to ddoc, contracts to sow and quote changes to scope-project.
---

# Compare scope options

Produce the reference itself: one self-contained HTML file with the scope matrix visible, plus a printable version when requested. A reader should be able to identify the difference between options and see what each price covers.

Before drafting, read [the build card](../_shared/build-card.md). Keep the commercial writing checks in [the proposal register](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/sow-proposal.md): preserve exact scope and avoid strengthening a delivery claim. Brand identity comes from the [canonical profile](references/estate/brand.md), resolved through `brand-renderer`. The skill contains no company palette or required logo.

## Resolve the input and mode

Name the client, quote IDs and requested order. One quote produces a single-option summary; several quotes produce a comparison. State the mode when beginning a real request. Do not assume that a more expensive option contains every cheaper option's items. Establish any ascending-scope relationship from the actual matrix.

Use the available quote connector for a current client reference. If it is unavailable, accept a user-supplied export with its source system, revision and capture time. The resulting reference describes that dated export. A local file does not establish current live state. Ask for a fresh export when the requested decision depends on changes since capture; never fabricate a connector or reuse remembered figures.

If neither a connector nor an export supplies the required scope, stop the dependent build and identify the missing records. A synthetic fixture is suitable for testing the skill, not for filling a client quote.

## Capture the full scope

Read [validation.md](validation.md) before assembling data. Save every quote's full item list and its active-item list. With an available scoping connector, this corresponds to `scoping_get_scope_hierarchy` with `activeOnly: false`, `includeHours: true`, `includeFinancials: false`, followed by the active-only read. Use the connector's actual schema; these operation names are an adapter example, not a promise that a tool is installed.

Retain stable item IDs and the quote's own hours. The four states remain distinct:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Included | Present and selected, without an optional flag. |
| Optional | Explicitly marked optional, even if also returned in the active read. |
| Available | Present but deselected. Adding it may require a price or schedule change. |
| Not included | Absent from that quote's full scope. |

Single-option mode still shows optional and available items when the quote contains them. Do not hide deselected work to force a two-state layout. An absent item in another option is not zero-hour work. The matrix shows each option's hours separately when they differ.

## Resolve price and staffing

List timeline snapshots first and identify the active snapshot ID. Read that snapshot by ID; do not select the newest merely because it was created last. Each displayed staffing variant needs its own actual snapshot, including revenue, currency, duration and staffing hours. Never derive another variant by multiplying a rate.

The headline price comes from the staffing snapshot. Per-item dollars are omitted because back-allocation may drift between snapshots. Item hours are scope estimates; staffing hours can also cover delivery activities. Do not force the two totals to match or infer that an optional item is already priced.

Display exact prices by default. If the user requests rounded prices, show the rounded amount as approximate and preserve the exact quote alongside it. Rounding never changes the working source. Show all requested staffing variants on the static page so printing retains every price and duration. For a prospect-facing selector, choose the interactive proposal or explorer mode and read [its complete workflow](../build-interactive-proposal/SKILL.md). The portable Scope Options package embeds it; static comparison rules do not substitute for its interaction and print checks.

## Reconcile before rendering

Use the source and presentation JSON contract in [validation.md](validation.md). The source holds captured facts; the presentation holds the intended matrix and option copy. The supplied validator compares them independently.

```bash
python3 scripts/scope_reference_validate.py SOURCE.json PRESENTATION.json
python3 scripts/build_scope.py SOURCE.json PRESENTATION.json OUTPUT.html
```

Both commands refuse mismatched item sets or states. They also reject changed names, conflicting IDs, missing description evidence and unsupported snapshot figures. The builder reruns reconciliation before writing. Keep the resulting `.reconciliation.json` with the artifact and inputs. Do not edit the final HTML to bypass a discrepancy.

Report the actual reconcile result and counts. Included and optional counts remain separate from available items. Never label a present-item count as an included-item count.

## Author and build

Read [build-guide.md](build-guide.md). Give each item a concise description grounded in its stored description, effort basis or supplied source. The portable input requires a reference to that evidence. A reference alone does not prove that an authored sentence is faithful; compare its meaning before delivery. For verbatim SOW descriptions, use the exported description field.

Preserve source names in the reconciliation record. If a name contains internal language that cannot appear in client copy, obtain an approved display-name mapping or correct the source. Never silently remove a material scope condition while sanitizing the wording.

Keep assumptions and exclusions that affect the client's choice visible. An unresolved internal issue belongs in the working record, but a condition that changes scope or price cannot be hidden from the reader. Do not recommend an option without supplied decision criteria.

## Inspect and deliver

Run brand preflight and the applicable writing checks through the packaged runtime. Read the complete output against the quote records. Inspect the matrix at desktop and narrow widths, and check every exported PDF page for missing rows or split labels. A clean numeric reconcile does not validate the option summaries.

Follow [the release gate](../_shared/release-gate.md). Keep failed attempts and the actual output alongside the source hashes and review record. Deliver the HTML and requested PDF with the quoted source date. Record any authorized knowledge-hub update separately; creating a local reference does not update the quote or publish it.

examples.title: Scope comparison of two repairs portal quotes with staffing variants
examples.markdown:
## Request

Please build the scope reference for Fernhill Housing Association comparing quotes Q-4101 and Q-4102 for the tenant repairs portal, Q-4101 first. The export is in inputs/ and I want both staffing variants shown with exact prices.

## Inputs

Run of the built `compare-scope-options` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Other files it produced, not shown here: `plan.json`, `scope.html`, `scope.reconciliation.json`, `source.json`.

#### quote-export.md

#### Quote export: tenant repairs portal

Source system: Quote desk export (CSV converted to Markdown by the account manager)
Revision: 14
Captured: 2026-10-28 09:40 +00:00
Client: Fernhill Housing Association

##### Q-4101 (Core)

Active snapshot: Q-4101-A

| ID | Item | Category | Hours | Optional | Active | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| repair-form | Repair request form | Intake | 40 | no | yes | Tenants report a repair with address, category and up to five photos. |
| triage-rules | Triage rules | Intake | 32 | no | yes | Sort each request as emergency, urgent or routine using Fernhill's approved rules. |
| contractor-sync | Contractor scheduling sync | Integration | 56 | no | yes | Send accepted jobs to the contractor scheduling system and read back appointment dates. |
| status-tracking | Tenant status tracking | Tenant experience | 24 | no | no | Let tenants see where a repair stands and its booked appointment. |
| sms | SMS notifications | Tenant experience | 16 | yes | no | Text tenants when a job is booked or rescheduled. |
| staff-training | Staff training | Handoff | 12 | no | yes | Train the repairs team to review and reassign triaged requests. |

| Snapshot | Label | Price | Weeks | Staffing hours |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q-4101-A | Standard team | GBP 48,600.00 | 7 | 300 |
| Q-4101-B | Lower-rate team | GBP 44,250.00 | 8 | 330 |

##### Q-4102 (Extended)

Active snapshot: Q-4102-A

| ID | Item | Category | Hours | Optional | Active | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| repair-form | Repair request form | Intake | 40 | no | yes | Tenants report a repair with address, category and up to five photos. |
| triage-rules | Triage rules | Intake | 40 | no | yes | Sort each request as emergency, urgent or routine using Fernhill's approved rules. |
| contractor-sync | Contractor scheduling sync | Integration | 56 | no | yes | Send accepted jobs to the contractor scheduling system and read back appointment dates. |
| open-job-import | Open-job import | Integration | 36 | yes | no | Load repairs already open in the legacy system once its field mapping is approved. |
| status-tracking | Tenant status tracking | Tenant experience | 28 | no | yes | Let tenants see where a repair stands and its booked appointment. |
| sms | SMS notifications | Tenant experience | 16 | no | yes | Text tenants when a job is booked or rescheduled. |
| audit-accessibility | Accessibility audit | Handoff | 20 | no | yes | Check the tenant pages against WCAG 2.2 AA and list defects found. |
| staff-training | Staff training | Handoff | 16 | no | yes | Train the repairs team to review and reassign triaged requests. |

| Snapshot | Label | Price | Weeks | Staffing hours |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q-4102-A | Standard team | GBP 71,900.00 | 10 | 440 |
| Q-4102-B | Lower-rate team | GBP 66,300.00 | 11 | 470 |
| Q-4102-C | Draft v3 (not active) | GBP 74,500.00 | 10 | 450 |

#### scope-notes.txt

Scope notes from the quote desk, applying to both quotes

- Tenant and repair records stay in Fernhill's housing management system. The portal reads and writes them through the existing interface.
- A native mobile app is outside both quotes.
- SMS message charges are paid by Fernhill to its messaging provider and are not in either price.
- Open-job import (Q-4102 only, optional) depends on Fernhill approving the legacy field mapping before work starts.
- Staffing hours cover delivery activities such as project management and testing. Item hours are estimates for each item.

## Output

I've built the scope reference for Fernhill Housing Association as one self-contained HTML page. It compares Q-4101 (Core) and Q-4102 (Extended) in that order. The mode is a two-quote static comparison with both staffing variants and exact prices. The quotes are as of the export captured 2026-10-28 09:40 (+00:00), revision 14, from the quote desk. A local export doesn't show live state, so ask for a fresh export if either quote has changed since then.

**I couldn't run the scripts or a browser, so the checks below were done by hand.** The validator, the builder, the brand preflight, the prose and brand checkers, the browser and print checks and the PDF export all need Python, Node or Chromium. I applied the reconcile rules from `validation.md` myself and wrote the HTML following the builder's structure and stylesheet. The reconciliation file is marked as hand-written and has no hashes. Please run the two scripts on `out/source.json` and `out/plan.json` before sending this to the client. You didn't ask for a PDF, so I didn't make one.

#### Prices and plans

Each price is exact and comes from the staffing snapshot. The matrix has no per-item prices.

| Option | Plan | Price | Duration | Staffing hours |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Core (Q-4101) | Standard team (active) | GBP 48,600.00 | 7 weeks | 300 |
| Core (Q-4101) | Lower-rate team | GBP 44,250.00 | 8 weeks | 330 |
| Extended (Q-4102) | Standard team (active) | GBP 71,900.00 | 10 weeks | 440 |
| Extended (Q-4102) | Lower-rate team | GBP 66,300.00 | 11 weeks | 470 |

The export also holds a third Q-4102 snapshot, "Draft v3 (not active)", at GBP 74,500.00 over 10 weeks and 450 hours. It isn't the active snapshot and you didn't ask for it, so it's left out. It stays in the source file.

#### What differs between the options

Counts are given per state. Available items aren't counted as included.

| Item | Core | Extended |
|---|---|---|
| Repair request form | Included, 40 h | Included, 40 h |
| Triage rules | Included, 32 h | Included, 40 h |
| Contractor scheduling sync | Included, 56 h | Included, 56 h |
| Open-job import | Not included | Optional, 36 h |
| Tenant status tracking | Available, 24 h | Included, 28 h |
| SMS notifications | Optional, 16 h | Included, 16 h |
| Accessibility audit | Not included | Included, 20 h |
| Staff training | Included, 12 h | Included, 16 h |

- **Core (Q-4101):** 4 included, 1 optional, 1 available, 2 not included.
- **Extended (Q-4102):** 7 included, 1 optional, 0 available, 0 not included.

Three points in the matrix are easy to misread:

- Tenant status tracking is present in Core but not selected. It is shown as Available, and adding it may change the price or schedule.
- Open-job import and the accessibility audit are absent from Core, so their cells show no hours.
- Hours differ by option for triage rules, tenant status tracking and staff training. Each cell shows its own quote's figure.

#### Scope conditions shown on the page

- Tenant and repair records stay in Fernhill's housing management system. The portal reads and writes them through the existing interface.
- A native mobile app is outside both quotes.
- SMS message charges are paid by Fernhill to its messaging provider and are not in either price.
- Open-job import depends on Fernhill approving the legacy field mapping before work starts.
- Staffing hours cover delivery activities such as project management and testing. Item hours are estimates for each item.

#### Checks and gaps

- **Reconciliation, by hand:** The 8 matrix items are the union of both quotes' items, with unique IDs. Every active ID is in its full list, and the active snapshots match the export. Snapshot figures were copied exactly. Absent items have null hours.
- **Descriptions:** Every description is the export's own wording, so I added no claims. There was no `effort_basis` field to cite.
- **Brand:** No project `brand.md` was supplied, so the page uses the neutral Baseline profile, with no logo. Its colours, type and 1px borders are inlined. I did not check contrast or the page's appearance, because I could not render it.
- **Not done:** No desktop, narrow-width or print inspection, and no scripted prose or brand check. I read the authored sentences. The option summaries (Core and Extended) follow the item states in the matrix. They give no recommendation, because you supplied no decision criteria.
- **Not published:** Creating this file doesn't change either quote or update any knowledge hub.

#### Files

- `out/scope.html`: the reference page, with the option panels, the staffing-plan tables, the grouped scope matrix, the state legend and the scope conditions.
- `out/source.json`: the normalized capture of the export, including the inactive draft snapshot.
- `out/plan.json`: the presentation record that the page was built from.
- `out/scope.reconciliation.json`: the hand-written reconciliation record, described above.
- `out/answer.md`: this reply.
