# Configure salesforce project

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`general.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/general.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

This skill puts Estate's delivery discipline onto a project and proves it is still
there later. It is **not** the thing you read while implementing a feature — that
contract lives in the project's `CLAUDE.md` (Claude) or `AGENTS.md` (Codex), where it is in context every session
without anything having to trigger.

The direct-delivery invariant is **`trunk === the org`**. In DevOps Center mode the
invariant becomes **DevOps Center owns stage branches and promotion**, while the local
loop owns WI worktrees, scoped org capture, quality, validation, and review handoff.

> **Successor to the retired solo workflow.** Same invariant, same worktree/validate/merge/
> deploy discipline, re-architected for four realities the solo skill never faced:
> the repo may belong to the client or not exist remotely at all; tickets may live in
> Jira; the person using it is probably not the person who wrote it; and the skill is
> not the delivery mechanism for the rules — `CLAUDE.md` is.
>
> **Not this skill:** multi-environment promotion, pipelines, org-to-org sync. Those are
> owned by `operate-salesforce-pipeline` or Salesforce DevOps Center. On an engine repo
> with a `pipeline.yml`, this skill still owns the local loop, with `trunk` set to the
> dev sandbox branch, `squash=merge`, and the environment branches in `protected`.
> See [references/init-guide.md](references/init-guide.md). On a DevOps Center repo,
> use [references/devops-center.md](references/devops-center.md); the managed
> `dx-devops-*` skills own work-item lifecycle, pipeline setup, and promotion.

---

## Sub-commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `/configure-salesforce-project init` | Detect → ask what cannot be inferred → write config → install hooks → seed the host instruction block → audit → emit the client-conversation checklist. Idempotent. Use `--platform claude`, `codex`, or `both` (default). [references/init-guide.md](references/init-guide.md) |
| `/configure-salesforce-project init --update` | Re-render everything after a skill upgrade, preserving the answers already recorded. |
| `/configure-salesforce-project audit` | Verify every installed piece is still armed. Read-only. `--fix` self-heals the mechanical items. [references/audit-guide.md](references/audit-guide.md) |
| `estate-ticket-status <TICKET>` | Read-only intake for an existing ticket. Reports matching Git work, the trunk landing commit, and clone-local validation/deploy evidence without treating absent local receipts as proof that work did not happen. [references/workflow-steps.md](references/workflow-steps.md) |
| `/configure-salesforce-project probe` | Find out what this project's tracker actually permits — types available, what automation can create, which required fields block it — and record it. Runs during init. [references/ticket-adapters.md](references/ticket-adapters.md) |
| `/configure-salesforce-project preflight` | Report which prerequisites are missing or unauthenticated, and walk the user through them one command at a time. Runs as phase 0 of init. [references/prerequisites.md](references/prerequisites.md) |
| `/configure-salesforce-project seed` | Org → empty repo, the one time the org is upstream. [references/seeding-guide.md](references/seeding-guide.md) |
| `/configure-salesforce-project uninstall` | The inverse of init: retract the Claude and Codex settings entries, remove `~/.estate`, clear the `estate.*` config and `core.hooksPath`, strip the exclude entries and managed instruction blocks, delete `.git/estate`. Removes only what init wrote; user-authored prose survives. `--machine-only` / `--repo` scope it. `scripts/uninstall.sh` |

Route on the argument: *setup / install / bootstrap / init / onboard* → init.
*audit / check / verify / armed / drift* → audit. *seed / baseline / retrieve /
forceignore / first commit* → seeding. *prerequisites / not installed / not authenticated /
command not found* → preflight. *uninstall / remove / rip out / tear down / deactivate* →
uninstall. Nothing else should reach this skill.

Seeding is also a phase **of** init. Running it standalone is for a repo that has the
stack but was never seeded — same guide, and it explains what the guards change about
the order.

---

## Before anything: prerequisites and the credentials rule

**Run `scripts/preflight.sh` before init.** It reports what is missing versus installed-but-
unauthenticated, with one command per gap. Some users will want help working through those
and others will not need any — read the output, offer the next command, take the lead from
them. Details: [references/prerequisites.md](references/prerequisites.md).

**Every auth step here is a browser or device flow. No token is ever typed, pasted, or
passed as an argument.** `gh auth login`, `sf org login web`. This is not a preference: never
accept a credential from a user, and never teach one to paste a secret into a chat window,
where it lands in a transcript. If a user offers you a token, decline and point at the
interactive command.

**Jira has no CLI in this stack.** All Jira work is done by the agent through the Atlassian
Rovo MCP — a connector explicitly authorized for the project in the current client, not on the command
line. A hook is a bash subprocess and cannot reach the session's MCP, so no hook does any Jira
network work; the agent does. See [references/ticket-adapters.md](references/ticket-adapters.md).

A corollary for the GitHub tracker CLI: **installed is not authenticated.** An expired OAuth
session leaves `gh` on `PATH` and every call failing, which looks exactly like a working
install. `preflight.sh` and `audit` report the auth state as its own thing.

---

## The three-layer model

The reason this skill is an installer rather than a workflow enforcer:

| Layer | Lives in | Job | Why it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Contract** | `CLAUDE.md` and/or `AGENTS.md` managed block (~60 lines) | The invariant, the step order, the rules | In context every session. No trigger to miss. |
| **Enforcement** | `~/.estate/` hooks + selected host settings | Walls and gates | Deterministic. Does not depend on any model reading anything. |
| **Reference** | this skill's `references/` | Setup, seeding, adapters, troubleshooting | Loaded rarely, on demand, by explicit path. |

Skill auto-triggering is probabilistic; a hook and a host instruction file are not. So the
hot path belongs to `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` and the walls belong to hooks. Putting the *whole*
skill in either file would be the anti-pattern — a 500-line instruction file degrades
adherence to everything in it, including the parts you were trying to make reliable.
Three guardrails keep the block from becoming that:

- **Size budget.** ~60 lines. Anything wanting more room goes in `references/` with a
  pointer from the block.
- **Hash fence.** The `BEGIN` marker carries a hash of the block's own body. A
  hand-edit inside the fence changes the body and not the hash.
- **Session-start self-check.** `verify-git-hooks.sh` re-hashes the block every
  session and reports a mismatch to the model. This is what makes *"an agent edited
  its own CLAUDE.md and deleted the enforcement rules"* self-announcing within one
  session instead of silently permanent.

Hooks are themselves a reliable context channel: `additionalContext` from a
SessionStart hook reaches the model deterministically, which no skill description can
promise.

---

## Two ownership modes

`estate.mode` is the master switch, and also the reason these hooks can be installed
machine-wide without affecting unrelated repos: **every hook exits 0 immediately in a
repo that has no `estate.mode`.**

| | `native` | `stealth` |
|---|---|---|
| Repo owner | Estate, or the client is fine with our tooling in-tree | The client. Nothing of ours gets committed. |
| Hooks | `~/.estate/`, armed via `core.hooksPath` | same |
| Host contract (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or both) | **committed** | untracked, in `.git/info/exclude`, symlinked into each worktree |
| Their husky / hooks | blocked (gate 1b) | **chained** — ours runs, then theirs |
| Prettier | their config, `--write` | `--check` only when they have no config |
| State/logs | `.git/estate/` | same |

The stealth rule of thumb, worth stating out loud to whoever is using this:
**govern your own behaviour silently; change their artifacts or their process only out loud.**
If a selected host contract is already tracked, `init` and `init --update` stop before
making any changes. Do not package the generated diff while the clone still declares
`stealth`; either leave the client's tracked file untouched or switch to `native`
deliberately before updating and committing the contract. Audit reports a tracked
managed-contract target in stealth as a failure.

---

## Configuration surface

Every per-repo decision is one `git config estate.*` key. Local git config is
invisible to the client (never tracked), shared automatically by every worktree of the
clone, readable from any hook in one call, and diffable by `audit`.

| Key | Values | Drives |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `native` \| `stealth` | artifact policy; **and the master gate** |
| `delivery` | `direct` \| `engine` \| `devops-center` | chooses the delivery invariant, managed contract, and hook behavior |
| `trunk` | branch name | direct/engine: org-synced branch; DevOps Center: topology-derived first landing branch |
| `host` | `github` \| `gitlab` \| `bitbucket` \| `azure` \| `none` | which merge surface the gate intercepts — [references/host-adapters.md](references/host-adapters.md) |
| `review` | `pr` \| `local` | hosted PR vs. the local review gate. `host=none` forces `local` |
| `ticket.system` | `github` \| `jira` \| `pattern` \| `none` | [references/ticket-adapters.md](references/ticket-adapters.md) |
| `ticket.project` | e.g. `SFO` | Jira project key — also narrows the ref pattern to *this* project's keys |
| `ticket.remote` | `ours` \| `client` | `client` turns **all** write automation off by default |
| `ticket.pattern` | regex | what `commit-msg` requires; defaults per system |
| `format` | `client` \| `check` \| `off` | prettier policy |
| `pmd` | `block` \| `advise` | PMD gate severity |
| `squash` | `require` \| `prefer` \| `merge` | hard in native; advisory in stealth when their repo policy differs. `merge` **inverts** it — merge commits required, `--squash`/`--rebase` refused — for a repo whose promotion model cherry-picks merge commits (`-m 1`) and reverts them (`-m 1`) |
| `protected` | space-separated branches | branches this clone may never merge **into**. Empty by default. Checked before the validate hatch, because "skip the dry run" is not "merge anywhere" |
| `sync` | `fetch` \| `off` | `fetch` (default) refreshes `origin/<trunk>` at session start and before every deploy, so a shared org + shared branch surfaces "you are behind" instead of a stale deploy. `off` = local-only, no session-start network. Never pulls/merges into the tree |
| `chainhooks` | path | the project's own hook dir, exec'd after ours |
| `drift` | `tracking` \| `off` | declares a source-tracked org; reconcile is reactive ([drift-reconcile.md](references/drift-reconcile.md)) |
| `qa` | `auto` \| `ask` \| `off` | acceptance-criteria QA at step 7: `ask` (offer, default), `auto` (run once deployed), `off`. The `estate-ac-qa` agent |
| `orgalias` | sf alias | local development org; only direct/engine require it to equal `trunk` |
| `devops.orgalias` | sf alias | the DevOps Center control org; required explicitly on `sf devops` commands |
| `devops.projectid` | record id | the connected DevOps Center project, rendered into the contract |
| `devops.pipelineid` | record id | pipeline whose linked stage topology owns the landing branch |
| `devops.branchpattern` | regex | WI branch shape; defaults to `^WI-[0-9]+$` |
| `devops.workmodel` | `isolated` \| `shared` | isolated uses the WI branch directly; shared adds a serialized development-integration branch |
| `devops.integrationbranch` | branch name | shared-org Git baseline; required only for `devops.workmodel=shared` |
| `devops.environment` | GitHub environment name | centralized successful-deployment receipt for the shared development org |
| `devops.developmentbranchpattern` | regex | shared development refs, with `^dev/WI-[0-9]+$` as the default |

---

## DevOps Center mode

Set `estate.delivery=devops-center` only in a repository dedicated to DevOps Center.
Do not combine it with a Deploy Engine `pipeline.yml` or its merge-tag assumptions.

Isolated development environments do not own Git branches. DevOps Center compares a development
environment to the first pipeline stage and gives each In Progress WI its own feature branch.
Init derives `trunk` from the unique first stage in the pipeline's `nextStageId` chain; a
pre-pipeline value is provisional and cannot pass a full audit.

The hot path is: DevOps Center WI -> In Progress -> existing `WI-######` branch -> linked
worktree -> scoped retrieve/build -> quality + dry run -> commit/push -> DevOps Center
review -> Ready to Promote. The agent does not merge the review or deploy a stage branch.
Use `manage-salesforce-devops` for WI state/review, `promote-salesforce-changes` for selective
promotion, and `dx-devops-pipeline-manage` for setup. Before promotion, inspect the installed
DevOps Center plugin version and the exact required commands and flags. Stop on missing or
obsolete capabilities. Full boundary, conflict recovery, and human/DX Inspector path:
[references/devops-center.md](references/devops-center.md).

Local hooks cannot observe a Salesforce or GitHub web UI action. Put company-required
quality gates in DevOps Testing or repository checks as well as local hooks.

For a deliberately shared, persistent development org, set `devops.workmodel=shared` and read the
shared development-org loop in [references/devops-center.md](references/devops-center.md). That
mode separates `dev/WI-######` development from the generated `WI-######` package, requires a
successful GitHub Deployment SHA as the cross-clone receipt, blocks local real deploys, and gates
the package against a durable scope ledger. A centralized receipt is required for safety, so the
current implementation supports GitHub only. The repository still owns the serialized landing
coordinator, its Salesforce authentication, test policy, branch protection, and verification.

---

## What is installed, and where

```
~/.estate/                       # once per machine; refreshed by init --update
  VERSION                          # audit compares this to the skill
  githooks/pre-commit, commit-msg  # armed per-clone via core.hooksPath
  claude-hooks/*.sh                # absolute paths in USER-level settings.json
  bin/estate-merge               # the local review gate (host=none)
  bin/estate-ticket-status       # read-only existing-ticket intake
  templates/                       # host instruction block, hook fragments, PMD ruleset, .forceignore

~/.claude/agents/estate-ac-qa.md # the acceptance-criteria QA agent (a capability, not a wall)
~/.claude/settings.json            # hook entries, jq-merged (no machine-wide deny rules)
~/.codex/hooks.json                # parallel Codex hook entries, jq-merged
<repo>/.git/estate/              # deploy-log, validate-log, hatch-log, approve-log,
                                   # drift-log, dod-state, pending-jobs
<repo>/.git/info/exclude           # per-clone gitignore (nothing added to theirs)
```

Three of these placements are load-bearing and worth understanding before changing:

**State inside `.git/`.** The predecessor kept logs at `<root>/.claude/.deploy-log`
and gitignored them. In a client repo that means either committing our bookkeeping to
their tree or editing their `.gitignore`. `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/estate/`
is untracked *by construction* — not in any working tree — while still being per-clone
(correct: these logs describe this clone's history against the org) and common across
worktrees (correct: a worktree's dry run must be visible to the merge gate).

**Hooks at user level, not in the repo.** A worktree agent can edit `.claude/hooks/` in
its own branch. It cannot edit `~/.estate/`. *"The repo must not disarm itself"*
becomes *"the repo cannot"*.

**`.git/info/exclude`, not `.gitignore`.** Same effect, but not a tracked file, so
stealth mode adds nothing to anything they will ever see.

---

## Key rules this stack enforces

| Rule | Why | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| Direct/engine: `trunk === org`; DevOps Center: service owns stage branches | prevents orphaned deploys and local pipeline bypass | delivery-specific contract + hooks |
| Shared DevOps Center: integration branch equals the latest successful development-org deployment SHA | prevents parallel agents from branching or validating against a Git baseline that is not true in Salesforce | `estate-devops-shared-status`, `guard-devops-shared.sh`, audit |
| Ticket first, in the project's own ref format | without it there is no path from an org change back to the reason for it | `commit-msg` |
| **Never a closing keyword or smart commit** | `fixes #42` closes the ticket at *merge* time, and this loop never closes a ticket on merge (tickets stay open — closure is prod/engine scope). In a client's repo it closes *their* #42 | `guard-closing-keywords.sh` + `commit-msg` |
| `force-app/` is worktree-only | editing it on trunk breaks the invariant before any deploy | `guard-force-app.sh`, `guard-force-app-bash.sh`, `pre-commit` gate 1 |
| Never nest worktrees | removing the outer one deletes the inner one's cwd; every later Bash call fails, including `cd /` | `guard-worktree-nesting.sh` |
| Validate before direct merge or DevOps review handoff | prevents unvalidated source from reaching its landing mechanism | `record-validate.sh`, `guard-pr-merge.sh`, `guard-devops-handoff.sh` |
| A human reviewed the diff | that is what a PR *is*; with no remote, `estate-merge` records it | `guard-pr-merge.sh` + `pre-commit` gate 1 carve-out |
| Deploy from clean trunk in direct mode; from a clean WI worktree in isolated DevOps Center; only through the central coordinator in shared mode | otherwise the target org holds source that cannot be identified and serialized in Git | `guard-sf-deploy.sh` |
| Shared DevOps Center packages contain exactly one accepted WI delta | prevents accumulated sandbox or overlapping component state from leaking into a later promotion | `estate-devops-package`, scope ledger, `guard-devops-handoff.sh` |
| Deploy only changed files; `RunSpecifiedTests` | whole-tree deploys hide what the ticket actually shipped | `guard-sf-deploy.sh` |
| `start --dry-run`, never `deploy validate` | `validate` is the prod quick-deploy path and rejects `NoTestRun` | `guard-sf-deploy.sh` |
| Never `--target-org` on local project commands; require the configured control org on `sf devops` | separates the development org from the DevOps Center API org | `guard-sf-flags.sh` |
| Never retrieve into the **main** tree | silently reverts anything deployed but not pulled back, with no diff anyone read; a linked worktree is allowed — its PR diff catches it | `guard-sf-flags.sh` (gated to managed repos; no machine-wide deny rule) |
| Ticket closure is out of the local loop | a sandbox deploy is not "done"; tickets stay open until production (the delivery system's domain). Close only if the user asks | the contract (no gate; deliberately removed) |
| Never write to a client's tracker unasked | automation editing their project management is not a feature | the contract + `auto-label-deploy.sh` note (`ticket.remote=client`) |
| Never fight the project's own hooks | re-arming ours while dropping theirs is the same sin, aimed at a client | `chainhooks` + `verify-git-hooks.sh` |
| Stage-sync commits gate the net WI delta relative to `MERGE_HEAD` | imported stage files are already promoted content, not new WI scope | merge-aware `pre-commit`; compatible chained lint-staged hooks receive the same diff base |
| `/simplify` before commit | AI quality gate for reuse, architecture, efficiency | **nothing — this one is on you** |
| Acceptance criteria met, judged against the UI | the code is not its own oracle — verifying behaviour from the source rationalises whatever the source does | judgment, aided by `estate-ac-qa` |
| User green light | nothing can check this for you | judgment |

These are deliberately unenforced. `/simplify` is a judgment call with no mechanical
signal — faking it with a marker file would be trivially gamed and would give false
confidence. "Acceptance criteria met" is the same shape: a gate on the *existence* of a
QA artifact would be satisfied by a rubber-stamp comment, so the QA pass is a **capability**
(`estate-ac-qa` — drives the org, screenshots each criterion, comments evidence to the
ticket), not a wall. It judges the AC from the running UI, never from the implementation.
Acceptance criteria are the user's, not the tooling's.

Full hook-by-hook detail, the exit-code contract, and the design rules:
[references/hooks/README.md](references/hooks/README.md).

---

## Escape hatches

Deliberate, **recorded**, never silent. Each appends `<utc> <kind> <sha> <detail>` to
`.git/estate/hatch-log` and emits a note.

`ALEY_ALLOW_UNVALIDATED_MERGE=1` · `ALEY_SKIP_DOD=1` · `ALEY_ALLOW_RETRIEVE=1` ·
`ALEY_ALLOW_UNVALIDATED_PUSH=1` (bitbucket only) · `git commit --no-verify` · the
`docs-only` / `no-deploy` ticket labels. The `SOLO_`/`SW_` prefixes from
the predecessor still work — a documented override that silently does nothing looks
like a broken gate, and gates that look broken get removed.

There is **no** hatch on the force-app-outside-a-worktree guards, and none on
`guard-closing-keywords.sh`. Those are walls, not gates.

None of them block. A hatch that argues with you is one people route around; the log is
what makes using one a decision on record.

**Scope, stated honestly:** `record-escape-hatch.sh` sees commands issued *through the
agent*. A `--no-verify` typed in a terminal or clicked in an IDE is invisible to it. Say
"hatches used through the agent are recorded", not "every commit is accounted for".

For a DevOps Center stage-sync merge, `--no-verify` is a last resort only when a chained
repository hook cannot safely consume the merge-aware diff base. Record the reason and retain
independent evidence for the net WI delta: file list against `MERGE_HEAD`, focused gates, the full
repository suite, and an exact-commit Salesforce dry run. See
[references/devops-center.md](references/devops-center.md).

---

## Org drift (`estate.drift`)

Reframes the Setup-click problem from prohibition to capture: **clicking in Setup is not
forbidden; unrecorded clicking is.**

The user's report is the primary trigger. The ticket-owning agent treats the named components as
candidates, verifies them through `SourceMember`, subtracts newer git and deploy activity, and
captures only the confirmed remainder into `tmp-retrieve` in the ticket worktree. A broad
SourceMember query is the fallback when the user cannot remember the component names.

This is reactive by design. There is no poller, scheduled job, cursor store, org-change inbox, or
automatic git writer. `SourceMember` identifies metadata; it does not prove author or intent.
Added and modified metadata are retrieved narrowly. An `IsNameObsolete` deletion is confirmed and
removed deliberately from source because a deleted component cannot be retrieved. The full path
lives in [references/drift-reconcile.md](references/drift-reconcile.md).

- **`tracking`** — the org is source-tracked (Dev/Dev Pro/scratch). Declares that the
  reconcile playbook applies here.
- **`off`** — default.

`audittrail` is **retired**. Building directly in a non-source-tracked org (partial/full copy,
production) is out of scope for this local loop. Pipeline-environment drift remains an
`operate-salesforce-pipeline` or DevOps Center concern. The local handoff begins once the reviewed change is
in source and ready for that delivery system.

---

## Related skills

- **`/simplify`** — the AI quality gate (step 3 of the contract).
- **`estate-ac-qa`** — the acceptance-criteria QA capability shipped with this stack
  (step 7). Verifies AC against the running UI, blind to the implementation; delegates
  browser mechanics to `capture-salesforce-screens` and posts its report as a ticket
  comment (GitHub via `gh`, Jira via the Rovo MCP with inline-image evidence),
  respecting `ticket.remote`. Claude installs it to `~/.claude/agents/`; Codex uses
  the shipped `references/agents/estate-ac-qa.md` as the delegated QA prompt.
- **`capture-requirements`** — how work is intaked: user story + Gherkin AC with a
  named persona. Those AC are what `estate-ac-qa` and step 7 measure against.
- **`capture-salesforce-screens`** — the headless browser driver `estate-ac-qa` calls
  to screenshot and assert against the org. The single source of truth for
  Salesforce UI waits and selectors. Wraps the `sfqa` CLI.
- **`github-issue-manager`** — creating and managing GitHub issues, when
  `ticket.system=github`.
- **`operate-salesforce-pipeline`** — everything from the PR into an environment branch upward:
  promotion, releases, rollback, freeze recovery. Do not bolt multi-environment
  concerns onto this skill; the invariant here stays one branch and one org, and on
  an engine-managed repo that branch is the dev sandbox. Run its `scripts/init.sh`
  to set `protected` from `pipeline.yml` rather than typing the branch list.
- **`manage-salesforce-devops`**: DevOps Center work-item state, generated WI branch,
  commit/push guidance, and review creation.
- **`promote-salesforce-changes`**: validate, prepare, selectively promote, and complete DevOps
  Center work-item promotion.
- **`dx-devops-pipeline-manage`**: pipeline, stage, environment, project, and activation
  management for the dedicated DevOps Center repository.
skills.html:
This skill puts Estate's delivery discipline onto a project and proves it is still there later. It is not the thing you read while implementing a feature — that contract lives in the project's CLAUDE.md (Claude) or AGENTS.md (Codex), where it is in context every session without anything having to trigger.

The direct-delivery invariant is trunk === the org. In DevOps Center mode the invariant becomes DevOps Center owns stage branches and promotion, while the local loop owns WI worktrees, scoped org capture, quality, validation, and review handoff.

Successor to the retired solo workflow. Same invariant, same worktree/validate/merge/
deploy discipline, re-architected for four realities the solo skill never faced:
the repo may belong to the client or not exist remotely at all; tickets may live in
Jira; the person using it is probably not the person who wrote it; and the skill is
not the delivery mechanism for the rules — CLAUDE.md is.
Not this skill: multi-environment promotion, pipelines, org-to-org sync. Those are
owned by operate-salesforce-pipeline or Salesforce DevOps Center. On an engine repo
with a pipeline.yml, this skill still owns the local loop, with trunk set to the
dev sandbox branch, squash=merge, and the environment branches in protected.
See references/init-guide.md (references/init-guide.md). On a DevOps Center repo,
use references/devops-center.md (references/devops-center.md); the managed
dx-devops-* skills own work-item lifecycle, pipeline setup, and promotion.

---

Sub-commands

CommandDoes
/configure-salesforce-project initDetect → ask what cannot be inferred → write config → install hooks → seed the host instruction block → audit → emit the client-conversation checklist. Idempotent. Use --platform claude, codex, or both (default). references/init-guide.md (references/init-guide.md)
/configure-salesforce-project init --updateRe-render everything after a skill upgrade, preserving the answers already recorded.
/configure-salesforce-project auditVerify every installed piece is still armed. Read-only. --fix self-heals the mechanical items. references/audit-guide.md (references/audit-guide.md)
estate-ticket-status <TICKET>Read-only intake for an existing ticket. Reports matching Git work, the trunk landing commit, and clone-local validation/deploy evidence without treating absent local receipts as proof that work did not happen. references/workflow-steps.md (references/workflow-steps.md)
/configure-salesforce-project probeFind out what this project's tracker actually permits — types available, what automation can create, which required fields block it — and record it. Runs during init. references/ticket-adapters.md (references/ticket-adapters.md)
/configure-salesforce-project preflightReport which prerequisites are missing or unauthenticated, and walk the user through them one command at a time. Runs as phase 0 of init. references/prerequisites.md (references/prerequisites.md)
/configure-salesforce-project seedOrg → empty repo, the one time the org is upstream. references/seeding-guide.md (references/seeding-guide.md)
/configure-salesforce-project uninstallThe inverse of init: retract the Claude and Codex settings entries, remove ~/.estate, clear the estate.* config and core.hooksPath, strip the exclude entries and managed instruction blocks, delete .git/estate. Removes only what init wrote; user-authored prose survives. --machine-only / --repo scope it. scripts/uninstall.sh

Route on the argument: *setup / install / bootstrap / init / onboard* → init. *audit / check / verify / armed / drift* → audit. *seed / baseline / retrieve / forceignore / first commit* → seeding. *prerequisites / not installed / not authenticated / command not found* → preflight. *uninstall / remove / rip out / tear down / deactivate* → uninstall. Nothing else should reach this skill.

Seeding is also a phase of init. Running it standalone is for a repo that has the stack but was never seeded — same guide, and it explains what the guards change about the order.

---

Before anything: prerequisites and the credentials rule

Run scripts/preflight.sh before init. It reports what is missing versus installed-but- unauthenticated, with one command per gap. Some users will want help working through those and others will not need any — read the output, offer the next command, take the lead from them. Details: references/prerequisites.md (references/prerequisites.md).

Every auth step here is a browser or device flow. No token is ever typed, pasted, or passed as an argument. gh auth login, sf org login web. This is not a preference: never accept a credential from a user, and never teach one to paste a secret into a chat window, where it lands in a transcript. If a user offers you a token, decline and point at the interactive command.

Jira has no CLI in this stack. All Jira work is done by the agent through the Atlassian Rovo MCP — a connector explicitly authorized for the project in the current client, not on the command line. A hook is a bash subprocess and cannot reach the session's MCP, so no hook does any Jira network work; the agent does. See references/ticket-adapters.md (references/ticket-adapters.md).

A corollary for the GitHub tracker CLI: installed is not authenticated. An expired OAuth session leaves gh on PATH and every call failing, which looks exactly like a working install. preflight.sh and audit report the auth state as its own thing.

---

The three-layer model

The reason this skill is an installer rather than a workflow enforcer:

LayerLives inJobWhy it holds
ContractCLAUDE.md and/or AGENTS.md managed block (~60 lines)The invariant, the step order, the rulesIn context every session. No trigger to miss.
Enforcement~/.estate/ hooks + selected host settingsWalls and gatesDeterministic. Does not depend on any model reading anything.
Referencethis skill's references/Setup, seeding, adapters, troubleshootingLoaded rarely, on demand, by explicit path.

Skill auto-triggering is probabilistic; a hook and a host instruction file are not. So the hot path belongs to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and the walls belong to hooks. Putting the *whole* skill in either file would be the anti-pattern — a 500-line instruction file degrades adherence to everything in it, including the parts you were trying to make reliable. Three guardrails keep the block from becoming that:

  • Size budget. ~60 lines. Anything wanting more room goes in references/ with a

pointer from the block.

  • Hash fence. The BEGIN marker carries a hash of the block's own body. A

hand-edit inside the fence changes the body and not the hash.

  • Session-start self-check. verify-git-hooks.sh re-hashes the block every

session and reports a mismatch to the model. This is what makes *"an agent edited its own CLAUDE.md and deleted the enforcement rules"* self-announcing within one session instead of silently permanent.

Hooks are themselves a reliable context channel: additionalContext from a SessionStart hook reaches the model deterministically, which no skill description can promise.

---

Two ownership modes

estate.mode is the master switch, and also the reason these hooks can be installed machine-wide without affecting unrelated repos: every hook exits 0 immediately in a repo that has no estate.mode.

nativestealth
Repo ownerEstate, or the client is fine with our tooling in-treeThe client. Nothing of ours gets committed.
Hooks~/.estate/, armed via core.hooksPathsame
Host contract (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or both)committeduntracked, in .git/info/exclude, symlinked into each worktree
Their husky / hooksblocked (gate 1b)chained — ours runs, then theirs
Prettiertheir config, --write--check only when they have no config

The stealth rule of thumb, worth stating out loud to whoever is using this: govern your own behaviour silently; change their artifacts or their process only out loud. If a selected host contract is already tracked, init and init --update stop before making any changes. Do not package the generated diff while the clone still declares stealth; either leave the client's tracked file untouched or switch to native deliberately before updating and committing the contract. Audit reports a tracked managed-contract target in stealth as a failure.

---

---

DevOps Center mode

Set estate.delivery=devops-center only in a repository dedicated to DevOps Center. Do not combine it with a Deploy Engine pipeline.yml or its merge-tag assumptions.

Isolated development environments do not own Git branches. DevOps Center compares a development environment to the first pipeline stage and gives each In Progress WI its own feature branch. Init derives trunk from the unique first stage in the pipeline's nextStageId chain; a pre-pipeline value is provisional and cannot pass a full audit.

The hot path is: DevOps Center WI -> In Progress -> existing WI-###### branch -> linked worktree -> scoped retrieve/build -> quality + dry run -> commit/push -> DevOps Center review -> Ready to Promote. The agent does not merge the review or deploy a stage branch. Use manage-salesforce-devops for WI state/review, promote-salesforce-changes for selective promotion, and dx-devops-pipeline-manage for setup. Before promotion, inspect the installed DevOps Center plugin version and the exact required commands and flags. Stop on missing or obsolete capabilities. Full boundary, conflict recovery, and human/DX Inspector path: references/devops-center.md (references/devops-center.md).

Local hooks cannot observe a Salesforce or GitHub web UI action. Put company-required quality gates in DevOps Testing or repository checks as well as local hooks.

For a deliberately shared, persistent development org, set devops.workmodel=shared and read the shared development-org loop in references/devops-center.md (references/devops-center.md). That mode separates dev/WI-###### development from the generated WI-###### package, requires a successful GitHub Deployment SHA as the cross-clone receipt, blocks local real deploys, and gates the package against a durable scope ledger. A centralized receipt is required for safety, so the current implementation supports GitHub only. The repository still owns the serialized landing coordinator, its Salesforce authentication, test policy, branch protection, and verification.

Three of these placements are load-bearing and worth understanding before changing:

State inside .git/. The predecessor kept logs at <root>/.claude/.deploy-log and gitignored them. In a client repo that means either committing our bookkeeping to their tree or editing their .gitignore. $(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/estate/ is untracked *by construction* — not in any working tree — while still being per-clone (correct: these logs describe this clone's history against the org) and common across worktrees (correct: a worktree's dry run must be visible to the merge gate).

Hooks at user level, not in the repo. A worktree agent can edit .claude/hooks/ in its own branch. It cannot edit ~/.estate/. *"The repo must not disarm itself"* becomes *"the repo cannot"*.

.git/info/exclude, not .gitignore. Same effect, but not a tracked file, so stealth mode adds nothing to anything they will ever see.

skills.excerptHtml:
This skill puts Estate's delivery discipline onto a project and proves it is still there later. It is not the thing you read while implementing a feature — that contract lives in the project's CLAUDE.md (Claude) or AGENTS.md (Codex), where it is in context every session without anything having to trigger.

The direct-delivery invariant is trunk === the org. In DevOps Center mode the invariant becomes DevOps Center owns stage branches and promotion, while the local loop owns WI worktrees, scoped org capture, quality, validation, and review handoff.

Successor to the retired solo workflow. Same invariant, same worktree/validate/merge/
deploy discipline, re-architected for four realities the solo skill never faced:
the repo may belong to the client or not exist remotely at all; tickets may live in
Jira; the person using it is probably not the person who wrote it; and the skill is
not the delivery mechanism for the rules — CLAUDE.md is.
Not this skill: multi-environment promotion, pipelines, org-to-org sync. Those are
owned by operate-salesforce-pipeline or Salesforce DevOps Center. On an engine repo
with a pipeline.yml, this skill still owns the local loop, with trunk set to the
dev sandbox branch, squash=merge, and the environment branches in protected.
See references/init-guide.md (references/init-guide.md). On a DevOps Center repo,
use references/devops-center.md (references/devops-center.md); the managed
dx-devops-* skills own work-item lifecycle, pipeline setup, and promotion.

examples.title: Audit Salesforce delivery hooks after a husky pull
examples.markdown:
## Request

I pulled the latest develop on our Northgate Freight Salesforce repo yesterday (it touched package.json) and since then my commit with "Fixes NGF-212" went through with no complaints. Can you audit whether the delivery standards are still armed here and tell me what to fix? The state I captured is in inputs/.

## Inputs

**Dry run.** This skill normally works on live systems or its owner's own setup. Here the system state is invented in the inputs below, and nothing was changed anywhere. Run of the built `configure-salesforce-project` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### claude-md-diff.txt

Managed block in CLAUDE.md (left = file, right = rendered from config)
BEGIN estate-managed hash=4be1a07c

  line 14   - Commit messages start with an NGF-### ref.
  line 15   - Never write a closing keyword (fixes, closes, resolves) in a commit message.   <- present only on the right
  line 15   + Keep commit messages short.                                                    <- present only on the left
  line 22   - Run /simplify before every commit.
  line 23   - Run `sf project deploy start --dry-run` before opening a PR.

Body hash of file as it stands: 91d03ac2 (recorded: 4be1a07c)
Note: CLAUDE.md is tracked in the client's repo (first added in commit 0b6e2f1 by someone at the client).

#### repo-state.txt

$ cd ~/work/ngf-sfdc && git config --local --get-regexp '^(estate|core\.hooksPath)'
core.hookspath .husky/_
estate.mode stealth
estate.delivery direct
estate.trunk develop
estate.host github
estate.review pr
estate.ticket.system jira
estate.ticket.project NGF
estate.ticket.remote client
estate.format check
estate.pmd advise
estate.squash prefer
estate.sync fetch
estate.chainhooks /Users/dana/work/ngf-sfdc/.husky/_
estate.drift tracking
estate.claudemd.hash 4be1a07c
(no estate.orgalias)

$ git log -3 --format='%h %s'
c91d0e2 Fixes NGF-212 route-optimiser timeout in FreightQuoteService
a7740b3 Merge pull request #88 from ngf/NGF-198
5e12f44 NGF-198 add carrier rate Flow

$ git diff HEAD~12 HEAD --stat -- package.json
 package.json | 3 +++   (adds "husky": "^9.0.0" and "prepare": "husky")

$ ls -l ~/.estate/githooks
-rwxr-xr-x  pre-commit
-rw-r--r--  commit-msg

$ cat ~/.estate/VERSION        -> 2.3.0
$ skill version                -> 2.5.0

$ ls .git/hooks | grep -v sample   -> (empty)
$ ls -ld .git/estate .git/info/exclude -> .git/estate is missing; exclude exists, contains CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md

$ git ls-files CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md

$ jq -r '.hooks|to_entries[]|.key+": "+(.value[].hooks[].command)' ~/.claude/settings.json | grep estate
PreToolUse: ~/.estate/claude-hooks/guard-force-app.sh
PreToolUse: ~/.estate/claude-hooks/guard-force-app-bash.sh
PreToolUse: ~/.estate/claude-hooks/guard-closing-keywords.sh
PreToolUse: ~/.estate/claude-hooks/guard-sf-deploy.sh
PreToolUse: ~/.estate/claude-hooks/guard-sf-flags.sh
PreToolUse: ~/.estate/claude-hooks/guard-pr-merge.sh
SessionStart: ~/.estate/claude-hooks/verify-git-hooks.sh
(no guard-worktree-nesting.sh, record-validate.sh, record-escape-hatch.sh, stop-dod-check.sh)
$ ls ~/.estate/claude-hooks | wc -l -> 14 scripts present, all executable
$ jq '.permissions.deny' ~/.claude/settings.json -> ["Bash(sf project retrieve*)"]

$ git worktree list
/Users/dana/work/ngf-sfdc            c91d0e2 [develop]
/Users/dana/work/ngf-sfdc-NGF-231    3f8a1b9 [NGF-231]
$ ls /Users/dana/work/ngf-sfdc-NGF-231 | grep -E 'CLAUDE|AGENTS'  -> (none)

$ sf org display -o ngf-dev  -> Connected Status: Connected
$ gh auth status             -> github.com: The token in keyring is invalid. (X) Failed to log in

## Output

### Audit: Northgate Freight Salesforce repo

**The standards are not armed.** Your `Fixes NGF-212` commit went through because git never ran our `commit-msg` hook. The cause is the husky install that arrived with your pull, and three other things are broken as well. I read the state you captured and did not run `scripts/audit.sh`, so I applied its documented checks by hand. This is a read-only audit and nothing has been changed.

#### Why the commit slipped through

1. **`core.hooksPath` was repointed.** It is now `.husky/_`, where it should be `~/.estate/githooks`. The pull added `"prepare": "husky"` to `package.json`, and husky sets `core.hooksPath` when it runs. Git now looks only in husky's directory, so neither of our hooks runs.
2. **`commit-msg` has lost its exec bit.** It is `-rw-r--r--` in `~/.estate/githooks`. Even with `hooksPath` fixed, git would skip it silently. This is the hook that rejects closing keywords and requires an `NGF-###` ref.
3. **The Claude-side backstop has gaps.** `guard-closing-keywords.sh` is registered in `settings.json`, so a commit made through the agent should have been caught. Your capture doesn't show how `c91d0e2` was made, so I can't say whether that guard missed it or the commit came from a terminal. A terminal commit would only have been caught by `commit-msg`.

`Fixes NGF-212` is a closing keyword. In a Jira project it can be read as a smart commit. Closing tickets is outside this loop, and the ticket is the client's (`ticket.remote=client`).

#### Results by check

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `estate.*` complete and coherent | **FAIL.** `estate.orgalias` is unset, so `sf` commands in a fresh worktree use the machine's global default org. Everything else is coherent. Jira with project `NGF` narrows the ref pattern correctly. |
| 2 | `core.hooksPath` and git hooks | **FAIL.** Repointed to `.husky/_`. `commit-msg` is not executable. `pre-commit` is fine. No stale copies in `.git/hooks/`. |
| 3 | `chainhooks` target | **Pass, with a caution.** It points to `.husky/_`, which is correct. Once `hooksPath` is restored, our hooks run first and then call husky's. |
| 4 | Claude hook entries and scripts | **FAIL.** `guard-worktree-nesting`, `record-validate`, `record-escape-hatch` and `stop-dod-check` are missing from `settings.json`. All 14 scripts exist and are executable. A machine-wide `Bash(sf project retrieve*)` deny rule is still present. It fires in every repo on your machine, including unrelated ones, and retrieve-blocking now lives in the gated `guard-sf-flags.sh`. |
| 5 | `~/.estate/VERSION` against the skill | **FAIL.** The install is 2.3.0 and the skill is 2.5.0. |
| 6 | `CLAUDE.md` managed block | **FAIL, and not fixable by `--fix`.** See below. |
| 7 | State dir and exclude entries | **FAIL.** `.git/estate/` does not exist, so no validate or deploy can be recorded and the merge gate would block everything. The `.git/info/exclude` entries are present. |
| 8 | Contract in each worktree | **FAIL.** `ngf-sfdc-NGF-231` has no `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`. An agent working there has no contract in context. |
| 9 | `ngf-dev` resolves | Pass. Status is Connected. |
| 10 | Tracker CLI auth | **Attention.** `gh` is installed but its token is invalid. `host=github` and `review=pr` depend on it. Jira runs agent-side through the Atlassian Rovo MCP, so there is nothing to check from a shell. |
| 11 | Client checklist | Unknown. `.git/estate/client-checklist` can't exist without the state dir. |

#### The `CLAUDE.md` problem needs your decision

Two things are wrong, and they affect each other.

- **The block was edited.** The hash on the file is `91d03ac2` and the recorded one is `4be1a07c`. The rule "never write a closing keyword" has been replaced by "Keep commit messages short." The cause is unknown. It could be an agent, a person at the client, or you. I can't tell, so I won't re-render over it, and neither will `--fix`.
- **The file is tracked by the client's repo.** `CLAUDE.md` was added in `0b6e2f1` by someone at the client. Your clone is `stealth`, which promises that nothing of ours goes into their tree. `.git/info/exclude` does not untrack a file that is already tracked. Re-rendering the block would modify the client's file, and this fails the stealth rule. `init --update` will stop here for the same reason.

You have two options:

- **Stay in stealth (my recommendation, since the client owns the repo).** Leave their `CLAUDE.md` alone and restore any local edit to it with `git checkout -- CLAUDE.md`. The contract then has no managed home in this clone. The hooks remain the enforcement layer, and the closing-keyword rule is enforced by `commit-msg` and `guard-closing-keywords.sh` whether or not the prose is there.
- **Switch to `native`.** Do this only if the client agrees to carry our tooling in-tree. You would run `git config estate.mode native`, then `scripts/install.sh --block`, and commit the contract deliberately.

If someone added a line worth keeping, move it outside the `BEGIN`/`END` markers before any re-render. Don't edit the hash.

#### Fix order

1. **Decide the ownership question above first.** It determines whether the block and the update can proceed.
2. **Run `scripts/audit.sh --fix`.** It should handle the mechanical items: restore `core.hooksPath` to `~/.estate/githooks`, restore the exec bit on `commit-msg`, add the four missing Claude hook entries, retract the stray retrieve deny rule, and create `.git/estate/`.
3. **Run `init --update`.** This brings 2.3.0 up to 2.5.0 and preserves your recorded answers. It will refuse while the tracked-contract conflict stands.
4. **Set the org alias.** Run `git config estate.orgalias ngf-dev`. I'm assuming `ngf-dev` is the org that `develop` syncs to. I couldn't confirm that from the evidence, so correct me if the alias is different.
5. **Re-authenticate GitHub.** Run `gh auth login` and use the browser flow. Never paste a token into a chat or a command.
6. **Re-run `scripts/audit.sh`.** Checks 1 to 8 should pass. Check 6 will still need the decision above.

#### Why the fix may not stick

husky's `prepare` script runs on every `npm install` and will repoint `hooksPath` again. `verify-git-hooks.sh` re-arms it at the start of each Claude session, but a terminal commit straight after an install is exposed. Run the audit after any pull that touches `package.json`. That is what happened this time.

#### The commit already made

`c91d0e2` has a closing keyword in its message. I can't see whether it was pushed. If it is still local, reword it to `NGF-212 route-optimiser timeout in FreightQuoteService` with `git commit --amend` after step 2, so `commit-msg` checks the new message. I haven't done this because it rewrites history. If the commit has been pushed or merged, leave it. Rewriting shared history would be worse. In that case, check in Jira whether NGF-212 was transitioned and reopen it if so. On a client-owned tracker, that is your call to make, not something I should do.

#### What I couldn't check

- Whether `AGENTS.md` exists. It's excluded and untracked, and your capture only listed tracked files.
- How `c91d0e2` was created.
- Whether the Jira connector is authorised in this client.
- Who edited `CLAUDE.md`.

skills.markdown:
---
name: deliver-salesforce-change
description: Prepare, check, and deliver changes to a single-org Salesforce project using isolated Git worktrees, generated permissions, local quality checks, and explicit org identity checks. Supports local preparation without an org. Use sf-deploy-engine for multi-environment promotion.
canon_exempt: 'engineering-doc'
canon_exempt_reason: 'setup, workflow and troubleshooting contracts an agent needs before touching a deploy'
---


# Deliver salesforce change

Use this workflow for a solo Salesforce project: prepare the change in a worktree, check its local outputs, validate against a confirmed org when available, merge the reviewed commit, deploy it, and verify the requested behavior. Claude Code and Codex can both use the workflow and Python tools. Claude-specific hooks only apply where installed and tested in Claude Code; their presence does not establish enforcement in Codex.

## Work without an org

No org is required to inspect the source, implement a change, generate a permission-set preview, run local checks, or prepare a reviewable PR. Do not select an existing CLI alias as a substitute for a user-confirmed test target. Do not run a deployment, dry run, retrieve, Apex test, or data query without that target.

1. Read the project requirements and inspect its SFDX package directories. Preserve current files and use a worktree for changes.
2. Run the project's installed local checks. Record missing tools and repair the local toolchain where authorized; a skipped check is not a pass.
3. Generate the permission set from source with [gen-permset.py](references/tools/gen-permset.py). `--init` creates the configuration; `--out /tmp/new-preview.xml` creates a new preview outside project trees; `--fail-on-drift` checks committed output; `--write` requires a verified worktree.
4. Review the generated XML and the changed metadata against the requested behavior. Retain the inputs, preview, local test results, and failed attempts.
5. Save a deployment handoff listing the exact commit, source files, proposed tests, and outstanding target requirement. Report **prepared locally**. Do not record a Salesforce validation or deployment success.

When an org becomes available, use [verify-salesforce-org](../verify-salesforce-org/SKILL.md) to compare its actual ID with the intended ID, then use that same explicit `--target-org` on subsequent CLI operations. Never copy a default alias into a worktree automatically. Identity verification and authorization for a write are separate requirements.

---

## Sub-commands

- **`/deliver-salesforce-change`** (no args) — Enforce the workflow during an implementation task. This is the default.
- **`/deliver-salesforce-change setup`** — Bootstrap a project with the full enforcement stack: git hooks, Claude hooks, Claude settings, and the workflow section for CLAUDE.md. See [references/setup-guide.md](references/setup-guide.md).
- **`/deliver-salesforce-change seed`** — Get an existing org's metadata into an empty repo for the first time: `.forceignore`, a manifest generated from the org and pruned, the retrieve, a tree prune, and a round-trip check. See [references/seeding-guide.md](references/seeding-guide.md).

If the argument contains "setup", "install", "bootstrap", or "init", follow the setup guide. If it contains "seed", "retrieve", "baseline", or "import", follow the seeding guide. Otherwise, enforce the workflow below.

Seeding is also Phase 2f *of* setup. Running it as its own sub-command is for the case where the stack is already installed and the repo was never seeded — same guide, and it will tell you what the guards change about the sequence.

---

## When This Skill Applies

Any task that will result in changes to `force-app/` (Apex, LWC, metadata, permissions, flows, objects, etc.) on a solo-developer, single-org Salesforce project. This includes:

- New feature implementation
- Bug fixes
- Metadata changes (objects, fields, permission sets, flows, flexipages)
- Refactoring existing code
- Any work that will ultimately be deployed to the org

Docs-only changes do not need deployment checks. Follow the repository’s normal branch and review rules.

**Does NOT apply to:** projects with a `pipeline.yml` or more than one environment branch. That's `operate-salesforce-pipeline` territory — this skill has no concept of promotion, staging, or an orchestration engine.

---

## The Invariant

The desired deployment state is that the managed metadata in the org matches the recorded release commit on `main`. A Git merge or local log cannot prove that state. Preserve the deployment result and acceptance evidence; report divergence when a deployment fails or remains pending.

```
worktree → PR (squash) → main → deploy → org
```

Every implementation task follows this sequence. Each step gates the next. Do not skip steps, do not reorder.

### Step 1 — Ticket First

Before writing any code, create or identify a GitHub issue.

- Use `work-in-github-repository` or the available GitHub CLI to search for existing issues
- Create a new issue if none exists
- Note the issue number — every branch and commit references it

**Why:** issues are the audit trail. Without a ticket there is no record of what was done or why.

### Step 2 — Work in a Worktree

All development happens in an isolated git worktree. Never commit deployable code directly to `main`.

- Use an available managed worktree tool or `git worktree add`. A runtime-specific Agent tool is optional.
- Branch naming: `feat/N-short-description` or `fix/N-short-description` (where N is the issue number)
- Worktrees branch from `main`
- Worktrees do not inherit `.sf/` configuration. Pass the confirmed org explicitly for org operations. `ensure-worktree-config.sh` can link local Node dependencies; it does not copy or set an org.

**CRITICAL — No nested worktrees:** An agent spawned with `isolation: "worktree"` is already isolated. It works directly in that worktree — branch, change, commit — and must NEVER create another worktree inside it. Nesting is unrecoverable: when the outer worktree is removed, the Bash tool's CWD points at a deleted directory and every subsequent shell command fails permanently, including `cd /`.

**Bash inside a worktree-isolated agent is sandboxed by the harness.** It refuses anything it cannot prove stays inside the worktree — `&&`/`;` chains, `cd … && for …`, and `<<'EOF'` heredocs (read as redirects):

> `…is too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree; break it into plain, separate commands`

That is **Claude Code, not this project's hooks** — there is nothing to find in `.claude/hooks/`, and it is **not** a stop-and-report condition. Split into plain commands, or write a script to the scratchpad and run it by path.

**If you are already in a worktree**, do NOT call `Agent` with `isolation: "worktree"` or run `git worktree add`. Just work where you are. The check — one plain command, because inside a worktree-isolated agent the harness refuses compound ones:

```bash
git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir
```
Read the answer off the path: `…/<repo>/.git` is the main checkout, `…/<repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>` is a worktree. This is the same topology the hooks use, so it cannot disagree with them.


Do not test this by looking for `.claude/worktrees/` in the path. A worktree created anywhere else (`git worktree add ../myproject-42`) is just as much a worktree, and the guards honour it.

**For rapid iteration and follow-up fixes** it is fine to leave a worktree open and continue to issue PRs. It is NOT ok to shift to editing `main` or its local files.

Read [references/workflow-steps.md](references/workflow-steps.md) for the exact command sequences.

### Step 3 — Quality Gates

#### 3a — Prettier, ESLint, PMD, Jest

When installed and configured, the reference `pre-commit` hook runs the applicable checks against staged files. Verify the hook and toolchain before relying on that enforcement. Run them early if you want faster feedback:

```bash
npm run pmd      # or: pmd check -d force-app/main/default/classes \
                 #       -R category/apex/bestpractices.xml,category/apex/security.xml,\
                 #          category/apex/design.xml,category/apex/errorprone.xml -f text
npm run lint
npm test
```

But the commit is the gate. A violation blocks it; prettier fixes and re-stages formatting for you.

#### 3b — /simplify

Use `simplify-code`, an available equivalent, or a direct code review before committing. This is the AI quality gate — it reviews for code reuse, efficiency, separation of concerns, and Salesforce best practices. Fix all issues found. Skip only for trivial metadata-only changes (single field, label update).

**This is the one quality gate no hook can enforce** — a judgment step with no mechanical signal, so it stays on you.

#### 3c — Commit

`refs #N` for in-progress commits, `fixes #N` on the final squash merge. The keyword is required, not decorative: `commit-msg` rejects a bare `#N`, because everything downstream (labelling, close permission, DoD checks) reads these refs out of commit messages, and a bare-`#N` scan picks issue numbers out of ordinary prose.

### Step 4 — Validate, Merge, Deploy (atomic sequence — do not reorder)

This sequence applies once an org is confirmed and the deployment is authorized. Without an org, complete the local preparation path above and retain the pending deployment handoff.

**From the worktree**, when the feature is ready:

1. **Jest and PMD** — retain the actual results for the changed commit. A commit alone does not prove hooks ran or checks passed.
2. **Identify Apex tests** — For each changed Apex class, include its `*Test` counterpart. For trigger/handler changes, cast a wider net. List classes explicitly.
3. **Validate against the org** (dry run — org unchanged, this is the merge gate):
   ```bash
   sf project deploy start --dry-run --target-org CONFIRMED_ORG --json \
     --source-dir force-app/main/default/classes/ChangedClass.cls \
     --source-dir force-app/main/default/classes/ChangedClassTest.cls \
     --test-level RunSpecifiedTests --tests TestA TestB TestC
   ```
   Deploy only changed files — never `--source-dir force-app` (the whole directory). This is hook-enforced.
   If validate fails, iterate in the worktree. Do not merge.

   A successful dry run is recorded against the current commit. **Commit first, then validate** — the merge gate is per-commit, so validating and then pushing another commit means re-validating.

   Use `start --dry-run` for a development-org check. For an authorized production validation and quick-deploy workflow, use the supported `validate` and `quick` commands with the required tests. See [Salesforce CLI deployment documentation](https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-deploy-retrieve).
4. **Create and squash merge the PR** to `main`:
   ```bash
   gh pr create --base main --title "feat: description (fixes #N)" --body "..."
   gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch
   ```
   Squash-only, and only with a recorded validate for the head commit — both hook-enforced.
5. **Deploy from `main`** (real deploy to the org):
   ```bash
   git checkout main && git pull
   sf project deploy start --target-org CONFIRMED_ORG --json \
     --source-dir force-app/main/default/classes/ChangedClass.cls \
     --source-dir force-app/main/default/classes/ChangedClassTest.cls \
     --test-level RunSpecifiedTests --tests TestA TestB TestC
   ```
   The `git pull` is not optional: the deploy guard blocks a `main` that is behind origin (you would ship an older tree than you merged), ahead of it (unpushed code reaching the org), or dirty.
6. **User tests** — hard-refresh browser, verify against acceptance criteria.
7. **Clean up worktree**: `git worktree remove <path>`

**Use the confirmed explicit `--target-org` on org operations.** Run `verify-salesforce-org` first. An alias by itself is not an identity check, and a machine default is not a confirmed project target.

**Test selection guidance:**

Choose tests from the changed behavior, its callers, the target org, and the project's release policy. `RunSpecifiedTests` can provide focused feedback; use `RunLocalTests` or `RunAllTestsInOrg` when broader coverage is required. Do not prohibit those levels to save time. Locate related Apex tests with `rg`, inspect their assertions, and retain the results.

`NoTestRun` is for supported development environments. Do not infer permission to skip production tests from a label such as “metadata-only.” Check the installed command's help and [Salesforce's test-level reference](https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-deploy-retrieve/blob/main/messages/deploy.metadata.md).

**If deployment fails:** preserve the result, job ID, release SHA, target ID, and actual org state. Choose fix-forward or a reviewed rollback using those facts. A Git revert does not undo an org mutation, and some metadata or data changes need a separate recovery procedure. Do not push a speculative revert or claim parity restored without verifying the subsequent result.

### Step 5 — Definition of Done (mandatory — do not skip)

For a task whose requested finish line includes deployment, completion requires all of these. For an offline preparation task, use the local handoff criteria above:

1. **Deployed to the org** — `sf project deploy start` succeeded (not just validate)
2. **In git and GitHub** — PR squash-merged to `main`, pushed to origin
3. **Acceptance criteria met** — every criterion from the GitHub issue is satisfied
4. **User gives green light** on all changes (they may want to do manual testing, etc.)
5. **Ticket updated and closed** — summary of what shipped, commit SHA or PR link, then `gh issue close N`
6. **Worktree cleaned up** — `git worktree remove <path>` and local branch deleted

**Common agent failures:** deploying but never closing the ticket. Closing the ticket but never removing the worktree. Reporting "done" after validate but before deploy. All of these are incomplete. `stop-dod-check.sh` refuses to end a turn with `main` ahead of the org or a deployed ticket still open — but items 3 and 4 are still yours to confirm.

**Keeping a worktree open across a deploy is expected, not a failure.** Same tree, same ticket, follow-up fixes as another PR — the workflow is built for it and no hook nags about it. Cleanup (item 6) is due when the **ticket** closes, not after every deploy. Two things when reusing a branch after its squash merge:

- **Sync it first:** `git merge main` after preserving and reviewing any local changes. The squash put your content on `main` under a commit the branch has never seen, so without this the next PR's diff re-shows all the original work.
- **Re-validate.** The merge gate is per-commit: a new commit needs its own dry run before `gh pr merge` will allow it.

---

## Seeding an Existing Org — the one time the org is upstream

Every rule above assumes the repo is the source of truth and the org is downstream
of it. Exactly once per project, that is backwards: an org already exists, the repo
is empty, and the metadata has to come **out** of the org to establish the baseline
the invariant is measured against.

Full procedure in [references/seeding-guide.md](references/seeding-guide.md). What
belongs in your head:

**Seed before installing the enforcement stack, not after.** The stack blocks
`sf project retrieve` at two layers, correctly, and the repo being empty is the only
window in which a retrieve cannot clobber anything. Seeding is Phase 2f of setup for
that reason.

**Sanitize at the manifest, not on disk.** `sf project generate manifest --from-org`
with `--excluded-metadata` filters before the retrieve, so the pass is one file of a
few hundred lines rather than a few thousand files. It also excludes managed and
unlocked package metadata by default, which removes the namespace sweep entirely.

**Exclude by reason class, not from a list.** Lists rot and teach nothing. Five
classes cover it: *not authored* (reports, dashboards, documents — users keep making
more), *not portable* (Connected Apps, External Client Apps, certificates — secrets
do not retrieve, so what deploys is a shell that fails silently), *not yours*
(package metadata), *superseded* (`FlowDefinition`, `CleanDataService`, `AppMenu`),
and *governed elsewhere*.

**Profiles are the "governed elsewhere" case, and the one worth understanding.** They
are excluded because this skill's permission model is one generated permission set,
not because profiles are bad. A retrieved profile is a second, hand-edited answer to
the question `gen-permset.py` already answers from the source tree — it conflicts on
every parallel build and carries FLS for fields the target branch may not have.

**`.forceignore` is the durable half.** Manifest exclusions govern one retrieve;
`.forceignore` governs every retrieve and deploy afterwards. Write it first, commit
it, and treat it like `CLAUDE.md` — a gitignored `.forceignore` does not exist in any
worktree. Template with per-line reason classes:
[references/templates/forceignore](references/templates/forceignore).

**Prove the round trip before committing.** A retrieve that cannot deploy back is a
snapshot, not a baseline:

```bash
sf project deploy start --dry-run --target-org CONFIRMED_ORG --source-dir force-app/main/default --test-level RunLocalTests
```

`force-app/main/default`, not bare `force-app` — the latter is blocked by
`guard-sf-deploy.sh` and there is no reason to learn the command two ways. Every
remaining failure gets fixed or written into `CLAUDE.md` with a reason. Then one
commit, not a series: this is the tree the whole project is diffed against.

**Afterwards, there is no second seed.** Something that exists only in the org gets a
ticket and a worktree like anything else. Retrieve it into a scratch tree from your
own terminal (`--output-dir tmp-retrieve`, gitignored, cannot touch tracked files),
copy across what you meant, and deploy it back — the deploy is what makes the two
copies the same thing again.

---

## Concurrent Deploys — Job ID Discipline

Multiple agents may be deploying to the org simultaneously. Never assume the "latest" deploy job is yours.

**NEVER use `--use-most-recent`** on any `sf project deploy` subcommand. This flag resolves to whatever deploy the org last received — which could be another agent's job.

| Dangerous | Safe equivalent |
|-----------|----------------|
| `sf project deploy report --use-most-recent` | `sf project deploy report --target-org CONFIRMED_ORG --job-id $JOB_ID` |
| `sf project deploy cancel --use-most-recent` | `sf project deploy cancel --target-org CONFIRMED_ORG --job-id $JOB_ID` |
| `sf project deploy resume --use-most-recent` | `sf project deploy resume --target-org CONFIRMED_ORG --job-id $JOB_ID` |

**Pattern — capture the job ID immediately:**
```bash
DEPLOY_RESULT=$(sf project deploy start --target-org CONFIRMED_ORG --source-dir <files> \
  --test-level RunSpecifiedTests --tests <TestClasses> --json --async)
JOB_ID=$(echo "$DEPLOY_RESULT" | jq -r '.result.id')
sf project deploy report --target-org CONFIRMED_ORG --job-id "$JOB_ID"
```

If you run a deploy/validate synchronously (without `--async`), the CLI blocks until completion — that's fine, no follow-up `report` call needed.

Note: this discipline covers *not confusing whose job is whose*. It does not by itself prevent two agents from submitting concurrent deploy/validate requests against the same org — Salesforce serializes/queues those at the platform level, and today this project relies on the workflow discipline above (worktree dry-runs, one squash-merge-and-deploy at a time from `main`) rather than an explicit lock to keep that orderly. If concurrent-agent collisions on the single org become a real problem in practice, that's worth revisiting — not a reason to avoid this skill's lighter-weight model in the meantime.

---

## Subagent Delegation — Do the Work Yourself

The main agent should do the work directly unless there is a clear, specific reason to delegate. You have full conversation context; subagents get a compressed summary and lose nuance.

**Good subagent uses:**
- Research/exploration — return findings to main agent for synthesis and ongoing work
- Parallelizable independent tasks (e.g., multiple worktrees for separate tickets)
- Long-running background tasks where the main agent continues other work

**Bad subagent uses:**
- "Go build the whole thing" — handing off implementation with a fraction of the context. This invariably fails because the subagent lacks business rules, prior decisions, and codebase understanding.

**Rule of thumb:** If you can do the task yourself in the current context, do it yourself.

## Fanning a Build Out — Generate Shared Metadata, Never Author It

When you *do* delegate a build to several worktree agents at once, the thing that breaks is not the
code. It is the handful of files **every** agent has to touch — the project permission set above
all, plus anything else that must list every object, field or class.

The framing to reject is "visible merge conflicts vs. invisible FLS gap". Both options are bad and
you do not have to pick one:

- Every agent edits the permission set → guaranteed conflict on the one file they all touch, every
  wave, forever.
- Agents skip it and you grant FLS later → the field deploys, nobody can see it, and it resurfaces
  as a phantom *"field does not exist"* that reads like a data-model bug and is not.

**Derive the file from the source tree instead of authoring it, and both disappear.** Two branches
that each add fields converge the moment the file is regenerated against the merged tree — nothing
to hand-merge, because the file is a pure function of what is on disk. And because you regenerate
**into the agent's worktree before merging**, the fields and their FLS land in the same PR and the
same deploy. No conflict, no invisible-field window.

[references/tools/gen-permset.py](references/tools/gen-permset.py) does this for the permission set.
Install it as `scripts/gen-permset.py`, run `--init` once to create `config/permset-gen.json`, and
add `"permset": "python3 scripts/gen-permset.py"` / `"permset:write": "… --write"` to
`package.json`.

| You are | You do |
|---|---|
| **A worktree agent** | **Never** edit the permission set. **Never** run `--write`. Run `npm run permset` (check mode) to confirm your new fields are still ungranted, and say so in your report. That's all. Sole exception: the ticket that creates the file for the first time. |
| **The orchestrator** | From the main clone, as the last step before merging: `python3 scripts/gen-permset.py --write --tree <agent worktree>` → commit into the worktree → **re-validate** (the merge gate is per-commit and you just added one) → merge → deploy. |

`--write` refuses to target the main checkout **from anywhere** — the refusal follows the *target*,
not your cwd, mirroring `guard-force-app-bash.sh`. That is what lets you resolve a generated file
from the main clone without bouncing the PR back to an agent. `--out PATH` dumps a copy for diffing
and is safe in the main clone. Check mode is the default and is safe everywhere.

The script preserves the historical field classifications: omit MasterDetail and required fields, and make formula, roll-up and AutoNumber fields read-only. Local tests verify those decisions. Validate the repaired output against the intended platform before claiming it deployed.

Read [references/tools/README.md](references/tools/README.md) for the config reference, the full
locally tested refusal cases, package handling, and retained-test workflow.

## Key Rules (quick reference)

| Rule | Why | Enforced by |
|------|-----|-------------|
| Verify the recorded release against the org | Git state alone does not prove deployment state | Deployment receipt and acceptance checks |
| Never deploy from a worktree | Only `main` deploys — worktrees validate only | `guard-sf-deploy.sh` |
| Never deploy a dirty or unpushed `main` | The org would hold code that is not in git / not on GitHub | `guard-sf-deploy.sh` |
| Use one explicit confirmed `--target-org` | Avoid accidental use of a machine default | `verify-salesforce-org` and `guard-sf-flags.sh` |
| Local preparation needs no org | Leave the target unset until confirmed | Explicit workflow mode |
| Deploy only changed files | Never `--source-dir force-app` | `guard-sf-deploy.sh` |
| Validate before you merge | Merging before a green dry run can strand `main` ahead of the org | `guard-pr-merge.sh` |
| Squash merges only | One ticket, one commit — the refs the automation reads stay in one place | `guard-pr-merge.sh` |
| `/simplify` before commit | AI quality gate for reuse, architecture, efficiency | **nothing — this one is on you** |
| Definition of Done = all 6 boxes | Deployed + in git + AC met + user green light + ticket closed + worktree removed | `guard-issue-close.sh`, `stop-dod-check.sh` |
| Fix forward, never reopen merged branches | New worktree + new issue off latest `main` | judgment |
| Worktrees live as long as their ticket | Reuse one across deploys for follow-up fixes; remove it when the ticket closes | `session-status.sh` reports open ones |
| Never nest worktrees | `isolation: "worktree"` agents are already in a worktree — creating another causes unrecoverable Bash failures | `guard-worktree-nesting.sh` |
| Never use `--use-most-recent` | Another agent's deploy may be the "most recent" — always use `--job-id` | `guard-sf-flags.sh` |
| Choose test scope from target and release policy | Broader tests may be required | Review and platform validation |
| Choose development dry-run or production validation deliberately | The commands support different deployment workflows | Target-specific plan |
| `RunSpecifiedTests` by default | Fast, targeted feedback — the whole point of a solo dev loop | — |
| Use `NoTestRun` only where supported | A small change does not override production requirements | Target-specific plan |
| Issue refs are keyword-anchored | A bare `#N` scan reads issue numbers out of prose and labels the wrong tickets | `commit-msg` |
| The permission set is generated, never hand-edited | It is the one file every parallel agent touches; derived from the tree, two branches converge on regeneration instead of conflicting | `gen-permset.py` refuses `--write` outside a worktree |
| Worktree agents run `npm run permset` in check mode only; the orchestrator runs `--write --tree <worktree>` before merging | Fields and their FLS land in the same PR and the same deploy — no window where a deployed field is invisible | judgment + the script's target-based refusal |
| **CLAUDE.md, `.claude/hooks/`, `.githooks/` and `.forceignore` must be committed, not gitignored** | Worktrees only ever materialize *tracked* content — anything ignored silently does not exist in any worktree, which defeats this entire skill | `verify-git-hooks.sh` reports it |
| Seed once, before the enforcement stack | The empty repo is the only window where a retrieve cannot clobber tracked content; after that the org is downstream forever | ordering in `setup-guide.md` Phase 2f |
| Sanitize at the manifest, not on disk | One file of a few hundred lines beats a few thousand files, and the retrieve is smaller too | judgment |
| Never `retrieve --source-dir force-app` | Overwrites tracked content with org state and silently reverts anything deployed but not yet pulled back — no ticket, no diff anyone read | `guard-sf-flags.sh` + deny rules |
| Prove the round trip before the seed commit | A retrieve that cannot deploy back is a snapshot, not a baseline — `main === org` would be false on day one | judgment |
