Attached are two exports from our Tasklane board for the online permits project (key prefix LP). Both are the full board, all items, using the "Table CSV" export.

  • export-2026-10-28.csv is last week's.
  • export-2026-11-03.csv is today's.

Column names in Tasklane differ from Jira: ID is the ticket key, Title is the summary, State is the status, Kind is the type, Parent is the epic, Cycle is the sprint, Estimate is story points, Tags are labels.

"Awaiting Council" is a state we added this week. It means the work is finished on our side and we need a council decision before it can move, so please treat it as blocked.

The board links are https://tasklane.example.com/items/LP-1 and so on.

Thanks, Priya

Output

Today's Tasklane export has 6 tickets. Compared with last week's, 1 was added, 1 was removed and 3 changed. I ran the intake steps by hand because I can't execute scripts/intake.py here, so the SHA-256 values are placeholders until the script is run on the original files.

What changed since 28 October
TicketChange
LP-7 Refund requestsAdded. Story under LP-1, Backlog, tagged payments, no estimate or cycle.
LP-6 SMS remindersRemoved from the export. It was a Backlog story estimated at 2 points. The export doesn't say whether it was deleted, archived or moved to another board.
LP-3 Upload supporting documentsState changed from In Progress to In Review. Still Cycle 4, 5 points.
LP-4 Fee paymentState changed from Ready to Awaiting Council, now category blocked. Moved from Cycle 4 to Cycle 5, and the estimate rose from 8 to 13. It is still blocked by LP-3.
LP-5 Case officer queueState changed from Backlog to In Progress. Now in Cycle 5 with a 3-point estimate; it had neither last week.

LP-1 and LP-2 have no tracked field changes. LP-1's updated date moved to 2 November, but the delta compares only summary, status, category, sprint, points, epic, type, description hash and blocked-by.

Conflicts
  • Duplicate key LP-7. The new export has two LP-7 rows: "Refund requests" and "Refund requests (duplicate row)". The adapter keeps the first and skips the second. Priya Nair should confirm whether the second row is a stray copy or a different ticket with a mistyped ID.
  • Unknown state "Awaiting Council". The default status list doesn't know it, so the adapter would have mapped it to todo and flagged it. Priya's email says it means a council decision is needed, so I added "Awaiting Council": "blocked" to tracker.status_map. With that in place there is no status conflict.
Read these with care
  • LP-4's estimate rose from 8 to 13 points and it slipped a cycle. The export records the change but not the reason, and it isn't an approved scope change. Priya or the product owner would need to confirm it.
  • The blocked category comes from Priya's description of the state. The export doesn't say what decision is outstanding or who at the council owns it.
  • LP-3 being In Review doesn't mean it is deployed.
  • Neither export has a Description column, so every ticket has empty acceptance and background extracts. Readiness checks downstream will show no acceptance criteria.
Setup and assumptions
  • Adapter: table-csv, because Tasklane isn't Jira. Column mapping, taken from Priya's email: ID to key, Title to summary, State to status, Kind to type, Parent to epic, Cycle to sprint, Estimate to points, Tags to labels, and Priority, Created, Updated and Blocked by to the matching fields.
  • Base URL: https://tasklane.example.com/items/, so pages can link each ticket.
  • Origin: Tasklane table CSV export sent by Priya Nair, Larkfield Council project manager, by email on 3 November 2026.
  • Scope: online permits project (prefix LP), full board, all items. I took this from her email.
  • Baseline: the 28 October export was processed first, giving 6 tickets and no delta. The 3 November export was then processed against it.
  • Dropped fields: the export has no comment, assignee or reporter columns, so nothing needed redacting. The intake record still carries the standard redaction notes.
  • Dates: the 3 November export's latest update (2 November) is newer than last week's (27 October), so --allow-older isn't needed.
  • Links: the LP-4 blocked-by LP-3 link appears on one side only. The adapter copies it across, so LP-3 now lists LP-4 under blocks.

To run it for real, use this command with the files saved to the engagement folder:

python3 scripts/intake.py --config config/site.json --input export-2026-11-03.csv \
  --out tracker --origin "Tasklane table CSV export from Priya Nair, Larkfield Council PM, email of 3 November 2026" \
  --scope "Online permits project (LP), full board, all items"

Run the same command on export-2026-10-28.csv first so the delta has a baseline. Keep both original files in the evidence folder, not in the site.

Next step

Hand tickets.json and delta.json to build-review-site refresh or build-moscow-story-map queue. The queue should list LP-7 as a new ticket to map or class, and LP-6 as no longer in the export. If the story map has a story tied to LP-6, someone needs to decide whether it leaves scope. The tracker can't make that decision.

Files

All in ./out/. These are hand-built stand-ins for the script's output.

  • config/site.json: the tracker block described above.
  • tracker/tickets.json: 6 canonical tickets from the 3 November export.
  • tracker/delta.json: added LP-7; removed LP-6; changed LP-3, LP-4 and LP-5 with the field-level changes in the table above.
  • tracker/intake-log.json: one record for each export, with origin, scope, adapter, ticket count and latest update. The second record carries the LP-7 duplicate-key conflict.

skills.markdown:
---
name: ingest-transcript
description: 'Preserve, normalize, identify, and index a consulting meeting transcript for a confirmed client opportunity or engagement. Use when a transcript, call recording export, meeting notes file, VTT, or plain-text conversation must enter the Knowledge Hub. Do not use for call preparation, general meeting summarization, or unsupported promotion of an AI summary into canonical truth.'
---


# Ingest transcript

Turn one meeting record into a durable, searchable source without loading every
transcript into later AI sessions.

## Required identity

Confirm the client and the opportunity or engagement before filing. Use a stable
context ID beginning with `opp-` or `eng-`. Stop when the meeting could belong to
more than one record.

## Ingest

1. Preserve the raw source without changing its bytes.
2. Create a normalized Markdown copy with transcript ID, client ID, context ID,
   context type, meeting date, title, participants, source hash, raw-file
   location, and ingestion time.
3. Add or update one entry in `transcripts.index` with topics, decisions, actions,
   and the normalized file location.
4. Register the raw transcript in `evidence.sources`.
5. Extract facts, decisions, commitments, actions, and open questions as proposed
   claims. Keep the transcript locator and relevant passage with each proposal.
6. Send proposed claims through `evidence-core` before promoting them into a
   lifecycle record.

An AI summary is navigation, not evidence. Preserve the raw transcript and cite
it when a claim matters.

## Available tools

Use `scripts/normalize_transcript.py` on a local surface. It accepts Markdown,
plain text, and VTT; preserves the source; creates Markdown; and refuses to
overwrite an existing transcript. Run its selftest after changes.

On Cowork, Claude.ai, or another surface without the script, apply the same
record contract with available file tools. If files cannot be persisted, return
the normalized Markdown and exact intended Hub targets. State `patch-returned`.

## Boundaries

- Never guess client or engagement identity from a participant name alone.
- Never delete or replace the raw transcript.
- Never copy a transcript into several client folders.
- Never treat a generated summary as a meeting quote.
- Never promote an unsupported interpretation into canonical client knowledge.
- Search `transcripts.index` before opening transcript bodies in later work.

Return the resolved identity, raw and normalized locations, source hash, index
change, proposed claim count, evidence result, and persistence state. Format the
durable run record with [`output-contract.md`](../_shared/output-contract.md).

examples.title: Filing a client kickoff call VTT with proposed claims
examples.markdown:
## Request

Please file the attached kickoff call VTT in the Hub against the Harbourline returns review opportunity (context details are in hub-context.md). I need it normalized, indexed, and the facts and actions pulled out as proposed claims.

## Inputs

Run of the `ingest-transcript` source module, which has no task package of its own. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### 2026-10-28-kickoff-call.vtt

WEBVTT

1
00:00:03.000 --> 00:00:11.000
Priya Nair: Thanks for joining. Today I want to cover how returns are handled at the Leeds depot and what you need from us.

2
00:00:11.500 --> 00:00:22.000
Tomas Wren: Returns are our biggest pain. We process about 4,200 returned parcels a week and roughly 18 percent sit unlogged for more than two days.

3
00:00:22.500 --> 00:00:31.000
Priya Nair: Is that 18 percent across all depots or only Leeds?

4
00:00:31.500 --> 00:00:40.000
Tomas Wren: Leeds only. I don't have the figure for Bristol or Glasgow yet.

5
00:00:40.500 --> 00:00:52.000
Aisha Okafor: Finance sees it as write-offs. Last quarter we wrote off 63,000 pounds of returned stock that couldn't be matched to an order.

6
00:00:52.500 --> 00:01:03.000
Priya Nair: So the aim is to cut the unlogged backlog, not to replace the warehouse system?

7
00:01:03.500 --> 00:01:15.000
Tomas Wren: Correct. The warehouse system stays. The board has ruled out replacing it before 2028.

8
00:01:15.500 --> 00:01:15.500
Tomas Wren: The board has ruled out replacing it before 2028.

9
00:01:16.000 --> 00:01:28.000
Aisha Okafor: We would want a decision on a pilot by the end of November, and a budget ceiling of 90,000 pounds for phase one.

10
00:01:28.500 --> 00:01:38.000
Priya Nair: I will send a two-page scope outline by 6 November. Tomas, can you share the returns log export for September?

11
00:01:38.500 --> 00:01:46.000
Tomas Wren: Yes, I will send it by Friday. I think the scanner firmware may be part of the problem, but I haven't tested that.

#### hub-context.md

#### Hub front door extract

Client: Harbourline Parcels Ltd, client ID `client-harbourline-parcels`

Open opportunity: Returns backlog review, context ID `opp-harbourline-returns-review` (stage: proposal)

No other open opportunity or engagement exists for this client.

Call: kickoff call, 28 October 2026, recorded on video conference, exported as VTT (`2026-10-28-kickoff-call.vtt`).

Attendees: Priya Nair (our lead consultant), Tomas Wren (Harbourline head of depot operations), Aisha Okafor (Harbourline finance manager).

Suggested transcript ID: `tx-20261028-harbourline-kickoff`

## Output

### Kickoff call filed as a patch, not yet persisted

I prepared the normalized transcript, the index entry and seven proposed claims. Nothing is written to the Hub, because I had no Hub access and could not run the normalizer script or `evidence-core`. State: **patch-returned**.

#### Resolved identity
- Client: `client-harbourline-parcels`
- Context: `opp-harbourline-returns-review` (opportunity)
- Transcript ID: `tx-20261028-harbourline-kickoff`, meeting date 2026-10-28
- Why this is safe to file: your Hub extract lists this as the client's only open opportunity, so the meeting cannot belong to another record. I did not infer identity from participant names.

#### Locations and hash
- Raw, to be copied byte for byte: `raw/tx-20261028-harbourline-kickoff.vtt` (from `inputs/2026-10-28-kickoff-call.vtt`)
- Normalized: `normalized/tx-20261028-harbourline-kickoff.md`
- Source SHA-256: **not computed**. The normalized file carries a `PENDING` placeholder in `source_sha256`. Compute the hash of the raw file and replace it before filing. I did not invent a value.

I normalized by hand following the script's VTT rules: removed the `WEBVTT` header, cue numbers and timing lines, kept speaker names and wording, and dropped only consecutive duplicate lines. Cue 8 repeats the end of cue 7 but is not an identical line, so I kept it. The normalized copy has no timestamps, so every claim below cites the cue number in the raw file.

#### Index change (`transcripts.index`)
- Topics: Leeds returns backlog; returns write-offs; warehouse system scope; pilot budget and timing
- Decisions: none made on the call; warehouse system replacement is out of scope
- Actions: scope outline (Priya Nair, 6 Nov); September returns log export (Tomas Wren, "Friday")

The raw VTT also needs an `evidence.sources` entry.

#### Proposed claims (7)
| # | Claim | Raw locator |
|---|-------|-------------|
| 1 | Leeds processes about 4,200 returned parcels a week (client-stated) | cue 2 |
| 2 | About 18% of Leeds returns sit unlogged for over two days; Bristol and Glasgow not measured | cues 2, 4 |
| 3 | 63,000 GBP of unmatched returned stock written off last quarter | cue 5 |
| 4 | Warehouse system stays; the board ruled out replacing it before 2028 | cues 7, 8 |
| 5 | Client wants a pilot decision by end of November and a 90,000 GBP phase one ceiling | cue 9 |
| 6 | Priya Nair to send a two-page scope outline by 6 November | cue 10 |
| 7 | Tomas Wren to send the September returns log export by Friday | cues 10, 11 |

Each claim has its quoted passage in `ingestion-record.md`.

#### Evidence result
`evidence-core` was not available, so the claims have not been checked and none is promoted. Figures are the client's own statements, not verified data.

#### Things to settle
- **Scanner firmware:** Tomas Wren said it "may be part of the problem" and that he had not tested it. I kept it as an open question, not a claim.
- **Budget and pilot timing:** Aisha Okafor said what finance would "want". That is a stated preference, not an approval.
- **"Friday":** the call was on Wednesday 28 October, so this probably means 30 October. The transcript gives no date, so please confirm it.
- **Output contract:** `_shared/output-contract.md` was not in the skill package, so the record uses the fields listed in SKILL.md.

#### Files
- `out/tx-20261028-harbourline-kickoff.md`: normalized transcript with front matter (client, context, date, participants, raw-file path, hash placeholder) and the speaker lines in order.
- `out/ingestion-record.md`: identity, targets, index entry, claims table with quoted passages, open questions and gaps.
- `out/answer.md`: this reply.

### File: ingestion-record.md

#### Ingestion record: tx-20261028-harbourline-kickoff

Persistence state: patch-returned

##### Identity
- Client: client-harbourline-parcels
- Context: opp-harbourline-returns-review (opportunity)
- Meeting date: 2026-10-28

##### Intended targets
- Raw (unchanged bytes): `raw/tx-20261028-harbourline-kickoff.vtt`, copied from `inputs/2026-10-28-kickoff-call.vtt`
- Normalized: `normalized/tx-20261028-harbourline-kickoff.md`
- Source hash: not computed (no way to run a hash here)

##### transcripts.index entry
- id: tx-20261028-harbourline-kickoff
- file: normalized/tx-20261028-harbourline-kickoff.md
- topics: Leeds returns backlog; returns write-offs; warehouse system scope; pilot budget and timing
- decisions: none made on the call; warehouse system replacement is out of scope
- actions: scope outline (Priya Nair, 6 Nov); September returns log export (Tomas Wren, Friday)

##### evidence.sources registration
- Raw VTT registered as the source; locator format is cue number from the raw file, because normalization removes cue numbers and timestamps.

##### Proposed claims (7), for evidence-core
| # | Type | Claim | Raw locator | Passage |
|---|------|-------|-------------|---------|
| 1 | fact (client-stated) | Leeds depot processes about 4,200 returned parcels a week | cue 2, 00:00:11.500 | "We process about 4,200 returned parcels a week" |
| 2 | fact (client-stated) | About 18% of Leeds returns sit unlogged for over two days; other depots not measured | cues 2 and 4 | "roughly 18 percent sit unlogged for more than two days" / "Leeds only." |
| 3 | fact (client-stated) | 63,000 GBP of unmatched returned stock written off last quarter | cue 5, 00:00:40.500 | "we wrote off 63,000 pounds of returned stock" |
| 4 | constraint | Warehouse system will not be replaced; the board ruled out replacement before 2028 | cues 7 and 8 | "The board has ruled out replacing it before 2028." |
| 5 | commitment/ask | Client wants a pilot decision by end of November 2026 and a phase one ceiling of 90,000 GBP | cue 9, 00:01:16.000 | "decision on a pilot by the end of November ... budget ceiling of 90,000 pounds" |
| 6 | action | Priya Nair sends a two-page scope outline by 6 November | cue 10 | "I will send a two-page scope outline by 6 November." |
| 7 | action | Tomas Wren sends the September returns log export by Friday | cues 10 and 11 | "Yes, I will send it by Friday." |

Open questions (not claims): the unlogged rate at Bristol and Glasgow; whether scanner firmware contributes (Tomas Wren said he had not tested it, cue 11, so it stays a hypothesis); who holds authority for the budget ceiling and pilot decision (Aisha Okafor stated a wish, not an approval).

##### Evidence result
Not run. `evidence-core` is not available here. All 7 claims remain proposals and none is promoted.

##### Gaps
- `../_shared/output-contract.md` was not in the package, so this record uses the fields listed in SKILL.md.
- The "Friday" deadline has no date in the transcript; the call was on Wednesday 28 October, so it likely means 30 October, which needs confirming.
- Cue 8 repeats the last sentence of cue 7; both are kept as in the source.

examples.title: Two Letter Print Then Cut sheets with exact sticker counts
examples.markdown:
## Request

I need Print Then Cut sheets for my Cricut Joy Explore on US Letter: 3 each of monstera_01 and monstera_02 at 2.5 inches, 12 cactus at 1.5 inches, and 2 watering cans at 3 inches wide. Keep every design even if two look alike, and put the monsteras on their own sheet. The project is in inputs/ (generator help and design inventory).

## Inputs

**Dry run.** This skill normally works on live systems or its owner's own setup. Here the system state is invented in the inputs below, and nothing was changed anywhere. Run of the built `lay-out-sticker-sheets` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Other files it produced, not shown here: `spec.json`.

#### design-inventory.md

#### Design inventory: Fernlight Plant Co. sticker project

Folder: designs/ (PNG, transparent background). Pixel hashes are SHA-1 of decoded RGBA data.

| File | Canvas px | Transparent-trimmed bounds px | Aspect | Pixel hash |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| monstera_01.png | 1800 x 1800 | 1500 x 1500 | 1:1 | 3f9a1c07 |
| monstera_02.png | 1800 x 1800 | 1500 x 1500 | 1:1 | b72e55d4 |
| cactus.png | 1200 x 1200 | 1000 x 1000 | 1:1 | 0c41ae92 |
| watering_can.png | 2400 x 1600 | 2100 x 1400 | 3:2 | d58810fb |
| fern_spare.png | 1800 x 1800 | 1500 x 1500 | 1:1 | 3f9a1c07 |

Notes
- fern_spare.png is not part of this order. It has the same pixel hash as monstera_01.png.
- monstera_01 and monstera_02 have different hashes (different leaf cut-outs), so they are separate designs.
- Project brand file: none present. No maker mark was requested.

#### generator-help.txt

$ python3 tools/make_sheets.py --help   (project: fernlight-stickers)
usage: make_sheets.py [-h] --spec SPEC [--paper {letter,a4}] [--canvas {paper,cutarea}]
                      [--dpi DPI] [--gap GAP_IN] [--no-brand] [--no-dedupe]
                      [--out DIR]

  --spec        JSON list of {file, width_in, count, sheet}
  --paper       physical paper (letter = 8.5 x 11 in)
  --canvas      paper: full printable page PNG; cutarea: image sized only to the cut area
  --dpi         default 300
  --gap         spacing between stickers, default 0.25 in
  --no-brand    do not add a maker mark (default adds the project mark)
  --no-dedupe   keep designs whose pixels match another design
  --out         writes sheet_N.png, manifest.json, contact_sheet.png

Project config (project.toml)
  letter_cut_area_in = [9.25, 6.75]   # last edited 2025-03; Design Space limit not re-verified
  orientation = landscape

## Output

Both sheets fit on US Letter with the counts you gave. I have not rendered them. The generator isn't available to me here, so I worked the layout out by hand from its `--help` and your design inventory. Run the command below to produce the PNGs, then check the output against the numbers here.

#### What I checked

- **Duplicates.** `monstera_01` (hash 3f9a1c07) and `monstera_02` (hash b72e55d4) have different pixels, so they are two designs. You asked to keep every design, so I'm passing `--no-dedupe` anyway. `fern_spare.png` has the same hash as `monstera_01`, but it isn't in your order and stays out of the spec.
- **Branding.** You didn't ask for a maker mark and the project has no brand file, so the command uses `--no-brand`. The help says the generator adds its project mark by default.
- **Sizes.** Sizes come from the transparent-trimmed bounds, not the canvas. The watering can is 2100 x 1400 px trimmed, which gives 3.0 x 2.0 in.
- **Paper and cut area.** Paper is Letter, 8.5 x 11 in. The cut area is a separate limit. `project.toml` sets it to 9.25 x 6.75 in, landscape, last edited 2025-03. I couldn't check Design Space's current limit, so confirm it before you print. If it has changed, the layouts below need to be redone.

#### Command

```
python3 tools/make_sheets.py --spec spec.json --paper letter --canvas paper \
  --dpi 300 --gap 0.25 --no-brand --no-dedupe --out out/
```

I used `--canvas paper` so you get a full printable page. A `cutarea` image would be only 2775 x 2025 px and isn't a Letter page. Spec file: `out/spec.json`.

#### Layout (inches from the top-left of the cut area, 0.25 in gaps)

**Sheet 1: monsteras, 6 stickers, using 8.0 x 5.25 in**

| Row | y | Stickers (x position) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | monstera_01 at 0, 2.75, 5.5 |
| 2 | 2.75 | monstera_02 at 0, 2.75, 5.5 |

**Sheet 2: cactus and watering cans, 14 stickers, using 8.5 x 6.75 in**

| Row | y | Stickers (x position) |
|---|---|---|
| A | 0 | cactus at 0, 1.75, 3.5, 5.25, 7.0 |
| B | 1.75 | cactus at 0, 1.75, 3.5, 5.25, 7.0 |
| C | 3.5 | watering can (3.0 x 2.0) at 0 and 3.25 |
| Right column | 3.5 and 5.25 | cactus at x = 6.5, two stacked |

Cactus total: 5 + 5 + 2 = 12. Watering cans: 2. Sheet 2 reaches the full 6.75 in height, so it has no spare room vertically. Its width is 8.5 of 9.25 in.

#### Pixel checks at 300 DPI

| Item | Printed size | Pixels | Source pixels (trimmed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monstera | 2.5 x 2.5 in | 750 x 750 | 1500 x 1500 |
| Cactus | 1.5 x 1.5 in | 450 x 450 | 1000 x 1000 |
| Watering can | 3.0 x 2.0 in | 900 x 600 | 2100 x 1400 |
| Letter canvas, landscape | 11 x 8.5 in | 3300 x 2550 | |
| Cut area | 9.25 x 6.75 in | 2775 x 2025 | |

All sources are larger than their print size, so nothing is upscaled.

#### Still to check once the PNGs exist

1. Open `manifest.json` and confirm 3 + 3 on sheet 1 and 12 + 2 on sheet 2.
2. Check `contact_sheet.png` for overlaps and that no sticker crosses the cut area.
3. Confirm each sheet is 3300 x 2550 px at 300 DPI and the artwork sits inside the cut area.
4. Confirm the Design Space cut-area limit for Letter.
5. Confirm there is no maker mark on either sheet.

#### Files

- `out/spec.json`: the generator spec with the four lines above (monstera_01 x3, monstera_02 x3 on sheet 1; cactus x12, watering_can x2 on sheet 2).
- `out/answer.md`: this reply.

No sheet images were created.

examples.title: Resuming a warehouse slotting case study with conflicting results
examples.markdown:
## Request

Resume my portfolio case study on the warehouse slotting project from the current sources. I need a short summary paragraph I can send a hiring manager at a logistics company, and tell me where we left off.

## Inputs

**Dry run.** This skill normally works on live systems or its owner's own setup. Here the system state is invented in the inputs below, and nothing was changed anywhere. Run of the built `load-project-context` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### hub-context-export.md

#### Hub context export (snapshot 2026-11-03 18:40, connection: portfolio-hub, scope: common contract + portfolio project)

Router: portfolio/ROUTER.md names `portfolio/slotting/AUTHORITY.md` as subject authority.
Contract revision: c-41. get_context query: "warehouse slotting case study".

##### Records returned
| ID | Title | Rev | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-102 | Slotting project brief | r7 | Dated 2025-03. Role: analyst on a 3-person team at Larkfield Distribution (fictional). Scope: re-slot 2,400 pick locations at one regional DC. |
| R-117 | Pilot results summary | r3 | States pick-travel distance fell 18% in the pilot zone (zones A–C). Marked "summary". |
| R-118 | Pilot measurement sheet | r2 | Raw: 6 weeks before / 6 weeks after, zones A–C only. Computed change in travel distance: 14.2%. |
| R-121 | Claims-and-rights ledger | r5 | Client name: public use NOT cleared. Figures: cleared as "about 14%" only after R-118 check. Method description: cleared. |
| R-130 | Voice notes, portfolio | r4 | Plain, first person, no adjectives of praise, state own role per decision. |

##### Conflicts
- R-117 (18%) vs R-118 (14.2%). R-117 has no source sheet cited. R-121 ledger entry for figures is "held".
- Rollout beyond the pilot zones: R-102 says planned; no record shows it happened.

Access note: the connection returned common-contract content and the portfolio project. Private career files were not part of this response.

#### project-state.md

#### Local project state: ~/portfolio/slotting/ (listing dated 2026-11-03)

```
case-study-draft.md      modified 2026-10-29   (uncommitted)
outline.md               modified 2026-10-21
receipt.json             modified 2026-10-29
handoff-note.txt         modified 2026-10-29
```

skills.markdown:
---
name: maintain-discovery-record
description: 'Maintain the discovery record for a pursuit: supported facts and ranked open questions tied to the scope they unblock. Use to prepare discovery content, identify questions that affect scope or price, ingest a post-call transcript, close answered questions, log decisions, or propose scope revisions. Route company research and a packaged call brief to prepare-sales-pursuit, scope and pricing changes to scope-project, and signed-engagement requirements to capture-requirements.'
---


# Maintain discovery record

## Caller context and source boundary

Use only the current task's supplied or explicitly authorized account, project sources and destinations. Resolve record names such as `client.profile` within that confirmed context; they are logical slots, not a default personal store. Connector availability alone does not authorize searching another account. Organization-specific pricing, capability catalogs, approval roles and policies must be supplied or confirmed; absent material context remains an explicit gap. Keep reusable package files immutable during a client task and save client records outside them. Never populate an example with private source material.


> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`readout-brief.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/readout-brief.md).**

This skill owns `opportunity.discovery`. It maintains a two-column ledger before
and after each pursuit discovery session. `prepare-sales-pursuit` uses that ledger to package
one upcoming call. `scope-project` decides whether proposed findings change
scope or price.

## The ledger

Build the ledger before writing a brief. Detailed fields and examples are in
[`ledger-spec.md`](references/ledger-spec.md).

**Column A: supported knowledge.** Each atomic claim carries a source ID, source
date, as-of date, and Confirmed or Inferred status. Confirmed needs authoritative
evidence. Inferred states its basis. A searched-for fact that remains absent
becomes a Column B question.

**Column B: open questions.** Write each question as it should be asked. Record
what was searched, the scope line or capability it unblocks, and its impact:

- High blocks sizing, creates a wide cost range, or gates a phase.
- Medium changes effort inside a workstream that can still be sized.
- Low refines the estimate at the margin.

Ask higher-impact questions first. For equal impact, prioritize the question
that gates other work. Remove questions that cannot change scope, effort, price,
or a delivery decision. An unresolved item carries `do not size until Q-nn` in
the relevant scope row.

## Inspection and persistence state

Record only sources actually inspected. If the input summarizes what “transcript line N says,” cite the supplied summary of line N; do not claim that the transcript itself was searched. A search field can say “supplied summary only; full transcript unavailable.” An excerpt or summary is not a full-transcript search; record its exact available lines and keep the missing source as a retrieval gap. An attributed statement establishes what that speaker said, not independently verified authority for sizing or approval. Narrow a question when the available evidence answers only part of it.

When no write occurred, present an unapplied ledger patch. If a write was attempted but its result or readback is missing, report persistence as unverified or unknown and inspect the destination before retrying; do not call that patch unapplied. Label evidence registration, refresh and validation as proposed actions unless they ran. Preserve supplied human text exactly; if the human block is absent, retain a placeholder for its unchanged contents rather than inventing a note or claiming it was checked.

## Evidence and commercial rules

Run `evidence-core` before building the ledger. Register sources in
`evidence.sources` and claims in `evidence.claims`. Generated artifacts and
worked examples have no evidence authority. A load-bearing Insufficient result
produces a discovery readiness gap memo and stops the full brief.

Every commercial number comes from an approved quote or explicit user-supplied
source. This skill can identify an unsized line. It cannot create hours, rates,
fees, or totals.

## Prepare discovery

1. Resolve the client and opportunity. Confirm the session, attendees, purpose,
   available time, opportunity ID, and quote identifier when one exists.
2. Read `client.front_door`, `client.profile`, `opportunity.front_door`,
   `opportunity.discovery`, and the relevant evidence index.
3. Read authoritative internal sources before asking a person. Include the RFP,
   capability scoring, CRM record, workshop transcripts, client documents, and
   approved commercial records that are available.
4. Build Column A from governed claims. Preserve conflicts.
5. Build and rank Column B from the remaining gaps. Tie every question to a
   named scope line or decision.
6. Validate the ledger before projecting the brief.

Use the section catalog in
[`section-catalog.md`](references/section-catalog.md) for the brief. The ranked
unknowns remain its spine. Add a flex section only when the ledger supports it.

## Ingest the call

Use `ingest-transcript` to preserve and normalize the raw source when it is
installed. Follow
[`post-call-ingestion.md`](references/post-call-ingestion.md):

1. Resolve the speaker-labeled transcript by stable context identity.
2. Walk each open question. Move a supported answer to Column A; narrow a partial
   answer; retain an unanswered question.
3. Extract new facts and decisions with transcript locations.
4. Send proposed claims through `evidence-core`.
5. Write supported findings to `opportunity.discovery`. Update `client.profile`
   only for durable client facts.
6. Send proposed scope changes to `scope-project` for confirmation.
7. Re-rank the remaining questions and refresh the brief.

Never close a question without transcript evidence. Preserve human-authored
blocks between `<!-- human -->` and `<!-- /human -->`. When revising a complete
Pursuit Brief, run prepare-sales-pursuit's before-and-after preservation check.

## Validate and release

```bash
python3 scripts/check_brief.py ledger.json
```

The gate checks source tokens, valid ranks, named scope lines, rank order,
unknown placement, and object structure. An empty JSON open-question list passes only when discovery_complete is explicitly true; punctuation alone does not fail this evidence gate. Exit 0 passes. A nonzero result
blocks release.

Apply `review-writing` to the brief and `brand-renderer` on any branded surface. Apply
`review-deliverable` before final delivery. The shared sequence is in
[`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md).

## Failure behavior

- Unavailable sources remain retrieval gaps; they do not prove absence.
- A question already answered by the record is removed from Column B.
- A priced unresolved item fails the brief.
- A source conflict stays visible until an authorized owner resolves it.
- A headless run may build and gate the ledger. It cannot invent an answer,
  approve scope, or close a client decision.
- Read-only Hub access returns exact patches and `patch-returned`.

## Durable result

Return the ledger, projected brief, or readiness gap memo under
[`output-contract.md`](../_shared/output-contract.md). Name the client and
opportunity, sources searched, records read, top open questions, gate result,
proposed scope changes, and persistence state.

## Files

- `references/ledger-spec.md`: Column A and B formats.
- `references/section-catalog.md`: brief sections and retrieval targets.
- `references/post-call-ingestion.md`: transcript-to-ledger protocol.
- `scripts/check_brief.py`: Markdown and JSON gate.
- `scripts/check_brief_selftest.py`: passing and failing fixtures.

examples.title: Starting a pursuit findings ledger after the first call
examples.markdown:
## Request

Update the Tidewater Freight Co. pursuit findings ledger from today's first discovery call. There is no existing ledger yet — start one. Notes and account background are in ./inputs/.

## Inputs

Run of the built `synthesize-discovery` task package in its "maintain pursuit findings" mode. All inputs below are invented. The run had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Files it also produced, not shown here: `ledger.json`.

#### account-notes.md

#### Tidewater Freight Co. — account notes (fictional)

- Regional less-than-truckload (LTL) carrier, 14 terminals across Virginia, the Carolinas and Georgia. About 1,900 employees, 1,100 tractors.
- Revenue about $410M (FY2025, company-reported in a trade-press interview).
- Customer service runs from one contact center in Norfolk: 62 agents, three shifts. Today they use a 2014-era on-premise ticketing tool ("ServiceDesk Pro") plus shared Outlook inboxes for claims.
- Transportation management system (TMS): "RouteLine 9", hosted by the vendor, REST API available for shipment status and proof-of-delivery images.
- Pain points raised by the inbound lead form: customers can't self-serve shipment status; freight-claims cycle averages 41 days; no single view of a shipper account across terminals.
- Inbound lead came from the VP of Customer Experience after a webinar on Service Cloud for logistics.


#### call-1-notes.md

#### Discovery call 1 — Tidewater Freight Co. (fictional). Notes taken by our AE.

Attendees: Dana Whitfield (VP CX), Marcus Oyelaran (Dir. IT Apps, second half), our AE, our solution consultant.

- Dana: "About 30% of our inbound calls are 'where is my freight.' If customers could look that up themselves we'd free up a third of the floor."
- Contact center: 62 agents. Average handle time on status calls 4.5 minutes. Dana estimated 1,800 status calls per day; she said she'd confirm with the WFM report.
- Claims: 41-day average cycle. Priya's team keys claims from email into a spreadsheet, then into ServiceDesk Pro. Dana: "Claims is where we lose customers."
- Target: online shipment tracking and online claim filing live before peak season — Dana said "October next year."
- Marcus: RouteLine 9 has a REST API for shipment status and POD images. Rate limit is 20 requests per second per tenant. He does not know whether claims data can be written back to RouteLine. "I'd need to ask the vendor."
- Marcus is concerned about owning another platform with a 3-person apps team.
- Budget: Dana said the CFO "would want to see something under half a million for phase one" — not a confirmed budget.
- Decision: Dana sponsors; CFO Tom Becker signs over $250K; Marcus has effective veto on architecture.
- Next step: second call with Priya (claims) and Marcus in two weeks.

## Output

### Tidewater Freight Co. — pursuit findings ledger, started after discovery call 1 (2026-11-04)

I started the ledger from the AE's call notes and the account background. It has 19 supported claims and 8 ranked open questions. It does not answer or close anything. The only call evidence is the AE's notes, not a transcript, so I recorded no question as closed. No commercial number is created or sized.

#### Assumptions and gaps

- **Evidence is secondary.** The notes (S-02) are not a verbatim transcript and most bullets carry no speaker label. Quotes below are exactly as the notes record them, and I can't confirm they are Dana's or Marcus's literal words. The account notes (S-01) are undated.
- **Where "Confirmed" is used.** Only for facts that two sources support and that the speaker owns: the 62 agents, the ServiceDesk Pro and Outlook tooling, and the RouteLine 9 API. Every client-stated metric stays Inferred because no report backs it.
- **No capability catalog, opportunity ID, quote or pricing was supplied.** Scope lines are descriptive and carry no capability codes. I did not size anything.
- **"October next year" is read as October 2027**, since today is 2026-11-04. That is my reading, and Q-05 asks about it.
- **I ran the steps by hand.** I couldn't run `evidence-core`, `check_brief.py`, `review-writing` or `review-deliverable`. I registered sources S-01 and S-02 and applied the gate rules by hand (details below). No tool receipts exist.
- **Not persisted to a Hub record.** No connector was available, so this is a returned patch. The only copy is `ledger.json` in `./out/`.

#### Column A: what we know

| Claim | Source | Confidence | As-of |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Regional LTL carrier, 14 terminals across Virginia, the Carolinas and Georgia, about 1,900 employees, 1,100 tractors | S-01 account notes, undated | Inferred | undated |
| Revenue about $410M (FY2025), company-reported in a trade-press interview | S-01 | Inferred | FY2025 |
| One Norfolk contact center, three shifts | S-01 | Inferred | undated |
| The contact center has 62 agents | S-01; S-02 call notes 2026-11-04 | Confirmed | 2026-11-04 |
| Tools: 2014-era on-premise ServiceDesk Pro plus shared Outlook inboxes for claims | S-01; S-02 (claims keyed into ServiceDesk Pro) | Confirmed | 2026-11-04 |
| Claims start in email; Priya's team keys them into a spreadsheet, then ServiceDesk Pro (Priya's surname and title not recorded) | S-02 (speaker not recorded); S-01 | Inferred | 2026-11-04 |
| Claims cycle averages 41 days; no claims report cited | S-01; S-02 | Inferred | 2026-11-04 |
| Dana Whitfield (VP CX): "Claims is where we lose customers." | S-02, Dana Whitfield | Inferred | 2026-11-04 |
| Dana Whitfield: "About 30% of our inbound calls are 'where is my freight.' If customers could look that up themselves we'd free up a third of the floor." Her estimate, not a report | S-02, Dana Whitfield | Inferred | 2026-11-04 |
| Average handle time on status calls is 4.5 minutes | S-02 (speaker not recorded) | Inferred | 2026-11-04 |
| About 1,800 status calls per day (Dana's estimate; she will confirm with the WFM report). Basis: 1,800 at 30% implies about 6,000 inbound calls a day. 1,800 × 4.5 min is about 135 agent-hours a day, roughly 27% of 62 agents' time if each works one 8-hour shift (our arithmetic, shift length assumed). Plausible against "a third of the floor", not verified | S-02, Dana Whitfield | Inferred | 2026-11-04 |
| Goal: online tracking and online claim filing live before peak season; Dana said "October next year" (read as October 2027, not confirmed as a hard date) | S-02, Dana Whitfield | Inferred | 2026-11-04 |
| TMS is RouteLine 9, vendor-hosted, with a REST API for shipment status and POD images | S-01; S-02, Marcus Oyelaran | Confirmed | 2026-11-04 |
| RouteLine API rate limit is 20 requests per second per tenant (Marcus; not checked against vendor docs) | S-02, Marcus Oyelaran | Inferred | 2026-11-04 |
| Marcus Oyelaran (Dir. IT Apps) is concerned about owning another platform with a 3-person apps team | S-02, Marcus Oyelaran | Inferred | 2026-11-04 |
| Dana said the CFO "would want to see something under half a million for phase one"; relayed, not a confirmed budget | S-02, Dana Whitfield | Inferred | 2026-11-04 |
| Decision path as stated: Dana sponsors; CFO Tom Becker signs over $250K; Marcus has effective veto on architecture. Speaker not recorded; Tom Becker did not attend | S-02 | Inferred | 2026-11-04 |
| Lead form pains: no customer self-serve status, 41-day claims cycle, no single shipper-account view across terminals (the third was not discussed on call 1) | S-01 | Inferred | undated |
| Lead came from the VP CX after a webinar on Service Cloud for logistics; the call notes record no platform preference | S-01 | Inferred | undated |

#### Column B: ranked unknowns

| ID | Question | Rank | Unblocks | Why open |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q-01 | What does phase one include (online tracking, online claim filing, the cross-terminal account view), and what does "under half a million" have to cover (licences, implementation, run cost)? Can Tom Becker confirm a number? | High | Phase-one boundary and every scope line below; budget fit | Only Dana's relayed figure and a $250K CFO signature threshold; no budget document or phase definition; CFO absent |
| Q-02 | Does ServiceDesk Pro stay, get replaced, or sit behind the new front end? | High | Case-management and platform foundation line; ServiceDesk Pro integration or migration line | Tool named in both sources, no disposition recorded; Marcus's ownership concern has no decision attached |
| Q-03 | Can claim data be written back to RouteLine 9 through the vendor API, and if not, where does the claim record live? | High | Online claim filing integration line (RouteLine write-back) | Marcus: "I'd need to ask the vendor." No vendor documentation supplied |
| Q-04 | How many claims arrive per month, through which channels, with what attachments, and what happens between receipt and settlement? | High | Claims intake and workflow line; online claim form scope | Only the 41-day average and the email-to-spreadsheet path; no volume, attachments, steps or owners; Priya absent |
| Q-05 | Is October 2027 a hard date, what does "live" mean on that date, and does it cover both tracking and claims? | Medium | Delivery phasing and staffing assumptions across the tracking and claims lines | "October next year" with no reason, contingency or capability coverage recorded |
| Q-06 | How many shipment-status lookups per second do you expect at peak once customers self-serve, and are there other consumers of the RouteLine API? | Medium | Tracking integration design line (caching and throttling) | 20 requests per second tenant limit known; expected online volume and other consumers not recorded |
| Q-07 | How do shippers and consignees identify themselves today (account number, PRO number, login), and where does the shipper master record live? | Medium | Customer identity and access line; shipper account view line | Neither source says how customers are identified or where account data sits |
| Q-08 | Who would run and support the solution after go-live, given a 3-person apps team: Tidewater staff, a managed service, or a mix? | Medium | Run and support / managed-service line | Marcus raised the concern; no support model discussed |

**Who can answer.** Q-01 needs Dana plus the CFO, who was absent. Q-02 and Q-03 need Marcus and the RouteLine vendor. Q-04 needs Priya. I put the questions in that order because Q-01 sets the boundary for the rest.

**Gate before design:** Q-01 and Q-03 must be answered first. Q-01 fixes what phase one is, and Q-03 decides whether claim filing can write into RouteLine at all.

#### Scope at stake (proposed; for the scoping owner, nothing committed)

| Candidate line | Phase | Flag in place |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Online shipment tracking via RouteLine status and POD API | Phase one per Dana (Q-01) | Do not size until Q-01, Q-06 |
| Online claim filing and RouteLine write-back | Phase one per Dana (Q-01) | Do not size until Q-01, Q-03, Q-04 |
| Claims intake and workflow | Unconfirmed | Do not size until Q-04 |
| ServiceDesk Pro disposition (integrate, retain or replace) | Unconfirmed | Do not size until Q-02 |
| Customer identity and shipper account view | Unconfirmed | Do not size until Q-01, Q-07 |
| Run and support model | Unconfirmed | Do not size until Q-08 |

Capability codes: not supplied. These lines are pattern-free; none is derived from an RFP, because none exists in the inputs.

#### Decisions, risks and assumptions

| Item | Reference | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Decision: Dana sponsors; CFO Tom Becker signs over $250K; Marcus has effective veto on architecture | AE notes 2026-11-04, no timestamp, speaker not recorded | Proposed |
| Decision: second call with Priya (claims) and Marcus in about two weeks (around 2026-11-18, date not set) | AE notes 2026-11-04 | Proposed |
| Risk: an architecture veto sits with someone who is already worried about platform ownership. Trigger: a proposal that adds a platform without a run-and-support answer (Q-08) | Marcus's stated concern | Open |
| Risk: the CFO signs over $250K and has not been in the room. Trigger: a phase-one figure in Q-01 that Tom Becker has not seen | Decision path above | Open |
| Assumption: "October next year" means October 2027 | Our reading; Q-05 | Assumption |

No decision changes prior scope, since there was no prior scope. Neither conflicts nor contested sources turned up between S-01 and S-02.

#### Next discovery actions

| Action | Closes | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ask the RouteLine vendor whether the API accepts claim writes | Q-03 | Marcus Oyelaran, who said he would ask |
| Get the WFM report for status-call volume. It supports the value case; it did not earn its own question because it does not change scope | Validates the 1,800 per day claim | Dana Whitfield, who offered it |
| Cover claims volume, channels, attachments and steps on the second call | Q-04 | Priya, with the AE leading; role-level owner, not named in the notes |
| Raise phase-one scope and the budget range with Dana, and ask for access to Tom Becker | Q-01 | AE, owner not assigned in the notes |
| Cover ServiceDesk Pro, identity and the support model on the second call | Q-02, Q-07, Q-08 | Marcus; owner of the session not assigned |
| Ask Dana for the reason behind the October date | Q-05 | AE |
| Get the full transcript or a verbatim export of call 1 and re-run ingestion | Retrieval gap | AE (assumed) |

#### Gate result, by hand

- Every Column A row has a source and a confidence of Confirmed or Inferred. None is Unknown.
- Column B has 8 rows, each with a non-empty question, rank and unblocks. The order is four High then four Medium, and the IDs run Q-01 to Q-08.
- No hours, rates, fees or totals appear. The $500K and $250K figures are quoted as client statements, not budgets.
- Not run: `check_brief.py`, `evidence-core`, `review-writing` and `review-deliverable`. The hand check above does not replace their receipts, so I'm not calling this final until those run.

#### Biggest judgment call

I ranked Q-04 (claims process and volume) High. The argument for Medium is that claims volume only changes effort inside a workstream that can still be sized. The argument for High is that Dana named claims as where Tidewater loses customers, and the notes say nothing about the process or volume. Without them I can't size the claims workstream at all, which is the High definition. I kept High.

#### Files

- `./out/ledger.json` — the ledger in the JSON format the gate expects: sources, Column A, Column B, decision log and scope-revision proposal. Its content is reproduced in the tables above.
- `./out/answer.md` — this answer.

---
name: maintain-skills-estate
description: Maintain a Skills Estate checkout by authoring or repairing workflows, validating and packaging them, installing reviewed releases, or replacing a skill in another host or account. Use for estate maintenance and select only the requested operation.
---


# Maintain skills estate

Keep one canonical Git checkout. Edit its `skills/`, `policies/`, and declared runtime dependencies; build complete portable packages from those sources. Claude Code and Codex use the same accepted versioned packages locally. Candidate builds and ZIPs remain separate from installed releases. A package includes the workflow, scripts, references, templates, and shared policies it needs.

Read [the skill standard](references/estate/skill-standard.md) before deciding whether a change is ready to install. A successful build checks packaging. It does not prove that a skill can perform its task.

## Choose the maintenance operation

- For an estate addition or behavioral repair, read [estate authoring](../author-estate-skill/SKILL.md). It carries the governed intake and scaffolder; use the host's general authoring tools when available.
- For build, package, local installation, drift or rollback, follow the procedures below.
- For another host or account, read [cross-platform release](../release-skill-package/SKILL.md). It preserves archive inspection, private-account replacement, ambiguous-upload recovery and destination invocation checks. Its generic method also supports sources outside this estate; do not require an estate checkout for that branch.

Read only the requested mode. A creation request does not authorize installation or account publication.

## Select the estate

Use the checkout already identified by the user or the installation's repository pointer. The bundled bridge resolves an explicit `--repo`, otherwise `~/.config/skills-estate/repository`. It refuses a missing pointer or a checkout without the expected tooling. It does not clone a repository, change accounts, or guess from the current directory.

Run from this skill's directory, replacing the example repository with the confirmed checkout:

```sh
python3 scripts/manage_estate.py --repo /path/to/Skills-Estate validate
python3 scripts/manage_estate.py --repo /path/to/Skills-Estate build
python3 scripts/manage_estate.py --repo /path/to/Skills-Estate bundle
python3 scripts/manage_estate.py --repo /path/to/Skills-Estate status
```

From the canonical checkout, the equivalent command is `python3 tools/estate.py <command>`. Development commands invoke that checkout’s tooling. Ordinary `update` runs the same updater implementation bundled in the installed maintenance package; its version follows activation and rollback, independently of the authoring branch. Python 3 and a writable canonical checkout are required. Status creates a local lock file and reads the build; it does not contact host services.

If no checkout is available, report the missing prerequisite and identify the user's existing repository. An isolated upload of this maintainer skill can inspect its own resources but cannot synchronize an estate that is absent from the host.

## Repair and verify before installing

1. Run `validate`. Fix malformed entry metadata, broken local links, missing declared runtime dependencies, or dependency cycles in source. Preserve working implementations when repairing instructions.
2. Run the changed skill's behavioral tests with representative inputs. Save the actual outputs, failures, and command receipts. Check generated prose and figures against the inputs, and inspect rendered artifacts. Use the checkout's `tools/run_preserved_test.py` for Python tests that create temporary files.
3. Run the estate's packaging and installation tests after changing shared policies, runtime assembly, or synchronization code. Shared changes can affect every dependent package.
4. Commit the reviewed source and version record, then run `build` and `bundle`. Build and plugin assembly read a clean snapshot of `HEAD`, including its policies, runtime dependencies, configuration and executable modes. Untracked, ignored, staged and modified working files are excluded without changing them. Manifests record the commit and source/package hashes. A changed HEAD during assembly is rejected. `validate` and tests still inspect working files for development. Bundle output is in `dist/`; use the release manifest's filenames instead of assuming an extension.
5. Confirm that the reviewed output belongs to the current source hash. Do not infer task quality from hashes, file counts, ZIP creation, or a structural selftest. A host invocation is separate evidence from local file installation.

The current canonical CLI does not automatically run every behavioral test before building. The agent must complete the applicable tests and content review before treating a build as ready. Preserve a skill's failed attempt and fix the capability; do not replace the workflow with a general description to make validation pass.

## Update from GitHub main

From this installed skill’s directory, use `python3 scripts/manage_estate.py update` for the owner's ordinary update. It fetches GitHub main into a fresh temporary checkout without pulling into the authoring branch. The existing verification guard requires a successful run for the exact revision, retaining the generated-publication commit exception for its immediately verified source parent. The fetched tooling runs local checks and builds before activation. Tests deferred locally remain named in the receipt; GitHub's accepted workflow supplies the full integration result.

Codex uses the existing immutable release store and durable repository pointer. Duplicate local Claude skills are backed up within the same activation transaction; Claude continues to use its marketplace plugin manager. This command does not update platform-managed plugin caches. Fetch, verification, local test and build failures leave installed links unchanged. Installation failures restore prior links and backups unless a concurrent edit requires preserving the recovery journal. Receipts identify the installed commit, remote run, local checks, previous release and restore operation.

Use `test-local` explicitly to test the authoring checkout and build committed HEAD candidates without installation. Keep normal GitHub updates separate from local development promotion.

## Install and keep local hosts consistent

Before rebuilding a legacy checkout whose installed links point into `build/`, run `pin-installed`. It preserves only the existing managed inventory and exact bytes in a versioned directory; it does not promote new source or change vendor installations.

After the requested repairs, independent review, and release checks pass, use the exact reviewed source hash:

```sh
python3 scripts/manage_estate.py --repo /path/to/Skills-Estate install --expected-source REVIEWED_SOURCE_HASH
python3 scripts/manage_estate.py --repo /path/to/Skills-Estate status
```

Installation copies packages into a verified version under `~/.local/share/skills-estate/releases/` and links that version into `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`. Existing matching legacy entries in `~/.codex/skills` are reconciled as well. Unrelated installed skills remain separate. The repository pointer lets this skill find the same checkout from either host.

An existing divergent file, directory, or link is a conflict. Inspect its unique work first. If replacement is authorized, `adopt` backs it up and records a restore receipt before linking. A failed install rolls back its changes. Never discard a divergent installation to force a green status.

`restore /absolute/path/to/receipt.json` reverses a recorded install only if its destinations still match what the installer wrote. It refuses to overwrite a subsequent user change.

`sync` runs build and bundle only. It refreshes candidates without changing installed versions. Git commit, checkout, and merge hooks never install or rebuild. Everyday promotion requires the reviewed source hash and completed release gates. `rollback RELEASE_ID` can reactivate a previously installed version after checking its integrity and the current destinations. For a test run, put `--home /absolute/path/to/test-home` before the command. This changes the install destination and repository pointer; build output still belongs to the selected checkout.

Status inspects the current source, build, ZIP hashes, installed release, local links, and reported account uploads. It continues to inspect ZIPs when the build is stale. Local states include `linked-current`, `pinned-older`, `legacy-mutable`, drift, missing, and broken entries. Overall success requires current build and ZIPs plus matching managed installations. An older pinned installation remains usable but is not the current candidate. A copied package remains outside managed release ownership. Open the updated skill in a fresh host session when discovery requires a reload, then run a representative task there and retain its output. Do not claim Claude Code execution based on a Codex run, or the reverse.

To promote a reviewed task package without changing other installed skills, use `install --skill review-writing --expected-source REVIEWED_SOURCE_HASH`; repeat `--skill` to select more packages. The selected workflows, their runtime dependencies and shared assembly must pass the existing release gates. Other installed links keep their exact versions. Status verifies every retained release and reports a mixed installation without claiming one shared source hash. `rollback RELEASE_ID` restores the complete inventory from the most recent activation of that release ID; use its `restore` receipt to recover originals from an adoption. A conflicting older installation still needs explicit, scoped `adopt --skill NAME --expected-source REVIEWED_SOURCE_HASH` after inspecting its files.

## Shared brand and dependency changes

Edit the canonical brand policy/profile once. Rebuild dependent packages so their vendored policy copies and runtime assets match. Do not edit generated `build/`, `dist/`, or installed package files. Compare a neutral-profile output and an explicitly selected alternate profile when the change affects branding. Missing declared assets must produce an actionable failure rather than silently restoring former company branding.

Runtime relationships belong in `config/runtime-dependencies.json`. A router must carry the scripts and references needed by its declared dependencies when used alone. Test the assembled package away from sibling source directories to reveal accidental source-tree dependencies.

## Prepare functional releases

The existing catalog contains eleven functional plugins: nine domain plugins and the separate opt-in `estate-career` and `estate-personal` packages. Follow [the release workflow](references/release-workflow.md) to verify changes, raise `config/plugin-bundles.json`'s version, record its content with `python3 tools/plugin_version.py --record 'CHANGE NOTE'`, and generate candidates with `python3 tools/plugins.py --candidate`. Keep explicit context external and preserve retirement mappings. The existing marketplace and owner update command remain the distribution route; source preparation does not authorize publication or installation.

## Account uploads and other surfaces

Local installation does not upload to Claude's account, a Codex account, Cowork, ChatGPT, or an API deployment. Check the destination's current supported format and available authorized upload method. Do not assume every surface accepts the same ZIP or provides a skill registry.

After an actual authorized account upload, record the specific skill and destination reference:

```sh
python3 scripts/manage_estate.py --repo /path/to/Skills-Estate record-publication \
  --surface claude-account --skill manage-consulting-knowledge --reference 'account and upload record'
```

The canonical ledger accepts `claude-account`, `codex-account`, `cowork`, and `chatgpt-personal`. A ledger row remains `verified_live: false`: it records the reported upload hash, not a readback or execution. Retain a separate receipt for a destination readback or task invocation. For another destination, retain its actual receipt and extend the adapter explicitly before claiming managed synchronization.

## Retained standalone audit tools

The earlier flat-estate tools remain bundled for explicit compatibility work. They are not the canonical release path:

- `scripts/estate_diff.py --source DIR --config FILE --json` compares a flat skills tree to configured local directories. It distinguishes missing skills, SKILL-only stubs, entrypoint drift, and resource drift; each fails the comparison. It also checks the older `_shared/build-card.md` contract, shared references, and declared prose exemptions. Use it on a tree following that contract, not as a substitute for canonical status.
- `scripts/build_bundles.py --source DIR --out DIR` gates flat-tree bundles on each skill's `*_selftest.py`, carries transitive shared resources, and preserves the original runtime-vendoring mechanism. Its optional release classification filters drafts. `--no-gate` is a diagnostic bypass and is not release evidence. It does not use the canonical dependency graph or manifests.
- `scripts/record_publish.py` retains the flat-tree publication-ledger format. The bundled ledger starts empty; old organization uploads are not evidence for this estate. Use explicit `--config FILE --dist DIR`; the configuration must name an external `ledger` path and the intended destinations. The shipped template has no configured surfaces and grants no access.
- `scripts/sync_build_card.py --skills-root DIR --check` checks the older shared-card/runtime references without generating brand literals.
- `scripts/estate_sync_selftest.py` exercises those compatibility functions with synthetic fixtures. It does not connect to a host or cloud account.

Use [the optional pre-commit hook](references/pre-commit.sh) only after inspecting existing hooks. It validates the canonical source without staging generated files. A hook is not installed or a recurring check scheduled merely because this file describes one.

## Completion record

State which source revision changed, which tasks produced usable outputs, which packages were built, and which destinations were actually updated. Link the outputs and installation or publication receipts. Name any remaining capability or host test and its next action. A missing service does not justify labeling that service's behavior verified; provide a working local path when the task supports one.

examples.title: Diagnose a stale build and a skill in the wrong plugin
examples.markdown:
## Request

After pulling main, our status check says the build is stale and contract-redline is showing up in the finance plugin instead of legal. I've pasted the status output and the two config excerpts; work out why and tell me what to do next, but don't install or publish anything.

## Inputs

**Dry run.** This skill normally works on live systems or its owner's own setup. Here the system state is invented in the inputs below, and nothing was changed anywhere. Run of the built `maintain-skills-estate` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### config-excerpts.md

#### config/skill-catalog.json (excerpt)

```json
{
  "tasks": {
    "contract-redline":  { "domain": "legal",   "modes": ["redline", "clause-compare"] },
    "invoice-matcher":   { "domain": "finance", "modes": ["match", "variance"] },
    "board-pack-builder":{ "domain": "finance", "modes": ["assemble"] },
    "clause-library":    { "domain": "legal",   "modes": ["lookup"] },
    "matter-intake":     { "domain": "legal",   "modes": ["intake"] }
  }
}
```

#### config/plugin-bundles.json (excerpt)

```json
{
  "version": "1.14.0",
  "plugins": {
    "estate-finance": { "tasks": ["invoice-matcher", "contract-redline", "board-pack-builder"] },
    "estate-legal":   { "tasks": ["clause-library", "matter-intake"] }
  }
}
```

#### git log -3 --oneline -- config/plugin-bundles.json config/skill-catalog.json

```
4be91c2 Merge branch 'legal-domain' (catalog: contract-redline domain finance -> legal)
9e0d7a4 Add matter-intake task
c3b18f0 Move contract-redline into estate-finance bundle for Q3 vendor review
```

#### config/plugin-version-history.json (latest entry)

```json
{ "version": "1.14.0", "fingerprint": "e90b…c4", "note": "Add matter-intake task" }
```

#### status-output.txt

$ python3 tools/estate.py status      (checkout: ~/src/Lindqvist-Estate, branch main @ 4be91c2)

source hash (current):   a7f3c10e92
build/ source hash:      5d21be8847      STALE
dist/ ZIPs hash:         5d21be8847      STALE (matches build, not source)

installed release:       rel-2026-10-21-1   (source 5d21be8847)
  ~/.claude/skills/contract-redline    linked-current -> rel-2026-10-21-1
  ~/.claude/skills/invoice-matcher     linked-current -> rel-2026-10-21-1
  ~/.claude/skills/board-pack-builder  pinned-older   -> rel-2026-09-02-1
  ~/.agents/skills/contract-redline    linked-current -> rel-2026-10-21-1
  ~/.codex/skills/invoice-matcher      legacy-mutable (divergent file: notes.md)

plugin candidates (plugins/):
  estate-finance      1.14.0   contains: invoice-matcher, contract-redline, board-pack-builder
  estate-legal        1.14.0   contains: clause-library, matter-intake

account uploads (publish-ledger): claude-account/invoice-matcher  verified_live: false

overall: FAIL (build stale; 1 pinned-older; 1 legacy-mutable)

## Output

There are two separate problems. Neither needs an install to fix, and I haven't installed or published anything. I worked only from the pasted status output and config excerpts and ran no commands, so everything below comes from those files.

#### 1. Why the build is stale

`status` compares three hashes:

| Item | Hash |
| --- | --- |
| Current source (`main` @ `4be91c2`) | `a7f3c10e92` |
| `build/` | `5d21be8847` |
| `dist/` ZIPs | `5d21be8847` |
| Installed `rel-2026-10-21-1` | `5d21be8847` |

The merge of `legal-domain` changed source after the last build. The build and ZIPs are consistent with each other but were made from the older source. The installed release was also built from that older source. So the installed `contract-redline` is linked correctly and still carries the old domain.

Rebuilding refreshes the candidates only. It does not change what is installed.

#### 2. Why contract-redline is in the finance plugin

Two config files answer different questions:

- `config/skill-catalog.json` says what each task is. The merge `4be91c2` changed `contract-redline` from `finance` to `legal` there.
- `config/plugin-bundles.json` decides which plugin ships each task. It still lists `contract-redline` under `estate-finance` and not under `estate-legal`.

Commit `c3b18f0` ("Move contract-redline into estate-finance bundle for Q3 vendor review") put it in the finance bundle on purpose. The merge touched the catalog but not the bundle file, so the bundle assignment is still the Q3 one. The `plugins/` candidates (`estate-finance` has three tasks, `estate-legal` has two) match the bundle file exactly, so the generator is working as designed.

**Assumption:** the Q3 vendor review is over, so the task should now live in legal only. If finance still needs it, keep it in both bundles. The skill allows a task in more than one plugin only if the bundle file says so. I would not assume that.

#### What to do next

Run these from the checkout root, in order:

1. Edit `config/plugin-bundles.json`. Remove `contract-redline` from `estate-finance` and add it to `estate-legal`.
2. Run `python3 tools/estate.py validate`. It catches broken links and missing runtime dependencies in `config/runtime-dependencies.json`.
3. Run the tests for `contract-redline`, using representative inputs, and save the actual outputs. Moving a task between plugins changes its routing, so also check that legal requests reach it and that finance requests such as invoice matching still go to `invoice-matcher`. Then run `python3 tools/run_tests.py --report .local/test-results.json`. A successful build only shows that packaging works, not that the skill can do its job.
4. Raise `version` in `config/plugin-bundles.json` from `1.14.0`. The history entry for `1.14.0` is bound to the old content ("Add matter-intake task"), and reusing a version for changed content fails. Then record the change:
   ```sh
   python3 tools/plugin_version.py --record 'Move contract-redline from estate-finance to estate-legal after the Q3 vendor review.'
   python3 tools/plugins.py --candidate
   ```
5. Run `python3 tools/estate.py sync`. This runs build and bundle only. Check that the new source hash appears in `build/` and `dist/`.
6. Open the generated `plugins/estate-legal` and `plugins/estate-finance` and the host manifests. Confirm that `contract-redline` appears in legal only, with its transitive dependencies.

Do not edit anything under `plugins/`, `build/`, `dist/` or the installed copies. Those are generated.

#### Other items in the status output

- **`board-pack-builder` is `pinned-older`** (`rel-2026-09-02-1`). It still works and needs no action unless you want it current. Promote it on its own later with `install --skill board-pack-builder --expected-source <reviewed hash>`.
- **`~/.codex/skills/invoice-matcher` is `legacy-mutable`** and has a divergent `notes.md`. Open that file first. If it holds work you want, move it into the source skill. Only then consider a scoped `adopt --skill invoice-matcher --expected-source <reviewed hash>`, which backs up the original and writes a restore receipt. Don't discard it to get a green status.
- **The publish ledger** lists `claude-account/invoice-matcher` with `verified_live: false`. That row records an upload hash only. It is not evidence that the skill ran in that account.

#### Before anything is installed

After steps 1–6 and an independent review, install only with the reviewed source hash. Use `install --expected-source <hash>`, or `--skill contract-redline` to promote that one package and leave the other links alone. Afterwards, open a fresh Claude Code session and run a real contract-redline task there. A Codex run does not count as Claude Code evidence. Publishing to the marketplace is a separate step that needs your authorization.

#### Status of this work

- Diagnosis: done, from the pasted files.
- Source change, tests, version bump, rebuild: not done; the steps are above.
- Installed releases: unchanged.
- Published or uploaded: nothing.

skills.title: Manage brand profile
skills.description: Apply a confirmed project or client brand to an artifact, or use the estate neutral profile. Use for branded deliverables and brand profile creation or updates.

guide.what: Apply the confirmed project or client identity.
guide.when: An artifact needs a brand profile or existing profile applied.
guide.inputs: The project’s confirmed colors, typography, assets, and usage rights.
guide.outputs: A selected or updated profile and an artifact checked against it.
guide.example: Apply this confirmed brand profile to the document and check the rendered result.
guide.expect: It chooses the brand from your explicit choice or the project's brand file, falling back to the neutral Baseline profile, and says which one governs. It marks a new profile as draft until you confirm it and checks the output for mixed identities.
guide.overview: It chooses the brand from your explicit choice or the project's brand file, falling back to the neutral Baseline profile, and says which one governs. It marks a new profile as draft until you confirm it and checks the output for mixed identities.
guide.value: Apply one consistent visual identity to an artifact, or turn a supplied brand guide into a profile that future work can use. It helps prevent mixed client identities and guessed colors or logos.

preparation.where: Provide a confirmed brand.md file or the brand guide and authorized logo/font assets. A brand profile is that record of exact values and usage rights; it is not an account connection. Select a brand explicitly when more than one could apply.
preparation.missing: With no confirmed brand selected, use the neutral profile. A newly extracted profile stays draft until confirmed; a missing logo is not redrawn or invented. You can begin with the neutral identity without creating a custom profile.

reuse.label: General use
reuse.reason: The method accepts the user’s project sources and takes private context as an explicit input.
reuse.basis: Source classification and automated reference scan; cross-environment execution has not been tested.

profile.expect: It chooses the brand from your explicit choice or the project's brand file, falling back to the neutral Baseline profile, and says which one governs. It marks a new profile as draft until you confirm it and checks the output for mixed identities.

skills.markdown:
---
name: manage-brand-profile
description: Apply a confirmed project or client brand to an artifact, or use the estate neutral profile. Use for branded deliverables and brand profile creation or updates.
---


# Manage brand profile

Read [the brand policy](references/estate/brand.md) before choosing visual values. It is generated from `policies/brand.md`, the only estate-wide branding authority. Do not copy its palette or type rules into this entrypoint or another skill.

Resolve the brand from the user's explicit choice or the current project's `brand.md`. If neither exists, use the neutral profile, which is Baseline. For a web page, dashboard or interactive artifact, read [the Baseline guide](baseline/GUIDE.md) and build from the bundled kit. State which profile governs. Read the profile and the assets it actually names; do not infer an identity from old templates.

When building a profile, record the source and date for colors, fonts, logos, layout, voice rules, and usage rights. Mark it draft until the user confirms it or explicitly authorizes its use for this artifact. Keep client assets beside the project profile. Never put them in this shared estate as defaults.

Apply the selected profile through the available rendering tool. Check the rendered result, metadata, notes, headers, and footers for mixed identities. Report the profile and any substitutions. The optional `tools/brand.py` in the estate checkout reads the profile's JSON block and emits CSS variables; a renderer still needs to use them.
