examples.title: Client brand profile and holiday-hours web notice
examples.markdown:
## Request

Fernhill Veterinary Cooperative sent their brand notes and the text for a holiday-hours notice. Please set up their brand profile and build the notice as a one-page web page in their brand; I authorise using the draft profile for this page.

## Inputs

Run of the built `manage-brand-profile` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Other files it produced, not shown here: `holiday-notice.html`.

#### brand-notes.md

#### Fernhill Veterinary Cooperative: brand notes

Source: brand sheet v2, sent by Priya Raman (communications lead), Sep 12, 2026. Priya says the sheet is not yet signed off by the board.

##### Colors
- Fern green: #2F5D50 (primary, headings, buttons)
- Cream: #F6F1E7 (page background)
- Clay: #B5532F (accent, used sparingly)
- Ink: #1E2A26 (body text)
- Light sage: #DDE6DF (panels)
- No chart colors or status colors defined.

##### Type
- Headings: Lora (licensed through the co-op's web font account; the files are not included here)
- Body: Source Sans 3 (same account)
- If unavailable: Georgia for headings, Arial for body

##### Logo
- A fern-leaf mark with the words "Fernhill Veterinary Cooperative". The file will follow from Priya. It may be used on the co-op's own pages and notices only.

##### Voice
- Warm and direct. "We" for the co-op, "you" for the pet owner. No exclamation marks. Say "pets" rather than "patients".

##### Layout
- Rounded corners of 8 px, thin 1 px sage borders, headings in sentence case.

#### holiday-notice.txt

Holiday hours notice, December 2026

Both clinics (Fernhill Road and Marsh Lane) change their hours over the holidays.

Dec 24: open 8:00 am to 1:00 pm, both clinics.
Dec 25 and Dec 26: closed. Emergency cases go to Northgate Animal Emergency, 24 hours, phone 555-0142.
Dec 27 to Dec 30: normal hours, 8:00 am to 6:00 pm.
Dec 31: open 8:00 am to 3:00 pm, both clinics.
Jan 1: closed. Emergency cases go to Northgate Animal Emergency.
Jan 2: normal hours resume.

Prescription refills: please request by Dec 19 so we can prepare them before the closures. Request through refills@example.com or the form at example.com/refills.

Contact for questions: reception@example.com.

## Output

I wrote the Fernhill brand profile and built the holiday-hours notice as a one-page web page. Both are saved locally and neither has been published. I have not rendered the page in a browser. I checked the markup and the contrast figures by reading and by hand calculation.

**Governing profile:** Fernhill Veterinary Cooperative, status **draft**. The brand sheet (v2, from Priya Raman, Sep 12, 2026) is not board-approved. Your instruction authorises these values for this notice only. The Baseline kit was not used, because a project profile was selected instead.

#### What the page contains

- Title "Holiday hours", with "Fernhill Veterinary Cooperative · December 2026" beneath it.
- An opening paragraph that says both clinics change hours and gives Northgate Animal Emergency (24 hours, 555-0142) for care while closed.
- A date table in a scrolling box, so it stays readable on a phone:
  - Dec 24: 8:00 am to 1:00 pm
  - Dec 25 and 26: closed
  - Dec 27 to 30: 8:00 am to 6:00 pm
  - Dec 31: 8:00 am to 3:00 pm
  - Jan 1: closed
  - Jan 2: normal hours resume
- A refills panel: request by Dec 19, with a button to example.com/refills and the address refills@example.com.
- A questions line with reception@example.com.

Copy follows the sheet's voice rules: "we" and "you", no exclamation marks, "pets" rather than "patients". Closed days carry the word "Closed" in bold, because the sheet defines no status colors and state is shown by label.

#### Brand values applied

| Role | Value |
|---|---|
| Background | Cream #F6F1E7 |
| Text | Ink #1E2A26 |
| Headings and links | Fern green #2F5D50, in Lora |
| Panels and table header | Light sage #DDE6DF |
| Button | Clay #B5532F with white text |
| Body type | Source Sans 3 at 16 px |
| Corners and borders | 8 px radius, 1 px sage |

#### Substitutions and gaps

- **Logo omitted.** The file has not arrived. I did not redraw the fern mark. The sheet limits it to the co-op's own pages, which this page is.
- **Fonts.** No font files were supplied and the page makes no network request. It names Lora and Source Sans 3 first, then the sheet's fallback of Georgia and Arial. Readers without those fonts installed will see the fallback. Add the licensed files from the co-op's font account to show the real faces.
- **Muted text color.** The sheet has none, so I used Baseline's neutral #535559 (6.6:1 on cream).
- **Charts and status colors.** The sheet defines none and the page uses none.

#### Contrast

- Ink on cream: above 12:1.
- Fern green on cream: 6.7:1.
- Fern green on sage: 5.9:1.
- White on clay (button): 4.9:1.
- **Clay on cream is 4.4:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum for body text.** The page never sets clay as small text on cream. It appears only as the button fill and as the keyboard focus ring. The profile records this restriction for later work.

Metadata check: the page title, the `lang` attribute and the footer area carry only Fernhill. There are no speaker notes, headers or other identities. All addresses use example.com.

#### Writing check

`writing_check.py` could not be run here, so I read the page copy and profile notes by hand against the writing standard. I found no filler, stock transitions or exclamation marks.

#### Decisions for you

1. Ask Priya Raman to confirm board approval of the sheet, or to confirm that the draft may be used elsewhere. Until then the profile applies to this notice only.
2. Ask Priya for the logo file and the web font files. With them I can add the mark to the header and reproduce the headings and body text in the brand fonts.
3. The source gives no year for the notice's dates other than "December 2026". Jan 1 and Jan 2 are shown without a year, as in the source.

#### Files

- `out/brand.md`: the draft profile with the JSON block (name, status, source, colors, type, logo, layout, voice), a substitutions table, and contrast notes.
- `out/holiday-notice.html`: the single-file page described above, with its styles inline and the profile colors as CSS variables.
- `out/answer.md`: this reply.

### File: brand.md

#### Fernhill Veterinary Cooperative brand profile

Status: draft. The brand sheet is not yet signed off by the board. The requester authorised these values for the December 2026 holiday-hours notice only. Confirm with Priya Raman before reusing them elsewhere.

skills.markdown:
---
name: manage-consulting-knowledge
description: 'Resolve, retrieve, and safely update durable consulting knowledge across a client, its opportunities, and its engagements, and stand up or check the pursuit workspace inside the hub. Use when work needs bounded account, pursuit, delivery, evidence, transcript, outcome, or deliverable context from local files, Google Drive, or supplied files, or when a pursuit needs its workspace created, audited, repaired, or gated against the workspace standards.'
---


# Manage consulting knowledge

The Hub owns consulting record identity, retrieval, and persistence. It follows
the client relationship from account context through pursuits, delivery,
outcomes, and expansion. `evidence-core` owns source and claim quality inside the
Hub. `ingest-transcript` preserves and normalizes meeting evidence.

Use the logical records in
[`record-registry.json`](references/record-registry.json). Read only the adapter
needed for the available store: [`drive-mcp-contract.md`](references/drive-mcp-contract.md)
for Drive or `scripts/hub_runtime.py` for guarded local writes. Supplied files
remain a read or patch surface unless the host confirms a write.

## Work with the Hub

1. Confirm the client. When the task concerns a pursuit or delivery, confirm one
   opportunity or engagement. Stop if identity remains ambiguous.
2. Read the manifest and the applicable front door: `client.front_door`,
   `opportunity.front_door`, or `engagement.front_door`.
3. Select the task route or up to four named logical records. Search transcript
   and evidence indexes before opening source bodies.
4. Preserve source IDs, contradictions, current or superseded state, dates, and
   unresolved gaps. Put the current answer before history.
5. Write only to the manifest's declared primary store. Existing local files
   require the SHA-256 observed during the read. Drive writes must follow the
   connector's actual capabilities. Never create a duplicate canonical record
   to bypass a missing update operation.
6. Read back or hash the result before reporting persistence. Mirror changes run
   only after the primary write succeeds. Divergent copies stop for review.

The directory is a catalog, not a template to fill with empty files. Create a
record when it has durable content. Store a fact once and point other records to
its canonical location.

## Stores and persistence

Supported primary stores are `local`, `google-drive`, and `supplied-files`.
When more than one is available, `primaryStore` decides; availability never
changes authority.

A `local` store can be any explicitly configured writable folder. Google Drive
and a synced mount are optional. The manifest's `stores.local.root` is resolved
relative to the manifest location when it is not absolute. A sync mount remains
one local access path; its presence never changes `primaryStore` automatically.
`hub_runtime.find_synced_hub_roots` requires an explicit caller-selected `base` directory. It can discover candidate mounts there, but identity, authority and actual read/write access must still be checked. Discovery grants no write authority, including for a folder labeled My Drive.

Use the record CLI for local work. It validates registered context identities,
returns content and its observed hash together, serializes cooperating local
writers, and reads back the written bytes:

```bash
python3 scripts/hub_records.py --hub "<hub>" routes
python3 scripts/hub_records.py --hub "<hub>" --opportunity <opp-id> context proposal
python3 scripts/hub_records.py --hub "<hub>" --opportunity <opp-id> read opportunity.discovery
python3 scripts/hub_records.py --hub "<hub>" --opportunity <opp-id> write opportunity.discovery --input discovery.md --create
python3 scripts/hub_records.py --hub "<hub>" --opportunity <opp-id> write opportunity.discovery --input discovery-revised.md --expected-hash <observed-sha256>
```

Use `--create` only for an absent record. A stale hash returns `conflict-held`;
read the current record, reconcile the competing evidence, and retry with the
new observed hash. A held local writer lock requires inspecting the active
writer before recovery. The lock does not coordinate separate cloud-sync hosts.
Drive connector capabilities must be inspected in the current session; use the
[adapter contract](references/drive-mcp-contract.md) for capability checks.

Use exactly one persistence state:

- `written-and-confirmed`
- `written-primary-mirrors-pending`
- `patch-returned`
- `not-written`
- `conflict-held`

A required Hub with no readable source blocks a fully client-grounded result.
An optional Hub may be skipped when supplied evidence is enough; state what was
not checked. A denied write returns the exact logical target and a patch when
safe. Never describe a patch as an update.

## The pursuit workspace

A hub on a local filesystem is also the working environment for a pursuit or a
delivery. `scripts/hub_workspace.py` owns that layer, with the verbs from the
enforcement standard and exit codes 0, 1, 2:

```bash
python3 scripts/hub_workspace.py init --hub "<AI Knowledge Hub>" --client "<name>" \
  --opportunity <opp-id> --opportunity-name "<pursuit>"
python3 scripts/hub_workspace.py init --hub "<AI Knowledge Hub>" --engagement <eng-id> --engagement-name "<delivery>"
python3 scripts/hub_workspace.py audit --hub "<AI Knowledge Hub>"
python3 scripts/hub_workspace.py doctor --hub "<AI Knowledge Hub>"
python3 scripts/hub_workspace.py check --hub "<AI Knowledge Hub>" [paths]
```

`init` creates or repairs the hub root: `hub.yaml`, `AGENTS.md` as the index
with `CLAUDE.md` as its one-line pointer, `TODO.md`, `00-CLIENT.md`, and copies of
[`workspace-standards.md`](references/workspace-standards.md) and
[`pursuit-methodology.md`](references/pursuit-methodology.md) as `STANDARDS.md`
and `METHODOLOGY.md`. With an opportunity it adds the front door and the
working areas `inputs/`, `research/`, `synthesis/`, `evidence/`, and
`deliverables/`, then initializes Git and commits only the files it created or updated. An
engagement receives its own front door and working areas. Existing uncommitted
work is preserved; initialization reports that an explicit reviewed commit is
needed. `--no-git` supports a folder without version control, and
`--synced-filesystem` declares a configured sync mount for a new hub. It never
overwrites a file that exists; human edits are authoritative.

`audit` runs at every session start, before any work, because `AGENTS.md` says
so. It is read only and reports Drive conflict copies, lock files, a missing
pointer, dormancy, and any commit a Drive sync race dropped off the branch. The
concurrency posture is detection and repair, not prevention: `doctor` reattaches
a dropped commit under `refs/heads/recovered/` for the orchestrator to merge,
removes a `.git` conflict copy that is byte-identical to its original, and
restores missing pointer files, saying so per fix.

`check` gates working-area files before the orchestrator commits: frontmatter,
the claim-tag vocabulary, the assumptions section, absolute dates, and every
`CLM-###` resolving to a claim event. It proves the ledger at
`evidence/evidence-ledger.jsonl` is append-only against the committed copy.
Claim discipline inside that ledger belongs to `evidence-core`; run its
`ledger_events.py check` in the same gate. The standards file says what each
rule means and why; the
[design decisions](references/design-decisions.md) describe the storage, ledger, and recovery boundaries.

## Compatibility and checks

The older eight-file Drive Hub and 12-file local research folders are migration
inputs. Map them through the registry. Report mode may inspect them but may not
rename, rewrite, or move client material.

Run:

```bash
python3 scripts/hub_resolver_selftest.py
python3 scripts/hub_runtime_selftest.py
python3 scripts/migration_report_selftest.py
python3 scripts/hub_workspace_selftest.py
```

Return resolved identity, logical records used, sources, findings, attempted
writes, persistence state, pending mirrors, conflicts, and exact patches. Format
the durable run record with
[`output-contract.md`](../_shared/output-contract.md).

Legacy migration inventory accepts an explicit `--bucket-scopes FILE` JSON mapping of existing folder names to `opportunity`, `engagement` or `unclassified`. Without that mapping, folders remain unclassified; their names never establish lifecycle authority. The report proposes mappings and preserves source bytes. Actual migration requires its own authorized write and readback.

examples.markdown:
## Request

I'm picking up the Tidewater Freight route-planning pursuit this morning. Check the hub is healthy first, then put the notes from Tuesday's call (inputs/call-notes.md) into the discovery record and tell me anything that conflicts with what we already have.

## Inputs

**Dry run.** This skill normally works on live systems or its owner's own setup. Here the system state is invented in the inputs below, and nothing was changed anywhere. Run of the built `manage-consulting-knowledge` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### call-notes.md

#### Call notes, Tuesday 2026-11-03 (follow-up with Tidewater)

Attendees: Imani Okafor (COO), Devon Reyes (dispatch manager), pursuit lead.

- Devon said the fleet is 138 trucks since the Harlow depot absorbed a leased group in September. Imani did not correct him.
- Go-live: Imani wants the pilot at one depot by 2027-02-01, full rollout by 2027-05-31. March 1 "was just a placeholder".
- Dispatchers spend about three hours each evening on planning (Devon's estimate).
- Imani said the budget is shared with the CFO, Tomasz Vance, who signs anything above 150,000.
- Devon thinks the dispatch system's API is "probably fine" for reading orders. Nobody on the call had checked.
- Next step: Tidewater to send a sample week of orders by 2026-11-13.
- Recording: none. These are the pursuit lead's typed notes, not a transcript.

#### hub-state.md

#### Hub state, 2026-11-04 08:40

Manifest (hub.yaml): primaryStore local, root `./AI Knowledge Hub`, client "Tidewater Freight Cooperative", opportunity `opp-route-planning`. Mirrors: none.

##### Listing of AI Knowledge Hub/ (synced folder, one writer)

```
AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md                      (contains: @AGENTS.md)
STANDARDS.md
METHODOLOGY.md
TODO.md
00-CLIENT.md
account/profile.md
opportunities/opp-route-planning/00-OPPORTUNITY.md
opportunities/opp-route-planning/discovery.md
opportunities/opp-route-planning/discovery (1).md
opportunities/opp-route-planning/evidence/source-register.md
opportunities/opp-route-planning/evidence/evidence-ledger.jsonl
opportunities/opp-route-planning/inputs/call-notes.md
.git/refs/heads/main
.git/refs/heads/recovered/20261029-a41c9e2   (not present in this listing's log of main)
```

Last commit on main: 2026-11-02 ("Add 2026-10-27 discovery call claims"). No lock files.

##### Files of interest

`discovery.md`: observed sha256 on read `5d0c2e71...e9a4`, 2026-11-04 08:41.
`discovery (1).md`: differs from discovery.md. It contains one extra paragraph on the dispatch system (SYS-02) that discovery.md lacks, dated 2026-10-29.

##### discovery.md (current content)

```
---
title: Discovery, route planning
status: draft
owner: pursuit lead
updated: 2026-10-27
sources:
  - SRC-001
---
# Discovery

- Tidewater runs 120 trucks across three depots. [STATED] SRC-001 (CLM-003)
- Routes are planned by hand each evening by two dispatchers. [STATED] SRC-001 (CLM-004)
- Target go-live is 2027-03-01. [STATED] SRC-001 (CLM-005)
- Budget owner is the COO, Imani Okafor. [STATED] SRC-001 (CLM-006)

## Assumptions to validate
- None.
```

SRC-001 is the 2026-10-27 discovery call transcript, authority 70.

## Output

The hub has two problems to deal with before the discovery write. I have not written anything to it. The update is ready as a patch, and the fleet size and go-live date from Tuesday's call conflict with what the hub holds.

#### Resolved identity and records

- Client: Tidewater Freight Cooperative. Opportunity: `opp-route-planning`. Both come from `hub.yaml`.
- Primary store: `local`, root `./AI Knowledge Hub`. No mirrors are configured.
- Records used: `opportunity.front_door`, `opportunity.discovery`, `evidence.sources` and `evidence.claims`, all under `opportunities/opp-route-planning/`.
- Evidence: SRC-001 is the 2026-10-27 call transcript (authority 70). The 2026-11-03 notes become SRC-002.

#### Session-start audit

I did this by hand from the listing you supplied, using the rules in `hub_workspace.py`. I did not run `audit`.

| Finding | Status | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| `discovery (1).md` beside `discovery.md` | Sync conflict copy. `audit` warns, and `check` blocks while it sits in a working area. | The two files differ. The copy has a paragraph on the dispatch system (SYS-02), dated 2026-10-29, that `discovery.md` lacks. |
| `refs/heads/recovered/20261029-a41c9e2` | Warning (GIT-RECOVERED) | An earlier `doctor` run reattached a commit dropped by a sync race. It awaits review and merge, and it may hold the work behind the conflict copy. |
| `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (`@AGENTS.md`), lock files | Clean | The pointer is intact and no writer holds a lock. |
| Dormancy | Clean | The last commit was 2026-11-02, two days ago. |

The listing does not show the content of the conflict copy or of the recovered commit, so I cannot say whether the SYS-02 paragraph is a newer or an older version of anything. I did not merge it and I have not deleted it. The standards require unique material to be kept until a duplicate is confirmed.

#### Conflicts between Tuesday's notes and the hub

| Topic | Hub today | Tuesday's notes | Handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fleet size | 120 trucks (CLM-003, SRC-001) | 138 trucks, from Devon Reyes, after the Harlow depot absorbed a leased group in September | Both kept. Not superseded: the 2026-10-27 call came after September, so the gap is unexplained. Imani Okafor did not correct 138, which is not confirmation. Ask which count includes the leased group. |
| Go-live | 2027-03-01 (CLM-005) | Pilot at one depot by 2027-02-01, full rollout by 2027-05-31. Imani Okafor called March 1 a placeholder. | CLM-009 supersedes CLM-005. She holds the budget, and she is the source of the correction. |

New items without a conflict:

- Planning takes about three hours each evening (Devon Reyes's estimate).
- The CFO, Tomasz Vance, co-owns the budget and signs anything above 150,000. The notes give no currency.
- Tidewater is to send a sample week of orders by 2026-11-13.
- The dispatch API is "probably fine", but no one checked. I tagged it `[ASSUMED]` with ASM-001, owner pursuit lead, closing when the sample week arrives or the vendor documents the API.

#### Evidence limit

The 2026-11-03 notes are typed by the pursuit lead and there is no recording. I propose SRC-002 as a notes source and left its authority to you. Anything under 70 makes every `[STATED]` claim from it project to Inferred in the ledger. The tags are authored as `[STATED]`; the ledger will show the status the authority supports.

#### Persistence: `patch-returned`

I did not write to the hub. A local write needs `hub_records.py`, which I cannot run here. Even if I could, I would hold the write until the conflict copy is dealt with. The record would otherwise gain a second divergent version.

Run these in order:

1. Open `discovery (1).md` and the recovered commit. Move any unique content, including the SYS-02 paragraph, into the patch below. Give SYS-02 its ID in `account/technology-landscape.md` rather than in discovery.
2. Re-read, so the hash is current:
   `python3 scripts/hub_records.py --hub "<hub>" --opportunity opp-route-planning read opportunity.discovery`
   The hash observed this morning was `5d0c2e71...e9a4`. If the merge changed the file, use the new one.
3. Write the patch:
   `python3 scripts/hub_records.py --hub "<hub>" --opportunity opp-route-planning write opportunity.discovery --input discovery-revised.md --expected-hash <observed-sha256>`
   A `conflict-held` result means the file changed after the read. Reconcile and retry.
4. Append to `evidence/evidence-ledger.jsonl` (append-only): the SRC-002 source event, claim events CLM-007 to CLM-011, a supersede line naming CLM-009 as replacing CLM-005, a conflict event for CLM-003 against CLM-007, and the ASM-001 register event. Add the SRC-002 row to `evidence/source-register.md`. Then run `ledger_events.py check` from `evidence-core` and `hub_workspace.py check`.
5. Remove `discovery (1).md` only after step 1, and resolve the recovered branch by merging it.

I did not mint the ledger JSON lines because the event schema belongs to `evidence-core`, and I did not want to guess its field names.

#### What the patch changes

The patch rewrites `discovery.md` as current truth and puts history in the changelog. Key content:

- Fleet: 138 (SRC-002, CLM-007) listed beside 120 (SRC-001, CLM-003), flagged as unreconciled.
- Timeline: pilot 2027-02-01, full rollout 2027-05-31 (CLM-009, supersedes CLM-005); sample week due 2026-11-13.
- Budget: COO Imani Okafor owns it; CFO Tomasz Vance signs above 150,000 (currency not stated).
- Systems: dispatch API read access is `[ASSUMED]` (ASM-001).
- Assumptions to validate: ASM-001, the fleet-size discrepancy and the threshold currency. The earlier "None" is replaced.
- Frontmatter: `updated: 2026-11-04`, sources SRC-001 and SRC-002. Status remains `draft`.

#### Gaps

- I did not run `audit`, `check` or the ledger tools, and nothing here has been read back from the hub.
- Pending mirrors: none, since none are configured.
- Open questions for Tidewater: the fleet count, the threshold currency, and the dispatch API.

#### Files

- `./out/discovery-revised.md` is the full replacement for `discovery.md`, pending the merge in step 1.
- `./out/answer.md` is this reply.

Use for cutover, go-live, runbooks, hypercare, deemed acceptance, closeout, support transition, or lessons learned. Route UAT to validate-delivery, ongoing status and changes to track-delivery, managed operations to their service owner, and contract authoring to sow.

guide.what: Prepare cutover, hypercare, and delivery closeout.
guide.when: An accepted release is approaching go-live or closeout.
guide.inputs: Executed scope, release evidence, owners, and the go or no-go decision.
guide.outputs: A cutover runbook, acceptance record, hypercare plan, and closeout materials.
guide.example: Prepare the cutover runbook and hypercare plan from this accepted release.
guide.expect: It builds the cutover runbook, the Go-Live Acceptance tracker, hypercare triage and the closeout record from the executed SOW and the signed readiness pack. It will not plan production cutover without the go decision, will not invent an acceptance deadline the SOW does not support, and leaves acceptance, rollback and closeout approvals to humans.

# Manage cutover closeout

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [Writing Integrity review](../review-writing/references/detailed-review.md).**

This skill brings an approved release into production and closes the engagement
on the record. Humans approve acceptance, rollback, and closeout. The skill
assembles the evidence, computes contractual dates, tracks the work, and drafts
the records.

## Project context required

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement, source records, private output location,
and intended audience. Map reference roles such as Program Lead, CSE, Solution Lead,
and Pursuit Lead to that project's authorized owners; these labels do not impose
an employer organization chart or signing authority. The executed agreement and
accepted project plan determine gates, commercial rules, and support obligations.
Keep account history, risk assessments, credentials, and client evidence outside
portable skill sources. A cached account, attached Project, or available connector
is not authorization to read, write, or publish.

## Source authority

Read `engagement.front_door`, `engagement.contract_commitments`,
`engagement.delivery_status`, `engagement.test_acceptance`, and
`deliverables.register`. The executed SOW owns scope, acceptance terms, fees,
and dates. The signed readiness pack owns the release decision. Timesheets own
actual effort. Record a missing load-bearing fact as a gap with an owner, due
date, and blocked gate.

Run `evidence-core` before drafting. Use `review-writing` for every prose artifact
and `brand-renderer` for a client-facing render. This skill records commercial
impact but never creates rates, hours, fees, or a change price.

## Workflow

### Cutover runbook

Build the executable plan from `references/runbook-format.md` and
`assets/cutover-runbook-template.md`. Name owners, timing, prerequisites,
verification, rollback triggers, communications, and evidence locations. Every
step must be observable. A rollback decision remains human-owned.

### Go-Live Acceptance

Read the exact executed-SOW acceptance mechanism. If it contains a deemed-acceptance
clause compatible with the calculator, compute its deadline from the sourced trigger
date and contract day-counting rules. Otherwise record the required acceptance actions
and the manual review gap; do not invent or calculate a deadline. Track delivery, client response,
exceptions, and deemed-acceptance status with
`references/acceptance-tracker-spec.md`. Never infer acceptance from silence
before the contractual clock expires.

### Hypercare

Classify each item with `references/hypercare-spec.md`. A defect inside the
accepted scope follows hypercare. A request that changes scope becomes a
change-order candidate for `track-delivery`. Keep severity, owner, evidence,
resolution, and verification. Only the authorized client owner closes a client
acceptance issue.

### Closeout and transition

Use `assets/hypercare-closeout-template.md`. Record delivered artifacts,
acceptance state, unresolved items, support ownership, access changes, final
communications, and transition evidence. Update `engagement.test_acceptance`,
`engagement.outcomes_closeout`, and `deliverables.register` with confirmed
states.

### Harvest

Use `references/harvest-spec.md` to capture measured outcomes, lessons, reusable
assets, comparable-engagement facts, referenceability, and follow-on needs.
Proposed reusable material retains its client restrictions until an authorized
owner approves promotion. Route a qualified follow-on need to
`engagement.expansion` or a new opportunity.

## Gate

Validate every runbook, acceptance tracker, and closeout record:

```bash
python3 scripts/closeout_gate.py artifact.md --type runbook
# Use --type acceptance only for a supported sourced deemed-acceptance clock;
# use --type closeout for the closeout Markdown record.
```

Exit 0 passes. Exit 1 reports content defects. Exit 2 reports invocation or
parse failure. Correct the source record and regenerate the artifact.

Before delivery, run the applicable prose, brand, and quality gates from
[`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md). Return their receipts with the
artifact.

## Failure behavior

- Missing go or no-go approval blocks production cutover planning.
- Missing SOW acceptance language blocks the contractual deadline calculation.
- An unverified hypercare fix remains open.
- An unpriced scope change routes to `track-delivery` and the commercial owner.
- A headless run may prepare artifacts and findings. It cannot record human
  acceptance, rollback approval, closeout approval, or asset promotion.
- Read-only Hub access returns exact patches and `patch-returned`.

## Durable result

Return the artifact or a run record following
[`output-contract.md`](../_shared/output-contract.md). Include the Hub identity,
sources, gate counts, computed deadline, open items, persistence state, and named
human actions. Closeout gives `deliverables.register` its final engagement state.

## Files

- `references/runbook-format.md`: runbook fields and execution rules.
- `references/acceptance-tracker-spec.md`: contractual acceptance calculation.
- `references/hypercare-spec.md`: defect and change boundary.
- `references/harvest-spec.md`: harvest record requirements.
- `assets/cutover-runbook-template.md`: working runbook template.
- `assets/hypercare-closeout-template.md`: closeout template.
- `scripts/closeout_gate.py`: deterministic artifact gate.
- `scripts/closeout_gate_selftest.py`: expected pass and failure cases.

examples.title: Cutover runbook and deemed-acceptance deadline for a scheduling migration
examples.markdown:
## Request

Steering committee signed the go decision for the Fernbank scheduling migration, and cutover is this weekend. Can you build the cutover runbook from the attached plan and set up the Go-Live Acceptance tracker with the deemed-acceptance deadline from the SOW clause?

## Inputs

Run of the built `manage-cutover-closeout` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### cutover-plan.md

#### Cutover plan v0.9 and readiness notes

Go decision: signed 2026-11-03 by the Fernbank steering committee (Dana Okafor, Client Sponsor; Priya Raman, Program Lead). Minutes ref SC-2026-11-03.

Window: Friday 2026-11-13 22:00 to Saturday 2026-11-14 04:00, Australia/Melbourne. War room: #fernbank-cutover, bridge https://meet.example.com/fernbank-cutover.

Team: Program Lead Priya Raman; Solution Lead Tomas Beck; TA/deploy Lena Ito; CSE Marcus Webb. Client: Dana Okafor (sponsor), Samir Qureshi (clinic ops IT), Joy Adeyemi (front-desk lead).

Sequence as planned:
1. Freeze legacy scheduler to read-only (Samir). Check: write attempt returns the read-only banner.
2. Full legacy database backup (Lena), stored in the vault bucket. Check: restore of the backup to staging reconciles row counts.
3. Export appointments for 42 clinics (Lena). Check: export count equals legacy count per clinic (last dry run: 18,406 total).
4. Import into new platform (Lena). Check: per-clinic counts match export. Reversible by wiping import and unfreezing legacy.
5. Switch DNS for booking.fernbank.example.com to new platform (Lena). TTL 300s. Reversible by repointing.
6. Enable SMS reminder job (Tomas). Check: test reminder received on Joy's test phone. Messages sent to patients cannot be recalled.
7. Test booking round-trip (Joy). Check: booking appears in clinic calendar and confirmation email arrives.
8. Send Go-Live Notice (Priya) on completion of steps 1-7.

Point of no return: step 6 (first real patient SMS). Rollback call: Priya, with Dana consulted, by 02:30.
Open defects at sign-off: DEF-017 (Sev 3, calendar colours reset on import; fix in hypercare), DEF-021 (Sev 4, report footer typo; accepted as known issue, ref SC-2026-11-03).
Freeze: code freeze since 2026-11-09. Backup: not yet taken.
Monitoring: booking error rate watched by Tomas through 2026-11-20; over 2% of bookings failing in any hour opens a hypercare issue. Legacy rollback needs about 45 minutes.

#### sow-excerpt.md

#### SOW-FB-2026-014 excerpt (Fernbank Dental Group, Appointment Scheduling Migration)

Executed 2026-07-20 by Fernbank Dental Group and the delivery firm.

Section 9.1 Definitions. "Business Day" means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Victoria, Australia. "Go-Live Notice" means the written notice from the delivery firm to the Client Sponsor that the Cutover Verification steps in the agreed cutover plan are complete.

Section 9.3 Go-Live Acceptance. "The Client must, within seven (7) Business Days after receipt of the Go-Live Notice, either (a) sign the Go-Live Acceptance Certificate or (b) notify the delivery firm in writing of any material non-conformance with the Accepted Scope. If the Client does neither within that period, the Go-Live Deliverables are deemed accepted at the end of the seventh Business Day."

Section 9.5 Hypercare. Hypercare runs 15 Business Days from Go-Live Notice and covers defects in the Accepted Scope only.

Acceptance criteria (Test Plan v1.2): AC-1 all 42 clinic calendars migrated with matching appointment counts; AC-2 online booking round-trips a test booking; AC-3 SMS reminders sent for next-day appointments.

## Output

I've built the cutover runbook and the Go-Live Acceptance tracker. The deemed-acceptance deadline is **Tuesday 2026-11-24**, if the Go-Live Notice goes out on Saturday 2026-11-14. Both files need a few facts confirmed before cutover (listed below).

#### Deadline

SOW-FB-2026-014 section 9.3 gives the client 7 Business Days after receipt of the Go-Live Notice to sign the certificate or contest in writing. Section 9.1 defines a Business Day as a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or Victorian public holiday. The clause is quoted word for word in the tracker.

Notice Saturday 2026-11-14 + 7 business days = **2026-11-24 (Tuesday)**. Days counted: Nov 16-20 and Nov 23-24. Weekend skipped: Nov 14-15. No holidays in the window.

Hypercare (section 9.5, 15 Business Days from the notice) ends 2026-12-04.

The trigger is the notice, not the end of the cutover window. If the notice moves, the deadline moves, so recompute it then.

#### Runbook

The window is 2026-11-13 22:00 to 2026-11-14 04:00 Melbourne time. It has eight steps, each with a named owner, a check a second person could run, and a rollback point:

| # | Step | Owner | Rollback point |
|---|------|-------|----------------|
| 1 | Set legacy scheduler to read-only | Samir Qureshi | RB-1 |
| 2 | Full legacy backup; staging restore reconciles | Lena Ito | RB-1 |
| 3 | Export appointments for 42 clinics | Lena Ito | RB-1 |
| 4 | Import; per-clinic counts match | Lena Ito | RB-1 |
| 5 | Repoint booking DNS (TTL 300s) | Lena Ito | RB-1 |
| 6 | Enable SMS reminders | Tomas Beck | No rollback: sent SMS cannot be recalled; remedy is a corrective message approved by the Client Sponsor |
| 7 | Test booking round-trip | Joy Adeyemi | No rollback: committed after step 6; failures go to hypercare |
| 8 | Send Go-Live Notice | Priya Raman | No rollback: starts the SOW clock; withdrawal is a CSE decision |

- **Point of no return:** step 6, because it sends the first real patient SMS. The rollback call is Priya Raman's, with Dana Okafor consulted, by 02:30. RB-1 takes about 45 minutes, so that time leaves room to finish inside the window.
- **RB-1:** returns to the legacy scheduler. It repoints DNS, wipes the import, unfreezes legacy and confirms a test write.
- **Monitoring:** Tomas Beck watches the booking error rate through 2026-11-20. More than 2% failing in any hour opens a hypercare issue.
- **Defects at sign-off:** DEF-017 (Sev 3, fix in hypercare) and DEF-021 (Sev 4, accepted as known issue, ref SC-2026-11-03).

#### Tracker

The tracker holds the three acceptance criteria (AC-1 to AC-3, from Test Plan v1.2), the two open defects, the status line and a surfacing log. The status is "Clock not started" because the notice has not been sent. Nothing is recorded as accepted. Only the client can accept, and only a human can record it.

#### Gaps and assumptions

- **Documents missing:** I had only cutover plan v0.9. There was no readiness pack, no Solution Design Document and no final signed plan. Tomas Beck should supply the first two and Priya Raman the signed plan, by 2026-11-10. Until then the step list is unconfirmed.
- **Code freeze:** the plan says it has been in place since 2026-11-09, but no evidence link was supplied. Tomas Beck, by 2026-11-10.
- **Phone numbers:** the escalation path has no contact numbers. Priya Raman, by 2026-11-12.
- **Holidays:** no Victorian holiday calendar was supplied, so I listed none. Priya Raman should confirm none falls on 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-24 by 2026-11-12. If one does, the deadline moves a day.
- **Time of day:** the clause says acceptance happens "at the end of the seventh Business Day". The calculator gives a date only, with no time cutoff. Marcus Webb and counsel should confirm before the notice goes out.
- **Receipt:** I assumed the client receives the notice the day it is sent. Dana Okafor's written acknowledgement (step 8) fixes the date.
- **Contests:** what counts as a "material non-conformance", and whether a contest stops the clock, is for Marcus Webb and counsel. The tracker does not interpret it.
- **Backup:** it has not yet been taken. Step 2 takes it, and step 3 should not start until the staging restore reconciles.

#### Checks

I couldn't run scripts here. I applied the rules of `closeout_gate.py` by hand instead, so no gate receipt exists yet.

- **Runbook:** all 8 rows have an owner, a verification and a rollback point or a reasoned "No rollback:". I found no failures by hand.
- **Acceptance:** the stated deadline matches my recomputation under the gate's convention (day 1 is the first qualifying day after the trigger). I found no failures by hand.
- **Style:** there are no em dashes, and I read all the prose myself. The prose, brand and quality validators were not run, and the files are plain Markdown with no branded render.
- **Next step:** please run `python3 scripts/closeout_gate.py <file> --type runbook` and `--type acceptance` before the files circulate.
- **Not persisted:** nothing is written back to the Hub records. `engagement.test_acceptance` and `deliverables.register` are unchanged.

#### Human actions

- Priya Raman and Dana Okafor approve the final runbook and make any rollback call.
- Priya Raman sends the notice and logs the first surfacing entry to herself and Marcus Webb.
- Dana Okafor, or an authorized client delegate, signs or contests.

#### Files

- `./out/cutover-runbook.md`: header, roles, entry conditions, the eight-step table, RB-1, the rollback rule, monitoring and gaps G1-G4.
- `./out/go-live-acceptance-tracker.md`: the verbatim clause, go-live date 2026-11-14, period 7 business days, deadline 2026-11-24, the worked count, criteria, defects, status line and gaps A1-A4.

### File: cutover-runbook.md

#### Cutover runbook: Fernbank Dental Group scheduling migration

- Client: Fernbank Dental Group
- Engagement: Appointment Scheduling Migration (SOW SOW-FB-2026-014)
- Cutover window: 2026-11-13 22:00 to 2026-11-14 04:00, Australia/Melbourne
- Go / no-go: signed 2026-11-03 by the Fernbank steering committee, Dana Okafor (Client Sponsor) and Priya Raman (Program Lead) (source: minutes SC-2026-11-03)
- War room: #fernbank-cutover, bridge https://meet.example.com/fernbank-cutover
- Sources: cutover plan v0.9 and readiness notes (no separate readiness pack or Solution Design Document was supplied; see gaps)
- As of: 2026-11-04, built from the cutover plan v0.9 only

##### Roles on the day

| Role | Delivery team | Client counterpart | Reachable via |
|------|---------------|--------------------|---------------|
| Program Lead | Priya Raman | Dana Okafor (Client Sponsor) | #fernbank-cutover, bridge |
| Solution Lead | Tomas Beck | Samir Qureshi (clinic ops IT) | #fernbank-cutover, bridge |
| TA / deploy | Lena Ito | Samir Qureshi | #fernbank-cutover, bridge |
| Front-desk verification | none | Joy Adeyemi (front-desk lead) | #fernbank-cutover, bridge |

Escalation path: first Priya Raman, then Tomas Beck, then CSE Marcus Webb. Phone numbers are not in the supplied plan (gap G3).

##### Go / no-go entry conditions

- Open defects at sign-off: DEF-017 (Sev 3, calendar colours reset on import; disposition: fix in hypercare). DEF-021 (Sev 4, report footer typo; disposition: accepted as known issue, client sign-off ref SC-2026-11-03).
- Environment freeze: code freeze in place since 2026-11-09 (source: cutover plan; evidence link not supplied, gap G2).
- Pre-cutover backup: not yet taken. Step 2 takes it, and step 3 does not start until the staging restore reconciles.

##### Step table

| # | Step | Owner | Verification | Rollback point |
|---|------|-------|--------------|----------------|
| 1 | Set the legacy scheduler to read-only | Samir Qureshi | A test write in the legacy scheduler returns the read-only banner | RB-1 |
| 2 | Take a full legacy database backup to the vault bucket | Lena Ito | Restoring the backup to staging gives row counts equal to the legacy counts | RB-1 |
| 3 | Export appointments for all 42 clinics from legacy | Lena Ito | Export count equals legacy count for each clinic; the total is compared with the 18,406 from the last dry run and any difference is explained in the channel | RB-1 |
| 4 | Import the export into the new platform | Lena Ito | Per-clinic counts in the new platform equal the export counts for all 42 clinics | RB-1 |
| 5 | Repoint DNS for booking.fernbank.example.com to the new platform (TTL 300s) | Lena Ito | `nslookup` from two networks returns the new platform address | RB-1 |
| 6 | Enable the SMS reminder job | Tomas Beck | A test reminder arrives on Joy Adeyemi's test phone | No rollback: reminders sent to patients cannot be recalled; the remedy is a corrective SMS approved by Dana Okafor |
| 7 | Run a test booking through online booking | Joy Adeyemi | The booking shows in the clinic calendar and the confirmation email arrives | No rollback: after step 6 the cutover is committed; failures go to hypercare as issues, not to rollback |
| 8 | Send the Go-Live Notice to the Client Sponsor | Priya Raman | Sent timestamp recorded in the tracker; Dana Okafor acknowledges receipt in writing | No rollback: the notice starts the SOW clock; a withdrawal is a CSE decision with the commercial owner |

Steps 1 to 5 precede step 6. Step 8 follows only when steps 1 to 7 are all verified.

##### Rollback procedures

###### RB-1: Return to the legacy scheduler

- Trigger: any verification in steps 1 to 5 fails and cannot be corrected before 02:30.
- Owner: Lena Ito, on Priya Raman's call
- Steps: 1. Repoint booking.fernbank.example.com to the legacy host (if step 5 ran). 2. Wipe the imported data in the new platform (if step 4 ran). 3. Remove the read-only flag on the legacy scheduler. 4. Confirm a test write succeeds in legacy.
- Duration: about 45 minutes (source: cutover plan)
- End state: legacy scheduler live and writable, new platform empty, no patient messages sent

##### Rollback decision rule

- Who can call it: Priya Raman, with Dana Okafor consulted. The decision is theirs; this runbook does not make it.
- Point of no return: after step 5 and before step 6 starts, because step 6 sends the first real patient SMS. The call must be made by 02:30 so RB-1 (about 45 minutes) finishes inside the window.
- Client communication on rollback: Priya Raman tells Dana Okafor in the bridge, then confirms in writing. Joy Adeyemi tells front-desk staff to keep using the legacy scheduler.

##### Post-cutover monitoring

| What | Watched by | Through | Threshold that opens a hypercare issue |
|------|------------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| Online booking error rate | Tomas Beck | 2026-11-20 | More than 2% of bookings failing in any one hour |
| DEF-017 calendar colours | Joy Adeyemi | 2026-12-04 | Any clinic reporting reset colours opens an HC issue carried from DEF-017 |

##### Open gaps

- G1: Readiness pack and Solution Design Document were not supplied. Owner: Tomas Beck. Due 2026-11-10. Blocks confirming the step list.
- G2: Evidence link for the code freeze. Owner: Tomas Beck. Due 2026-11-10.
- G3: On-call phone numbers for the escalation path. Owner: Priya Raman. Due 2026-11-12.
- G4: The plan is v0.9; a signed final version is needed. Owner: Priya Raman. Due 2026-11-10.

### File: go-live-acceptance-tracker.md

#### Go-Live Acceptance tracker: Fernbank Dental Group scheduling migration

- SOW: SOW-FB-2026-014, executed 2026-07-20
- Go-live date: 2026-11-14 (planned date of the Go-Live Notice, the trigger named in section 9.3; cutover runbook step 8. Recompute if the notice is sent on another date.)
- Acceptance period: 7 business days
- SOW clause (verbatim): Section 9.3, SOW-FB-2026-014, executed 2026-07-20: "The Client must, within seven (7) Business Days after receipt of the Go-Live Notice, either (a) sign the Go-Live Acceptance Certificate or (b) notify the delivery firm in writing of any material non-conformance with the Accepted Scope. If the Client does neither within that period, the Go-Live Deliverables are deemed accepted at the end of the seventh Business Day."
- Business Day definition (section 9.1): a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Victoria, Australia.
- Deemed-acceptance deadline: 2026-11-24
- Holidays observed: none listed; no Victorian public holiday calendar was supplied (gap A1)

##### Computation

Request

Steering committee signed the go decision for the Fernbank scheduling migration, and cutover is this weekend. Can you build the cutover runbook from the attached plan and set up the Go-Live Acceptance tracker with the deemed-acceptance deadline from the SOW clause?

Inputs

Run of the built manage-cutover-closeout task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

cutover-plan.md
Cutover plan v0.9 and readiness notes

Go decision: signed 2026-11-03 by the Fernbank steering committee (Dana Okafor, Client Sponsor; Priya Raman, Program Lead). Minutes ref SC-2026-11-03.

Window: Friday 2026-11-13 22:00 to Saturday 2026-11-14 04:00, Australia/Melbourne. War room: #fernbank-cutover, bridge https://meet.example.com/fernbank-cutover.

Team: Program Lead Priya Raman; Solution Lead Tomas Beck; TA/deploy Lena Ito; CSE Marcus Webb. Client: Dana Okafor (sponsor), Samir Qureshi (clinic ops IT), Joy Adeyemi (front-desk lead).

Sequence as planned:

  1. Freeze legacy scheduler to read-only (Samir). Check: write attempt returns the read-only banner.
  2. Full legacy database backup (Lena), stored in the vault bucket. Check: restore of the backup to staging reconciles row counts.
  3. Export appointments for 42 clinics (Lena). Check: export count equals legacy count per clinic (last dry run: 18,406 total).
  4. Import into new platform (Lena). Check: per-clinic counts match export. Reversible by wiping import and unfreezing legacy.
  5. Switch DNS for booking.fernbank.example.com to new platform (Lena). TTL 300s. Reversible by repointing.
  6. Enable SMS reminder job (Tomas). Check: test reminder received on Joy's test phone. Messages sent to patients cannot be recalled.
  7. Test booking round-trip (Joy). Check: booking appears in clinic calendar and confirmation email arrives.
  8. Send Go-Live Notice (Priya) on completion of steps 1-7.

Point of no return: step 6 (first real patient SMS). Rollback call: Priya, with Dana consulted, by 02:30. Open defects at sign-off: DEF-017 (Sev 3, calendar colours reset on import; fix in hypercare), DEF-021 (Sev 4, report footer typo; accepted as known issue, ref SC-2026-11-03). Freeze: code freeze since 2026-11-09. Backup: not yet taken. Monitoring: booking error rate watched by Tomas through 2026-11-20; over 2% of bookings failing in any hour opens a hypercare issue. Legacy rollback needs about 45 minutes.

sow-excerpt.md
SOW-FB-2026-014 excerpt (Fernbank Dental Group, Appointment Scheduling Migration)

Executed 2026-07-20 by Fernbank Dental Group and the delivery firm.

Section 9.1 Definitions. "Business Day" means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Victoria, Australia. "Go-Live Notice" means the written notice from the delivery firm to the Client Sponsor that the Cutover Verification steps in the agreed cutover plan are complete.

Section 9.3 Go-Live Acceptance. "The Client must, within seven (7) Business Days after receipt of the Go-Live Notice, either (a) sign the Go-Live Acceptance Certificate or (b) notify the delivery firm in writing of any material non-conformance with the Accepted Scope. If the Client does neither within that period, the Go-Live Deliverables are deemed accepted at the end of the seventh Business Day."

Section 9.5 Hypercare. Hypercare runs 15 Business Days from Go-Live Notice and covers defects in the Accepted Scope only.

Acceptance criteria (Test Plan v1.2): AC-1 all 42 clinic calendars migrated with matching appointment counts; AC-2 online booking round-trips a test booking; AC-3 SMS reminders sent for next-day appointments.

Output

I've built the cutover runbook and the Go-Live Acceptance tracker. The deemed-acceptance deadline is Tuesday 2026-11-24, if the Go-Live Notice goes out on Saturday 2026-11-14. Both files need a few facts confirmed before cutover (listed below).

Deadline

SOW-FB-2026-014 section 9.3 gives the client 7 Business Days after receipt of the Go-Live Notice to sign the certificate or contest in writing. Section 9.1 defines a Business Day as a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or Victorian public holiday. The clause is quoted word for word in the tracker.

Notice Saturday 2026-11-14 + 7 business days = 2026-11-24 (Tuesday). Days counted: Nov 16-20 and Nov 23-24. Weekend skipped: Nov 14-15. No holidays in the window.

Hypercare (section 9.5, 15 Business Days from the notice) ends 2026-12-04.

The trigger is the notice, not the end of the cutover window. If the notice moves, the deadline moves, so recompute it then.

Runbook

The window is 2026-11-13 22:00 to 2026-11-14 04:00 Melbourne time. It has eight steps, each with a named owner, a check a second person could run, and a rollback point:

#StepOwnerRollback point
1Set legacy scheduler to read-onlySamir QureshiRB-1
2Full legacy backup; staging restore reconcilesLena ItoRB-1
3Export appointments for 42 clinicsLena ItoRB-1
4Import; per-clinic counts matchLena ItoRB-1
5Repoint booking DNS (TTL 300s)Lena ItoRB-1
6Enable SMS remindersTomas BeckNo rollback: sent SMS cannot be recalled; remedy is a corrective message approved by the Client Sponsor
7Test booking round-tripJoy AdeyemiNo rollback: committed after step 6; failures go to hypercare
8Send Go-Live NoticePriya RamanNo rollback: starts the SOW clock; withdrawal is a CSE decision
  • Point of no return: step 6, because it sends the first real patient SMS. The rollback call is Priya Raman's, with Dana Okafor consulted, by 02:30. RB-1 takes about 45 minutes, so that time leaves room to finish inside the window.
  • RB-1: returns to the legacy scheduler. It repoints DNS, wipes the import, unfreezes legacy and confirms a test write.
  • Monitoring: Tomas Beck watches the booking error rate through 2026-11-20. More than 2% failing in any hour opens a hypercare issue.
  • Defects at sign-off: DEF-017 (Sev 3, fix in hypercare) and DEF-021 (Sev 4, accepted as known issue, ref SC-2026-11-03).
Tracker

The tracker holds the three acceptance criteria (AC-1 to AC-3, from Test Plan v1.2), the two open defects, the status line and a surfacing log. The status is "Clock not started" because the notice has not been sent. Nothing is recorded as accepted. Only the client can accept, and only a human can record it.

  • Documents missing: I had only cutover plan v0.9. There was no readiness pack, no Solution Design Document and no final signed plan. Tomas Beck should supply the first two and Priya Raman the signed plan, by 2026-11-10. Until then the step list is unconfirmed.

skills.markdown:
---
name: manage-decision-register
description: Keep the client questions awaiting answers during release refinement as a decision register grouped by epic. Each question has an editable status and can carry an owner and saved answers; the register exports to the client's tracker as CSV or a decision log. Use to record questions from meeting notes, track which decisions are open or blocked, find questions without an owner, or export recorded answers. Do NOT use for discovery synthesis (discovery), recording decisions already made in the RAID log (track-delivery), or requirements capture (capture-requirements).
---

# Manage decision register

The register is `content/questions.json`. Each question belongs to a group, usually an epic, and has a status. An owner, an answer and links to stories and tickets are optional. On the published Decisions page, people change a question's status, record answers and comment. The page saves those to the shared store for everyone.

## Record questions

Take questions from the sources the user supplied: refinement notes, ticket comments, the epic description or a meeting summary. Write each question as the decision it needs. Add one or two sentences of `context` that say what depends on it.

Fill in the other fields:

- `status`: one of Open, Proposed, Partly answered, Answered, Deferred, Blocked and Sandbox check.
- `owner`: only when the sources name one. Never assign an owner.
- `answer`: `Proposed answer` for the team's proposal, and `Answer` only for a decision the client recorded. Keep a recorded answer in the client's words.
- `stories` and `tickets`: the work that waits on the question.

A source that changes an answer supersedes the old answer only when it records the decision. A newer meeting summary that mentions a topic does not by itself close a question.

## Check

```bash
python3 scripts/decisions.py check --content <project>/content --tickets <project>/tracker/tickets.json
```

The check lists unknown groups, stories and tickets and any duplicate ids. It also counts questions by status and names the ones with no owner.

## Export answers

Read the `answers` collection from the published page with the artifact data tool and save it as JSON. Then run:

```bash
python3 scripts/decisions.py export --content <project>/content --saved answers.json --out <project>/exports
```

The export writes two files:

- `decisions.csv`: one row per question and ticket, for import as tracker comments.
- `decisions.md`: a decision log grouped by epic.

Saved statuses and answers from the page override the authored ones in both files. Ask the user before writing anything to the tracker. The export prepares the file; the import is the client's action or needs their approval.

## Page behavior

The page behavior follows rules R-DEC-1 and R-DEC-2 in [the review rules](../review-site-runtime/references/review-rules.md). A closed card shows the question and its status. The owner, the answer, the context, linked work, the answer form and comments sit inside the card. Hide answered and No owner only filter the list. The epic list counts questions per group.

#### Refinement notes, 29 October 2026

- Does an invoice need the tenant's sign-off before payment? Open, no owner agreed. RP-142.

skills.markdown:
---
name: manage-linked-task
description: Start, continue, or close a configured task-vault-linked Codex work item. Use when a Brain task ID or daily ready item is the work source, or when finishing a linked task.
---


# Manage linked task

Resolve the task-vault root, task helper and bridge script from explicit caller or project configuration. Do not infer them from a machine path, owner name or an environment variable left by another installation. The supported adapter uses notes under `Today/Tasks/` and project briefs under `System/Projects/`; confirm those conventions in its current documentation. Preserve the task ID, evidence and status history. Set `TASK_BRIDGE` and `TASK_HELPER` to the inspected absolute script paths before running the examples below. No helper or task data ships with this adapter.

## Start or continue work

When the user starts a ready item, set its status to `in-progress` with the Brain task helper. If the current chat is already linked, continue here. Otherwise create its working chat through the Codex app:

1. Run `python3 "$TASK_BRIDGE" --pending`. It returns each unlinked active task's title, prompt, desktop project ID, and note hash.
2. Use `list_projects` to confirm the returned project ID and folder. Reserve the selected task with the bridge's `--reserve TASK_ID --expected-hash HASH` command. A reservation stops repeated runs from creating another chat.
3. If the plan has `existing_thread_id`, reuse that chat. Otherwise call the Codex app's `create_thread` tool with the returned title and prompt, `target.type=project`, the verified desktop project ID, and `environment.type=local`. Keep the user's configured model. Create a chat only when the user has authorized it directly or through a current, explicit task-sync plan; this reusable skill does not provide that authorization.
4. Link the returned `threadId` using the bridge's `--link TASK_ID THREAD_ID --expected-hash HASH` command. It saves the returned ID locally, checks desktop membership and working folder, and links the Brain note only if the note still matches. A `clientThreadId` is pending setup, not a thread ID.
5. Run the bridge once without options and read `System/Sync/Health.md`. The working chat carries out the next action; do not execute that same action in both chats.

If creation or linking has an uncertain outcome, retain the reservation and recover the returned chat ID from the tool result. Do not retry creation blindly. A changed Brain note, unavailable folder, or wrong project stays visible as a queued item or conflict. An existing linked chat is reused.

The daily view at `Today/Ready Work.md` shows every ready item grouped by project and includes each linked chat. Inspect the configured updater and its actual execution receipts before reporting that it recovers changes between sessions. Do not create a schedule or assume a daily time from this adapter.

## Record a work boundary

Use the project's current source folder and guidance. At a real work boundary, record the actual result in Brain:

```sh
python3 "$TASK_HELPER" receipt TASK_ID --status complete --result 'What changed' --verification 'What was checked'
```

Use `blocked` or `in-progress` when that is the actual state. A completion receipt needs specific verification. An idle or archived chat does not close a task. After recording a receipt, run the bridge once so it refreshes the daily view and archives a chat only for an explicit Brain closure.

If Brain is unavailable, retain the result in the chat and report that Brain has not been updated. Keep local preparation, employer submission, publication, deployment, and verified results in their exact states. Preserve the user's existing authorizations; do not infer new external actions from chat creation.

Former-employer actions marked `closed-no-longer-owned` stay historical. Create a new independent task for continuing work.

Start task T-0142 from today's ready list and set up its working chat, I'm authorizing the chat creation. Config and the current bridge output are in the inputs folder.

## Inputs

**Dry run.** This skill normally works on live systems or its owner's own setup. Here the system state is invented in the inputs below, and nothing was changed anywhere. Run of the `manage-linked-task` source module, which has no task package of its own. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill.   {

]

#### config.md

- Task vault root: /Users/sam/Vaults/Tenancy
- TASK_HELPER: /Users/sam/Vaults/Tenancy/System/Tools/task_helper.py
- TASK_BRIDGE: /Users/sam/Vaults/Tenancy/System/Tools/task_bridge.py
- Notes: Today/Tasks/  Project briefs: System/Projects/

- T-0139 Fix rent-statement PDF footer — ready — chat: thread-8c21
- T-0142 Add arrears-reminder opt-out to settings page — ready — chat: none

###### Maintenance Desk

##### list_projects result (desktop)

- proj-5120  Maintenance Desk  /Users/sam/Code/maintenance-desk

## Output

T-0142 is ready to start, and nothing blocks creating its chat. I have not run anything. There is no helper, bridge or Codex app connection in this session, so below are the checks I made against your inputs and the exact steps to run, in order.

#### What I checked

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Script paths | Taken from your config, not inferred: `TASK_HELPER=/Users/sam/Vaults/Tenancy/System/Tools/task_helper.py`, `TASK_BRIDGE=/Users/sam/Vaults/Tenancy/System/Tools/task_bridge.py`. I could not inspect the scripts themselves, so confirm both exist at those paths before running anything. |
| Ready Work.md | T-0142 is ready under Tenant Portal and has no linked chat. |
| Bridge `--pending` output | T-0142 is listed with project `proj-4471` and note hash `a91f03c7`. `existing_thread_id` is null, so a new chat is needed. |
| Project match | `list_projects` shows `proj-4471` as Tenant Portal at `/Users/sam/Code/tenant-portal`. That matches the task's project. |
| Authorization | You asked for the chat directly, which covers creating it for T-0142 only. |

T-0139 already has `thread-8c21`, so it needs nothing. T-0150 (Maintenance Desk, `proj-5120`) is also unlinked, but you did not ask for it, so I am leaving it alone and it stays queued.

#### Steps to run for T-0142

1. Set the status:
   `python3 "$TASK_HELPER"` with its status command for T-0142 set to `in-progress`. I do not have the helper's subcommand syntax for status changes in the material provided, so check its `--help` first rather than guessing it.
2. Reserve the task so a repeated run cannot create a second chat:
   `python3 "$TASK_BRIDGE" --reserve T-0142 --expected-hash a91f03c7`
   If the hash is rejected, the note changed after the pending listing. Stop, re-run `--pending` and read the new prompt before continuing.

   - `environment.type=local`

4. Link the returned `threadId`:
   `python3 "$TASK_BRIDGE" --link T-0142 <threadId> --expected-hash a91f03c7`
   If the tool returns only a `clientThreadId`, setup is still pending. Do not link it as a thread ID.
5. Run `python3 "$TASK_BRIDGE"` once with no options and read `System/Sync/Health.md`. The new chat then carries out the work. I will not repeat the same actions in this chat.

If creation or linking ends in an unclear state, keep the reservation, recover the chat ID from the tool result, and do not retry creation.

#### Expected state afterwards

- T-0142 status `in-progress`, with the new chat shown in `Today/Ready Work.md` under Tenant Portal.
- Nothing is complete. When the work finishes, record it with `python3 "$TASK_HELPER" receipt T-0142 --status complete --result '…' --verification '…'`. The verification must name what was run, for example the reminder job's skip-logic unit tests and the settings page test from the task's acceptance line. An idle chat does not close the task.

- Your config lists no updater and no execution receipts, so I am not claiming that changes made between sessions are picked up automatically. Today's view only updates when the bridge runs.
- The writing checker script was not available here; I read the text over by hand instead.
