examples.markdown:
## Request

From real client work: the journey stage of the develop-product pathway, which routes to map-journey's method, was asked to turn a client's planning workbook and design decisions into current-state and proposed journeys for a sales and contracting workspace. It was not a standalone map-journey run.

## Inputs

The client's planning workbook (questions, decisions and stories), a metadata scan of the existing system, and the product definition from earlier pathway stages. None of these inputs is included. The output was redacted before it was added here: client, project and product names, legacy record-type and team names, and every reference into the client's workbook are replaced with bracketed placeholders. The journey, persona and job labels (UJ, P and J numbers) are the document's own. The 340B/VA price classes show the client is in US healthcare; the owner approved keeping them.

## Output

### Sales workspace current and proposed journeys

Journey records UJ01–UJ06, revision 1, product [PRODUCT-ID], proposed for review. The current-state column is a reconstruction from [planning workbook] planning statements, not observed user behavior. Proposed interactions are design hypotheses linked to requirements and tests. All permissions must be tested against the final [decision ref] matrix.

#### UJ01 Assess and work a site opportunity

Actors P01/P03, jobs J01/J07. Trigger: a manual pursuit or a candidate from an approved rule. Preconditions: site and indication identified, permitted territory access; required parent relationship resolved.

| Step | Current evidence | Proposed interaction, state and handoff | Exception and recovery |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Find next work | Separate legacy [legacy record types] opportunities and monthly fields are described in [story ref] | Site workspace lists existing pursuits and source of creation; rep inspects why a generated candidate exists | Missing/inaccessible site routes to data/access review; do not create a duplicate as a workaround |
| Assess potential | [question ref] assigns [operations team] maintenance and [potential-market fields] validation | Read [market data source] and provenance; validate permitted fields; stamp validator and time; Discovery remains until required facts exist | Missing metrics creates/reuses an exception record. Conflicting estimate sources remain explicit. Rep cannot bypass FLS |
| Classify pursuit | [question ref]/[answer ref]/[story ref] consolidate reason and types | Choose Category → Type → Reason, indication and allowed products. First value: one justified, valid pursuit | [decision ref] determines uniqueness. Competing pursuit is shown with link and permitted attach/skip path; simultaneous submissions yield one result |
| Plan work | [story ref] proposes Action Plans; templates deferred | Show next action, owner role and parent contract context; task routing follows approved template | Missing template is an actionable error, not an empty “successful” plan |
| Progress or postpone | [planning workbook] stage rows and [question ref] | Record stage evidence and Delay Reason when date moves later; surface missing fields near the action | Stage-specific validation explains unmet gate and preserves input |
| Close and learn | [question ref]/[story ref] and parking first-dose request | Capture win/loss reason and Other notes; invalid generated record closes Lost with special reason; pending revenue moves only under approved actual-dose matching | A late or unmatched dose is held for review; a closed record is not silently reopened. Reversal policy [decision ref] remains open |

Readiness: [requirement refs] are designed as scenarios, but [decision ref] prevent final acceptance. Tests: corresponding acceptance-criteria IDs, especially duplicate and unauthorized-edit cases.

#### UJ02 Coordinate a contract and its sites

Actors P02/P07/P01/P06, jobs J02/J07. Trigger: new contract, amendment or Realignment (semantics [decision ref]), on a Contracting Entity. Preconditions: authorized contract territory/access, target products and eligible child-site facts.

| Step | Current evidence | Proposed interaction, state and handoff | Exception and recovery |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open contract pursuit | [question ref] replaces separate [strategic record type]-to-[legacy record type] creation with parent/child coordination | Create contract opportunity, select product scope, preview all child sites and existing pursuits | No children or ambiguous site parent produces a review list; no silent creation under another entity |
| Associate sites | [question ref] requires every child site; [question ref] supports two contracts if products differ | Preview create/attach/conflict counts. Select or confirm associations under [decision ref]; display exact product coverage | Existing opportunity with conflicting coverage stays unchanged; operations are idempotent and errors show which site failed |
| Develop terms | Contract Solution stage requires linked Schedule Terms | Create/link terms and show version; hand off pricing review in Negotiate | Missing Product Terms or mismatched variants blocks economic approval |
| Evaluate price | [question ref]/[story ref] bypass or pricing committee review | Show price class mix, gross/net revenue, margins and applicable rule version; record bypass or approval | Missing threshold cannot imply approval; revised pricing invalidates stale approval per proposed policy |
| Execute and synchronize | [question ref] | Only contract won + signed/executed terms (Active interpretation [decision ref]) + eligible site/product can move children to Pending Revenue | Lost parent leaves children open. Replayed/out-of-order events are safe; held events retry after facts resolve |
| Maintain economics | [question ref]/[story ref] | Reprice eligible Commercial lines; preserve VA/340B and previous values; roll up child figures for contract context | Missing price keeps prior/list price and exception; closed-child policy requires [decision ref] |

First value: a contract pursuit with an explainable site/product coverage map. Exit: lifecycle complete with linked terms and child outcome audit. Source-only contract roll-ups are contextual and excluded from site forecast totals.

#### UJ03 Estimate product mix and review the forecast

Actors P01/P03/P05, jobs J03/J04. Trigger: initial annual brand estimate or a changed estimate/price. Preconditions: validated product mapping, business-day calendar, price-class mix and governed rates.

1. Rep enters an annual **brand-level** quantity while viewing site [market data source] ([question ref]). If no mix exists, prompt for estimated Commercial/340B/VA shares; record that basis.
2. Preview the 12-month allocation using approved business-day metadata and product mix. Show annual total, class totals and monthly subtotals before save. Missing or invalid mix/calendar blocks generation with specific correction.
3. Save monthly facts under the selected [decision ref] option. Rep edits permitted product-line values; show whether an edit pins the month or redistributes the remainder. Preserve a before/after summary. Do not overwrite edits on regeneration without an approved policy.
4. Calculate [question ref] gross/net revenue and gross/net margin; display missing fee/COGS inputs as incomplete rather than zero. Show formula inputs and effective dates to permitted reviewers.
5. Finance selects period, brand/product, territory and net measure. Site facts roll up once to region/US; contract value is a separate contextual view. Gross view is a desired optional alternative, not an accepted toggle implementation.
6. Drill into differences. Correct mapping or source values through their steward, regenerate only impacted facts and preserve audit. No quota means no attainment percentage; target period/basis requires [decision ref].

Current evidence: legacy monthly fields cannot support the multi-product cycle ([story ref]); the source does not establish a currently functioning net forecast. First value: one complete reconciled estimate. Acceptance: [requirement refs] plus [requirement ref], with [decision ref] gating build.

#### UJ04 Review and activate opportunity generation

Actors P04/P03, job J05. Current evidence: [data gate] gates remain unstarted; [question ref] values are placeholders; [question ref] replaces the fallback with missing-metrics logs.

| State | Proposed work and output | Failure/recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Draft rule | Select immutable rule version, look-back, effective product mapping and threshold bands | Unknown thresholds remain draft; do not interpret dry-run acceptance as production approval |
| Dry run | Produce candidate ledger with reason, metrics, proposed action and duplicate disposition; no opportunity inserts | Missing metrics log tied to site/run; missing actuals distinguished from confirmed zero |
| Reconciled | Compare validated seed and candidate set by inclusion/exclusion, changed population and source freshness | Count equality alone insufficient; explain every discrepancy and get disposition |
| Approved | [data gate] evidence, owner/date completion and Sales Ops sign-off bind to exact rule/configuration version | Any material rule/source change returns to review; no approval copied to a new version |
| Active | Authorized activation enables insert/attach/skip and Action Plans in bounded batches | Error isolation, retry keys and kill switch prevent repeats; monitoring receipt records outcomes |
| Suspended | Disable further creation while investigating affected run and record lineage | Correct source/config, rehearse replay, obtain required renewed approval and resume |

First value: an explainable candidate list is useful before production activation. [story ref] launch generation and [story ref] gap/capacity rules share duplicate/idempotency controls; launch does not bypass [data gate]. [requirement refs] discovery remains outside active rules.

#### UJ05 Renew or record product loss

Actors P02/P07/P01, job J06. Trigger: Active non-base terms approach 120-day renewal point ([question ref]/[story ref]), expire without equivalent coverage, or have an earlier end date ([question ref]/[story ref]).

1. Preview/source job identifies the terms and exact product coverage. Create/reuse one renewal; record terms identity and source event.
2. Link appropriate site opportunities under [decision ref] and show expiration, terms scope and Action Plan.
3. If a successor activates, compare covered products, not merely presence of a successor. A complete renewal can win; partial renewal separates covered and uncovered products without double counting.
4. Non-renewal/early termination records loss and assigns reason follow-up. Existing child selling opportunities remain open.
5. If dates or coverage are corrected, route to the authorized reviewer using original event lineage. Do not manufacture an additional lost opportunity each daily run.

First value: a timely renewal with product-specific exposure. Current job implementation and backlog run semantics are unverified. [requirement refs] acceptance needs boundary-day, missed-run, repeated-event and partial-product fixtures.

#### UJ06 Align territories and cut over

Actors P04/P03/P05, job J08. Current evidence: [question ref] describes monthly minor changes and ad hoc model replacement; [story ref] identifies legacy flows and fields.

1. Preview changed account territories, access memberships and primary forecast assignments separately. Unresolved [strategic record type] mapping blocks that cohort.
2. Compare old/new visibility and totals. Authorized users retain intended edit rights; unrelated users do not gain access. Open opportunities move; closed-history handling follows approved reporting policy.
3. Rehearse migration and cutover using immutable extracts, field/value crosswalks and dependencies. Validate EMEA/APAC and CLM as distinct regression populations.
4. At approved cutover, close [legacy record type] records per source decision; handle [strategic record type] with a separately approved disposition. Change shared probabilities only at the accepted time.
5. Freeze/deactivate legacy writers only after parity and downstream sign-off. Retain old fields read-only until consumers and retention allow removal.
6. If reconciliation or access fails, stop generation, restore the approved prior configuration and replay/compensate data through the migration ledger; recheck forecast and permissions before reopening.

First value: a tested transition plan with visible affected records. This package executes none of these steps. Test destinations and required receipts are in the delivery plan.

examples.title: New-patient journey and service blueprint for a dental group
examples.markdown:
## Request

Build a new-patient journey map and service blueprint for Brightwell Dental Partners from the research notes in ./inputs/, with the opportunities it shows. Make it something the ops director can review.

## Inputs

Run of the built `map-journey` task package. All inputs below are invented. The run had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### research-notes.md

#### Brightwell Dental Partners — new-patient journey research (fictional)

Sources: 6 front-desk staff interviews (2 offices), 8 new-patient phone interviews, call-log sample of 200 new-patient calls, and the current paper intake packet.

Findings:
- Patients find Brightwell through insurance directory (45% of interviewees) or Google Maps (40%).
- Booking is phone only. Call log: 31% of new-patient calls go to voicemail at lunch or after 5pm; 1 in 3 voicemails is never returned the same day.
- Front desk asks for insurance details on the phone; staff say 25% of patients don't have the card handy.
- Patients receive a 6-page paper packet at check-in. Interviewees: "I filled in my medications twice." Average 18 minutes to complete in the waiting room (front-desk estimate).
- Front desk re-keys the packet into DentaCore; staff report 10–15 minutes per new patient and frequent illegible handwriting.
- Insurance verification happens the morning of the appointment; 12% of new patients have a coverage problem discovered at check-in (staff estimate).
- After the first visit, the treatment plan and cost estimate is printed; 3 of 8 patients said they did not understand what insurance would pay.
- Patients who had a good front-desk interaction mentioned the person's name.

## Output

### Brightwell new-patient journey map: ready for the ops director's review

I built a Markdown journey map, service blueprint and opportunity map for a new patient who books by phone, from searching for a dentist to receiving the printed treatment plan and cost estimate. It is a current-state map, version 0.1. The full document is `out/brightwell-new-patient-journey-map.md`.

#### What the research shows

The losses sit before the patient reaches the chair:

- **Booking:** 31% of the 200 sampled new-patient calls go to voicemail at lunch or after 5pm, and 1 in 3 voicemails is not returned the same day.
- **Insurance:** staff say 25% of patients don't have the card handy on the phone. Verification runs the morning of the appointment, and staff estimate 12% of new patients have a coverage problem found at check-in.
- **Check-in:** patients fill in a 6-page paper packet in the waiting room (about 18 minutes, front-desk estimate), then staff re-key it into DentaCore (10–15 minutes, staff report). One patient said, "I filled in my medications twice."
- **After the visit:** 3 of 8 patients did not understand what insurance would pay.
- **Keep:** patients who had a good front-desk interaction remembered the person's name.

#### Journey phases

| Phase | Reported or observed | Feeling captured |
|---|---|---|
| P1 Find (directory 45%, Google Maps 40%) | Directory and Maps listings | Not captured |
| P2 Book (phone only, voicemail, insurance on the call) | Call log, staff | Not captured |
| P3 Before the visit (verification the morning of) | Staff | Not captured |
| P4 Check-in (paper packet, re-keying, coverage surprise) | Patient quote, staff | Repetition, not a named feeling |
| P5 First visit | Not captured | Not captured |
| P6 Plan and cost | Patient interviews | Confusion about insurance payment (3 of 8) |

The notes carry almost no feelings, so there is no emotional curve and no invented scores.

#### Blueprint finding

The notes don't say what patients can see of staff work. Voicemail callbacks, the morning verification, re-keying and estimate preparation therefore sit in a "visibility not captured" row and not in back-stage. No back-stage action is established from the evidence. Confirming where these fall is the first validation task.

#### Opportunities (effort and impact are labels; owners and outcomes are proposals)

| # | Opportunity | How it changes the step | Measure | Effort / impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Named person per office clears voicemail at midday and close; same-business-day callback | Acts after the voicemail is left, so it recovers calls and does not reduce voicemails | Share of new-patient voicemails with an outbound call the same business day (voicemail timestamp to first outbound call), baselined from the call log | S / H |
| O2 | Verify insurance on the day of booking; ask patients to have the card ready; follow up with those who don't | Acts days before check-in, while the patient can still be reached | Share of new patients whose coverage problem is first found at check-in; count from records, since 12% is an estimate | M / H |
| O3a | Audit the packet and remove repeated questions | Changes content, not when it is filled in | Pages and fields before and after | S / M |
| O3b | Intake before the visit that writes into DentaCore | Moves completion off the waiting room and removes re-keying, if DentaCore can accept it (not captured) | Timed arrival-to-check-in minutes; staff minutes per new patient | L / H |
| O4 | Estimate shows insurance payment and patient balance separately, with a staff walk-through | Acts after the plan is printed, on understanding, not on cost | Patient can state what insurance pays and what they owe at handoff | M / M |
| O5 | Keep named, personal front-desk contact in any change | Protects a reported strength | None proposed | none |

Quick wins are O1 and O3a. O3b is the one strategic bet. I did not propose online booking: the notes record no patient demand for it.

#### Limits to know

- The 18 minutes, 10–15 minutes, 25% and 12% are staff estimates, not measurements.
- The discovery shares of 45% and 40% don't divide evenly into 8 interviews, and the notes don't give the base.
- The packet's contents were not supplied, so which pages repeat the medication question is unknown.
- The first visit, patient goals and most thoughts and feelings are not captured. The document lists seven validation questions with whom to ask.

#### Checks

Done by hand: claim-to-source reconciliation, feeling and quote parity, blueprint visibility classification and measure timing against each action. Not run: the bundled build and self-test scripts (no script execution here), the writing checker, quality gate and brand rendering. No HTML board was built. Evidence-core does not apply, because this is a standalone research map with no engagement ledger.

#### Files

- `out/brightwell-new-patient-journey-map.md`: full journey map, blueprint, opportunity map, source ledger and validation questions
- `out/answer.md`: this summary

### File: brightwell-new-patient-journey-map.md

#### Brightwell Dental Partners: new-patient journey map, service blueprint and opportunities

Version 0.1 · 2026-11-04 · Current state · For review by the operations director

##### Recommendation

Fix the front end of the journey first. The notes show three losses before the patient reaches the chair: voicemails that go unreturned (booking), insurance problems found only at check-in (before the visit and check-in), and a paper packet that patients complete in the waiting room and staff then re-key (check-in). The after-visit cost estimate is the fourth problem, and the one patients said they did not understand.

Proposed order, each a proposal to validate:

1. Set a same-day callback rule for voicemails, with lunch and after-5pm coverage. Small effort.
2. Move insurance verification from the morning of the visit to the day of booking, and ask for the card ahead of the call. Medium effort.
3. Audit the packet for repeated questions, then move intake before the visit. The audit is small. Pre-visit intake is a larger bet, because it depends on what DentaCore can accept, and the notes do not say.
4. Rework the cost estimate so it shows what insurance pays and what the patient owes. Medium effort, after finding out how estimates are built.

##### Scope

**Actor:** a new adult patient who books by phone at one of the Brightwell offices.
**Journey:** from searching for a dentist to receiving the printed treatment plan and cost estimate after the first visit.
**State:** current. Nothing here shows a changed process.
**Offices in the research:** 2 (not named in the notes).

##### Evidence basis

| Source | Size | Type | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|

research-notes.md
Brightwell Dental Partners — new-patient journey research (fictional)

Sources: 6 front-desk staff interviews (2 offices), 8 new-patient phone interviews, call-log sample of 200 new-patient calls, and the current paper intake packet.

Findings:

  • Patients find Brightwell through insurance directory (45% of interviewees) or Google Maps (40%).
  • Booking is phone only. Call log: 31% of new-patient calls go to voicemail at lunch or after 5pm; 1 in 3 voicemails is never returned the same day.
  • Front desk asks for insurance details on the phone; staff say 25% of patients don't have the card handy.
  • Patients receive a 6-page paper packet at check-in. Interviewees: "I filled in my medications twice." Average 18 minutes to complete in the waiting room (front-desk estimate).
  • Front desk re-keys the packet into DentaCore; staff report 10–15 minutes per new patient and frequent illegible handwriting.
  • Insurance verification happens the morning of the appointment; 12% of new patients have a coverage problem discovered at check-in (staff estimate).
  • After the first visit, the treatment plan and cost estimate is printed; 3 of 8 patients said they did not understand what insurance would pay.
  • Patients who had a good front-desk interaction mentioned the person's name.

Output

Brightwell new-patient journey map: ready for the ops director's review

I built a Markdown journey map, service blueprint and opportunity map for a new patient who books by phone, from searching for a dentist to receiving the printed treatment plan and cost estimate. It is a current-state map, version 0.1. The full document is out/brightwell-new-patient-journey-map.md.

What the research shows

The losses sit before the patient reaches the chair:

  • Booking: 31% of the 200 sampled new-patient calls go to voicemail at lunch or after 5pm, and 1 in 3 voicemails is not returned the same day.
  • Insurance: staff say 25% of patients don't have the card handy on the phone. Verification runs the morning of the appointment, and staff estimate 12% of new patients have a coverage problem found at check-in.
  • Check-in: patients fill in a 6-page paper packet in the waiting room (about 18 minutes, front-desk estimate), then staff re-key it into DentaCore (10–15 minutes, staff report). One patient said, "I filled in my medications twice."
  • After the visit: 3 of 8 patients did not understand what insurance would pay.
  • Keep: patients who had a good front-desk interaction remembered the person's name.

Recommendation

Fix the front end of the journey first. guide.overview: It reads the supplied notes, workbooks and exports to reconstruct each process from its trigger to completion. It identifies the people involved, handoffs, record grain and authoritative system for each business record, including territory and opportunity ownership where relevant. It produces an explanation, diagram and ownership tables with source-linked questions wherever the evidence does not establish a rule.
guide.value: Reconstruct who does what from the event that starts a sales process through its handoffs and completion. It explains which system owns each record so territory or opportunity rules do not become disconnected boxes on a diagram.

---
name: map-sales-process
description: Map sales processes from discovery files, workbooks, CRM or Jira exports and operating notes. Trace triggers, ownership, handoffs and systems of record, including territory assignment and opportunity creation when relevant.
---

# Map sales process

Explain the business process first: what the customer is trying to accomplish, what starts the work, who moves it forward, and what counts as finished. Connect that explanation to the records and systems used along the way.

## Establish the source set

Start with supplied files and the project's current source authority. Inventory the available material before asking the user for more. Record each source's title, date or revision, type, and useful locator: page, section, worksheet and row, issue key, or event ID. Preserve originals.

Read the relevant content completely in bounded parts. A filename, attachment tile, HTML application shell, short Markdown pointer, or summary does not establish the underlying process. Follow an accessible referenced source; otherwise identify the missing content and proceed with the supported portion.

For CSV exports, preserve repeated headers and every comment column by position or indexed names. Handle quoted multiline cells and byte-order marks. Reconcile duplicate issue keys and revisions without discarding conflicting statements. A ticket assignee is not automatically the business owner. A ticket marked Done does not establish deployed behavior or business adoption.

If Computer History is supplied, use its skill to locate the relevant events and distinguish submitted requests, unsent drafts, user actions, and assistant explanations. Upgrade factual claims to the underlying files or connected records. Do not make Computer History a prerequisite for ordinary mapping requests.

## Find the actual processes

Identify the customer and selling model from the evidence. Distinguish buyer, contracting entity, operating site, service recipient, product or indication, and other entities where they change the workflow. Explain their relationships in ordinary language.

Treat labels such as new business, existing business, expansion, renewal, and lead conversion as candidates. Use the names and boundaries the sources support. Do not impose a generic lead-to-cash funnel or assume that every sale starts with a lead. A lead conversion, new product at an existing site, contract negotiation, onboarding, and recurring order may be separate processes with different triggers and owners.

Begin with a short business explanation and a process inventory. For each process establish its start event, entry conditions, business outcome, customer or product scope, and relationship to other processes. Show which process is being changed by the requested solution. Keep adjacent processes visible only where they supply an input or receive a handoff.

## Trace each process

Map the supported path as:

`business event → eligibility or decision → action → record change → handoff → completion`

For each meaningful step, capture:

- The business trigger, required inputs, and decision rule. Separate the business event from a database creation event, a scheduled job, or a stage transition.
- The person or role doing the work, the accountable decision owner where known, and the next recipient. Keep process owner, account owner, opportunity owner, territory member, and task assignee distinct.
- The record created or updated, its grain, and the system that owns the relevant fact. State what one record represents, such as a site/product pursuit or a contracting-entity agreement.
- The output, recipient acceptance condition, and exit criterion. A handoff is incomplete if the receiving team or required record is missing.
- Material rejection, duplicate, missing-data, reassignment, and rework paths supported by the sources. Mark an undocumented path as an open question rather than filling it with a plausible rule.

Keep current behavior, documented requirements, and proposed changes separate. Retain dates and release stages when an older rule differs from a newer one. Resolve a conflict only through an authoritative decision or direct verification; recency alone does not settle it.

## Resolve assignment and record authority

When territory or opportunity ownership matters, trace each relationship separately:

`territory definition → account coverage → opportunity territory → opportunity owner → task assignments`

Check what defines territories, which source supplies boundaries and membership, what assigns the account, what selects an opportunity's territory, and what chooses its owner. Explain tie-breaks, vacancies, multiple matches, manual overrides, staffing changes, and open versus closed records only to the extent documented. Keep record access and forecast rollup separate from ownership. A territory assignment is not evidence that an opportunity must be created.

For opportunity creation, identify the initiating person or system, qualifying business condition, required account and product context, record grain, duplicate check, and resulting owner. Separate manual and automated routes when both exist. Do not infer an opportunity from every order, activity, product interest, or account update.

Build system-of-record assignments at the entity or fact level. Distinguish where a fact originates, where users maintain it, where it is synchronized, and where it is reported. Name the synchronization direction and timing when supported. A CRM, ERP, spreadsheet, and reporting dashboard may own different facts in the same process. Do not assign all authority to the most visible application or infer an integration from two matching values.

## Deliver the map

For a full map, read [the output model and worked example](references/output-model.md). Adapt its fields to the requested scope; a focused ownership question needs only the relevant path and evidence.

Default to a concise explanation, a readable process diagram, and supporting tables. Use Mermaid for a small static map; use an editable document or interactive view when the requested scale or format warrants it. Match diagram labels and step IDs to the tables. Show customer events, decisions, roles, and handoffs in the primary view; put field names and technical details beside the relevant step or in an appendix.

Include source locators for rules and a short decision list for consequential gaps. For each gap state what is unknown, which path it affects, and who can resolve it if the evidence identifies that role. Any suggested reviewer is a proposal. Missing sources should narrow the claim, not stop all useful mapping.

## Check the result

Walk one representative case from trigger through completion and one material exception using the supplied evidence. Confirm that the diagram and tables agree about owners, sequence, record grain, and system authority. Check that every supported rule has a locator and every unresolved rule stays unresolved in both views. Ensure that a generated explanation has not become its own factual source.

Apply `review-writing` to the complete map and accompanying replies. Read its full pattern references, preserve the source facts and qualifications, and review manually if its scanner is unavailable. When writing as a named person, apply their confirmed writing profile if supplied.

Read the finished map for business meaning: a reader should be able to say what happens, why it starts, who acts next, and where the result is recorded. A diagram render or schema check cannot establish those facts.

Creating a map does not authorize changes to CRM records, territory rules, Jira issues, permissions, or source files, or sending the map to another person. Report the saved location and validation performed without claiming implementation or adoption.

examples.title: Map add-on opportunity creation and ownership at existing hospital sites
examples.markdown:
## Request

We're rolling out automatic opportunity creation and owner assignment for add-on product sales at existing hospital sites. Can you map how this works today and what's being proposed, using the attached notes, Jira export and systems register? I need to know who owns what and which questions are still open before we brief the CRM team.

## Inputs

Run of the built `map-sales-process` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### jira-export.csv

Key,Summary,Status,Assignee,Description,Comment,Comment
TERR-21,Auto-create add-on opportunity from ERP first-order signal,To Do,Devon Reyes,"Create an opportunity when the ERP shows an order for a product line the site has not bought before.",Ana Silva: This would create opportunities after the sale. Should it be at request time instead?,Devon Reyes: Parked until TERR-24 is settled.
TERR-24,Select territory for add-on opportunity,In Progress,Devon Reyes,"Site has one geographic territory and one specialty territory per product line. Opportunity territory = specialty territory for the product line. Owner = the territory's primary rep.","Ana Silva: If the primary rep seat is vacant, fall back to the geographic territory rep?","Devon Reyes: Not decided. Sales leadership to rule."
TERR-26,Block duplicate add-on opportunities,Done,Kofi Mensah,"Duplicate check on site + product line in CRM.","Kofi Mensah: Rule added to the test sandbox 20 Oct.","Priya Anand: Not in production yet; release is not scheduled."

#### operating-note.md

#### Add-on product requests: operating note
Revision 3, 12 Sept 2026. Author: Priya Anand, Commercial Operations

##### 1. Scope
Northwind Clinical Supply sells infusion, monitoring and wound-care product lines to hospital systems. A hospital system signs a master agreement (the contracting entity). Each hospital in the system is a site that orders and uses product. This note covers a site that already buys from us and asks for an additional product line.

##### 2. Current process
1. A site's materials manager emails or calls their account manager to ask for a new product line.
2. The account manager logs the request in the shared Requests tab of the "Add-on tracker" spreadsheet (site, product line, date, requester).
3. Commercial Operations checks the CRM for an open opportunity for the same site and product line. A closed-lost opportunity less than 90 days old also blocks a new one.
4. If none exists, the account manager creates the opportunity in the CRM and owns it.
5. Pricing under the master agreement is confirmed by Contracts before a quote is issued. If the product line is not on the agreement, Contracts opens an amendment; the opportunity waits.
6. When the first order is placed, Customer Onboarding takes over setup for the new line.

##### 3. Known problems
Account managers sometimes skip step 2. Duplicates appear when two managers cover one health system.

#### systems-register.md

#### Systems register (extract)
Updated 30 Sept 2026

| Row | Fact | System | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Product line codes, orders, first-order date | ERP | CRM receives product line codes nightly |
| 3 | Site, contracting entity, territory assignment of site | CRM | Maintained by Sales Operations |
| 5 | Opportunity, stage, owner | CRM | |
| 6 | Master agreement terms, amendments | Contract repository | Managed by Contracts; not synced to CRM |
| 8 | Add-on request log | Add-on tracker spreadsheet | Manual entry; not synced |

## Output

I mapped add-on opportunity creation and ownership from the operating note, the Jira export and the systems register. Today the account manager creates and owns the opportunity. Territory-based owner selection is only proposed, and it conflicts with the second proposal in two places. Eight questions are open, listed at the end.

#### The business process

Northwind contracts with a hospital system under a master agreement, and each hospital is a site that orders product. A site that already buys asks for another product line. That is a product expansion at an existing site, not a lead conversion. The sources describe no new-customer path, so I did not map one.

| Process | Start | Outcome | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Add-on request to opportunity | Site asks its account manager for a new line | Opportunity in CRM, or request blocked | Current (operating note §2.1-2.4) |
| B. Pricing confirmation | Opportunity exists | Pricing confirmed, or amendment opened and opportunity waits | Current (§2.5) |
| C. Onboarding | First order placed | New line set up | Current, one line only (§2.6) |
| D. Territory and owner selection | Opportunity created | Territory and owner set by rule | Proposed, TERR-24, In Progress |
| E. Auto-create from ERP first order | ERP shows an order for a line new to the site | System creates opportunity | Proposed, TERR-21, To Do and parked |

#### Current path

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["Site asks for another product line"] --> A1["A1: Account manager logs request in tracker"]
    A1 --> A2["A2: Commercial Operations checks CRM for open or recent closed-lost"]
    A2 --> Q{"Blocking opportunity?"}
    Q -->|Yes| X["Duplicate handling: unresolved"]
    Q -->|No| A3["A3: Account manager creates CRM opportunity and owns it"]
    A3 --> B1{"B1: Product on master agreement?"}
    B1 -->|Yes| B2["B2: Contracts confirms pricing; quote"]
    B1 -->|No| B3["B3: Contracts opens amendment; opportunity waits"]
    B2 --> C1["C1: First order; Customer Onboarding sets up line"]
    A3 -. "Proposed TERR-24" .-> D1["D1: Specialty territory selects owner"]
    D1 -. "Vacant seat" .-> V["Fallback undecided"]
    C1 -. "Proposed TERR-21: ERP first order creates opportunity" .-> E1["E1: Auto-create, after the sale"]
```

Solid lines are current. Dotted lines are proposals, and none is confirmed as running.

1. **A1.** The account manager logs site, product line, date and requester in the Add-on tracker spreadsheet. Managers sometimes skip this.
2. **A2.** Commercial Operations checks the CRM by site and product line. An open opportunity blocks creation, and so does a closed-lost one under 90 days old.
3. **A3.** If nothing blocks, the account manager creates the opportunity. One opportunity represents one site and one product line. The creator owns it.
4. **B.** Contracts confirms pricing under the master agreement before a quote. If the line is not on the agreement, Contracts opens an amendment and the opportunity waits.
5. **C1.** The first order triggers Customer Onboarding.

#### Ownership

| Object | Rule | Responsible | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Request row | Manual entry | Account manager | Operating note §2.2 |
| Opportunity, today | Creator owns | Account manager | §2.4 |
| Opportunity, proposed | Territory = the site's specialty territory for the product line. Owner = that territory's primary rep | Territory primary rep | TERR-24 |
| Jira tickets | Work assignment only | Devon Reyes (TERR-21, TERR-24), Kofi Mensah (TERR-26) | Export |

The Jira assignees are not the business owners. The sources do not say whether the account manager and the territory primary rep are the same person.

#### Systems of record

| Fact | System | Maintainer | Transfer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Product line codes, orders, first-order date | ERP | Not stated | Codes sent to CRM nightly (register row 2) |
| Site, contracting entity, site territory | CRM | Sales Operations | n/a (row 3) |
| Opportunity, stage, owner | CRM | Account manager today | n/a (row 5) |
| Agreement terms and amendments | Contract repository | Contracts | Not synced to CRM (row 6) |
| Request log | Add-on tracker | Account managers | Manual, not synced (row 8) |

#### What the tickets do and do not establish

- **TERR-26** (duplicate block) shows Done. Priya Anand's comment says the rule is in the test sandbox only, since 20 Oct, with no production release scheduled. It is not running. Its description also leaves out the 90-day closed-lost condition from the operating note.
- **TERR-21** would create the opportunity from the ERP first-order signal. That is after the sale, while today's process creates it at request time. Ana Silva raised this in a comment and the ticket is parked behind TERR-24.
- **TERR-24** is In Progress. Its vacancy fallback is undecided, and sales leadership is to rule.

#### Decisions needed

| Question | Affects | Proposed decision owner |
|---|---|---|
| Is the opportunity created at request time (A3) or from the ERP first order (E1)? E1 would fire after A3 already created it. | A3, E1 | Commercial Operations with sales leadership |
| What happens to a blocked request, and who tells the account manager? | A2 | Unknown |
| Who owns the opportunity when the territory primary rep differs from the requesting account manager? | A3, D1 | Sales leadership |
| What is the fallback for a vacant primary seat, and how are staffing changes and multiple matches handled? | D1 | Sales leadership (named in TERR-24) |
| Does the production duplicate rule include the 90-day closed-lost block? | A2, TERR-26 release | Unknown |
| Are Commercial Operations (operating note) and Sales Operations (register row 3) the same team? | A2 owner, CRM maintainer | Unknown |
| How does Contracts learn of an opportunity, and what stage marks "waiting on amendment"? | B3 | Contracts, as a proposal |
| What does the geographic territory do beyond the TERR-24 fallback? | D1 | Unknown |

#### Walk-through

**Typical case.** A materials manager asks for the wound-care line. The account manager logs it (A1). No open or recent closed-lost opportunity exists (A2). The account manager creates and owns the opportunity (A3). The line is on the agreement, so Contracts confirms pricing (B2). The first order starts onboarding (C1).

**Exception.** The line is not on the agreement. Contracts opens an amendment and the opportunity waits (B3). What releases the wait is not documented. The vacant-seat case exists only in the proposal and is also unresolved.

#### Limits

I wrote no scripts or scanner runs. I checked the prose against the writing patterns by reading it, because the scanner was not run here. Nothing in CRM, Jira, territory rules or the source files was changed, and nothing was sent to anyone. The map is prepared locally.

#### Files

- `out/addon-process-map.md`: the full map, with the inventory, step-detail table, ownership and systems tables, the decisions table and the walk-through. The tables above are condensed from it.

### File: addon-process-map.md

#### Add-on product opportunities at existing hospital sites

##### What happens and why

Northwind Clinical Supply contracts with a hospital system under a master agreement. Each hospital in the system is a site that orders product. When a site that already buys from Northwind asks for another product line (infusion, monitoring or wound care), the request is a product expansion at an existing site. It is not a lead conversion, and the sources describe no new-customer path.

Sources used:
- S1: operating note, revision 3, 12 Sept 2026, sections 2 and 3
- S2: Jira export, TERR-21, TERR-24, TERR-26
- S3: systems register extract, 30 Sept 2026, rows 2, 3, 5, 6, 8

##### Process inventory

| Process | Scope | Start and entry condition | Completion | Related process | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Add-on request to opportunity (current) | One site and one product line | Site materials manager asks the account manager; site already buys | Opportunity exists in CRM, or request is blocked as a duplicate | Hands to B | S1 §2 steps 1-4 |
| B. Pricing confirmation (adjacent, current) | Contracting entity's master agreement | Opportunity exists | Pricing confirmed, or amendment opened and opportunity waits | Receives from A | S1 §2 step 5 |
| C. Onboarding (adjacent, current) | New line at the site | First order placed | Setup of the new line (not described further) | Receives from A/B | S1 §2 step 6 |
| D. Territory and owner selection (proposed) | Site and product line | Opportunity created | Opportunity territory and owner set by rule | Would run inside A | S2 TERR-24, In Progress |
| E. Auto-create from ERP first order (proposed) | Site and product line | ERP shows an order for a line the site has not bought | Opportunity created by system | Would replace or duplicate A step A4 | S2 TERR-21, To Do |

##### Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["Site asks for another product line"] --> A1["A1: Account manager logs request in tracker"]
    A1 --> A2["A2: Commercial Operations checks CRM for open or recent closed-lost"]
    A2 --> Q{"Blocking opportunity?"}
    Q -->|Yes| X["Duplicate handling: unresolved"]
    Q -->|No| A3["A3: Account manager creates CRM opportunity and owns it"]
    A3 --> B1{"B1: Product on master agreement?"}
    B1 -->|Yes| B2["B2: Contracts confirms pricing; quote"]
    B1 -->|No| B3["B3: Contracts opens amendment; opportunity waits"]
    B2 --> C1["C1: First order; Customer Onboarding sets up line"]
    A3 -. "Proposed TERR-24" .-> D1["D1: Specialty territory selects owner"]
    D1 -. "Vacant seat" .-> V["Fallback undecided"]
    C1 -. "Proposed TERR-21: ERP first order creates opportunity" .-> E1["E1: Auto-create, after the sale"]
```

Solid lines are current (S1). Dotted lines are proposals; none is confirmed as running.

##### Step detail

| Step | Trigger or decision | Action and performer | Accountable role | Record and system | Output and recipient | Exception | Evidence and state |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Site request by email or call | Account manager logs site, product line, date, requester | Unresolved | One request row; Add-on tracker, manual | Row visible to Commercial Operations | Managers sometimes skip it | S1 §2.2, §3; S3 row 8; current |
| A2 | Request logged | Commercial Operations searches CRM by site and product line | Unresolved | Reads opportunities; CRM | Go or block decision to account manager | Open opportunity, or closed-lost under 90 days, blocks creation. Handling of a blocked request is undocumented | S1 §2.3; current |
| A3 | No blocking opportunity | Account manager creates the opportunity | Account manager (owner) | One opportunity per site and product line; CRM | Opportunity ready for pricing | None documented | S1 §2.4; S3 row 5; current |
| B1-B3 | Opportunity exists | Contracts checks the agreement; quotes or opens an amendment | Contracts | Agreement terms; contract repository | Priced quote, or amendment with opportunity waiting | Waiting stage and release condition undocumented | S1 §2.5; S3 row 6; current |
| C1 | First order placed | Customer Onboarding sets up the line | Customer Onboarding | First-order date; ERP | Line set up | Not described | S1 §2.6; S3 row 2; current |
| D1 | Opportunity created | Opportunity territory = the site's specialty territory for the product line; owner = that territory's primary rep | Sales leadership (rules on gaps) | Opportunity territory and owner; CRM | Owner assigned | Vacant primary seat: undecided | S2 TERR-24; proposal |
| E1 | ERP order for a line new to the site | System creates opportunity | Unresolved | Opportunity; CRM fed by ERP | Opportunity created | Fires after the order | S2 TERR-21; proposal, parked |

Note on TERR-26: the duplicate rule on site and product line is in the test sandbox since 20 Oct and is not in production, with no release scheduled (Priya Anand's comment). Its description omits the 90-day closed-lost condition from S1. The status Done reflects sandbox work only.

##### Ownership

| Object or task | Assignment input | Rule | Responsible | Override | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Add-on request row | Account manager's contact with site | Manual entry | Account manager | None documented | S1 §2.2 |

Add-on product requests: operating note

Revision 3, 12 Sept 2026. Author: Priya Anand, Commercial Operations

1. Scope

Northwind Clinical Supply sells infusion, monitoring and wound-care product lines to hospital systems. A hospital system signs a master agreement (the contracting entity). Each hospital in the system is a site that orders and uses product. This note covers a site that already buys from us and asks for an additional product line.

2. Current process
  1. A site's materials manager emails or calls their account manager to ask for a new product line.
  2. The account manager logs the request in the shared Requests tab of the "Add-on tracker" spreadsheet (site, product line, date, requester).
  3. Commercial Operations checks the CRM for an open opportunity for the same site and product line. A closed-lost opportunity less than 90 days old also blocks a new one.
  4. If none exists, the account manager creates the opportunity in the CRM and owns it.
  5. Pricing under the master agreement is confirmed by Contracts before a quote is issued. If the product line is not on the agreement, Contracts opens an amendment; the opportunity waits.
  6. When the first order is placed, Customer Onboarding takes over setup for the new line.
3. Known problems

Account managers sometimes skip step 2. Duplicates appear when two managers cover one health system.

skills.markdown:
---
name: operate-salesforce-pipeline
description: 'Operate a repo''s sf-deploy-engine Salesforce pipeline (pipeline.yml): validate and deploy to preprod, staging or production, cut a release, roll back by ticket or SHA, revalidate, recover a frozen environment, pause or resume the engine, or provision a new instance. Use for deploy to prod, promote, what needs to ship, rollback, validation failed, environment frozen, or a PR that targets an environment branch. For the local sandbox loop, worktrees and git hooks, use configure-salesforce-project.'
metadata:
  canon_exempt: 'engineering-doc'
  canon_exempt_reason: 'auth contract, API payloads and the refusal matrix must be in hand before the agent acts on an org'
---


# Operate salesforce pipeline

The engine is an always-on orchestrator that owns Salesforce deployments to
**pipeline environments** through GitHub webhooks, one single-threaded FSM worker
per environment, and strict git-to-org synchronization. It takes over at the
first environment branch and owns everything upward.

**This skill starts at the PR into an environment branch.** Everything before
that — the ticket, the worktree, the local dry run, the deploy to your own dev
sandbox, the git and agent lifecycle hooks that enforce it — is `configure-salesforce-project`,
and that skill works the same whether or not an engine sits above it. Do not
duplicate its rules here and do not answer local-loop questions from this skill.

**This is a layer, not a fork.** The engine ships its own two guards
(`scripts/init.sh` installs them), which read `pipeline.yml` and nothing else.
They add refusals on top of the local-loop stack, read none of its config, and
write none of its files. **An agent working the local loop needs to know nothing
about this layer and change nothing to accommodate it.** If you find yourself
about to edit `configure-salesforce-project` to make something here work, stop — that
is the seam being crossed, and the answer is a rule in this skill's own hooks.

**What the guards bind, stated precisely.** A Claude or Codex hook fires on a tool
call the *model* makes. A command a human types in a terminal or runs from an IDE
never passes through the harness. So the true claim is *"an agent cannot deploy
to a pipeline org through this session"* — **not** *"the pipeline orgs are
protected."* The controls that bind a human are branch protection and the org's
own permissions. Do not let anyone read more into a green `doctor.sh` than that.

---

## Sub-commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `/sf-deploy-engine` (no args) | Operate the pipeline. The default: status, promote, release, rollback, retry, revalidate. |
| `/sf-deploy-engine doctor` | Is this pipeline actually healthy? Read-only. `scripts/doctor.sh` |
| `/sf-deploy-engine init` | Point an existing repo at an already-running engine. `scripts/init.sh` |
| `/sf-deploy-engine provision` | Stand up a **new** engine instance: GCP, GitHub App, secrets, SSO. [references/provisioning.md](references/provisioning.md) |

Route on the argument: *status / promote / release / rollback / retry / frozen /
revalidate / what needs to ship* → operate. *doctor / audit / health / is the
engine ok / drift* → doctor. *init / onboard this repo / point at the engine* →
init. *provision / new instance / new client / GCP / GitHub App / rotate keys /
add an environment / build the vsix* → provisioning.

Provisioning is rare and one-time-per-client. It lives in a reference so it never
loads during a deploy.

---

## The boundary — get this right before anything else

| Where | Who deploys | How |
|---|---|---|
| Your dev sandbox | **You**, directly | `sf project deploy start`, governed by `configure-salesforce-project` |
| Any environment in `pipeline.yml` | **The engine**, exclusively | PR → engine validates → merge → engine deploys |

**Never run `sf project deploy` against a pipeline environment's org, for any
reason, including to fix something.** A manual deploy desyncs `deployed/<branch>`
from the org and the engine has no way to detect it. The recovery is Pause →
reconcile git and the tag by hand → Resume, and it is worse than whatever you
were trying to shortcut.

The two exceptions the schema allows are both narrow. `tier: sandbox` rows are
registered for **visibility only** — they produce the Dev Sandboxes board column
and are a legal `/api/release` source into a route entry point, but get no
worker, no `deployed/<branch>` tag and no engine-driven deploy. And `freeze:
advisory` relaxes the freeze gate for low-stakes tiers. Neither makes a sandbox
engine-managed. See `docs/decisions/sandboxes-are-environments.md` in the engine
repo before proposing otherwise.

---

## Core model

| Ref | Means | Moved by |
|---|---|---|
| Branch HEAD (`preprod`) | **Desired** org state | Merged PRs |
| Tag `deployed/<branch>` | **Actual** org state | The engine only |

Deltas are computed `deployed/<branch>` → SHA with sfdx-git-delta. A failed
deploy leaves the tag unmoved, so git still describes the org *at the tag* and
the gap stays queryable.

```
SETTLED → DEPLOYING → SETTLED (tag advanced)
             ↓ failure
          FROZEN → retry → DEPLOYING
             ↓ rollback (the revert lands as a push)
          DEPLOYING → SETTLED
```

Quick deploy (skip the 15-minute test run on merge) is eligible only when all
three hold: the validation ran on the same SHA, the org state is unchanged (the
tag has not moved), and the validation is under 10 days old. Any miss falls back
to a full deploy — that fallback is the design, not a bug.

**Fail-closed by construction:** engine down → required checks never go green →
nothing merges → nothing breaks.

---

## Authentication — do this first, once

`/` and `/api/*` are locked to Google Workspace SSO. **A bare `curl` against
`/api/*` returns 401 or 503, and older runbooks that show unauthenticated curl
are wrong.** Browser cookies do not reach a bash process and the VS Code token
lives in the OS keychain, so terminal callers mint their own:

1. Open `$ENGINE_URL/auth/login?redirect=cli` in a browser and sign in.
2. Follow that endpoint's login flow. Save the resulting token privately in an endpoint-specific file with mode 600; set `SFDE_TOKEN_FILE` to its absolute path. Never paste a token into chat.
3. Re-run that login when a call reports 401. The token lasts 30 days.

`scripts/engine.sh` reads only the explicit `SFDE_TOKEN_FILE` (or `SFDE_TOKEN`) and sends
`Authorization: Bearer`. No default token file is read. Confirm the token and endpoint belong to the same authorized account. Use the helper rather than hand-rolled curl — the release and
rollback payloads are the fiddly part.

```bash
export ENGINE_URL=$(grep '^engine_url:' pipeline.yml | awk '{print $2}')
scripts/engine.sh status
```

**Everything 503s but `/health`?** In always-on that is the SSO gate failing

## Daily operations

The command examples use synthetic ticket keys, branch names and sandbox labels. Resolve actual values from the authorized project configuration; examples do not identify an account or grant access.

Full payloads, response shapes and every endpoint:
[references/operations.md](references/operations.md).

### Where does everything stand

```bash
scripts/engine.sh status          # FSM state, in-flight item and queue per env
scripts/doctor.sh                 # the same, plus tag drift, config drift, auth, webhook health
```

`SETTLED` idle · `DEPLOYING` in progress · `FROZEN` failed, waiting on a human.

### What is ready to ship

```bash
scripts/doctor.sh --ready         # unpromoted merge commits per promotion edge
```

Promotions are cherry-picks, so a promoted merge gets a new SHA downstream and
`git log main..preprod` reports it as pending forever. This compares by
**patch-equivalence** of each merge's first-parent diff, which is what actually
drops shipped work off the list.

### Promote

Bulk, everything on the upstream branch:

```bash
gh pr create --base main --head preprod --title "RELEASE: preprod -> main ($(date +%F))"
```

Merge commit, never squash. Never delete the upstream branch.

Selective, specific tickets — this is what the dashboard's release builder does:

```bash
scripts/engine.sh release --from preprod GH-397 GH-401 EXAMPLE-42
```

Ticket identifiers are provider-aware: `GH-397`, a Jira key like `EXAMPLE-42`, the
canonical `jira:EXAMPLE-42`, or a bare issue number. An identifier no **configured**
provider recognises is rejected rather than guessed at.

One release can span several sources — different dev sandboxes, or a sandbox and
preprod together. `--from` applies to every ticket after it, until the next one:

```bash
scripts/engine.sh release --to preprod --from sandbox-a GH-397 --from sandbox-b GH-401
```

**`--from` is required** — there is no default source, and the API rejects a flat
ticket list without one. `--to` *is* optional: it defaults to the target every
selected source agrees on, and with no shared target the request is refused
rather than one being picked.

Two refusals worth recognising, both deliberate:

- *"No merged PR delivering GH-397 found on \<src\>"* — a release cherry-picks
  merge commits. Work pushed straight to a branch shows on the board (which reads
  commit messages) but is not releasable until it lands as a merge.
- An **unattributed commit** check fails the release when a candidate merge
  carries work no selected ticket accounts for. That is the ride-along guard;
  read what it names before overriding.

### Roll back

```bash
scripts/engine.sh rollback --env main --ticket GH-397        # resolves the deploy that carried it
scripts/engine.sh rollback --env main --sha <merge-commit>   # or name the merge yourself
```

`--mode pr` (default) opens a revert PR so the inverse deployment is validated
first. `--mode direct` pushes the revert straight to the branch — emergencies
only. `git revert -m 1` produces a diff sgd turns into the exact inverse package:
modified components at prior versions in `package.xml`, added components in
`destructiveChanges.xml`.

**Re-land pattern:** never reuse the original branch. New branch, `git revert
<revert-sha>`, add the fix, new PR.

### Re-validate a PR

```bash
scripts/engine.sh revalidate --pr 412
```

Re-runs validation at the PR's live head SHA, clears the recorded failure and
bypasses the attempt cap — a human asking is explicit intent. This replaces the
old empty-commit workaround.

### Recover a freeze

```bash
scripts/engine.sh status                  # read freezeReason first
scripts/engine.sh retry preprod           # re-enqueue the deploy at branch HEAD
```

Retry only works on a `FROZEN` environment. If the cause is bad metadata rather
than a transient failure, roll back instead of retrying into the same wall.

### Pause for maintenance

Only when git has to be reconciled to the org by hand:

```bash
scripts/engine.sh pause
git tag -f deployed/main <sha> && git push origin deployed/main --force
scripts/engine.sh resume
```

Webhooks are acknowledged but not processed while paused. Tell the team — a
paused engine looks exactly like a quiet one.

## What the engine reacts to

| GitHub event | Engine reaction |
|---|---|
| `pull_request` opened/synchronize → env branch | Enqueue validation |
| `push` to env branch | Enqueue deploy |
| `pull_request` closed unmerged | Cancel queued validations; abandon an in-flight one, discarding its result |
| `pull_request` reopened | Re-enqueue validation |
| Issue label `express` | Auto-merge after validation, auto-promote after deploy |
| Label `qa:passed` / `qa:failed` | Update board state |
| Label `destructive-approved` | Satisfies the destructive gate |
| Label `run-tests` | Forces tests even when smart-test skip would apply |
| Route entry label | Permits a direct PR into a gated entry point |

**Labels the engine writes are write-only.** `env:*`, `deploy:failed` and
`rolled-back` exist so a human browsing GitHub can see where things are; the
engine never reads them back as truth. Delivery state comes from the event log.
The labels above that express **human intent** are read, and should be.

### Test level per tier

- **Pipeline environments** — the configured `test_level`, usually
  `RunLocalTests`, downgraded to `NoTestRun` only when `smart_tests` proves the
  whole delta is safe metadata. No partial trust: provably safe, or the full suite.
- **Production** — Salesforce forbids `NoTestRun` outright. Batch promotions into
  releases so N tickets cost one 15-minute run instead of N of them.

`smart_tests` never applies to a `production: true` environment, and any unsafe
type in the delta (ApexClass, CustomObject, Flow, LWC) means full tests. Config
and the safe-type list: [references/pipeline-config.md](references/pipeline-config.md).

---

## Route topology

`routes:` replaced `promotions:`. A config with only `promotions:` still loads —
it is translated into a synthetic `standard` route and warns — but it cannot
express hotfix entry points or back-merge, so migrate it.

- A **forward edge** is a consecutive pair on any route's `path`. Promote-only,
  by cherry-pick or PR. The union of all forward edges must be acyclic.
- **`entry_requires_label`** gates direct PRs into a route's entry point. Engine-owned
  head branches (`release/`, `express/`, `backmerge/`, `revert/`) and bulk
  promotion from an upstream env's branch are exempt — the gate only catches a
  fresh direct entry, which is exactly the hotfix case it exists for.
- **`back_merge`** targets fire after a successful deploy to a route's terminal
  env and must be strictly upstream, so a back-merge can never introduce a
  forward promotion path.

Full semantics and worked configs:
[references/pipeline-config.md](references/pipeline-config.md).

---

## Pre/post-deploy Apex hooks

Repo-versioned anonymous Apex the engine runs **around** a deploy, for imperative
org actions metadata cannot express. Off unless `deploy_hooks.enabled`.

```
deploy-hooks/
  pre/   01-disable-automation.apex
  post/  123-delete-orphan-flow-versions.apex
```

Scripts live outside `force-app/` so sgd never treats them as metadata. They are
**delta-driven and run-once**: discovered from the same `deployed/<branch>` → SHA
window as metadata, so a script appears in exactly one deploy's window. Add it in
the same PR as the change it supports.

```
compute delta → gates → [PRE] → sf deploy → [POST] → advance tag
```

The tag advances **last** — it means "org fully reconciled, hooks included." A
pre-hook failure freezes with nothing deployed. A post-hook failure freezes with
the tag **not** advanced, so Retry re-runs deploy + post: **write hooks
idempotently.** Hooks never run during validation — anonymous Apex has no
`checkOnly`, so a hooks-only PR validates trivially green and then runs its
scripts on merge with no metadata deploy at all.

---

## Ticket providers

Absent `tickets:` means GitHub only, exactly as before providers existed.

- `extract` — regexes over commit and PR text. Free, read-only. Once a tracker
  has ever been used, leave it on permanently: commits written in that period
  name its tickets forever.
- `board` — the kanban's card source, and a **credentialed** read when it
  includes `jira`. Validated at config load; the engine refuses to start without
  `base_url`, `email` and `projects`, because the failure it prevents is a board
  rendering with every Jira card silently missing, which reads as "nothing to
  ship."

`projects` is load-bearing: the Jira key regex is built from the allowlist, never
from the general key shape, because `/[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\d+/` also matches `UTF-8`
and `ISO-8601`. No allowlist, no Jira extraction. The token never appears in
`pipeline.yml` — mount `JIRA_API_TOKEN` from Secret Manager.

---

## Key rules

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| Pipeline environments are the engine's, exclusively | A manual deploy desyncs `deployed/<branch>` with no way for the engine to detect it |
| Merge commits everywhere, never squash | `git revert -m 1` and `git cherry-pick -m 1` both need real merge commits |
| Never move `deployed/<branch>` unless paused | The tag is the engine's statement about the org |
| A `pipeline.yml` change is not live until the engine restarts | Config is read once at bootstrap; merging it is necessary, not sufficient |
| Mint a CLI token; never expect bare curl to work | `/api/*` is behind Workspace SSO |
| Release by ticket, not by SHA, when you can | The ticket → deploy join is what the model exists for, and it catches ride-alongs |
| Batch production promotions | `NoTestRun` is illegal in production, so every promotion costs a full test run |
| Never `--use-most-recent` on any `sf` command | Another deploy — yours, another agent's, or the engine's — may be the most recent |
| Deploy hooks must be idempotent | A Retry re-runs them; a post-hook freeze re-runs the whole deploy + post |
| Loosen quick-deploy eligibility only with a false-positive argument | A false negative costs 30 minutes; a false positive ships untested metadata |
| Engine down = frozen line, and that is correct | Required checks never go green, so nothing merges |

---

Verify against the engine repo's issue list rather than trusting this section to
be current.

- **Failure-path drills have never been run** (engine repo #4): freeze, rollback,

- **Scale-to-zero has never run against a real org.** Every timing constant is
  reasoned, not observed. Read the known-risk list before enabling it.
- **`Deploy.contentHash` exists and nothing populates it** — quick deploy is
  still SHA-based.

examples.title: Recovering a frozen preprod after a deploy fails on a missing field
examples.markdown:
## Request

Preprod has been frozen since this morning and my team lead says to just hit retry so the queue moves. I've pasted the status and the recent history; can you tell me what to do and give me the exact commands?

## Inputs

**Dry run.** This skill normally works on live systems or its owner's own setup. Here the system state is invented in the inputs below, and nothing was changed anywhere. Run of the built `operate-salesforce-pipeline` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### history.md

#### preprod activity, 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-04 (from /api/history, newest first)

- 2026-11-04 08:12  deploy FAILED  sha b93d2f6  PR #418 "EXAMPLE-88 Escalate P1 cases by tier"  -> environment FROZEN, tag stays 7e41c09
- 2026-11-04 07:58  PR #418 merged (merge commit b93d2f6) into preprod
- 2026-11-04 07:41  validation PASSED  PR #418 at sha 4fd8e21 (test level RunLocalTests)
- 2026-11-03 17:05  validation PASSED  PR #418 at sha 4fd8e21 -- note: PR head was then rebased/merged from sandbox-a, field metadata not in diff
- 2026-11-03 15:30  deploy SETTLED  sha 7e41c09  PR #409 "GH-377 Quote footer text"

#### PR #418 diff summary
- flows/Case_Escalation.flow-meta.xml (modified; reads Case.Escalation_Tier__c)
- classes/EscalationRouter.cls and EscalationRouterTest.cls (modified)

#### Board notes
- EXAMPLE-91 "Add Escalation_Tier__c to Case" is on the Dev Sandboxes column, carried by sandbox-a. Its PR merged on sandbox-a only; never released to preprod.
- PR #421 (GH-380, footer typo) is queued for validation behind the freeze. It touches one email template.

#### status.json

{
  "paused": false,
  "repo": "northfield-labs/crm-metadata",
  "environments": {
    "preprod": {
      "state": "FROZEN",
      "deployedTag": "7e41c09",
      "inFlightJobId": null,
      "deployUrl": "https://northfield--preprod.example.com/lightning/setup/DeployStatus/page?address=0Af000000000123",
      "freezeReason": "Deploy failed: flows/Case_Escalation.flow-meta.xml: field Case.Escalation_Tier__c does not exist (Component Failures: 1, Tests run: 0)",
      "currentItem": { "type": "deploy", "sha": "b93d2f6", "pr": 418 },
      "queueLength": 1,
      "queue": [ { "type": "validation", "pr": 421, "sha": "5c0aa17" } ]
    },
    "main": {
      "state": "SETTLED",
      "deployedTag": "2d90e5b",
      "inFlightJobId": null,
      "deployUrl": null,
      "freezeReason": null,
      "currentItem": null,
      "queueLength": 0,
      "queue": []
    }
  }
}

## Output

Don't retry yet. A retry would fail again, and it would also cost another test run.

#### What the status says

`preprod` is `FROZEN`, and `main` is `SETTLED` and unaffected. The `freezeReason` is a Salesforce deploy error, not a transient one:

> Deploy failed: flows/Case_Escalation.flow-meta.xml: field Case.Escalation_Tier__c does not exist

The failed item is PR #418 (EXAMPLE-88, merge commit `b93d2f6`). Its flow reads `Case.Escalation_Tier__c`, but the field belongs to EXAMPLE-91, which is only on `sandbox-a` and was never released to preprod. The PR's validation passed because the field was missing from the diff and from the org it checked. That is a gap in how the dependency was released, and it is not an engine fault.

The tag `deployed/preprod` is still `7e41c09`, so git still describes the org correctly. Nothing was half-deployed. Retry re-enqueues a deploy of the same metadata at `b93d2f6`, and the missing field would fail it again.

PR #421 (GH-380, an email template typo) is waiting in the queue behind the freeze. It has no dependency on this problem.

#### Recommended path: fix forward by releasing EXAMPLE-91, then retry

Retry becomes the right command once the field is in preprod's branch, because it deploys branch HEAD, which will then include both changes.

1. Set up auth if you haven't. Open `$ENGINE_URL/auth/login?redirect=cli`, sign in, save the token to a mode-600 file, and export `SFDE_TOKEN_FILE` with its absolute path. A bare curl returns 401 or 503.

   ```bash
   export ENGINE_URL=$(grep '^engine_url:' pipeline.yml | awk '{print $2}')
   scripts/engine.sh status        # re-read freezeReason; confirm still FROZEN
   ```

2. Release the field ticket from its sandbox into preprod:

   ```bash
   scripts/engine.sh release --to preprod --from sandbox-a EXAMPLE-91
   ```

   `--from` is required. Read the response before going further. The release cherry-picks EXAMPLE-91's merge, so it only works because that PR merged on `sandbox-a`. If the engine refuses with "unattributed commits", the merge carries other work too. Read what it names and either add those tickets or use the fallback below.

3. Wait for the release PR's validation to pass, then merge it with a **merge commit**, not a squash. Validation computes the delta from `deployed/preprod` (`7e41c09`), so it covers the flow, the Apex and the new field together.

4. Once the release has merged, retry:

   ```bash
   scripts/engine.sh retry preprod
   ```

   This lifts the freeze and deploys current HEAD. When it finishes, the status should show `SETTLED` with the tag advanced, and PR #421 then validates.

#### Fallback: roll back EXAMPLE-88

Use this if the EXAMPLE-91 release is refused, or if the field turns out to need work in `sandbox-a` first.

```bash
scripts/engine.sh rollback --env preprod --sha b93d2f6
```

I used `--sha` because the failed deploy never completed, and a ticket-based rollback looks up "the deploy that carried it". That lookup may not find one. The default `--mode pr` opens a revert PR so the inverse deployment is validated first; keep it. `--mode direct` is for emergencies only. To re-land afterwards, don't reuse the original branch: create a new branch, run `git revert <revert-sha>`, add the fix, and open a new PR, with EXAMPLE-91 released first.

#### Things I could not confirm from what you pasted

- Whether the engine validates the release PR while preprod is `FROZEN`. PR #421 is sitting in the queue, which suggests validations may wait. The skill documents retry and rollback as the freeze exits, and does not say whether a validation can run during a freeze. If the release PR stays queued, `rollback` is the way to unfreeze first.
- Whether EXAMPLE-91 includes field-level security or a permission set. Check this before step 3. The Apex test run happens on the same deploy, and a missing permission will fail tests, not the field itself.
- I haven't run any of these commands. Everything above is from the status and history you pasted.

#### What not to do

- Don't deploy the field to the preprod org yourself with `sf project deploy`. The engine can't detect a manual deploy, and `deployed/preprod` would then misstate the org. The recovery for that is Pause, then reconcile by hand, then Resume.
- Don't move the `deployed/preprod` tag.
- Don't add `--use-most-recent` to any `sf` command.

#### For your team lead

The quick answer: retry only helps when the failure was transient (auth, network, git). This one is a missing dependency in the metadata, so the order is to land the field first and retry second. If the team wants to confirm quickly, EXAMPLE-91 is the card sitting in the Dev Sandboxes column of the board.
