skills.markdown:
---
name: plan-offering-artifacts
description: 'Orchestrates the full Estate playbook artifact suite. Knows what a complete playbook is, what order the artifacts get built in, which skill builds each one, and what has to pass before anything ships. Use whenever someone wants to build, complete, audit, conform, or publish an Estate playbook, or asks what is left on one. Trigger on "build the playbook", "what''s left on PB-CPQ", "conform this playbook", "playbook artifacts", "is this playbook ready", "run the playbook suite", or any PB-code paired with build, audit, gate, or ship. Do NOT trigger for a single artifact when the user named that artifact directly; call the owning skill instead.'
---


# Plan offering artifacts

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`readout-brief.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/readout-brief.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

The coordinator for the playbook artifact suite. It decides what must exist, in what order, who builds it, and what blocks the next step. Content decisions stay with the skill that owns each artifact.

## The spec is upstream

The caller supplies the current approved offering specification, manifest schema,
qualifier schema, and stage-gate workbook as explicit project paths. This package
does not include those authorities or an installed playbook-spec dependency.
Read [spec-inputs.md](references/spec-inputs.md) before treating a plan as current.

The scripts retain a version 1.1 compatibility model. They check that model and
manifest assertions; they do not load or validate the caller's specification or
schemas. Their output therefore says `spec_authority.status: unverified` and
`release_ready: false`, including when every modeled artifact is complete.
A current specification with different requirements needs an explicit reviewed
adapter update; changing only a version string does not implement its rules.

## The suite is ten numbered slots

Nine required; the ROM deck (06) is the one conditional slot. Numbering never changes.

## Where the files are

This skill uses the standard nested layout: `scripts/` holds `plan.py` and `conformance_audit.py`, `references/` holds `conformance-procedure.md` and `phase-2-extension.md`. Every command below is written for that layout.

## How the plan is produced

Never assemble a build order by hand. Run the planner:

```bash
python3 scripts/plan.py manifest.json --format text
```

Pass `--format text`. The default `--format json` is the machine contract for a phase 2 executor and runs several times larger and slower. Step 6 below re-runs the planner after every artifact, so the compact format matters.

It reads the playbook's `manifest.json`, expands the artifact table against that playbook's options and its ROM flag, resolves dependencies, and emits an ordered plan with one action per artifact: `build`, `finish_and_gate`, `run_gates`, `fix_gate_failure`, or `complete`. It raises findings on missing Q-numbers, missing timeline snapshots, any tier below the confirmed project margin floor, and a manifest whose declared spec version is not the planner's.

The planner is deterministic and content-free. Read `phase-2-extension.md` before changing anything in `plan.py`.

## Working a playbook

1. **Confirm the specification inputs.** Follow [spec-inputs.md](references/spec-inputs.md),
   record the supplied paths and versions, and validate `manifest.json` against the
   supplied manifest schema. If no manifest exists, inventory the folder and draft
   one for validation; its absence alone does not establish its age or conformance.
   Missing authority permits a labeled diagnostic inventory, not release approval.
2. **Run the planner.** Report the totals and every finding. Do not narrate the run.
3. **Take the next ready step.** Use the plan’s `invocation.skill` and `invocation.mode`, with the artifact number, option and source quote. The `builder` field retains a historical identifier for existing executors; it is not the current installed skill name. Artifact 09 is a local template-copy operation, with no skill invocation.
4. **Gate the result.** All three gates, every artifact, written disposition each. A FAIL is not shippable.
5. **Update the manifest.** Status and gate results, immediately. A manifest that lags the folder makes the next plan wrong.
6. **Re-run the planner** and continue until nothing is outstanding.

Do not build ahead of the plan. An artifact built before its dependency exists gets rebuilt.

## Who builds what

| Artifact | Skill |
|---|---|
| 01 README | this skill, from the manifest |
| 02 Overview | `manage-service-offering`, offering package planning mode; use the available document tool for the specified DOCX |
| 03 One-pager | `manage-service-offering`, internal brief or external handout mode |
| 04 Talk Track and Objections | `manage-service-offering`, offering package planning mode; use the available document tool for the specified DOCX |
| 05 Qualifier | this skill, plus the `qualifier.json` twin |
| 06 ROM deck | `scope-project` rough estimate supplies the figures; `build-deck` renders the deck |
| 07 DDOC | `build-deck`, scope decision deck mode |
| 08 Proposal | `build-deck` for the prescribed presentation format |
| 09 Pre-Engagement Stage Gate | copy the template, adapt rows |
| 10 SOW | `write-statement-of-work` |

Gates on everything: `brand-renderer` for parity, a human or model for visual, `review-writing` for prose. Writing review is `review-writing`, applied during the build and not as a pass afterwards.

## Artifact 05 has a machine-readable twin

The Qualifier ships as a .docx for humans and a `qualifier.json` for the fit router, both generated from the same source. They must not drift. When the Qualifier changes, regenerate both in the same step, and validate the JSON against the caller-supplied qualifier schema before marking the artifact done.

## The DDOC mode is a scope fact

Decision mode when the client is choosing between options. Confirmation mode when there is one option. Both are required; a single-option playbook still gets a DDOC, because the artifact's job is putting the client on record accepting a boundary, not comparing prices. The mode follows from the option count in the manifest, so the orchestrator passes it rather than asking.

## Conformance runs

To audit an existing playbook against the spec rather than build a new one:

```bash
python3 scripts/conformance_audit.py PLAYBOOK_DIR --manifest manifest.json
```

`--infer` drafts a manifest from filenames when none exists. `--json` switches the report to JSON; the default text report is the compact one and is the one to use.

It reports what is present, what is missing, what is misnamed, what carries no gate result, and what is likely off-spec by format. It reads the filesystem and the manifest only. It does not open documents, so it cannot judge whether an artifact's contents match the spec. That judgment is the visual gate and stays with a person.

## Rules

- **Never fabricate a number.** No price, duration, margin, or count that the quote or the source does not ground. Flag it as an open decision.
- **Never mark an artifact complete without three gate dispositions.** A clean tool run is not a release authorization.
- **Never renumber artifacts.** The numbers are stable across the whole catalog.
- **Carry unchanged content verbatim.** Re-transcribing introduces drift. Copy and edit only the target section.
- **Flag decisions, do not assume them.** Collect them and surface them with the delivery.
- **Report counts, not adjectives.** "0 fail, 4 warn" rather than "clean".

## Files

- `plan.py` · the planner. Shared with the phase 2 workflow engine.
- `conformance_audit.py` · audits an existing playbook folder against the spec.
- `phase-2-extension.md` · the contract that keeps phase 2 additive.
- `conformance-procedure.md` · the six-step conformance run.

The manifest and qualifier schemas are caller inputs described in [spec-inputs.md](references/spec-inputs.md). The planner does not perform JSON Schema validation.
## Commercial policy input

The package planner reads `commercial_policy` from the manifest. Supply
`margin_floor_pct` with its `source` and `verified_at` date from confirmed
project policy. No percentage is supplied by this skill. Without a verified
policy, the planner flags approval as unresolved while preserving the build
plan and known economics. An example threshold has no authority for another
engagement.

  1. Run the planner. Report the totals and every finding. Do not narrate the run.
  2. Take the next ready step. Use the plan’s invocation.skill and invocation.mode, with the artifact number, option and source quote. The builder field retains a historical identifier for existing executors; it is not the current installed skill name. Artifact 09 is a local template-copy operation, with no skill invocation.
  3. Gate the result. All three gates, every artifact, written disposition each. A FAIL is not shippable.
  4. Update the manifest. Status and gate results, immediately. A manifest that lags the folder makes the next plan wrong.
  5. Re-run the planner and continue until nothing is outstanding.

Do not build ahead of the plan. An artifact built before its dependency exists gets rebuilt.

Who builds what

ArtifactSkill
01 READMEthis skill, from the manifest
02 Overviewmanage-service-offering, offering package planning mode; use the available document tool for the specified DOCX
03 One-pagermanage-service-offering, internal brief or external handout mode
04 Talk Track and Objectionsmanage-service-offering, offering package planning mode; use the available document tool for the specified DOCX
05 Qualifierthis skill, plus the qualifier.json twin
06 ROM deckscope-project rough estimate supplies the figures; build-deck renders the deck
07 DDOCbuild-deck, scope decision deck mode
08 Proposalbuild-deck for the prescribed presentation format
09 Pre-Engagement Stage Gatecopy the template, adapt rows
10 SOWwrite-statement-of-work

Gates on everything: brand-renderer for parity, a human or model for visual, review-writing for prose. Writing review is review-writing, applied during the build and not as a pass afterwards.

Artifact 05 has a machine-readable twin

The Qualifier ships as a .docx for humans and a qualifier.json for the fit router, both generated from the same source. They must not drift. When the Qualifier changes, regenerate both in the same step, and validate the JSON against the caller-supplied qualifier schema before marking the artifact done.

The DDOC mode is a scope fact

Decision mode when the client is choosing between options. Confirmation mode when there is one option. Both are required; a single-option playbook still gets a DDOC, because the artifact's job is putting the client on record accepting a boundary, not comparing prices. The mode follows from the option count in the manifest, so the orchestrator passes it rather than asking.

Conformance runs

To audit an existing playbook against the spec rather than build a new one:

python3 scripts/conformance_audit.py PLAYBOOK_DIR --manifest manifest.json

--infer drafts a manifest from filenames when none exists. --json switches the report to JSON; the default text report is the compact one and is the one to use.

It reports what is present, what is missing, what is misnamed, what carries no gate result, and what is likely off-spec by format. It reads the filesystem and the manifest only. It does not open documents, so it cannot judge whether an artifact's contents match the spec. That judgment is the visual gate and stays with a person.

Rules

  • Never fabricate a number. No price, duration, margin, or count that the quote or the source does not ground. Flag it as an open decision.
  • Never mark an artifact complete without three gate dispositions. A clean tool run is not a release authorization.
  • Never renumber artifacts. The numbers are stable across the whole catalog.
  • Carry unchanged content verbatim. Re-transcribing introduces drift. Copy and edit only the target section.
  • Flag decisions, do not assume them. Collect them and surface them with the delivery.
  • Report counts, not adjectives. "0 fail, 4 warn" rather than "clean".

Files

  • plan.py · the planner. Shared with the phase 2 workflow engine.
  • conformance_audit.py · audits an existing playbook folder against the spec.
  • phase-2-extension.md · the contract that keeps phase 2 additive.
  • conformance-procedure.md · the six-step conformance run.

The manifest and qualifier schemas are caller inputs described in spec-inputs.md (references/spec-inputs.md). The planner does not perform JSON Schema validation.

Commercial policy input

The package planner reads commercial_policy from the manifest. Supply margin_floor_pct with its source and verified_at date from confirmed project policy. No percentage is supplied by this skill. Without a verified policy, the planner flags approval as unresolved while preserving the build plan and known economics. An example threshold has no authority for another engagement.

examples.title: Build order and blockers for a half-finished assessment playbook
examples.markdown:
## Request

We're building the playbook for our Data Platform Readiness Assessment (PB-DPR) and I've got a half-finished folder. Can you work out what's left to build, in what order, and what's blocking it? Folder listing and my quote notes are attached.

## Inputs

Run of the built `manage-service-offering` task package in its "offering package planning" mode. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Other files it produced, not shown here: `manifest.draft.json`, `plan.txt`.

#### folder-listing.txt

Folder: PB-DPR Data Platform Readiness Assessment
Listing taken 2026-11-03. No manifest.json in the folder.

PB-DPR_01_readme.md            started, headings only
PB-DPR_02_overview.docx        finished; parity gate passed, visual gate passed, prose gate not run
PB-DPR_03_one-pager.pdf        exported last week; no gates run
PB-DPR_05_qualifier.docx       draft, three questions still marked TODO
(no qualifier.json yet)

Nothing else exists. No talk track, no stage gate workbook, no DDOC, no proposals, no SOWs, no ROM decks.

#### quote-notes.md

#### PB-DPR quote notes (Priya's working notes)

Shape: Assess. Stage: build.

We sell two options.

- **Core**: four-week readiness assessment of one data platform. Quote Q-4471. Active timeline snapshot TS-0912. Modelled margin 41%.
- **Extended**: Core plus a second platform and a migration sequencing workshop. No quote number yet. No timeline snapshot yet. Margin not modelled.

Fee bands are not final. The practice lead recorded a band spread of 2.6 between the Core and Extended bands.

Margin floor: Finance mentioned in a hallway chat that the floor is 35%. I have nothing in writing and no date.

The playbook spec we work to is version 1.2. I do not have the spec document, the manifest schema, the qualifier schema or the stage-gate workbook to hand. They live with the PMO.

Open question from the sales team: should the Extended proposal and SOW wait until the Core ones are signed off? I have not decided.

## Output

PB-DPR has 13 artifacts required and none are complete. 3 are ready to start now, 10 are waiting on earlier artifacts, and nothing can be called release-ready yet.

I ran the planner's rules by hand against your folder listing and notes, because I can't run `plan.py` here. I also had to draft a `manifest.json`, since the folder has none.

#### Gaps in what I was given

- **No specification inputs.** I don't have the approved spec, the manifest schema, the qualifier schema or the stage-gate workbook. You said they sit with the PMO. I could not validate the draft manifest, so treat this as a labeled diagnostic plan and not a conformance result.
- **Spec version mismatch.** You work to version 1.2. The planner models version 1.1, and a changed version string does not make it apply 1.2's rules. The artifact set below may differ under 1.2, and the PMO needs to confirm it before anything is built.
- **No verified margin floor.** The 35% from Finance is a hallway remark with no source and no date, so I left it out of the manifest. Core's 41% margin has nothing to be compared against.

#### Findings

1. No verified margin floor, so commercial approval is unresolved.
2. Extended has no Q-number.
3. Extended has no active timeline snapshot, so its revenue, cost and margin are unsourced.
4. The manifest declares spec 1.2 and the planner is on 1.1.

Core has Q-4471 and snapshot TS-0912, which are your figures.

#### Which artifacts are required

- Shape Assess carries the full suite.
- A band spread of 2.6 is above 2, so the ROM deck (06) is planned for each option. I took your "2.6" to be the number the planner expects. Please confirm that is how the spread is defined.
- That gives 7 playbook-level artifacts (01 to 05, 07, 09) plus 06, 08 and 10 for each of Core and Extended, which makes 13.

#### Plan, in order

| Artifact | Action | Blocked by | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| 02 Overview | run the gates | none | `manage-service-offering`, offering package planning |
| 05 Qualifier | finish and gate | 02 | `manage-service-offering`, offering package planning |
| 03 One-pager | run the gates | 02 | `manage-service-offering`, internal brief or external handout |
| 04 Talk Track and Objections | build | 02 | `manage-service-offering`, offering package planning |
| 09 Pre-Engagement Stage Gate | build | none | copy the template and adapt the rows |
| 06 ROM deck (Core, Extended) | build | 02 | `build-deck` with a `scope-project` rough estimate |
| 07 DDOC | build | 02, 05 | `build-deck`, scope decision deck |
| 08 Proposal (Core, Extended) | build | 07 | `build-deck` |
| 10 SOW (Core, Extended) | build | 07 | `write-statement-of-work` |
| 01 README | finish and gate | none | this skill, from the manifest |

**Ready now:** 02, 09 and 01.

The next step is the 02 Overview prose gate. The Overview is the dependency for six other artifacts, so that gate is the one holding up the rest. It is the only gate left on that file. Parity and visual have passed, and prose has not run. Once 02 passes, 05, 03, 04 and 06 are all unblocked. 05 then unblocks 07, and 07 unblocks the proposals and SOWs.

Other points:
- **03 One-pager** was exported before 02 passed its gates. If the prose gate changes the Overview, it will need a re-check.
- **05 Qualifier** needs its three TODO questions closed. It also needs a regenerated `qualifier.json`, validated against the supplied qualifier schema, which does not exist yet.
- **06 ROM** is a conditional slot. The 2.6 spread plans it, and the ROM figures come from a rough estimate. Extended has no quote number or snapshot, so that estimate has nothing to rest on until they exist.
- **07 DDOC** runs in decision mode, because there are two options.

#### Decisions to lock

1. **Margin floor.** Someone needs to supply the percentage with its source and verification date. Until then no option can be checked against a floor.
2. **Extended's Q-number and timeline snapshot.** Both are needed before 06, 08 and 10 for Extended carry any figure. No fee bands are final, and I have not filled in any.
3. **Spec version.** The PMO needs to supply the approved spec and schemas, and confirm whether 1.2 changes the artifact set.
4. **Band spread definition.** Confirm that 2.6 is the figure the spec means.
5. **Your sales team's question.** Should the Extended proposal and SOW wait for Core sign-off? I did not pick an answer. The plan has no dependency between them today, so both are blocked only by 07.

#### Not done

I did not run any gates, because I only have a file listing and not the documents. I did not mark anything complete or update gate results. I did not write the missing artifacts, since 04, 06, 07, 08 and 10 are blocked on an earlier artifact or the open decisions above.

#### Files

- `out/manifest.draft.json`: the draft manifest. It holds code PB-DPR, shape Assess, stage build, spec_version "1.2" and band_spread 2.6. The margin floor is null with no source or date. Core has Q-4471, TS-0912 and 41%, and Extended is empty. Four artifacts are listed: 01 draft, 02 present with parity and visual passed, 03 present with no gates, and 05 draft.
- `out/plan.txt`: the hand-run plan above in the planner's text format, with the findings.

skills.title: Plan sprint
skills.description: Plan one sprint on an agile engagement or product team: sprint goal, per-person capacity, commit and stretch work sized against that capacity, owned dependencies recorded in the RAID log, risks and the team definition of done, checked by a blocking gate before the team commits. Use for "plan the next sprint", "sprint planning", "how much can we commit", "capacity for sprint N", "why do we keep missing sprints", or a Sprint 1 plan after kickoff. Do NOT use for grading or splitting backlog items (refine-backlog), ranking candidates (prioritization), the Sprint 0 mobilization plan (start-delivery), weekly status or RAID upkeep (track-delivery), or a quarter or release roadmap (build-roadmap).

guide.what: Plan one sprint against measured team capacity.
guide.when: A team is about to commit to a sprint, or sprints keep missing their goal.
guide.inputs: Team availability, the refine-backlog readiness report, the RAID log, recent velocity and the definition of done.
guide.outputs: A sprint plan with a goal, capacity, commit and stretch work, owned dependencies and a gate result.
guide.example: Plan sprint 5 for a team of four with one person out for three days.
guide.expect: It asks for capacity, velocity, the definition of done and the readiness report, then drafts a sprint goal and a commit and stretch split and runs a gate script. The gate exits 1 on over-capacity or not-ready commitments, and the plan is a proposal because the team decides the commitment and the tracker is never changed.
guide.requires: Python 3 for the gate script, plus a readiness report from backlog refinement and a RAID log if you want the gate to check them.
guide.overview: It asks for capacity, velocity, the definition of done and the readiness report, then drafts a sprint goal and a commit and stretch split and runs a gate script. The gate exits 1 on over-capacity or not-ready commitments, and the plan is a proposal because the team decides the commitment and the tracker is never changed.
guide.value: Match a proposed sprint commitment to actual availability and ready work. It makes capacity overruns, unresolved dependencies and stretch work visible before the team commits.

preparation.where: Bring team availability, recent velocity, a definition of done and the readiness report from Refine backlog. The RAID log lists risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies. Equivalent team records can explain these inputs; they are not supplied by connecting a tracker alone.
preparation.missing: Missing estimates or readiness evidence must be supplied by the team or prepared through refinement. The gate cannot approve over-capacity or not-ready commitments. The plan is a proposal; it does not change tracker tickets or choose the team's commitment.

preparationSkills.reason: Prepares the readiness report used to select a proposed commitment.

reuse.label: General use
reuse.reason: The method accepts the user’s project sources and takes private context as an explicit input.
reuse.basis: Source classification and automated reference scan; cross-environment execution has not been tested.

profile.expect: It asks for capacity, velocity, the definition of done and the readiness report, then drafts a sprint goal and a commit and stretch split and runs a gate script. The gate exits 1 on over-capacity or not-ready commitments, and the plan is a proposal because the team decides the commitment and the tracker is never changed.

skills.markdown:
---
name: plan-sprint
description: 'Plan one sprint on an agile engagement or product team: sprint goal, per-person capacity, commit and stretch work sized against that capacity, owned dependencies recorded in the RAID log, risks and the team definition of done, checked by a blocking gate before the team commits. Use for "plan the next sprint", "sprint planning", "how much can we commit", "capacity for sprint N", "why do we keep missing sprints", or a Sprint 1 plan after kickoff. Do NOT use for grading or splitting backlog items (refine-backlog), ranking candidates (prioritization), the Sprint 0 mobilization plan (start-delivery), weekly status or RAID upkeep (track-delivery), or a quarter or release roadmap (build-roadmap).'
---

# Plan sprint

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [the planning chain](../_shared/planning-chain.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

A sprint plan says what the team will finish, what it will attempt if the commitment lands early, and what could stop it. This skill drafts the plan from the refined backlog and the team's real capacity, runs the gate, and hands the plan to the team. The team decides the commitment. The skill never commits on the team's behalf and never estimates work the team has not estimated.

## Project context required

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement or product team, its backlog, its RAID log and the intended audience. Map roles such as Program Lead, Scrum Master and Product Owner to the people the project actually names. A connected Jira or Linear workspace is a read source when the user authorizes it; this skill does not create sprints, move issues or write to the tracker.

## Inputs

| Input | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate items with IDs and team estimates | The readiness report from `refine-backlog` | Run refine-backlog first. Without it the gate relies on self-reported flags and says so. |
| Capacity per person | Sprint length, working days, PTO, meetings, on-call and interrupt hours, focus factor | Ask for the two or three that change the total most. Use a 0.7 focus factor otherwise and state it. |
| Velocity for the last three to five sprints | The tracker or the previous sprint reports | Plan on hours only and say velocity was unavailable. |
| RAID log | Seeded by `start-delivery`, maintained by `track-delivery` | Dependencies stay in the plan with a warning; propose RAID entries through track-delivery. |
| Team definition of done | The team's working agreement | Ask once. Without it, completion criteria cannot be checked and the gate warns. |
| Sprint goal candidates | The Product Owner, the roadmap Now column, the quarter objective | Draft one and mark it proposed. |

## Workflow

1. **Pin the sprint.** Name, dates, team and the previous sprint's report. Carry unfinished items forward explicitly; an item that disappears between sprints is the failure mode.
2. **Write the goal.** One sentence that states the outcome, such as "a new admin can finish guided setup without a support ticket". A list of features is not a goal. The goal is what lets the team refuse off-goal requests mid-sprint.
3. **Calculate capacity per person.** Multiply working days after PTO by hours per day, subtract the person's overhead hours, then apply the focus factor. Read [capacity and commitment](references/capacity-and-commitment.md) for the worked calculation and calibration against actuals.
4. **Select items.** Only READY items from the refinement report are eligible to commit. A REFINE or DISCOVERY item goes back to refine-backlog with its failed criteria, not into the sprint.
5. **Split commit and stretch.** Commit roughly 75 to 85% of capacity and hold 10 to 15% for stretch. Nothing in the commitment depends on a stretch item.
6. **Record dependencies.** Every dependency gets an owner, a needed-by date, the owner's confirmation and a RAID dependency ID (D-###). New dependencies are proposed to track-delivery for the RAID log; this skill does not write the log.
7. **Record risks.** One or two per committed item where they exist: technical, dependency, estimate or capacity risk, each with a mitigation and an owner. Risks that outlive the sprint go to the RAID log as R-### entries through track-delivery.
8. **Check the definition of done.** List which team DoD items each item plans to meet.
9. **Run the gate** and fix the plan until it passes, then fill [the template](assets/sprint-plan-template.md).

## Gate

```bash
python3 scripts/sprint_check.py plan.json --readiness readiness.json --raid-log RAID.md
```

The plan format is in [plan format](references/plan-format.md). The gate exits 1 on any fail finding: no goal, no capacity, committed work above capacity, a committed item that is not READY or not in the refinement report, a committed item's dependency with no owner, or a RAID ID that is not in the log. Warnings and information findings do not block. Report the counts it prints and the utilization percentage in place of adjectives.

`scripts/sprint_check_selftest.py` runs the gate against passing and failing fixtures. Run it after any change to the gate.

## Diagnosing missed sprints

When sprints keep missing, compare the last three plans with their actuals before changing anything. Each cause listed in [capacity and commitment](references/capacity-and-commitment.md) has its own fix and its own evidence, so name the cause the records show. Report what the records show and what remains unknown.

## Durable output

Each run leaves `sprint-NN-plan.md` (the filled template) and the gate report in the engagement or team folder, named by sprint number, per `_shared/output-contract.md`. A run that stops at a failed gate still leaves the gate report and the open questions. Deliver or link the files.

## Boundaries

- Does not grade, estimate or split items. That is `refine-backlog`.
- Does not rank candidates. That is `prioritize-work`; the Product Owner orders the backlog.
- Does not write the RAID log or the status report. That is `track-delivery`.
- Does not plan Sprint 0 or mobilization. That is `start-delivery`.

A sprint plan says what the team will finish, what it will attempt if the commitment lands early, and what could stop it. This skill drafts the plan from the refined backlog and the team's real capacity, runs the gate, and hands the plan to the team. The team decides the commitment. The skill never commits on the team's behalf and never estimates work the team has not estimated.

Project context required

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement or product team, its backlog, its RAID log and the intended audience. Map roles such as Program Lead, Scrum Master and Product Owner to the people the project actually names. A connected Jira or Linear workspace is a read source when the user authorizes it; this skill does not create sprints, move issues or write to the tracker.

Inputs

InputSourceIf missing
Candidate items with IDs and team estimatesThe readiness report from refine-backlogRun refine-backlog first. Without it the gate relies on self-reported flags and says so.
Capacity per personSprint length, working days, PTO, meetings, on-call and interrupt hours, focus factorAsk for the two or three that change the total most. Use a 0.7 focus factor otherwise and state it.
Velocity for the last three to five sprintsThe tracker or the previous sprint reportsPlan on hours only and say velocity was unavailable.
RAID logSeeded by start-delivery, maintained by track-deliveryDependencies stay in the plan with a warning; propose RAID entries through track-delivery.
Team definition of doneThe team's working agreementAsk once. Without it, completion criteria cannot be checked and the gate warns.
Sprint goal candidatesThe Product Owner, the roadmap Now column, the quarter objectiveDraft one and mark it proposed.

Workflow

  1. Pin the sprint. Name, dates, team and the previous sprint's report. Carry unfinished items forward explicitly; an item that disappears between sprints is the failure mode.
  2. Write the goal. One sentence that states the outcome, such as "a new admin can finish guided setup without a support ticket". A list of features is not a goal. The goal is what lets the team refuse off-goal requests mid-sprint.
  3. Calculate capacity per person. Multiply working days after PTO by hours per day, subtract the person's overhead hours, then apply the focus factor. Read capacity and commitment (references/capacity-and-commitment.md) for the worked calculation and calibration against actuals.
  4. Select items. Only READY items from the refinement report are eligible to commit. A REFINE or DISCOVERY item goes back to refine-backlog with its failed criteria, not into the sprint.
  5. Split commit and stretch. Commit roughly 75 to 85% of capacity and hold 10 to 15% for stretch. Nothing in the commitment depends on a stretch item.
  6. Record dependencies. Every dependency gets an owner, a needed-by date, the owner's confirmation and a RAID dependency ID (D-###). New dependencies are proposed to track-delivery for the RAID log; this skill does not write the log.
  7. Record risks. One or two per committed item where they exist: technical, dependency, estimate or capacity risk, each with a mitigation and an owner. Risks that outlive the sprint go to the RAID log as R-### entries through track-delivery.
  8. Check the definition of done. List which team DoD items each item plans to meet.
  9. Run the gate and fix the plan until it passes, then fill the template (assets/sprint-plan-template.md).

Gate

python3 scripts/sprint_check.py plan.json --readiness readiness.json --raid-log RAID.md

The plan format is in plan format (references/plan-format.md). The gate exits 1 on any fail finding: no goal, no capacity, committed work above capacity, a committed item that is not READY or not in the refinement report, a committed item's dependency with no owner, or a RAID ID that is not in the log. Warnings and information findings do not block. Report the counts it prints and the utilization percentage in place of adjectives.

scripts/sprint_check_selftest.py runs the gate against passing and failing fixtures. Run it after any change to the gate.

Diagnosing missed sprints

When sprints keep missing, compare the last three plans with their actuals before changing anything. Each cause listed in capacity and commitment (references/capacity-and-commitment.md) has its own fix and its own evidence, so name the cause the records show. Report what the records show and what remains unknown.

Durable output

Each run leaves sprint-NN-plan.md (the filled template) and the gate report in the engagement or team folder, named by sprint number, per _shared/output-contract.md. A run that stops at a failed gate still leaves the gate report and the open questions. Deliver or link the files.

  • Does not grade, estimate or split items. That is refine-backlog.
  • Does not rank candidates. That is prioritize-work; the Product Owner orders the backlog.
  • Does not write the RAID log or the status report. That is track-delivery.
  • Does not plan Sprint 0 or mobilization. That is start-delivery.
  • Does not commit, approve or start the sprint. The team commits; the tracker is changed by a person or an authorized workflow.

Files

  • references/capacity-and-commitment.md: how to calculate capacity and size the commitment, plus mid-sprint descoping and missed-sprint diagnosis.
  • references/plan-format.md: the plan JSON fields the gate reads.
  • assets/sprint-plan-template.md: the plan the team reviews.
  • scripts/sprint_check.py: the gate. Standard library only.
  • scripts/sprint_check_selftest.py and scripts/fixtures/: passing and failing cases.
  • UPSTREAM.md and LICENSE-UPSTREAM: the source this skill adapts and its license.

Release gate (required)

Before you deliver, run the gate. Full spec in release-gate.md (../_shared/release-gate.md).

  2. Run review-deliverable before you call it final.

Do not present the plan as final until both checks have passed.

examples.markdown:
## Request

Plan Sprint 41 for the Packwise team. Capacity, velocity and the ready backlog are in ./inputs/. Give me the sprint goal, what's in and out, and the risks.

## Inputs

Run of the built `plan-sprint` task package. All inputs below are invented. The run had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Files it also produced, not shown here: `sprint-41-gate-report.md`.

#### sprint-context.md

#### Packwise — Sprint 41 planning inputs (fictional)

Sprint: 2 weeks, 10 working days. Sprint goal candidate: "Crews can complete a job with no signal."
Team: 5 developers, 1 QA. Availability: Ana out 3 days; Ravi on-call (counts at 50%); a public holiday on day 6 for everyone.
Velocity: last 4 sprints 34, 29, 38, 31 points.
Carry-over: OFF-12 (13 pts, 60% done by the dev's estimate).

Ready backlog (refined, estimated):
| Key | Story | Points | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| OFF-12 | Cache today's jobs on device | 13 | carry-over |
| OFF-14 | Queue status updates offline and sync | 8 | depends on OFF-12 |
| OFF-15 | Conflict rule when office edits job while crew offline | 5 | needs PM decision on "last write wins" |
| OFF-16 | Offline photo capture with deferred upload | 8 | |
| OFF-18 | Offline indicator banner | 2 | |
| QBO-3 | QuickBooks sync spike | 3 | timeboxed |
| BUG-221 | Invoice PDF cuts off long addresses | 2 | customer-reported, P2 |
| BUG-230 | Login loop on Android 15 | 3 | P1, 11 tickets |

## Output

### Sprint 41 plan for Packwise

I'd commit 18 points: finish the offline cache, build offline queue and sync, fix the Android 15 login loop, and add the offline banner. That is 71% of what this team can deliver this sprint. The plan is proposed until the team commits.

#### Sprint goal

Crews can complete a job with no signal. I kept your candidate wording. The Product Owner should confirm it.

#### Capacity

Availability cuts the team to 46.5 of 60 person-days: Ana is out 3 days, Ravi is on-call at 50%, and day 6 is a holiday for everyone. That is 193.2 effective hours.

| Person | Hours | Basis |
|---|---:|---|
| Ana | 22.4 | 6 days after holiday and PTO |
| Ravi | 14.0 | 9 days, half of them on-call |
| Developers 3, 4, 5 | 39.2 each | 9 days |
| QA | 39.2 | 9 days |

Assumptions I made because the inputs don't say: 8 hours per day, 10 meeting hours and 6 interrupt hours per person, focus factor 0.7. Names for the other three developers weren't given.

No item has an hour estimate, so I sized the commitment in points. Velocity averages 33.0 (34, 29, 38, 31). Scaling by 77.5% availability gives a forecast of about 25.6 points (range 22.5 to 29.5). That assumes the four earlier sprints ran at full availability, which the inputs don't state.

#### In

| ID | Item | Points | Note |
|---|---|---:|---|
| OFF-12 | Cache today's jobs on device (remaining work) | about 5 | 40% of 13. The 60% done figure is the developer's own estimate. Re-estimate the remainder on day 1. |
| OFF-14 | Queue status updates offline and sync | 8 | Starts after OFF-12 |
| BUG-230 | Login loop on Android 15 (P1, 11 tickets) | 3 | Start on day 1 |
| OFF-18 | Offline indicator banner | 2 | First to drop if the sprint slips, unless the Product Owner ranks it higher |

Committed: 18.2 points, 71% of forecast.

**Stretch, in order:**

| ID | Item | Points | Condition |
|---|---|---:|---|
| OFF-15 | Conflict rule for office edits while crew is offline | 5 | PM decides on "last write wins" by day 2 |
| BUG-221 | Invoice PDF cuts off long addresses (P2) | 2 | none |

Stretch of 7 points is above the usual 15% target (about 4). Commit plus stretch totals 25.2, equal to the forecast, so pulling both means the team hit its full adjusted velocity.

#### Out

| ID | Item | Points | Why |
|---|---|---:|---|
| OFF-16 | Offline photo capture with deferred upload | 8 | Adding it takes the commitment to 26.2 points, 102% of forecast. Suggest Sprint 42. |
| QBO-3 | QuickBooks sync spike | 3 | Doesn't serve the goal. The Product Owner can swap it for BUG-221 if it has a deadline. |

#### Risks

| Risk | Mitigation | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| OFF-12's remaining work is larger than 40% of 13 points, which pushes OFF-14 (8 points) past the sprint | Re-estimate on day 1. Check that OFF-12 is done by day 4. | OFF-12 developer |
| OFF-14 has about 5 working days after OFF-12 lands, with day 6 a holiday | Start the queue against the cache interface from day 1 | OFF-14 developer |
| The conflict rule isn't decided, so OFF-14 sync could ship with undefined behaviour when the office edits a job | PM decision by day 2. If it slips, OFF-15 stays out and the team agrees an interim behaviour. | PM |
| BUG-230's cause is unknown and 3 points may be low | Start on day 1, report on day 2 | Android developer |
| Ravi's on-call load exceeds 50% | Keep him off the OFF-12 to OFF-14 critical path | Scrum Master |
| The forecast rests on an assumption about past availability | Replace it with actual committed and delivered points after this sprint | Scrum Master |

If the sprint slips, drop stretch first, then the committed item the Product Owner ranks lowest. Add nothing without removing something of equal size.

#### Checkpoints

Dependencies confirmed before day 1. PM decision day 2. OFF-12 done day 4. Mid-sprint check-in day 5, before the holiday. Sprint dates weren't supplied, so these are day numbers.

#### Gate

I couldn't run `sprint_check.py` in this session, so I applied its rules by hand in points. Result: 0 fail, 18 warn, 0 info. The warnings are: no hour estimates (6), no assignees (6), unconfirmed dependencies with no RAID ID (5), and no definition of done (1). No readiness report or RAID log was supplied, so I took readiness from your description of the backlog as refined and estimated. I did not verify it against criteria.

#### Open items for the team

1. The definition of done, which the gate needs to check completion criteria.
2. Names for the OFF-12 developer, the PM and the assignees. The team assigns work.
3. Sprint dates and which three days Ana is out.
4. Whether OFF-12 at 13 points should be split. It exceeds the 5-day limit for a committed item, so I planned only the remainder.
5. Proposed RAID entries for track-delivery: two dependencies (OFF-14 on OFF-12; the PM conflict-rule decision) and three risks (OFF-12 remainder, Ravi's on-call load, BUG-230 cause). I did not write the log.

#### Files

- `out/sprint-41-plan.md`: the full plan from the team template, with the per-person capacity basis
- `out/sprint-41-gate-report.md`: the gate rules applied by hand, with the findings table
- `out/answer.md`: this summary

No RAID log was supplied, so the D-### numbers are not assigned.

Not supplied. The team states its list at planning; until then the gate cannot check completion criteria.

- Dependency confirmations: before day 1
- PM decision on conflict rule: day 2
- OFF-12 complete: day 4
- Mid-sprint check-in: day 5 (day 6 is the holiday)

Descoping order if the sprint slips: stretch items first, then the committed item the Product Owner ranks lowest. Add nothing without removing something of equal size.

skills.markdown:
---
name: plan-team-onboarding
description: 'Design a structured first-three-month ramp for employees, contractors, and agency partners. Use for a new starter, team restructure, inconsistent onboarding process, or knowledge transfer from one critical person. Covers engineering, design, product, marketing, and operations roles. Do not use for performance management, technology-specific training, hiring, or commercial offering design.'
---


> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [Writing Integrity review](../review-writing/references/detailed-review.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

A repeatable framework for building an onboarding plan that ramps new team members predictably without burning out the people training them.

## When to use

- An employee needs a written onboarding plan.
- An existing onboarding process is informal and inconsistent.
- A team is growing fast and onboarding is the bottleneck.
- An external team member needs to ramp quickly.
- A team member is leaving and their knowledge needs capturing.
- Onboarding currently takes too long and you want to reduce it.

## When NOT to use

- For ongoing performance management. That is a different problem.
- For training on a specific technology. Use targeted docs and tutorials.
- For general documentation strategy. That is a separate discipline.
- For role definition or hiring. That is a different upstream problem.

## Required inputs

- The role: what the person will do, what success looks like at 90 days.
- Existing artifacts: docs, runbooks, codebases, design files.
- The team: who will mentor, who will pair, who answers what kind of question.
- Tools and access: what accounts and systems the new person needs.
- Time budget: how much time team members can invest in onboarding.

## The framework

A good onboarding plan operates on 4 layers. Build all four.

### Layer 1: Belonging (Day 1 to Week 1)

The first week establishes belonging. Productivity follows once the person has access, relationships, and a safe way to ask questions.

- Welcome message before they start.
- Workspace and accounts ready before day 1. No "we will get to that".
- A buddy or onboarding partner assigned (someone other than the manager).
- Day 1 schedule with focused work and a small number of useful meetings.
- Introductions to the people they will work with regularly.
- A first-week rhythm: daily check-in with manager or buddy.

### Layer 2: Context (Week 1 to Week 4)

The next phase is context. The new person needs to understand the system before they can change it.

- The product or business: what we do, who we serve, why we exist.
- The team: who owns what, how decisions get made.
- The technical or operational landscape: the architecture diagram, the main tools, the key files.
- The recent past: major decisions, recent launches, current priorities.
- Active projects: what is in flight and how it fits.

A reading list is part of this. Keep it short. Annotated. Curated.

### Layer 3: Contribution (Week 2 to Week 6)

By week 2 or 3, they should make a real contribution. Early delivery exposes the context they still need.

- A first task that is small, scoped, and shippable in week 2.
- Pairing or shadowing on a real piece of work in week 3.
- Independent ownership of a small project by week 4 or 5.
- Code review, design critique, or equivalent peer feedback from the start.

The first task matters. Pick something that touches the main systems but cannot break anything important. Something that ships gives confidence and visibility.

### Layer 4: Mastery (Month 2 to Month 3)

By the end of 90 days, the person should be a full member of the team.

- Owning a project end to end.
- On-call or on-rotation if the team has one.
- Contributing to roadmap discussions and execution.
- Mentoring or supporting the next new hire.

At 90 days, document what worked and what was missing for the next person.

## The 30/60/90 plan

Every onboarding plan needs explicit milestones after the first, second, and third months.

### 30 days

- Workspace, tools, and access fully set up.
- Has met every team member.
- Understands the product, the team, and the recent context.
- Has shipped or contributed to at least one real piece of work.
- Has a clear picture of their first major project or area.

### 60 days

- Owns a project or area independently.
- Knows where to find answers without asking every time.
- Has formed working relationships beyond the immediate team.
- Has made at least one meaningful improvement to a process, doc, or codebase.

### 90 days

- Fully productive in the role.
- Participating in roadmap and planning discussions.
- Capable of training the next new hire on parts of the system.
- Comfortable raising concerns and pushing back.

If someone is significantly behind at these three checkpoints, address it directly. Either the plan is wrong, the support is wrong, or the role fit is wrong. Hoping it resolves itself does not work.

## The role-specific overlay

The four layers apply to every role, with different evidence of progress:

| Role | First contribution | Independent ownership |
|---|---|---|
| Engineering | Ship a small bug fix or refactor | Own a feature or component and join the on-call path |
| Design | Own a bounded surface such as a setting page | Lead a feature design and its review |
| Product | Write a discovery record or competitive analysis | Own a feature specification and roadmap area |
| Marketing or content | Ship a small content change | Own a campaign, channel, or complete content asset |

Use `references/onboarding-checklist.md` for the detailed role-specific sequence.

## Workflow

1. Start the plan before the new person arrives. Do not write it on day 1.
2. Pre-stage accounts, hardware, and access. This is the most common day-1 failure point.
3. Assign a buddy with written responsibilities.
4. Send the welcome message and the day-1 schedule before they start.
5. Use the first week to establish belonging and context.
6. Check in daily for the first week, weekly for the first month.
7. Run formal milestone check-ins after each month.
8. After 90 days, do a retrospective: what worked, what was missing.
9. Update the plan based on the retrospective. Onboarding is a living doc.

## Failure patterns

- **No plan.** Day 1 with no schedule, no laptop, no accounts. Sets a tone.
- **Drinking from a firehose.** 8 hours of meetings on day 1. People remember nothing.
- **No real work for too long.** Three weeks of "reading docs" is demoralizing. Ship something small early.
- **All buddy, no manager.** Buddies are great but cannot evaluate or advocate. Manager is still on the hook.
- **Tribal knowledge as gating.** "Just ask the one person who knows" works until that person is on vacation. Document the answers they keep giving.
- **No milestone evidence.** Busyness does not prove that the person can perform the role.
- **Generic plan for every role.** Engineering and marketing have different first-week needs. Use the role overlay.
- **No retrospective.** The same gaps catch every new hire because nobody updated the plan.
- **Buddy with no time.** Assigning a buddy who is also drowning is a recipe for poor onboarding and burnout. Protect their time.
- **Skipping the customer or product context.** Engineers without customer context build the wrong things. Marketers without product context write thin copy.

## Output format

Deliverables:

1. **Pre-day-1 checklist**: accounts, hardware, access, buddy assignment, welcome message.
2. **Day-1 schedule**: meeting list, intros, first deliverable.
3. **First-week reading list**: 5-10 curated, annotated docs.
4. **Three-month milestones**: the explicit checkpoints for this role.
5. **Buddy guide**: responsibilities for the onboarding partner.
6. **Manager check-in cadence**: scheduled 1:1s and milestone reviews.
7. **Retrospective template**: to fill out at 90 days for next-time improvement.

Deliver as chat output by default. Write files only if the user asks and a writable workspace exists; on an ephemeral or hosted filesystem, keep everything in the reply.

## Reference files

- [`references/onboarding-checklist.md`](references/onboarding-checklist.md): A day-by-day, week-by-week checklist for the first 30 days, with role-specific variants and a three-month review template.

## Release gate (required)

Before you deliver, run the required gate. Full
spec in [`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md).

1. Apply review-writing to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For
   a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.
2. Run review-deliverable before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until both checks have passed.

examples.title: Onboarding plan for a content manager replacing a departing lead
examples.markdown:
## Request

We have a new content marketing manager, Dana Okafor, starting Monday 7 December, and Tomas Reyes, who currently runs all our content, leaves on 18 December. Can you build the onboarding plan so Dana ramps over three months and we capture what Tomas knows before he goes? Role brief and team notes are attached.

## Inputs

Run of the built `plan-team-onboarding` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### role-brief.md

#### Content marketing manager: role brief

Company: Fernhill Software (Example Ltd), 45 people, sells scheduling software to independent clinics. Marketing team of four.

Reports to: Aisha Bakr, Head of Marketing.

What the role does
- Owns the blog (2 posts a week), the monthly customer newsletter (about 6,200 subscribers) and the case-study programme.
- Briefs and edits two freelance writers.
- Works with Product Marketing (Luis Ferreira) on launch copy.

Success at 90 days (from Aisha)
- Publishes the January and February newsletters without Tomas.
- Owns the editorial calendar for March.
- Has shipped at least two case studies.
- Organic blog sessions are not lower than the current 38,000 a month.

Known risk
- Tomas keeps the freelancer briefs, the SEO keyword sheet and the newsletter send checklist mostly in his head. The CMS publishing steps are undocumented.

#### team-and-tools.md

#### Team, tools and time

People
- Tomas Reyes, current content lead, last day Fri 18 Dec. Can give about 6 hours a week to handover, more in week 1.
- Luis Ferreira, product marketing. Can be buddy; about 2 hours a week.
- Aisha Bakr, manager. Weekly 1:1 already in calendar (30 min).
- Mei Tanaka, web developer (part-time, Tue/Thu), owns the CMS.
- Customer success lead: Joanna Pike, runs customer calls and picks case-study candidates.
- Freelance writers: Ravi and Elena (contracts run to end of March).

Tools
- CMS: Webflow-style hosted CMS (editor seat needed), Google Workspace, Slack, Mailchimp-style email platform (admin seat needed), SEO tool (shared login, to be replaced by a named seat), Notion for the editorial calendar.
- Laptop: ordered, due 25 Nov.

Existing docs
- Brand voice guide (14 pages, current).
- Editorial calendar in Notion, filled to 19 Dec.
- Last four case studies.
- No written CMS, newsletter or freelancer process.

Calendar notes
- Company closed 24 Dec to 1 Jan.
- December newsletter goes out Thu 17 Dec.

## Output

### Onboarding plan: Dana Okafor, content marketing manager

Dana has only 10 working days (7 to 18 Dec) with Tomas, and the company closes 24 Dec to 1 Jan. So the plan front-loads handover: Dana learns by running Tomas's live tasks, and writes down the process as they go. Dana publishes a post in week 1, sends the December newsletter on 17 Dec with Tomas watching, and shows on 16 and 18 Dec that the written steps work without him.

#### Decisions and assumptions for Aisha

- **Tomas's time.** The notes allow about 6 hours a week for handover. That is too little for five undocumented processes in two weeks. I planned for about 12 hours in week 1 and 10 in week 2. If Tomas can't give that, drop the freelancer introductions first, and keep the newsletter and CMS sessions.
- **Seats.** The notes say the CMS editor seat, email platform admin seat and a named SEO seat are needed. I assumed none exist yet and put them on the pre-day-1 list. The shared SEO login is used until the named seat exists.
- **Laptop.** Due 25 Nov. If it is late, Dana needs a loaner by 4 Dec.
- **Review dates.** The holiday closure falls inside month 1, so reviews are set by working time: day 30 is the week of 11 Jan, day 60 the week of 8 Feb, day 90 the week of 8 Mar. These are my dates; adjust them if Aisha prefers calendar days.
- **Not in the notes.** Freelancer rates and contract terms, the content of the SEO keyword sheet, and whether the January newsletter is already drafted. Tomas should confirm each in handover session 4.
- **Buddy.** Luis Ferreira, at about 2 hours a week, is named buddy. Aisha stays responsible for evaluation.

#### 1. Pre-day-1 checklist (complete by Fri 4 Dec)

| Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|
| Laptop delivered and tested | Aisha | 25 Nov |
| Google Workspace, Slack, Notion accounts | Aisha | 2 Dec |
| CMS editor seat | Mei Tanaka | 2 Dec |
| Email platform admin seat | Tomas | 2 Dec |
| Named SEO tool seat (ask vendor; shared login in the meantime) | Aisha | 4 Dec |
| Add Dana to marketing channels, the Notion calendar and the Thursday newsletter planning invite | Aisha | 4 Dec |

skills.description: Plan usability sessions, write neutral task scripts, or synthesize supplied participant observations. Use for explicit usability research requests; ordinary QA, code fixes, and agent walkthroughs do not establish participant evidence.

guide.what: Plan usability research or synthesize observations.
guide.when: A team needs participant tasks, sessions, or findings.
guide.inputs: The research questions, interface, participant context, and supplied observations.
guide.outputs: A session plan, neutral task scripts, or supported usability findings.
guide.example: Write neutral participant tasks for these research questions and this interface.
guide.expect: It starts from the decision the research should inform, then writes a session plan with neutral task wording or synthesizes the observations you supply. It keeps what participants said, what was observed and interpretation separate, and returns a plan or labeled provisional findings rather than inventing participants, quotes or success rates.
guide.overview: It starts from the decision the research should inform, then writes a session plan with neutral task wording or synthesizes the observations you supply. It keeps what participants said, what was observed and interpretation separate, and returns a plan or labeled provisional findings rather than inventing participants, quotes or success rates.
guide.value: Learn whether people can complete the tasks the product is meant to support. It turns a research question into neutral participant tasks or organizes supplied observations into findings that can guide a decision.

preparation.where: Provide the decision to inform, target interface, participant context and research questions. For synthesis, supply actual session notes or observations. A research plan is an output; recorded sessions are only required when asking for findings from completed research.
preparation.missing: With no observations it can prepare a study, not report participant outcomes. Thin evidence produces provisional findings. Participants, quotations and success rates cannot be invented to complete a report.

reuse.basis: Source classification and automated reference scan; cross-environment execution has not been tested.

skills.markdown:
---
name: plan-usability-study
description: "Plan usability sessions, write neutral task scripts, or synthesize supplied participant observations. Use for explicit usability research requests; ordinary QA, code fixes, and agent walkthroughs do not establish participant evidence."
license: MIT
---


# Plan usability study

Choose a research question that can change a product decision. Use the supplied product context and existing research before requesting information already available. A missing participant roster does not prevent a useful test plan.

For planning, read [Session design](references/session-design.md). Select the audience and product state, then write scenarios around participants' goals. Keep navigation labels and intended click paths out of task wording. Define observable completion conditions separately for the moderator.

Use a sample suited to the question and distinct user groups. A small formative study can reveal problems; it cannot establish population rates or prove that most problems have been found. Record the recruitment rationale and the groups not represented.

For findings, read the complete supplied observations. Keep participant reports, directly observed behavior, and interpretation distinct. Link each finding to its task and source. Count observed opportunities as well as failures. Preserve a severe problem seen by one participant even when it is uncommon in the sample.

Agent walkthroughs and static inspections can identify issues to investigate. Label their evidence accurately. Do not invent participants, quotations, timestamps, recordings, success rates, or research validation. With no session evidence, return a plan or provisional inspection findings and the evidence needed to evaluate them.

Use participant codes and omit unnecessary identifying details. Record consent requirements before recording or recruitment; a plan does not authorize contacting people or uploading recordings. Avoid real purchases or other consequential actions in test tasks unless already authorized.

Deliver the requested plan or findings with the decision each finding informs. Recommend a repair and a focused retest when supported. A recommendation is not a verified fix.

This skill adds research methods to the existing setup. Its source authority, voice, brand, and completion rules remain with the governing instructions and their existing skills.

## Request

I've attached my brief and moderator notes from four usability sessions on the Larchmont Library app, build 4.2. Please synthesize the findings by task and tell me what we should fix before the 18 November release.

## Inputs

Run of the built `plan-usability-study` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### brief.md

#### Larchmont Library app, build 4.2: study brief

Decision: which loan and hold issues to fix before the 18 November release.

Setup: moderated, in person, test accounts on a test server, 30 minutes each. Participants recorded with written consent; notes below are moderator notes, not transcripts. No task times were recorded.

Tasks (wording given to participants):
- T1: "One of your books is due tomorrow and you want to keep it longer. Do that."
- T2: "You want the novel *The Salt Road*, which is checked out. Reserve it for pickup at the Eastgate branch."
- T3: "Find out whether you owe the library any money."

Moderator completion conditions:
- T1: loan due date is extended.
- T2: hold placed with Eastgate as pickup branch.
- T3: participant states the correct balance.

Stopping rule: moderator gives a hint after about 2 minutes without progress and records it.

Recruited: 4 current cardholders from the library's volunteer panel. No under-18s, no screen-reader users.

#### session-notes.md

#### Moderator notes

##### P1 (adult, uses app weekly, iPhone)
- T1: Account > Loans > "..." menu > Renew. No hint. Done.
- T2: Searched title, tapped Reserve, picked Eastgate. No hint. Done.
- T3: Read balance from Account home. Stated it correctly. No hint.

##### P2 (older adult, first time in the app, Android)
- T1: Opened Loans, tapped the book title, looked around the detail page. Said: "I expected a button next to the book." Stalled about 2 minutes; I pointed to the "..." menu. Renewed after the hint.
- T2: Done, no hint.
- T3: Stated balance correctly, no hint.

##### P3 (parent, mostly uses the website, iPhone)
- T1: Found "..." menu, renewed. No hint.
- T2: Placed the hold but chose Northgate by mistake. Went to My Holds and tapped "Remove" to fix it. The hold was cancelled and it was number 14 in the queue. Said: "I thought it would just take it off my screen." I recreated the hold for Eastgate; the new hold is last in the queue. Counted as completed with a mistake, not a clean completion.
- T3: Stated balance correctly, no hint.

##### P4 (student, uses app monthly, Android)
- T1: Renewed from "..." menu. No hint.
- T2: Not attempted. Room booking ended the session at 25 minutes.
- T3: Stated balance correctly, no hint.

## Output

### Larchmont Library app 4.2: findings from four sessions

Fix the "Remove" button on My Holds before 18 November, and make Renew visible on the loan row. Both came from single participants in a four-person study, so the counts below describe these sessions only.

#### Results by task

| Task | Attempted | Clean, unassisted | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 Renew a book | 4 of 4 | 3 | P2 needed a hint |
| T2 Reserve for Eastgate pickup | 3 of 4 | 2 | P3 completed with a mistake; P4 not attempted |
| T3 Check what you owe | 4 of 4 | 4 | No problems |

No task times were recorded, so none are reported. The notes are moderator notes, not transcripts. The one quote below is the moderator's written record of what was said.

#### Findings

**1. Removing a hold cancels it and loses the queue place (T2, P3). Severity: high.**
P3 placed the hold with Northgate by mistake. To fix it, they tapped "Remove" in My Holds. The hold was cancelled at queue position 14. P3 said: "I thought it would just take it off my screen." The moderator recreated the hold for Eastgate, and it went to the back of the queue.

- Observed: the button cancelled the hold, and P3 did not expect that.
- Harm: the loss of queue place is not recoverable by the participant. One observation is enough to rank this high, because a real cardholder would lose a place in a long queue.
- Opportunity count: only P3 used "Remove". The other two who attempted T2 did not need to correct a hold, so the sample says nothing about how often others would.
- Hypothesis, not tested: the label "Remove" reads as hiding an item, and nothing warns that the queue place is lost. Whether the label, the missing confirmation, or both caused the mistake is not established.
- Second issue in the same sequence: P3 had no obvious way to change the pickup branch on an existing hold. The notes do not say whether such an option exists, so check the build.

**2. Renew is inside a "..." menu (T1, P2). Severity: medium.**
P2, new to the app, opened the book's detail page instead. They said: "I expected a button next to the book." After about 2 minutes without progress, the moderator pointed to the "..." menu, and P2 renewed. That is an assisted completion and should not be counted as unassisted.

- 3 of 4 found the menu without help (P1 weekly user, P3 mostly a website user, P4 monthly user). Only the first-time user failed, so the finding concerns discoverability for new users. The study did not test that directly.
- Harm: the task was recoverable with a hint, but a cardholder with a book due tomorrow and no moderator could abandon it. Whether they would is unknown.
- Hypothesis: a visible Renew button on the row would remove the problem. This is a proposal, not a verified fix.

**3. Checking the balance worked (T3).**
All four stated the balance correctly from Account home with no hints. No change is indicated by this evidence.

#### What the study cannot say

- T2 has three attempts. P4's session ended after 25 minutes because of a room booking, so there is no data from them on the reserve flow.
- Only four cardholders from the library's volunteer panel took part. There were no under-18s and no screen-reader users, so accessibility of the "..." menu and the holds list is untested.
- Neither finding supports a rate for all users.

#### Recommended before 18 November

1. **Hold removal.** Rename "Remove" to "Cancel hold" and add a confirmation that states the queue position will be lost. If the pickup branch can be changed on an existing hold, expose that option in the same screen.
2. **Renew.** Add a Renew button to each loan row, keeping the "..." menu for other actions.
3. **Retest.** Rerun T1 and T2 on the revised build with at least 3 participants, including two who have not used the app before and one screen-reader user. Reuse the same task wording and completion conditions. Add a variant of T2 where the participant has picked the wrong branch, so the correction path is observed deliberately. Record the build number and who participated.

Neither change is a verified fix until that retest is done. I did not contact anyone or alter any records.

#### Evidence record

| Participant | Task | Build | Behavior | Outcome | Assistance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | T1, T2, T3 | 4.2 | Used "..." menu; reserved Eastgate; read balance | Complete | None | session-notes.md, P1 |
| P2 | T1 | 4.2 | Opened detail page; stalled about 2 min | Complete | Hint to "..." menu | session-notes.md, P2 |
| P2 | T2, T3 | 4.2 | As expected | Complete | None | session-notes.md, P2 |
| P3 | T1, T3 | 4.2 | As expected | Complete | None | session-notes.md, P3 |
| P3 | T2 | 4.2 | Chose Northgate; tapped "Remove"; hold cancelled at position 14 | Completed with mistake | Moderator recreated hold | session-notes.md, P3 |
| P4 | T1, T3 | 4.2 | As expected | Complete | None | session-notes.md, P4 |
| P4 | T2 | 4.2 | Not attempted | Not attempted | n/a | session-notes.md, P4 |

#### Files

No files were generated beyond this answer: `./out/answer.md`. The bundled writing checker script could not be run here, so I read the text through by hand for filler and unsupported claims.
