---
name: prepare-delivery-handoff
description: 'Owns the Estate sales-to-delivery handoff at signature: the handoff package built from the executed SOW, quote, and deal record, and the incoming delivery handoff brief accepted before kickoff. Use when a deal signs and someone asks for the handoff package, the delivery handoff brief, the warm transfer, what delivery inherits, or what was promised on a signed deal. Do NOT use for technical deliverability judgment (assess-solution-delivery), the kickoff meeting or project charter (start-delivery), requirements extraction (capture-requirements), or pre-sale research and call prep (prepare-sales-pursuit).'
---


# Prepare delivery handoff

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [Writing Integrity review](../review-writing/references/detailed-review.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

A signed deal crosses from the people who sold it to the people who deliver it, and
most of what the seller knows is about to walk out of the room. This skill captures
it in one artifact family with one schema, produced at two moments:

- **Moment 1, at signature: the handoff package.** Assembled from the executed SOW,
  the quote, and the deal record. What was sold, what was decided and why, who was in
  the room, what was promised, what is still open. The SSL walks it to the delivery
  team in a recorded warm-transfer session.
- **Moment 2, at delivery acceptance: the handoff brief.** The incoming team's
  orientation document. Same sections, now completed with the readiness view, the
  week-one discovery agenda, and the definition of done. Delivery accepting this
  brief is the gate into Mobilize.

Both moments share the 12-section catalog and one manifest schema. Earlier drafts
split this across a sell-side agent and a delivery-side agent with two divergent
schemas and no defined mapping between them; facts died at the seam. That defect is
why this is one skill. The package is the brief at an earlier state of completion,
never a different document.

## Project context required

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement, source records, private output location,
and intended audience. Map reference roles such as Program Lead, CSE, Solution Lead,
and Pursuit Lead to that project's authorized owners; these labels do not impose
an employer organization chart or signing authority. The executed agreement and
accepted project plan determine gates, commercial rules, and support obligations.
Keep account history, risk assessments, credentials, and client evidence outside
portable skill sources. A cached account, attached Project, or available connector
is not authorization to read, write, or publish.

## Governance, delegated

- **evidence-core runs first.** Every load-bearing claim enters the ledger
  with source, confidence, and as-of date before any section is written. If a
  required domain is Insufficient, produce the handoff readiness gap memo and stop;
  a full handoff after an Insufficient gate is a hard fail. The artifact contract is
  `sales_to_delivery_handoff` in evidence-core's `reference/artifact-registry.json`.
- **brand-renderer owns the rendered surface.** No inlined hex, no
  duplicated palette. Brand applies during the build.
- **Writing-integrity owns writing review.** Run its bundled diagnostics on the rendered prose. No em
  dashes, sentence-case headings, no AI-tell constructions.
- **The money rule.** Contract figures come from the executed SOW and its quote
  (Q-number) only. Never from Slack, never from memory, never from the proposal
  deck, which may predate the final negotiation. This skill renders figures; it
  never authors them.

If a governor is not installed on the current surface, state the check it would
have run, do the best manual substitute, and say that is what you did.

## Source authority, in order

The executed SOW is the most authoritative source; read its scope, exclusions,
deliverables, fee model, dates, and assumptions verbatim. Then, in order: the quote,
Salesforce (account, opportunity, stage history, contact roles), Drive (proposal,
discovery decks, transcripts), Slack and Gmail (late changes, verbal commitments,
access blockers), calendar and call notes. The AE/CSE debrief comes last and narrow:
only the tacit room context no system holds. Mine the systems before interviewing
anyone. Recency can override authority on current state: a recent thread reopening a
settled clause outranks the SOW on where things stand now, and that conflict is
surfaced, never silently resolved. Full connector table, search anchors, and
corroboration rules: `references/source-authority.md`.

## The 12 sections

Full catalog with each section's job and bar: `references/brief-catalog.md`.

| # | Section | # | Section |
|---|---------|---|---------|
| 01 | The engagement | 07 | Sell-cycle promises |
| 02 | What came before | 08 | Risks, assumptions, gaps |
| 03 | Process and current state | 09 | The people |
| 04 | System landscape | 10 | Relevant prior engagements |
| 05 | Solution shape | 11 | Discovery sessions |
| 06 | Decisions inherited | 12 | What good looks like |

Structural rule, inherited from the provenance doctrine: **sections are never
dropped.** Every section is present in every handoff. It is either filled with
sourced facts, or it carries an explicit named gap with an owner, a resolve-by
date, and the gate it blocks. A section that genuinely does not apply (greenfield,
no prior engagement) says so in one sourced line. A blank is a gate failure.

Three sections carry special rules:

- **07 Sell-cycle promises.** Anything said to the client that is not in the
  executed SOW is a flagged liability, sourced to where and when it was said, with
  an owner. Promises confirmed to be in the SOW are listed with the clause. This
  section exists because unwritten promises are the single most common way sales
  gets pulled back into delivery after signature.
- **11 Discovery sessions.** The week-one agenda, built directly from the ledger's
  Unknowns and Inferreds. Every session names an owner, the right attendees, and
  the concrete output that closes the question. Never droppable.
- **12 What good looks like.** The definition of done plus the readiness checklist.
  Every criterion is observable, carries a binary test, and ladders to the one
  outcome stated in section 01. Never droppable.

Specs for 11 and 12, including the readiness checklist items:
`references/week-one-definition-of-done.md`.

## Workflow

1. **Orient.** Find the executed SOW and the Q-number. Confirm the deal is signed;
   this skill does not run pre-signature. Pin the moment: package (signature) or
   brief (delivery acceptance). Stamp the manifest with client, engagement,
   source snapshot, and as-of date.
2. **Run evidence-core.** Harvest in the authority order above. Read transcripts
   verbatim, never summaries. An un-searched source is an Unknown, not a confirmed
   absence. Carry the delivery-lens and maturity-gap flags forward from the pursuit
   so delivery inherits them instead of rediscovering them.
3. **Build the manifest.** JSON, schema in `references/package-spec.md`. Fill the
   12 sections from the ledger: roughly 80 percent of a clean deal assembles
   mechanically from the SOW and quote. Everything the ledger could not source
   becomes a gap entry with owner, resolve-by, and blocked gate. Mark every scope
   item in or out. Log promises with where they were said and whether they are in
   the SOW.
4. **Gate it.**
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/check_handoff.py manifest.json
   ```
   Exit 0 passes, 1 fails, 2 is a usage or parse error. Report the counts it
   prints, never an adjective. The gate is blocking at both moments.
5. **Render.** Project the manifest through brand-renderer as the styled
   HTML or portable Markdown brief. Confidence maps to presentation: Confirmed
   reads as fact, Inferred as inference with its basis, Unknown as a named open
   question, conflicts as flagged divergences with both values shown. Run
   review-writing on the rendered prose. Never hand-patch the render; fix the manifest
   and re-render.
6. **Transfer and land.** Moment 1: support the warm transfer (the SSL walks the
   package to the Program Lead and Solution Lead in a recorded session), then
   ingest that session's transcript to close open questions. Moment 2: delivery
   accepts the brief; record the acceptance. Deliver the file, commit it to the
   client folder, write session memory pointing at the files.
7. **Close the loop.** Top three things delivery inherits, then the landmines.
   Flag the biggest judgment call in the handoff and argue the other side of it.

### Seed DELIVERY-STATE.md at acceptance

When delivery accepts the brief (Moment 2), create `DELIVERY-STATE.md` at the
engagement folder root per delivery-orchestrator's `references/delivery-state-spec.md`:
engagement meta, current stage, all eight gate statuses with `brief_accepted` marked
accepted with the date, artifact locations (including the brief), and the first
append-only dated log line. If the file already exists, update the gate and log
instead of recreating it.

## Durable output

Every run leaves a Markdown record per `_shared/output-contract.md`: the
rendered brief itself when one ships, or a run record carrying the gate
counts, the open gaps with owners, and the outstanding human actions when the
run stops early. Deliver or link the file with the manifest; never just say
it was written.

## Depth tests during authoring

- Name real things: systems, people, numbers, clauses, each with a source. No
  "the platform", no "various stakeholders".
- State the success spine early in 01 and return to it in 12.
- Decisions carry status, owner, and rationale; open ones are visible, not buried.
- Every assumption states what breaks if it is false.
- People postures are sourced, never asserted; deal-versus-delivery stakeholder
  mismatches are explicitly flagged, because a sponsor who vanishes at kickoff is
  a top cause of failed starts.
- Section 11 is built from the Unknowns: every open question maps to a session
  whose output closes it, or names why it waits.

## When time is short

Cut in this order, and say what you cut: 10 (prior engagements, keep a one-line
pointer), 03 (keep the breaks list, drop the full as-is map), 05 (point at the
Solution Brief), depth in 02. Never cut: sourcing, section 07, the gap entries
with owners, sections 11 and 12, or the gate.

## Running unattended

The warm transfer and the acceptance need humans. On a headless run: build the
manifest, run the gate and review with review-writing, and stop with the findings and the open
gaps. Say plainly that the transfer session and acceptance are outstanding. Never
record an acceptance nobody gave.

## Boundaries

This skill is the first delivery link in the chain that runs SOW, then
prepare-delivery-handoff, then kickoff, then status, then UAT, then manage-cutover-closeout. Its
upstream producer is the sales side: the executed SOW and quote arrive as
fixed input. Its downstream consumer is start-delivery, which
turns the accepted brief into the charter and governance pack.

- Does not judge technical deliverability or carry implementation depth. Section
  05 is orientation only; the deep answer is assess-solution-delivery.
- Does not run the kickoff or write the project charter. That is
  start-delivery.
- Does not extract or structure requirements. That is capture-requirements.
- Does not do pursuit research or call prep. That is prepare-sales-pursuit, pre-sale
  only.
- Does not price, staff, commit dates, or reinterpret scope. The quote owns every
  number; the Pursuit Lead and delivery leads own the decisions. It assembles and
  transfers.
- Does not initiate change orders. If delivery intent already differs from the
  SOW, that is a flagged conflict for the Pursuit Lead, not a rewrite.

## Files

- `scripts/check_handoff.py`: the gate. Validates a handoff manifest: all 12
  sections present and either sourced or gapped with owner and resolve-by, 11 and
  12 non-empty, every scope item marked in or out, promises sourced, contract
  figures traced to the SOW or quote, no em dashes. Stdlib only.
- `scripts/s2d_selftest.py`: runs the gate against the shipped fixtures and fails
  loudly on any drift. Run it after any edit to the checker.
- `scripts/fixtures/`: passing and failing manifests the selftest uses.
- `references/brief-catalog.md`: the 12 sections, each with its job and its bar.
- `references/package-spec.md`: the manifest schema, moment semantics, warm
  transfer, and record seeding.
- `references/week-one-definition-of-done.md`: section 11 and 12 specs and the
  readiness checklist.

A signed deal crosses from the people who sold it to the people who deliver it, and most of what the seller knows is about to walk out of the room. This skill captures it in one artifact family with one schema, produced at two moments:

  • Moment 1, at signature: the handoff package. Assembled from the executed SOW,

the quote, and the deal record. What was sold, what was decided and why, who was in the room, what was promised, what is still open. The SSL walks it to the delivery team in a recorded warm-transfer session.

  • Moment 2, at delivery acceptance: the handoff brief. The incoming team's

orientation document. Same sections, now completed with the readiness view, the week-one discovery agenda, and the definition of done. Delivery accepting this brief is the gate into Mobilize.

Both moments share the 12-section catalog and one manifest schema. Earlier drafts split this across a sell-side agent and a delivery-side agent with two divergent schemas and no defined mapping between them; facts died at the seam. That defect is why this is one skill. The package is the brief at an earlier state of completion, never a different document.

Project context required

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement, source records, private output location, and intended audience. Map reference roles such as Program Lead, CSE, Solution Lead, and Pursuit Lead to that project's authorized owners; these labels do not impose an employer organization chart or signing authority. The executed agreement and accepted project plan determine gates, commercial rules, and support obligations. Keep account history, risk assessments, credentials, and client evidence outside portable skill sources. A cached account, attached Project, or available connector is not authorization to read, write, or publish.

Governance, delegated

  • evidence-core runs first. Every load-bearing claim enters the ledger

with source, confidence, and as-of date before any section is written. If a required domain is Insufficient, produce the handoff readiness gap memo and stop; a full handoff after an Insufficient gate is a hard fail. The artifact contract is sales_to_delivery_handoff in evidence-core's reference/artifact-registry.json.

  • brand-renderer owns the rendered surface. No inlined hex, no

duplicated palette. Brand applies during the build.

  • Writing-integrity owns writing review. Run its bundled diagnostics on the rendered prose. No em

dashes, sentence-case headings, no AI-tell constructions.

  • The money rule. Contract figures come from the executed SOW and its quote

(Q-number) only. Never from Slack, never from memory, never from the proposal deck, which may predate the final negotiation. This skill renders figures; it never authors them.

If a governor is not installed on the current surface, state the check it would have run, do the best manual substitute, and say that is what you did.

Source authority, in order

The executed SOW is the most authoritative source; read its scope, exclusions, deliverables, fee model, dates, and assumptions verbatim. Then, in order: the quote, Salesforce (account, opportunity, stage history, contact roles), Drive (proposal, discovery decks, transcripts), Slack and Gmail (late changes, verbal commitments, access blockers), calendar and call notes. The AE/CSE debrief comes last and narrow: only the tacit room context no system holds. Mine the systems before interviewing anyone. Recency can override authority on current state: a recent thread reopening a settled clause outranks the SOW on where things stand now, and that conflict is surfaced, never silently resolved. Full connector table, search anchors, and corroboration rules: references/source-authority.md.

The 12 sections

Full catalog with each section's job and bar: references/brief-catalog.md.

#Section#Section
01The engagement07Sell-cycle promises
02What came before08Risks, assumptions, gaps
03Process and current state09The people
04System landscape10Relevant prior engagements
05Solution shape11Discovery sessions
06Decisions inherited12What good looks like

Structural rule, inherited from the provenance doctrine: sections are never dropped. Every section is present in every handoff. It is either filled with sourced facts, or it carries an explicit named gap with an owner, a resolve-by date, and the gate it blocks. A section that genuinely does not apply (greenfield, no prior engagement) says so in one sourced line. A blank is a gate failure.

Three sections carry special rules:

  • 07 Sell-cycle promises. Anything said to the client that is not in the

executed SOW is a flagged liability, sourced to where and when it was said, with an owner. Promises confirmed to be in the SOW are listed with the clause. This section exists because unwritten promises are the single most common way sales gets pulled back into delivery after signature.

  • 11 Discovery sessions. The week-one agenda, built directly from the ledger's

Unknowns and Inferreds. Every session names an owner, the right attendees, and the concrete output that closes the question. Never droppable.

  • 12 What good looks like. The definition of done plus the readiness checklist.

Every criterion is observable, carries a binary test, and ladders to the one outcome stated in section 01. Never droppable.

Specs for 11 and 12, including the readiness checklist items: references/week-one-definition-of-done.md.

Workflow

  1. Orient. Find the executed SOW and the Q-number. Confirm the deal is signed;

this skill does not run pre-signature. Pin the moment: package (signature) or brief (delivery acceptance). Stamp the manifest with client, engagement, source snapshot, and as-of date.

  1. Run evidence-core. Harvest in the authority order above. Read transcripts

verbatim, never summaries. An un-searched source is an Unknown, not a confirmed absence. Carry the delivery-lens and maturity-gap flags forward from the pursuit so delivery inherits them instead of rediscovering them.

  1. Build the manifest. JSON, schema in references/package-spec.md. Fill the

12 sections from the ledger: roughly 80 percent of a clean deal assembles mechanically from the SOW and quote. Everything the ledger could not source becomes a gap entry with owner, resolve-by, and blocked gate. Mark every scope item in or out. Log promises with where they were said and whether they are in the SOW.

  1. Gate it.

``bash python3 scripts/check_handoff.py manifest.json `` Exit 0 passes, 1 fails, 2 is a usage or parse error. Report the counts it prints, never an adjective. The gate is blocking at both moments.

  1. Render. Project the manifest through brand-renderer as the styled

HTML or portable Markdown brief. Confidence maps to presentation: Confirmed reads as fact, Inferred as inference with its basis, Unknown as a named open question, conflicts as flagged divergences with both values shown. Run review-writing on the rendered prose. Never hand-patch the render; fix the manifest and re-render.

  1. Transfer and land. Moment 1: support the warm transfer (the SSL walks the

package to the Program Lead and Solution Lead in a recorded session), then ingest that session's transcript to close open questions. Moment 2: delivery accepts the brief; record the acceptance. Deliver the file, commit it to the client folder, write session memory pointing at the files.

  1. Close the loop. Top three things delivery inherits, then the landmines.

Flag the biggest judgment call in the handoff and argue the other side of it.

Seed DELIVERY-STATE.md at acceptance

When delivery accepts the brief (Moment 2), create DELIVERY-STATE.md at the engagement folder root per delivery-orchestrator's references/delivery-state-spec.md: engagement meta, current stage, all eight gate statuses with brief_accepted marked accepted with the date, artifact locations (including the brief), and the first append-only dated log line. If the file already exists, update the gate and log instead of recreating it.

Durable output

Every run leaves a Markdown record per _shared/output-contract.md: the rendered brief itself when one ships, or a run record carrying the gate counts, the open gaps with owners, and the outstanding human actions when the run stops early. Deliver or link the file with the manifest; never just say it was written.

Depth tests during authoring

  • Name real things: systems, people, numbers, clauses, each with a source. No

"the platform", no "various stakeholders".

  • State the success spine early in 01 and return to it in 12.
  • Decisions carry status, owner, and rationale; open ones are visible, not buried.
  • Every assumption states what breaks if it is false.
  • People postures are sourced, never asserted; deal-versus-delivery stakeholder

mismatches are explicitly flagged, because a sponsor who vanishes at kickoff is a top cause of failed starts.

  • Section 11 is built from the Unknowns: every open question maps to a session

whose output closes it, or names why it waits.

Cut in this order, and say what you cut: 10 (prior engagements, keep a one-line pointer), 03 (keep the breaks list, drop the full as-is map), 05 (point at the Solution Brief), depth in 02. Never cut: sourcing, section 07, the gap entries with owners, sections 11 and 12, or the gate.

The warm transfer and the acceptance need humans. On a headless run: build the manifest, run the gate and review with review-writing, and stop with the findings and the open gaps. Say plainly that the transfer session and acceptance are outstanding. Never record an acceptance nobody gave.

Boundaries

This skill is the first delivery link in the chain that runs SOW, then prepare-delivery-handoff, then kickoff, then status, then UAT, then manage-cutover-closeout. Its upstream producer is the sales side: the executed SOW and quote arrive as fixed input. Its downstream consumer is start-delivery, which turns the accepted brief into the charter and governance pack.

  • Does not judge technical deliverability or carry implementation depth. Section

05 is orientation only; the deep answer is assess-solution-delivery.

  • Does not run the kickoff or write the project charter. That is

start-delivery.

  • Does not extract or structure requirements. That is capture-requirements.
  • Does not do pursuit research or call prep. That is prepare-sales-pursuit, pre-sale

only.

  • Does not price, staff, commit dates, or reinterpret scope. The quote owns every

number; the Pursuit Lead and delivery leads own the decisions. It assembles and transfers.

  • Does not initiate change orders. If delivery intent already differs from the

SOW, that is a flagged conflict for the Pursuit Lead, not a rewrite.

Files

  • scripts/check_handoff.py: the gate. Validates a handoff manifest: all 12

sections present and either sourced or gapped with owner and resolve-by, 11 and 12 non-empty, every scope item marked in or out, promises sourced, contract figures traced to the SOW or quote, no em dashes. Stdlib only.

  • scripts/s2d_selftest.py: runs the gate against the shipped fixtures and fails

loudly on any drift. Run it after any edit to the checker.

  • scripts/fixtures/: passing and failing manifests the selftest uses.
  • references/brief-catalog.md: the 12 sections, each with its job and its bar.
  • references/package-spec.md: the manifest schema, moment semantics, warm

transfer, and record seeding.

  • references/week-one-definition-of-done.md: section 11 and 12 specs and the

readiness checklist.

  • references/source-authority.md: connector table, search anchors, corroboration

and conflict rules.

a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.

  1. Run brand-renderer on the branded artifact: palette, borders, radii, logo,

footer.

  1. Run review-deliverable before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until every check that applies has passed.

examples.title: Handoff package for a signed Service Cloud support migration
examples.markdown:
## Request

The Tidewater Provisions deal signed on 30 October. Can you build the handoff package for the delivery team from the SOW excerpt and my deal notes in inputs/? I'm walking it to the delivery leads later this week, so I need to know what we promised and what is still open.

## Inputs

Run of the built `prepare-delivery-handoff` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Other files it produced, not shown here: `manifest.json`.

#### deal-notes.md

#### Deal notes (from the AE, Priya Nandakumar), 2026-11-03

Team on our side: Priya (AE), Tom Aldous (Pursuit Lead), Jun Park (CSE). Delivery leads not yet assigned beyond Sam Whitcombe (Solution Lead).

**Client people.** Marguerite Lindqvist (COO, signed, economic buyer, drove the deal). Callum Reyes (Head of Support, day-to-day contact, will own go-live). Dee Okafor (IT Manager, owns NetSuite). Dee was never in a deal meeting; Callum says she "will sort access".

**Things said during the sale**

skills.markdown:
---
name: prepare-job-application
description: Assess, tailor, prepare interviews, fill, or resume the candidate's applications using current postings and private career evidence. Never submit without explicit authorization.
---


# Prepare job application

Use only the candidate identity, career records, thresholds, author profile and destinations explicitly supplied or authorized for this task. Record names below describe a suggested source map; resolve them under the confirmed career root or accept equivalent supplied records. None is a bundled personal default. Missing optional context does not block a bounded draft from supplied facts.

Run one role at a time from current evidence without relying on conversation history.

## Start here

Resolve the career evidence root from explicit task input or the candidate's confirmed operating context. Do not search a machine-specific default. Paths below are a suggested record layout under that root, not files bundled with this skill. Accept an equivalent source map when the candidate organizes records differently.

Read `00_Master/Career_Application_Operating_Context.md` first. Then load only:

- the current live posting;
- the current role's `Role_Work_Record.md`, when one exists; and
- the source files named by the operating context for the current mode.

Do not load every prior application or reconstruct the full job-search folder unless a cross-surface correction requires it.

This estate package contains workflow instructions and validation code. Private career evidence, submitted applications, and resumes remain in the subject authority. If that source is unavailable, ask for the specific current evidence needed for the request or use an explicitly supplied dated bundle. Do not assume this package includes those private records. Return proposed record changes for the user to save when the live destination is unavailable.

## Invocation modes

Infer the mode from the candidate's request. The candidate can also state it directly.

- Codex: `$prepare-job-application assess <URL>`
- Claude Code: `/prepare-job-application assess <URL>`
- Claude chat or Cowork: enable **Career Application**, then say `Use Career Application to assess <URL>`.

- `$prepare-job-application assess <URL>`: verify the live posting, screen the role, and recommend pursue or skip.
- `$prepare-job-application find <criteria>`: find current roles, screen them, and return a shortlist. Do not create application folders until the candidate chooses a role.
- `$prepare-job-application tailor <URL>`: create or update the role work record and a role-specific resume copy. Do not overwrite a master resume.
- `$prepare-job-application interview <company or role>`: build a role-specific interview plan from the current posting and evidence-backed story bank.
- `$prepare-job-application fill <URL>`: open the form, fill supported factual fields, upload approved materials, and stop at the authorization boundaries below.
- `$prepare-job-application status <company or role>`: read the tracker and role work record, then report the verified state and next action.
- `$prepare-job-application continue <company or role>`: resume from the saved role work record rather than from prior chat history.

If the request does not specify a mode, use `assess` for a new URL and `continue` for a named existing role.

## Assess

1. Verify the employer's current posting. Treat reposts, aggregators, and old snapshots as secondary.
2. Screen the role against the candidate’s confirmed opportunity criteria. Derive the work requirements from the live posting; do not score it against a fixed career identity.
3. Map requirements into four groups: strong evidence, transferable evidence, real gaps, and unsupported or unanswered questions.
4. Give a direct pursue or skip recommendation. Do not tailor materials for a skip.
5. When the candidate explicitly chooses pursue or skip, update `03_Tracker/applications.md` in the live source. A skip needs no application folder unless notes would prevent repeated research. In a portable session, create an updated tracker copy for the candidate instead of claiming the live tracker changed.

## Tailor and prepare

1. Create `01_Applications/Current/YYYY-MM-DD_Company_Role/` under the live source.
2. Copy `02_Templates/Role_Work_Record_Template.md` into that folder as `Role_Work_Record.md` and fill it from evidence.
3. Read `00_Master/Career_Narrative_Translation_Guide.md`. Map the role’s actual requirements to relevant evidence in the role record before drafting. Derive emphasis from the posting and current request rather than a standing career theme.
4. Select program records through the confirmed evidence map for the role's mandates. For a reusable product or governed system, preserve its problem, user, mechanism, risk-specific tests, growth path and verified state. Keep distribution, persistence and adoption claims distinct; do not lead with artifact counts.
5. For client-facing or transformation roles, select the supported decisions and results that demonstrate the posting. Client, portfolio, people and practice examples are available when relevant; no pair is mandatory. Keep pursuit, project, authored-quote and realized-outcome counts distinct. No named historical client or metric is a default input.
6. For product, platform, identity, security or responsible-AI roles, select relevant product evidence from the supplied map. Keep local build and test proof separate from deployment, access, usage and adoption.
7. For assessment, workforce, enablement or people-system roles, preserve source-bank authorship, human-review boundaries, and the difference between built, published privately, shared, run and adopted.
8. For each selected program, preserve the problem or decision, the candidate's ownership, the mechanism, the evidence-backed result, and the real gap or state boundary. Retain the constraint or pivot when it proves leadership or judgment. For governed skills, distinguish original authorship, later estate governance or integration, and later contributor authorship; admission, repair, rename, or consolidation does not establish sole authorship of every package.
9. Select the base resume using the operating-context router. Copy it into the role folder before editing.
10. Before drafting, inventory relevant prior role-specific resumes and historical variants. Read the versions that cover the role mandate and note in the role work record what prior wording or layout to retain, revise, or exclude. Treat them as writing history, never as current claim authority; recheck carried claims against current evidence. A clipped read is incomplete.
11. Tailor only what the posting supports: headline, executive profile, expertise order, selected bullet order or wording, and technology emphasis. Intentional selection is required; do not collapse unrelated programs into one “AI tools” bullet, a platform list, or a playbook count; do not force the entire portfolio into the document.
12. Keep private evidence notes separate from employer-facing materials. Do not place client-sensitive facts, internal identifiers, repositories, or unsupported metrics in application files.
13. Apply the candidate's `apply-author-style` with an explicitly supplied confirmed profile and `review-writing` rules. Run the bundled writing diagnostics as a deterministic gate where it is installed, not as permission to flatten real resume lists.
14. Render and inspect every changed DOCX. Verify accessibility and document integrity. Separately read the finished copy against the role mandate and evidence map; layout review does not prove content quality.
15. Complete the `Resume source review` receipt in the role work record and run `python3 scripts/check_role_resume_readiness.py` against that record before calling a tailored resume prepared locally. The checker verifies a completed receipt and readable files, not the truth or quality of its prose; perform the content review yourself.
16. Update the role work record and tracker with the exact local state. When the source is unavailable, use a supplied role-work-record template or clearly label a new draft record and return it for the user to save.

## Prepare for interviews

1. Verify the current posting and read the role work record. Do not prepare from a remembered title or an expired posting when a live source is available.
2. Read `00_Master/Leadership_Interview_Evidence_Map.md`, `04_Interview/Interview_Preparation.md`, and `05_Reference/Story_Bank/Success_Stories.md`. Add only the program records needed for the role's primary mandates.
3. Derive likely interview areas from the posting and current request. Select relevant evidence rather than requiring a standard set of career themes. Do not turn the result into a generic question dump.
4. Select no more than six anchor stories. For each one, prepare a 30-second headline, a two-minute causal answer, likely follow-ups, the difficult decision or conversation, the turnaround mechanism, the result, and the evidence boundary.
5. Use the order: problem or stakes, the candidate's mandate, decision, mechanism, resistance or constraint, turning point, evidence-backed result, and learning. Name what changed because of the candidate rather than only describing the artifact.
6. Preserve ownership boundaries. Do not claim that the candidate performed every delivery task, that forecast value was realized, that UAT equals production, or that an opportunity became a win without evidence.
7. Do not fabricate a direct-report performance case, hiring decision, promotion decision, team-conflict case, or quantified adoption result. If a target role is likely to test one of those areas, mark it as an evidence gap and ask the candidate for a real event before drafting the answer.
8. Keep closed corrective-action history out of routine preparation. Use it only if the candidate explicitly chooses that material for a specific answer.
9. Save role-specific interview work inside the application folder. Do not overwrite the master interview book for one employer.

## Fill and submit

Filling an application does not authorize submission.

Fill supported factual fields and upload reviewed files. Pause for the candidate on:

- salary expectations;
- unconfirmed work authorization or sponsorship answers;
- demographic or self-identification questions;
- legal attestations, signatures, and acknowledgments;
- MFA and CAPTCHA; and
- the final Submit action.

Submit only when the candidate explicitly authorizes that specific application. After submission, capture the confirmation or receipt and record it in `Role_Work_Record.md` before marking the tracker `Submitted`.

## Preserve execution truth

Use these states precisely: `researching`, `skipped`, `prepared locally`, `filled and awaiting submission`, `submitted`, `screen`, `interview`, `offer`, and `closed`.

A generated file is only `prepared locally`. A populated form is only `filled and awaiting submission`. `Submitted` requires destination-side confirmation or a receipt.

End material work with four facts: **changed now**, **verified**, **still unchanged**, and the **exact next action**.

## Boundaries

- Preserve official titles and dates exactly.
- Do not invent scope, reporting lines, direct-report counts, adoption analytics, production scale, compensation, or realized savings.
- Do not turn a difficult conversation into a fabricated conflict story or remove the evidence boundary to make an answer sound more decisive.
- Do not recast historical titles to match a posting.
- Do not update a downstream claim first. New evidence enters through the evidence ledger and program portfolio, then propagates according to the translation guide.
- Use the candidate’s explicitly confirmed role target; do not substitute another level or career lane without their choice.
- Do not publish, message recruiters, or submit an application unless the candidate asks for that action.
- Do not treat remembered role details as current when the live posting can be checked.
- Treat supplied career records and any explicitly requested evidence bundle as private personal material. The reusable workflow contains no career records; do not attach private evidence to its distributable plugin.

## Audience and content review gate

Before drafting, declare the audience, document purpose, intended reader action, author voice, and consequence level. These determine style, density, terminology, and prose-review depth. Internal updates use light review; hiring, public portfolio, client proposals, and consequential work use deep review. Accuracy and privacy are required at every depth. Do not apply a word blacklist or AI-detector scoring.

For a résumé, retrieve the career foundation and relevant prior résumé before selecting examples. Check roles, dates, responsibilities and ownership for accuracy. Review why the selected evidence fits the role; leadership, client, commercial and product examples are not universally required sections. A portfolio handout is a separate purpose and must not replace a résumé. Choose length after selecting substantive coverage.

The source-review section must include `Content review` pointing to an absolute JSON receipt. The receipt contains `artifact_sha256` for the entire DOCX, `brief`, `review`, and `source_files` with IDs, absolute paths, exact file SHA256 hashes, and snapshot revisions. `review` binds the exact DOCX paragraph text hash, pins all reviewed sources, names the reviewer, supplies exact draft excerpts for required coverage, and separately records accuracy, representation, writing, and layout reviews with concrete notes. The shared `content-review.ts` module supplies the schema, required dimensions, and audience-derived depth. Review the full finished prose; a passing gate checks bindings and attestations, not semantic truth. Changing the draft, source, or brief invalidates the review. Run the readiness checker before replacing or uploading the artifact. Existing prepared artifacts are dated history until rechecked; never rewrite submitted packets.

## Explicit private evidence export

The reusable plugin contains methods and validators, not a candidate's records. If a private evidence snapshot is requested, run `python3 scripts/build_portable_bundle.py --source-map /approved/private/sources.json --output /approved/private/new-export`. Both paths must be explicitly selected; there is no automatic career-folder discovery. The new output must be outside all source skills trees and enclosing plugin packages.

The JSON source map has `format: 1`, an authorized `owner`, and a nonempty `files` array. Each entry supplies an absolute `source`, a safe relative `destination`, and its exact `sha256`; optional `required` lists mandatory destinations. Pin only evidence authorized for this export. A stale hash, missing required source, path escape or existing output blocks it. The resulting `career-evidence.zip` is a private evidence snapshot with workflow copies for provenance; it is not an independently installable skill and requires the separately installed workflow and dependencies. The helper neither installs nor uploads it.

  5. Use the order: problem or stakes, the candidate's mandate, decision, mechanism, resistance or constraint, turning point, evidence-backed result, and learning. Name what changed because of the candidate rather than only describing the artifact.
  6. Preserve ownership boundaries. Do not claim that the candidate performed every delivery task, that forecast value was realized, that UAT equals production, or that an opportunity became a win without evidence.
  7. Do not fabricate a direct-report performance case, hiring decision, promotion decision, team-conflict case, or quantified adoption result. If a target role is likely to test one of those areas, mark it as an evidence gap and ask the candidate for a real event before drafting the answer.
  8. Keep closed corrective-action history out of routine preparation. Use it only if the candidate explicitly chooses that material for a specific answer.
  9. Save role-specific interview work inside the application folder. Do not overwrite the master interview book for one employer.

Fill and submit

Filling an application does not authorize submission.

Fill supported factual fields and upload reviewed files. Pause for the candidate on:

  • salary expectations;
  • unconfirmed work authorization or sponsorship answers;
  • demographic or self-identification questions;
  • legal attestations, signatures, and acknowledgments;
  • MFA and CAPTCHA; and
  • the final Submit action.

Submit only when the candidate explicitly authorizes that specific application. After submission, capture the confirmation or receipt and record it in Role_Work_Record.md before marking the tracker Submitted.

Preserve execution truth

Use these states precisely: researching, skipped, prepared locally, filled and awaiting submission, submitted, screen, interview, offer, and closed.

A generated file is only prepared locally. A populated form is only filled and awaiting submission. Submitted requires destination-side confirmation or a receipt.

End material work with four facts: changed now, verified, still unchanged, and the exact next action.

Boundaries

  • Preserve official titles and dates exactly.
  • Do not invent scope, reporting lines, direct-report counts, adoption analytics, production scale, compensation, or realized savings.
  • Do not turn a difficult conversation into a fabricated conflict story or remove the evidence boundary to make an answer sound more decisive.
  • Do not recast historical titles to match a posting.
  • Do not update a downstream claim first. New evidence enters through the evidence ledger and program portfolio, then propagates according to the translation guide.
  • Use the candidate’s explicitly confirmed role target; do not substitute another level or career lane without their choice.
  • Do not publish, message recruiters, or submit an application unless the candidate asks for that action.
  • Do not treat remembered role details as current when the live posting can be checked.
  • Treat supplied career records and any explicitly requested evidence bundle as private personal material. The reusable workflow contains no career records; do not attach private evidence to its distributable plugin.

Audience and content review gate

Before drafting, declare the audience, document purpose, intended reader action, author voice, and consequence level. These determine style, density, terminology, and prose-review depth. Internal updates use light review; hiring, public portfolio, client proposals, and consequential work use deep review. Accuracy and privacy are required at every depth. Do not apply a word blacklist or AI-detector scoring.

For a résumé, retrieve the career foundation and relevant prior résumé before selecting examples. Check roles, dates, responsibilities and ownership for accuracy. Review why the selected evidence fits the role; leadership, client, commercial and product examples are not universally required sections. A portfolio handout is a separate purpose and must not replace a résumé. Choose length after selecting substantive coverage.

The source-review section must include Content review pointing to an absolute JSON receipt. The receipt contains artifact_sha256 for the entire DOCX, brief, review, and source_files with IDs, absolute paths, exact file SHA256 hashes, and snapshot revisions. review binds the exact DOCX paragraph text hash, pins all reviewed sources, names the reviewer, supplies exact draft excerpts for required coverage, and separately records accuracy, representation, writing, and layout reviews with concrete notes. The shared content-review.ts module supplies the schema, required dimensions, and audience-derived depth. Review the full finished prose; a passing gate checks bindings and attestations, not semantic truth. Changing the draft, source, or brief invalidates the review. Run the readiness checker before replacing or uploading the artifact. Existing prepared artifacts are dated history until rechecked; never rewrite submitted packets.

Explicit private evidence export

The reusable plugin contains methods and validators, not a candidate's records. If a private evidence snapshot is requested, run python3 scripts/build_portable_bundle.py --source-map /approved/private/sources.json --output /approved/private/new-export. Both paths must be explicitly selected; there is no automatic career-folder discovery. The new output must be outside all source skills trees and enclosing plugin packages.

The JSON source map has format: 1, an authorized owner, and a nonempty files array. Each entry supplies an absolute source, a safe relative destination, and its exact sha256; optional required lists mandatory destinations. Pin only evidence authorized for this export. A stale hash, missing required source, path escape or existing output blocks it. The resulting career-evidence.zip is a private evidence snapshot with workflow copies for provenance; it is not an independently installable skill and requires the separately installed workflow and dependencies. The helper neither installs nor uploads it.

examples.title: Tailoring an application for a senior solutions consultant role
examples.markdown:
## Request

Tailor Jordan Reyes's application for the Northbeam Analytics Senior Solutions Consultant posting: resume bullets and a short cover letter. The candidate record and posting are in ./inputs/. Do not submit anything.

## Inputs

Run of the built `prepare-job-application` task package. All inputs below are invented. The run had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Files it also produced, not shown here: `Role_Work_Record.md`.

#### candidate-record.md

#### Candidate record (fictional person, supplied for this task)

Name: Jordan Reyes. Location: Columbus, OH (open to remote).
Target: Senior Solutions Consultant roles at B2B SaaS companies.

Experience (dates and figures confirmed by the candidate):
- Solutions Consultant, Ardent Logistics Software (2021–present). Ran 120+ technical discovery calls and demos per year for a TMS product. Built a demo environment reused by 14 account executives. Supported deals totaling $8.2M in closed-won ACV in 2024. Wrote the RFP response library (240 answers) that cut average RFP turnaround from 9 to 4 business days.
- Implementation Consultant, Ardent Logistics Software (2018–2021). Led 22 customer implementations; average go-live 11 weeks. Trained 300+ end users.
- Operations Analyst, Midstate Freight (2015–2018). Built Excel/SQL reporting for a 40-terminal network.

Skills: SQL, REST APIs, Postman, Salesforce (admin cert 2020), Looker basics, demo storytelling.
Education: B.S. Supply Chain Management, Ohio State University, 2015.
Not true / do not claim: Python, people management, Snowflake.


#### job-posting.md

#### Senior Solutions Consultant — Northbeam Analytics (fictional posting)

Northbeam builds a supply-chain visibility and analytics platform for mid-market shippers and 3PLs.

You will:
- Partner with account executives on discovery, tailored demos and proofs of concept for VP-level buyers in logistics.
- Own technical win for deals from $80K–$400K ARR.
- Respond to RFPs and security questionnaires.
- Feed product with field insights.

You have:
- 5+ years in pre-sales or implementation for B2B SaaS, ideally logistics or supply chain.
- Comfort with APIs, data models and SQL.
- Experience with Snowflake or another cloud data warehouse (nice to have).
- Excellent presentation skills.

## Output

### Jordan Reyes — Northbeam Analytics, Senior Solutions Consultant

Recommendation: pursue. Jordan meets the 5+ years requirement (pre-sales and implementation since 2018) and has logistics, demo and RFP evidence. Two things in the posting have no support in the record, so they stay off the materials (see Gaps).

**Audience and purpose:** Northbeam hiring manager and recruiter. The goal is a screen. Consequence is high, so the review is deep. Accuracy comes first, and every figure is the candidate's stated figure, unrounded.

#### Resume bullets (tailored copy)

**Headline:** Senior Solutions Consultant — logistics and supply chain SaaS (TMS, RFPs, technical discovery and demos)
**Expertise:** Technical discovery · Tailored demos · Proofs of concept · RFP responses · SQL · REST APIs · Postman · Data models · Salesforce · Looker

*Note:* "Proofs of concept" and "Data models" are the posting's own terms, kept in the expertise line for ATS matching. The record does not describe either as work Jordan has done, so Jordan should confirm both or cut them before this goes anywhere.

**Solutions Consultant, Ardent Logistics Software (2021–present)**
- Run 120+ technical discovery calls and demos a year for a TMS product, partnering with account executives; supported deals totaling $8.2M in closed-won ACV in 2024.
- Built a demo environment that 14 account executives reuse.
- Wrote the RFP response library, 240 answers, and cut average RFP turnaround from 9 to 4 business days.

**Implementation Consultant, Ardent Logistics Software (2018–2021)**
- Led 22 customer implementations at an average go-live of 11 weeks.
- Trained 300+ end users.

**Operations Analyst, Midstate Freight (2015–2018)**
- Built Excel/SQL reporting for a 40-terminal network.

**Skills:** SQL, REST APIs, Postman, Salesforce (admin certified 2020), Looker
**Education:** B.S. Supply Chain Management, Ohio State University, 2015

#### Cover letter (about 280 words, four paragraphs)

No salutation line: no hiring manager is named in the posting, and I did not look outside the inputs.

> Northbeam's supply-chain visibility platform for mid-market shippers and 3PLs sits close to the work I have done at Ardent Logistics Software since 2018. As a Solutions Consultant on a TMS product, I run 120+ technical discovery calls and demos a year, and in 2024 I supported deals totaling $8.2M in closed-won ACV. Working with logistics buyers on discovery and demos is what I already do every week.
>
> The posting asks for tailored demos with account executives and RFP responses. I built a demo environment that 14 account executives reuse. I also wrote our RFP response library, 240 answers, and average RFP turnaround fell from 9 to 4 business days. Before pre-sales, I was an Implementation Consultant who led 22 customer implementations, averaged an 11-week go-live and trained 300+ end users. That work shows me what the buyer lives with after the demo, and I scope with that in mind.
>
> On the data side, I started in operations at Midstate Freight, where I built Excel/SQL reporting for a 40-terminal network. Today I work in SQL, REST APIs, Postman and Looker, and I hold a Salesforce admin certification (2020). That is the base I would bring to the data model and API questions that come up in technical evaluations.
>
> I would like to talk first about how Northbeam qualifies deals in the $80K–$400K ARR range, and what the technical win plan and first proof of concept look like when an account executive and a solutions consultant pick up a new opportunity together.
>
> Jordan Reyes
> Columbus, OH (open to remote)

#### Gaps and assumptions

| Posting item | Handling |
| --- | --- |
| Snowflake or another cloud warehouse (nice to have) | No evidence. Left off both documents. Adjacent: SQL, Excel/SQL reporting, Looker. |
| Security questionnaires | No evidence. The RFP library is the closest match, and the letter claims only the RFP work. |
| Owning technical win on $80K–$400K ARR deals | The record shows $8.2M supported ACV but no per-deal size or technical-win ownership. The letter says "supported", as the record does. |
| VP-level buyers, presentation skills | Not in the record. No claim made. |
| Field insights to product | Not in the record. No claim made. |
| Python, people management | Not claimed. |
| Why this move | Jordan's own reason was not supplied and there was no one to ask. The letter ties interest to the work only. Add one sentence in Jordan's words if there is a reason. |

- The 8-year span (2018 to now) is the only calculation. It appears only as "since 2018". Basis is in the work record.
- Jordan's confirmed writing-style profile was not supplied. The drafts follow the skill's writing rules (no filler openers, a number or system in each sentence), and I checked them by reading. No writing scan ran.

#### Process notes
- I could not run scripts. The readiness checker (`check_role_resume_readiness.py`) and the content-review receipt were not produced. The drafts are Markdown, not DOCX, so there was no rendering or ATS layout check. I checked the figures against the candidate record by hand.
- I did not search for a named recipient and I did not fill or submit anything.

#### State
- **Changed now:** four draft files created in `./out/`.
- **Verified:** every figure, title and date matches `candidate-record.md`. No Python, Snowflake or people-management claim appears.
- **Still unchanged:** no master resume, tracker or live record was touched. State is `prepared locally` (drafts). Nothing is filled or submitted.
- **Exact next action:** Jordan confirms whether "Proofs of concept" and "Data models" are real experience (otherwise cut them from the expertise line) and supplies a reason for the move. Then the text goes into the master resume layout as a DOCX, the readiness check runs, and Jordan decides whether to apply.

#### Files
- `out/Jordan_Reyes_Northbeam_Senior_Solutions_Consultant_Resume_Bullets.md`
- `out/Jordan_Reyes_Northbeam_Senior_Solutions_Consultant_Cover_Letter.md`
- `out/Role_Work_Record.md` (draft record with translation table and estimate basis)
- `out/answer.md`

### File: Jordan_Reyes_Northbeam_Senior_Solutions_Consultant_Resume_Bullets.md

**Headline:** Senior Solutions Consultant — logistics and supply chain SaaS (TMS, RFPs, technical discovery and demos)

**Expertise line:** Technical discovery · Tailored demos · Proofs of concept · RFP responses · SQL · REST APIs · Postman · Data models · Salesforce · Looker

**Solutions Consultant, Ardent Logistics Software (2021–present)**
- Run 120+ technical discovery calls and demos a year for a TMS product, partnering with account executives; supported deals totaling $8.2M in closed-won ACV in 2024.
- Built a demo environment that 14 account executives reuse.
- Wrote the RFP response library, 240 answers, and cut average RFP turnaround from 9 to 4 business days.

**Implementation Consultant, Ardent Logistics Software (2018–2021)**
- Led 22 customer implementations at an average go-live of 11 weeks.
- Trained 300+ end users.

**Operations Analyst, Midstate Freight (2015–2018)**
- Built Excel/SQL reporting for a 40-terminal network.

**Skills:** SQL, REST APIs, Postman, Salesforce (admin certified 2020), Looker
**Education:** B.S. Supply Chain Management, Ohio State University, 2015

### File: Jordan_Reyes_Northbeam_Senior_Solutions_Consultant_Cover_Letter.md

Northbeam's supply-chain visibility platform for mid-market shippers and 3PLs sits close to the work I have done at Ardent Logistics Software since 2018. As a Solutions Consultant on a TMS product, I run 120+ technical discovery calls and demos a year, and in 2024 I supported deals totaling $8.2M in closed-won ACV. Working with logistics buyers on discovery and demos is what I already do every week.

The posting asks for tailored demos with account executives and RFP responses. I built a demo environment that 14 account executives reuse. I also wrote our RFP response library, 240 answers, and average RFP turnaround fell from 9 to 4 business days. Before pre-sales, I was an Implementation Consultant who led 22 customer implementations, averaged an 11-week go-live and trained 300+ end users. That work shows me what the buyer lives with after the demo, and I scope with that in mind.

On the data side, I started in operations at Midstate Freight, where I built Excel/SQL reporting for a 40-terminal network. Today I work in SQL, REST APIs, Postman and Looker, and I hold a Salesforce admin certification (2020). That is the base I would bring to the data model and API questions that come up in technical evaluations.

I would like to talk first about how Northbeam qualifies deals in the $80K–$400K ARR range, and what the technical win plan and first proof of concept look like when an account executive and a solutions consultant pick up a new opportunity together.

Jordan Reyes
Columbus, OH (open to remote)

Northbeam builds a supply-chain visibility and analytics platform for mid-market shippers and 3PLs.

You will:

  • Partner with account executives on discovery, tailored demos and proofs of concept for VP-level buyers in logistics.
  • Own technical win for deals from $80K–$400K ARR.
  • Respond to RFPs and security questionnaires.
  • Feed product with field insights.

You have:

  • Comfort with APIs, data models and SQL.
  • Experience with Snowflake or another cloud data warehouse (nice to have).

---
name: prepare-sales-pursuit
description: 'Plan a sales pursuit in two modes: maintain its canonical Pursuit Brief or prepare one upcoming call. Use for a pursuit overview, recommended call sequence, objective, attendee plan, agenda, tailored questions, talk track, negotiation preparation, or prospect, account, and competitor research before a sales conversation. Route post-call discovery and transcript ingestion to maintain-discovery-record, scope and pricing to scope-project, and signed work to delivery skills.'
---


# Prepare sales pursuit

## Caller context and source boundary

Use only the current task's supplied or explicitly authorized account, project sources and destinations. Resolve record names such as `client.profile` within that confirmed context; they are logical slots, not a default personal store. Connector availability alone does not authorize searching another account. Organization-specific pricing, capability catalogs, approval roles and policies must be supplied or confirmed; absent material context remains an explicit gap. Keep reusable package files immutable during a client task and save client records outside them. Never populate an example with private source material.


> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`readout-brief.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/readout-brief.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

One skill turns the firm's pursuit knowledge into an actionable plan. Mode A
maintains the canonical opportunity overview. Mode B prepares one upcoming call.
Every run leaves a durable Markdown record per `_shared/output-contract.md`.

Two rules carry both modes:

**Every claim traces to a source.** Sellers repeat what you write to a client. A confident sentence with no provenance is a live grenade. Footnote everything.

**Every inference is labeled as one.** Who probably signs, what a competitor probably cannot do, what a number probably means: worth having, dangerous to say out loud as facts. Each carries an ID, a confidence band, its basis, and an explicit verdict on whether it is safe to say to the client.

And one boundary: this skill never owns the post-call record. Transcript ingestion, closing answered questions, and the discovery ledger belong to **maintain-discovery-record**. Hand the transcript there; read its output here.

## Choosing the mode

- The user wants an overview of the pursuit, asks which calls to schedule, or new facts have arrived that should update the standing picture: **Mode A**.
- A specific call is on the calendar and someone needs to walk in ready: **Mode B**. Mode B reads the Pursuit Brief first and updates it after (via Mode A) when prep surfaced something new.
- Neither exists yet and a call is imminent: run Mode B for the call, then seed the Pursuit Brief from what the prep produced.

## Mode A: maintain the Pursuit Brief

Create it once the org and opportunity are understood. Maintain one concise
canonical document per pursuit and update that file in place.

### Required content

Every Pursuit Brief carries these sections, and `scripts/check_pursuit_brief.py` verifies them:

1. **Client and opportunity context**: who they are, what is in play, where the pursuit stands.
2. **Situation**: the overall picture in a few paragraphs.
3. **Desired business outcomes**: what the client is trying to change, in their terms.
4. **Confirmed facts**: each with a named source and date.
5. **Assumptions**: every entry is a bulleted line starting `Assumption:` (optionally with an ID, `Assumption A-03:`), with basis and confidence. Nothing unlabeled enters this section, and no assumption hides among the facts.
6. **Important unknowns**: what was searched for and not found.
7. **Stakeholders**: known people with roles, and the missing stakeholder ROLES the pursuit still needs. Never invent a name, a title-holder, availability, or a commitment. When the identity is unknown, recommend the role ("we need the person who owns quoting operations"), never a guessed person.
8. **Risks and warning signs**.
9. **Qualification status**: where the deal sits and what evidence supports that.
10. **Recommended calls**: the calls to schedule and their sequence. Each call is a `###` subheading carrying three labeled lines: `Purpose:`, `Desired outcome:`, and `Prerequisites:` (the evidence each call is expected to produce or require).
11. **Immediate next steps**: each with an owner and timing.
12. **Decisions needed**: what the team must decide and who decides it.
13. A **last-updated provenance line**: `Last updated: YYYY-MM-DD by <who or what run>, from <sources>`.

Record genuinely unknown content under Important unknowns. An unresolved
placeholder (`TBD`, `TKTK`, `{{ }}`) fails the brief.

### The brief is a living artifact

Repeated runs update it idempotently: re-running on the same facts changes nothing, and new facts update the sections they belong to rather than appending duplicates.

Human-authored material is protected with HTML comment markers:

```markdown
<!-- human -->
The CFO told me directly he will not fund this before Q3. Do not push timeline.
<!-- /human -->
```

Updates must NEVER rewrite, trim, or reflow anything between `<!-- human -->` and `<!-- /human -->`. Content moves around them, not through them. The checker enforces this: run `check_pursuit_brief.py --before old.md --after new.md` before replacing the file, and abort the update if it fails.

### Where it lives

The Pursuit Brief draws its durable client facts from `client.profile` and
`client.relationships`, then points to the active `opportunity.front_door`.
Update only the records this skill owns, idempotently, under the Hub contract.
The full brief remains a durable Markdown artifact per
`_shared/output-contract.md`, named `<client>-pursuit-brief.md`.

### Gate it

```bash
python3 scripts/check_pursuit_brief.py <client>-pursuit-brief.md
python3 scripts/check_pursuit_brief.py --before old.md --after new.md   # on updates
```

Exit 0 passes. Correct every reported brief defect.

## Mode B: the Upcoming Call Brief

Prepares ONE specific call. Start from the calendar event: when the call is, who is on the invite, who organized it. The attendee list is the stakeholder map and drives the audience partition below. If no event exists, ask who is in the room before researching.

### Required content

1. **Call objective**: the one or two things the call must produce.
2. **Desired decisions or outcomes**.
3. **Attendees and roles**, both sides.
4. **Known context**: what the record already establishes, sourced.
5. **Run of show**: a concise sequence of moves.
6. **Agenda with time allocation**.
7. **Questions**: tailored and ranked. When a discovery ledger exists (built by maintain-discovery-record), pull the ranked Column B questions from it rather than inventing a parallel list; add call-specific questions only where the ledger is silent, and say which are which.
8. **Risks and sensitivities**.
9. **Facts vs assumptions vs unknowns**, explicitly separated.
10. **Follow-up plan**.
11. **Relationship to the Pursuit Brief**: name the pursuit brief file, which of its recommended calls this one is, and what it should feed back.

Gate it with `python3 scripts/check_pursuit_brief.py --mode call <file>.md`.

### Evidence disciplines the call brief inherits

These four behaviors are load-bearing, not optional polish:

**Sections are earned by evidence, never required by a template.** A talk track requires a verbatim ask from a transcript. A Q&A bank requires questions the counterpart actually raised. A figure ledger requires reconciled figures. A section whose evidence is absent is omitted, and the gap is reported in chat. Four sections built entirely from the record beat ten where six were inferred.

**No figure without reconciliation.** Every number is written into an evidence ledger (`assets/evidence.schema.json`) and checked against every other source that mentions it:

```bash
python3 scripts/reconcile.py evidence.json
```

It fails on unsourced figures, unreconciled conflicts, and leaks of `never`-tagged material. Conflicts are surfaced, never silently resolved by picking the better-reading number: both values go in the brief with the disagreement named, and the presenter decides.

**No voice without a recording.** Spoken lines in a talk track are assembled from the presenter's own recorded phrasing: their analogies, their framings, their register, mined from transcripts where they speak. Absent such a transcript, produce intents only, say so in chat, and never simulate a voice from a job title.

**Every retrieved statement carries an audience tag.** `public` may appear anywhere; `internal` appears in the brief only, usually as a landmine or Q&A answer; `never` (a person assessing a named individual, for instance) is excluded from every artifact and may appear only as an explicit do-not-repeat instruction with no detail. The counterpart's statements about their own organization are `internal`: reflectable back to them, not portable to their colleagues.

**Gaps go in chat, never in the artifact.** After building, report: sections omitted and why, figures that could not be reconciled, stale evidence, and any decision the presenter must make before the call. The artifact stays clean; the user gets the honest picture.

## The research machinery, supporting both modes

Depth is set by the clock. Two hours means parallel research agents and the full pack. Twenty minutes means one research pass and a tight brief; say what you are cutting rather than half-building more.

**Harvest internal knowledge first.** Public research is commodity work any competitor can do. Search the authorized project sources and connected account relevant to this task, such as Slack, Drive, CRM and calendar. Do not broaden to other personal or employer accounts. A zero-result Salesforce search is itself a finding. Read transcripts verbatim, never summaries: a summary may omit the actor, mechanism or qualification that changes the decision. Preserve those details from the authorized source rather than inventing an example.

**Then public research, in parallel, with citation discipline.** Spawn two subagents in the same turn: Agent A on the business (how they make money, who pays them, financial condition, priorities), Agent B on the people and the field (attendees, absent deciders, competitors, platform landscape). Prompt templates are in `references/research-prompts.md`; the two demands worth preserving in any edit are the inline source URL next to every claim and the `[ASSUMPTION]` label with confidence on unverified reasoning. Write agent output to disk and read it there.

**Make the money flow a first-class object.** Who pays, through what instrument, how pricing moves over a deal's life, where revenue leaks. Then reconcile that against the client's operational pain; the collision between what their filings say and what their transcript says is where differentiated insight lives. The client's own filings usually describe the consequence of the operational problem they are about to describe to you.

**Find what nobody else has.** Vendor changes since the client last evaluated, whether a competitor's product literally applies, the org-chart diff since a past initiative died, numbers that moved since the client formed their opinion. Each must survive a hostile read as a plain fact with a source, or it goes to the assumptions register instead.

**Write the atomic knowledge base** when depth allows: topic-per-file Markdown, each independently footnoted, per `references/knowledge-base-spec.md`. Footnote types: `[^S1]` filings and company sources, `[^W1]` web, `[^I1]` internal, `[^A1]` assumptions. Flag conflicts rather than resolving them silently, and keep the assumptions register as its own file with a client-safety verdict column.

**Build the interactive HTML brief** when the call warrants it: `assets/brief-template.html` is the working shell (footnote popovers, assumption highlighting, money-flow explorer, drill mode); you fill in content, not mechanics, per `references/html-brief-spec.md`. Build and verify with:

```bash
python3 scripts/build_brief.py draft.html -o out.html --verify
```

It resolves the explicitly selected project brand profile (or neutral default), embeds declared assets, and verifies the result only in permitted browser infrastructure. Missing assets or unavailable rendering remain acceptance gaps. The file must stay fully self-contained, no CDN dependencies: these get opened on planes and in client parking lots. The HTML is secondary; the Markdown brief is the canonical record per `_shared/output-contract.md`.

## Landing the work

Deliver the artifact, register its location, update `client.profile` and
`client.relationships` with supported changes, and write session memory pointing
at the records rather than restating them.

Close with the top three facts, then the landmines. Then flag your biggest judgment call and argue the other side of it honestly. A brief presented as settled when it contains a real fork is the failure mode.

## Quality gates

- `scripts/check_pursuit_brief.py` for each Pursuit Brief and Call Brief, plus
  `--before/--after` when revising an existing Pursuit Brief.
- `scripts/reconcile.py` on the evidence ledger whenever a Mode B brief carries figures.
- **review-writing** owns writing review: run its bundled diagnostics on the prose. No em dashes, no buzzwords, no AI-construction patterns. Report the counts it prints.
- **brand-renderer** and `_shared/build-card.md` own any branded surface. Use `--profile` for an explicitly supplied profile; the renderer otherwise stays neutral and never discovers an employer brand from personal folders.

## Boundaries

- **maintain-discovery-record** owns post-call transcript ingestion, question closure,
  decision logging, and its two-column ledger. Mode B reads that record and
  carries supported post-call updates into the Pursuit Brief.
- NOT scope item creation, quote editing, or pricing. That is **scope-project** and the Pricing System.
- NOT post-sale delivery work, project status, or requirements sessions.
- Never invents stakeholder names, availability, commitments, or facts. Roles, not guessed people.

## What to skip when time is short

Cut in this order and say what you cut: drill-mode content, the full knowledge base (keep index, current-state, stakeholders, deal-strategy, assumptions), Agent A's deep financial history. Never cut: the internal harvest, the assumptions register, the landmines, citations, or the checkers.

## Files

- `scripts/check_pursuit_brief.py` · the gate for both brief modes and the human-marker idempotency check. Stdlib only; exits nonzero on failure.
- `scripts/check_pursuit_brief_selftest.py` · runs the gate against `scripts/fixtures/`.
- `scripts/reconcile.py` · the figure and evidence gate for Mode B ledgers.
- `scripts/reconcile_selftest.py` · its selftest.
- `scripts/build_brief.py` · inlines brand assets into the HTML brief and render-verifies it.
- `assets/evidence.schema.json` · the Mode B evidence ledger structure.
- `assets/brief-template.html` · the working interactive shell.
- `references/research-prompts.md` · prompt templates for the two research subagents.
- `references/knowledge-base-spec.md` · atomic file list, footnote conventions, assumptions register format.
- `references/html-brief-spec.md` · HTML section structure, content schemas, brand constraints.

## Release gate (required)

Before delivery, run the required gate. Complete it during production. Full spec in
[`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md).

1. Apply review-writing to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For
   a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.
2. Run brand-renderer on the branded artifact: palette, borders, radii, logo,
   footer.
3. Run review-deliverable before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until every check that applies has passed.
