---
name: release-skill-package
description: "Package, replace, and inspect a shared skill across Codex and Claude. Use when preparing a portable release, replacing an account skill, or checking that both hosts received the intended files."
---

# Release skill package

Release one shared skill from its maintained source and verify each requested destination. Carry its instructions, references, scripts, templates, assets, and runtime dependencies together.

Use this workflow for a release spanning local installations and account interfaces. For an estate-wide build or installation repair, use the repository's existing sync tools. Creating a new skill's behavior belongs in the skill creation workflow; changing global instructions or publishing a plugin requires its own scope.

## Identify the release

Resolve the skill name, source folder, intended change, and requested destinations from the task and current project guidance. Distinguish local Codex, local Claude Code, a Claude account, Cowork, and organization distribution. Record only the destinations the user requested. Reuse existing authorization; prepare the package before asking for any missing upload or publication approval.

Inspect the source revision and working tree, the installed paths, and any existing package. Preserve unrelated edits. Compare a downloaded or account-exported copy with the maintained source before choosing which bytes to release. A newer filename or host version does not establish source authority. For Skills Estate, read [the estate adapter](references/estate-release.md).

Before a replacement, retain the previous package or available host version and record how to recover it. Inventory the files and the capabilities they support. Explain intentional removals; resolve unexpected missing resources before proceeding.

## Build and inspect the package

Use the project's existing packager. Build from a stable source snapshot so concurrent edits cannot enter the archive unnoticed. If the build would update unrelated installed skills, stage an isolated build or use a supported targeted operation.

1. Validate the skill name, description, host metadata, and archive layout against the intended host's current requirements. Use its current interface or official documentation when a constraint is uncertain. Keep one discoverable top-level `SKILL.md`; retain supporting workflows under their intended paths.
2. Inspect the archive member list and extract it into an empty temporary directory. Check archive integrity, relative references, executable resources, and runtime dependencies. A reference to a Mac-only path needs an available host equivalent or an explicit fallback. Exclude private logs, credentials, caches, and unrelated source material.
3. Compare the extracted tree with the intended built package, including file bytes and relevant executable permissions. Record the archive's SHA-256, source revision or dirty-source snapshot, and file inventory. Do not infer equality from matching filenames or file counts.
4. Exercise a representative task using the extracted package. Check an adjacent request that should keep its existing workflow and a relevant failure case, such as a missing dependency. Inspect the actual output against the task's requirements. Report an unavailable runtime test separately from a passing file check.

Keep the source version, archive filename, archive hash, and host-assigned version in separate fields. An archive named `example-v003.zip` can become host version `v4`.

## Install or replace the requested copies

For a local installation, use the supported installer or managed link. Check an occupied destination before replacing it. Preserve divergent local edits and use a reviewed backup or adoption procedure when needed. Resolve the installed path afterward and compare its files with the package. Start a fresh host session if discovery is cached; invoke the skill there before reporting that host behavior passed.

For an account replacement, inspect the current signed-in account, skill identity, visibility, and version. Use the available connected tool or supported browser workflow. In Claude, the observed workflow was to open the existing skill, choose **Replace**, select the ZIP, and upload it. Treat those labels as navigation clues and inspect the current UI before acting. Creating a duplicate skill is not a substitute for an intended replacement.

Immediately before upload, confirm that the selected file has the reviewed hash and that the current request authorizes this account and visibility. Keep a private replacement private. A separate **Publish to org** action requires authorization for organization distribution. Do not change browser permissions or account settings merely to make automation available. If the interface cannot be controlled, provide the exact package and remaining action for the user.

After an ambiguous timeout or missing confirmation, reopen the skill and inspect its current version before retrying. If the outcome remains unknown, stop further uploads and report the unresolved state. Do not create successive versions through blind retries.

## Inspect the destination

Reopen the installed or uploaded skill and record the displayed identity, version, visibility, and update time when available. Open `SKILL.md` and the support files that the workflow actually needs: references, runtime workflows, scripts, templates, or wordlists. Compare their paths and visible content with the reviewed package. Use a downloaded copy for a full byte comparison when the host supports it. If only part of a file is visible, record the inspected portion and leave full parity unverified.

Run a small representative invocation in each requested host and inspect its output. Confirm that required resources can be read or executed there and that any documented fallback works. A file browser showing a Python script establishes its presence; successful execution needs a runtime result. Local Claude Code installation does not establish Claude account or Cowork discovery.

Record the result in the existing release record with the package hash, destination, observed version, inspected files, invocation result, and remaining action. An upload receipt records an upload; it does not establish behavior in another host. When the host cannot expose exact bytes, state the inspection limit once.

Report what changed, what was verified, which requested destinations remain pending or unchanged, and the exact next action. Use precise states such as packaged locally, installed locally, replaced in the private account, invocation verified, or published to the organization. Stop at the requested destinations.

examples.markdown:
## Request

Replace the invoice-triage skill in my private Claude account with the current build from our finance-skills repo, and install the same package for Claude Code and Codex on this laptop. Don't publish it to the org. The status listing and account notes are in inputs/.

## Inputs

**Dry run.** This skill normally works on live systems or its owner's own setup. Here the system state is invented in the inputs below, and nothing was changed anywhere. Run of the built `maintain-skills-estate` task package in its "release to another host or account" mode. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### account-notes.txt

Claude account (signed in as the requester), Settings > Skills
 invoice-triage  | visibility: Private | version v3 | updated 2026-10-20 | uploaded by requester
 "Publish to org" button present, not used.

Export downloaded from the account (invoice-triage-account-v3.zip) members:
 SKILL.md
 references/approval-limits.md
 references/vendor-terms.md
 references/tax-codes.md
 scripts/match_po.py
 templates/query-email.md
Account export SKILL.md line 41 also reads: For VAT treatment see references/tax-codes.md
Account export approval-limits.md says auto-approve limit 2,000 (source says 2,500).

Upload attempt, 2026-11-04 11:02 (browser session, Replace > select invoice-triage-v003.zip):
 11:02:12 file chosen, upload started
 11:02:41 spinner, no confirmation banner
 11:03:40 "Request timed out" toast
 Page not reopened afterwards. No second upload was attempted.

#### source-and-package-state.txt

== Source: ~/work/finance-skills/skills/invoice-triage ==
branch main, HEAD 4e1a9c7 "Add export_ledger.py, merge tax codes into approval-limits"

 M skills/invoice-triage/scripts/match_po.py     (modified 2026-11-03 16:40, uncommitted)
git log -3 --oneline -- skills/invoice-triage:
 4e1a9c7 Add export_ledger.py, merge tax codes into approval-limits
 b81d3f2 Raise auto-approve limit wording to 2,500
 0c5e6aa Initial invoice-triage

Source files:
 SKILL.md
 references/approval-limits.md   (now contains the tax-code table, section "Tax codes")
 references/vendor-terms.md
 scripts/match_po.py
 scripts/export_ledger.py
 templates/query-email.md

grep -n "tax-codes" SKILL.md references/*:
 SKILL.md:41: For VAT treatment see references/tax-codes.md
 (no other hits; references/tax-codes.md does not exist in source)

grep -n "/Users/" scripts/*:
 scripts/export_ledger.py:12: OUT = "/Users/priya/Documents/ledger-exports/"

== Built package ==
dist/release.json entry:
 skill: invoice-triage, archive: invoice-triage-v003.zip
 sha256: 91c4d07e...a3  (recorded 2026-11-03 09:12)
 source_revision: 4e1a9c7 (clean at build time)

sha256 of dist/invoice-triage-v003.zip on disk now: 91c4d07e...a3  (matches release.json)
Zip modified 2026-11-03 09:12; match_po.py in zip is the 09:12 version.
Zip members (unzip -l): SKILL.md, references/approval-limits.md, references/vendor-terms.md,
 scripts/match_po.py, scripts/export_ledger.py, templates/query-email.md

== Local installs ==
~/.claude/skills/invoice-triage  -> real directory (not a link), edited 2026-10-12, 5 files
   files: SKILL.md, references/approval-limits.md, references/vendor-terms.md, scripts/match_po.py, templates/query-email.md
   diff vs v003 zip: SKILL.md differs, match_po.py differs, export_ledger.py missing
~/.agents/skills/invoice-triage  -> not present
~/.codex/skills/invoice-triage   -> not present

## Output

I have not replaced or installed anything yet, and I recommend against shipping the v003 package as it stands. It has two defects that would reach every destination, and your 11:02 upload may have already put it in the account. I've written the plan and record to `out/release-record.md`.

#### 1. Check the account before anything else

The Replace upload at 11:02 ended in a "Request timed out" toast with no confirmation, and the page wasn't reopened. Open Settings > Skills > invoice-triage and read the version, update time and file list.

- If it still shows v3 (updated 2026-10-20), the upload didn't land.
- If it shows a newer version or a 2026-11-04 update time, v003 landed. It has the defects below, so it needs a corrected replacement, but only after you've seen its state.

Don't retry blindly. Repeated uploads create successive versions you can't tell apart. If the page is unclear, stop and report that.

#### 2. Problems in the v003 package

| # | Finding | Evidence | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Dead reference. `SKILL.md:41` says "see references/tax-codes.md", which isn't in the package. | Commit 4e1a9c7 merged tax codes into `references/approval-limits.md`. The account's v3 still has `tax-codes.md`, so v3 works and v003 doesn't. | Point line 41 at the "Tax codes" section of `approval-limits.md`. The file removal is intentional. |
| 2 | Mac-only path. `scripts/export_ledger.py:12` writes to `/Users/priya/Documents/ledger-exports/`. | Fails in an account runtime and on any other machine. | Take the output folder from an argument or environment variable, default to a folder in the working directory, and create it if missing. |
| 3 | Uncommitted edit to `scripts/match_po.py`, made 2026-11-03 16:40. | v003 was built at 09:12 from clean 4e1a9c7, so it doesn't include the edit. | You decide. If the edit is meant to ship, commit it. If it isn't, stash it. Either way the archive must match a known revision. |

Two other differences are intended, but you should know them:

- The account's v3 says the auto-approve limit is 2,000. The source says 2,500 (commit b81d3f2). Replacing v3 changes what invoices the skill will auto-approve.
- `export_ledger.py` is new. It's in neither the account copy nor the local Claude Code copy.

The account export and the local copy are older than the source here, and source history explains each difference. I'm treating the repository as the authority, not the newer upload date.

#### 3. Local destinations

- **Claude Code:** `~/.claude/skills/invoice-triage` is a plain directory, edited 2026-10-12, with 5 files. Its `SKILL.md` and `match_po.py` differ from v003. Diff both against the repository history first. If it holds work that isn't in git, copy it into the repo. Then back it up and replace it using the estate's `adopt` for this one skill. That keeps a restore receipt.
- **Codex:** `~/.agents/skills/invoice-triage` and `~/.codex/skills/invoice-triage` are both missing, so a normal install works. Use `install --skill invoice-triage --expected-source <reviewed hash>`, which leaves other installed skills alone.
- Open a fresh session in each host before testing. Cached discovery can hide the new version.

#### 4. Order of work

1. Reopen the account page (section 1).
2. Fix findings 1 and 2, settle finding 3, and commit.
3. Run `validate`, the tests, `build` and `bundle`. I can't run these from here. Run `tools/estate.py` yourself or have me run it in the checkout.
4. Compare the new zip's SHA-256 with `dist/release.json`, extract it to an empty folder, and diff it against `build/skills/invoice-triage` including file modes.
5. Using the extracted package, run one sample invoice, one adjacent request that should be unaffected, and one run with the ledger output folder missing.
6. Install locally for Claude Code and Codex, then invoke the skill in a fresh session of each.
7. In the account, choose **Replace** on the existing skill, not a new upload. Confirm the selected file has the reviewed hash and visibility stays Private. Don't touch **Publish to org**.
8. Reopen the account skill, record version, update time and file list, open `SKILL.md`, `approval-limits.md` and `export_ledger.py`, and run an invocation.
9. Only then run `record-publication --surface claude-account --skill invoice-triage --reference '...'`. That entry records the upload, not that it worked. Keep the invocation output separately.

Keep the archive filename, source version and the version the account assigns as separate fields. A file called `-v004.zip` can become account v5.

#### Questions for you

- Should the `match_po.py` edit ship?
- Is 2,500 the intended auto-approve limit going to the account?

#### Current state

| Destination | State |
| --- | --- |
| Source | Needs two fixes, one decision |
| Package | v003 built and hash-matched, not fit to release; new build pending |
| Private account | Unknown after a timed-out upload |
| Claude Code | Unchanged, divergent older copy |
| Codex | Not installed |
| Organization | Not requested, untouched |

Files: `out/release-record.md` (the table, three blockers and nine-step sequence above), `out/answer.md`.

### File: release-record.md

#### Release record: invoice-triage

Requested destinations: private Claude account (replace), Claude Code (local), Codex (local). Not requested: organization distribution.

| Field | Value |

skills.markdown:
---
name: render-offering-brief
description: 'Render a defined offering into a two-page internal sales brief and one-page external PDF. Use for playbook handouts, sales enablement sheets, or a catalog of offering PDFs. Accepts structured Markdown or rich JSON with qualification criteria, talking tracks, delivery steps, and scope boundaries. Applies the project brand profile or neutral estate profile, checks actual PDF page counts and browser layout, and retains outputs for review.'
---

# Render offering brief

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`readout-brief.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/readout-brief.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

Turns one playbook into two branded PDFs, using the same visual system every time:

- **Internal brief** (`*-internal-brief.pdf`): sales enablement, two pages. The seven Clarity questions as numbered sections (01-07), with optional qualifier/disqualifier boxes, a talking-tracks table, numbered delivery steps, and Positioning / Two-gears callouts. Footer, "INTERNAL USE ONLY".
- **External one-pager** (`*-external-onepager.pdf`): client-facing, one page. Headline, subtitle, intro, a "What you get" grid, a two-column "who it's for / why it matters" band, a "How it works" callout, and a footer with the cost/CTA line.

This is the rendering mode of **manage-service-offering**. Its primary workflow,
[manage-service-offering](../manage-service-offering/SKILL.md), defines the offering and its
house-format entry. The separate [plan-offering-artifacts](../plan-offering-artifacts/SKILL.md)
mode plans the artifact package and its dependencies. This workflow renders
the agreed entry to PDF; it does not define the offering or mark the suite complete.

## Shared brand and runtime

Select a confirmed profile with `--profile /path/to/brand.md`; otherwise the renderer uses the current project's `brand.md` or the packaged neutral estate profile. Colors, font stack, minimum body type size, radius, and optional logo come from that profile. A missing declared font or logo fails the build. The neutral profile needs no logo or custom font. Keep client assets in their project.

The layout files contain component rules, not a separate brand authority. Use the author's confirmed voice profile for wording; the renderer does not impose a company voice or invent contact details.

The renderer uses Python `Jinja2` and `pypdf`, plus Node.js, Playwright and Chromium. Install the pinned requirements into a project virtual environment and the Node dependencies locally:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
npm install --ignore-scripts
npx playwright install chromium
PYTHON=.venv/bin/python bash scripts/setup.sh
```

Set `ESTATE_NODE` when Node is not on PATH, `ESTATE_NODE_MODULES` when Playwright lives outside the current project's `node_modules`, and `PW_CHROMIUM` to use an existing Chromium executable. The renderer launches an isolated browser and blocks remote resources. It does not use personal browser sessions.

## Two input modes

**Plain, from the house format.** Point the renderer at a manage-service-offering entry or a whole corpus. It maps the seven internal answers and six external answers straight into the templates. The rich components stay off, so you get a clean 7-part brief and a standard one-pager. Best for rendering a catalog quickly and consistently.

```bash
# one entry by its number
python scripts/render_playbook.py --md CATALOG.md --entry 01 --out ./pdfs
# the whole catalog
python scripts/render_playbook.py --md CATALOG.md --all --out ./pdfs
```

**Rich, from a JSON spec.** Supply a spec to light up the extra components: qualifier/disqualifier boxes, talking-tracks table, a delivery bar, numbered steps, Positioning/Two-gears callouts, an external kicker, subtitle, and a labelled two-column band with a centered note. Use this for a flagship offering you want to look like the hand-built exemplar.

```bash
python scripts/render_playbook.py --json spec.json --out ./pdfs --prefix "01-"
```

The JSON schema and the full field-to-slot mapping are in `references/field-mapping.md`. Read it before hand-authoring a spec.

## How to choose

- Rendering a catalog, or a play that only has the standard seven/six answers: use `--md`. Fast, consistent, nothing to author.
- A front-door or flagship offering that deserves the qualifier boxes, talking tracks, and step-by-step delivery: author a JSON spec (start from `references/field-mapping.md`), render with `--json`, and it will match the exemplar layout.
- You can mix: render the whole catalog with `--all`, then render flagship plays with `--json` into a separate attempt directory. Existing output files are never overwritten.

## Discipline

- **Render only what the source says.** The PDFs restate the playbook's facts; they add none. Do not invent a headline claim, a metric, a price, or a duration to fill a slot. If a required slot has no grounded content, obtain it before rendering. Omit optional slots when their source is absent.
- **Free vs paid footer.** The renderer sets the external footer from the tier in the heading: `(free)` gets "What it costs: nothing. It is how we start."; anything else gets a neutral "Ready when you are." Do not label a paid play as free.
- **Same visual every time.** Don't hand-tune spacing or colors per play. If content overflows, revise the wording without dropping scope, claims, or qualifiers, then render another attempt. Keep the failed output.

## Workflow

1. Read the offering source and confirm the requested audience. Use the primary `manage-service-offering` workflow for offering definition; this mode renders the agreed definition.
2. Run the dependency preflight and select the brand profile.
3. Use `--md` for standard entries or `--json` for the richer components. Read [field-mapping.md](references/field-mapping.md) before authoring JSON.
4. Render into a new, empty attempt directory. Strict parsing rejects unknown labels and required-content gaps. Source HTML permits only inline emphasis; scripts, images, arbitrary attributes, and resource loads are rejected.
5. Inspect the saved HTML, PDF, page images, and checks. The browser checks page bounds and footer overlap; `pypdf` checks the actual PDF page count. Render the PDF pages to images and inspect every page before delivery.
6. Compare the PDF text with the source: scope, exclusions, audience, delivery steps, quantities, and contact details. Parser tests alone do not establish an acceptable deliverable.
7. Deliver the two requested PDFs, or the requested single variant. Retain the source, all attempts, checks, and manifest. A failed render can leave a PDF for diagnosis; its presence is not a passing result.

## Output and failure handling

A successful run writes a source/profile/asset manifest with artifact hashes and page counts. The internal brief has two pages; the external handout has one. Missing content, assets, dependencies, overflow, footer collisions, and unexpected PDF page counts fail the run. Repair the cause and use a new output directory.

`--no-strict` permits parser warnings for an explicitly requested diagnostic draft; it does not bypass required JSON fields or PDF layout checks. Never deliver a draft whose source fields were ignored.

## Files

- `templates/internal_brief.html`, `templates/external_onepager.html`: the two layouts, including optional rich components.
- `assets/brand.css`: layout rules using the shared profile's CSS variables.
- `scripts/render_playbook.py`: Markdown parsing, JSON rendering and manifest generation.
- `scripts/pdf_runtime.py`, `scripts/render_pdf.mjs`: input validation, actual PDF generation and layout checks.
- `scripts/setup.sh`: read-only dependency and profile preflight.
- `fixtures/synthetic-offering.json`: a fictional offering covering the rich components.
- `references/field-mapping.md`: field schema and Markdown-to-slot mapping.

examples.markdown:
## Request

I need an internal sales brief and a client handout for our new Renewal Risk Review offering, built from the notes in the inputs folder. Sales will use the internal one at pitch prep and we'll send the handout to prospects.

## Inputs

Run of the built `manage-service-offering` task package in its "internal brief or external handout" mode. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Other files it produced, not shown here: `spec.json`.

#### offering-notes.md

#### Renewal Risk Review: working notes (Larkfield Partners, subscription practice)

Paid, fixed-scope, one-off engagement. Sits after our free "Revenue Health Call" (play 01) and before the "Renewal Operations Build" (play 04, multi-month, quoted separately).

**Who**
- Heads of Customer Success or Revenue Operations at B2B subscription software companies, roughly 50 to 300 staff, who own the renewal number.
- They already export renewal data from a CRM and a billing system.
- Not a fit: companies with under 100 paying customers (not enough to see a pattern), or anyone wanting us to run renewals for them.
- A CS manager can sponsor, but the head of CS/RevOps must attend the readout.

**What**
- We review the last 12 months of renewals and churn for one customer segment and show which accounts in the current renewal book look at risk and why.
- It is not a forecasting model, a CRM audit or a customer survey.

**Client value**
- They walk out knowing which upcoming renewals to work first and which warning signs have actually preceded churn in their own data.

**Our reason**
- Converts to Renewal Operations Build. Also gives us a view of their data quality before we quote the build. Fee band: not set yet, finance to decide.

**Included**
- Intake call to agree the segment
- Analysis of one 12-month renewal and churn export plus usage or support data if they have it
- Risk-signal list ranked by how often each signal preceded churn
- Account watchlist for the current quarter's renewals
- 60-minute readout with the head of CS/RevOps

**Not included**
- Data cleanup or pipeline fixes (that is play 04)
- Building a scoring model inside their CRM (play 04)
- More than one segment (a second segment is a separate review)
- Outreach to customers or running save plays

**Delivery**
- Client sends exports within 5 working days of the intake call.
- One analyst, one reviewer. Analysis takes about 10 working days after data arrives (Dana Okafor, delivery lead, to confirm).
- Readout is remote. Deliverables as a PDF report and a spreadsheet.

#### sales-call-feedback.txt

Feedback from Priya Raman (sales), after two pilot conversations:

- Prospects ask "is this just a dashboard?" Say clearly that it is a one-off review of their own history, with a named list of accounts, not software.
- Both prospects wanted to know what they need to send us. Put the data list up front.
- One prospect asked if we would call their customers. We won't.
- Contact for the handout: reviews@example.com
- Do not promise a churn reduction number. We have no results data yet.

## Output

I wrote the content for both documents, but I did not produce the two PDFs. I can't run the renderer here, so the content is ready to render but the PDFs aren't built and nobody has checked page counts or layout.

The internal brief is a rich spec for the two-page layout. The client handout is the one-page layout. Both are in one file, `out/spec.json`. Rendering is one command, run from the one-pager module directory:

`python scripts/render_playbook.py --json out/spec.json --out ./pdfs --prefix "02-"`

After rendering, check that the internal brief is exactly 2 pages and the handout exactly 1. If either overflows, shorten the wording, keeping every boundary and qualifier, and render into a new folder.

#### Decisions for you to lock

1. **Fee band.** Your notes say finance hasn't set it. No price appears in either document. The handout footer reads "Ready when you are." and doesn't say the offering is free.
2. **Delivery duration.** The notes say about 10 working days of analysis after the data arrives, with Dana Okafor to confirm. The internal brief shows it marked as pending. I left it off the handout so you don't publish a time the delivery lead hasn't confirmed. The handout only states the 5-working-day data window.
3. **Play number.** Your notes name plays 01 and 04 but not this one. I used 02 as a placeholder, and the number in `--prefix` is the same placeholder. Confirm it against any other numbering, such as CRM or catalog IDs.
4. **Segment size.** The notes give "roughly 50 to 300 staff" and "under 100 paying customers" as the disqualifier. The handout uses only the 100-customer line. Say if you want the staff range there too.
5. **Churn claim.** Priya's feedback says there is no results data, so neither document states a churn reduction figure.
6. **Logo and brand.** No brand profile was supplied, so the renderer would use the neutral house profile. Point `--profile` at your brand file if you have one.

#### Internal brief (2 pages, sales prep)

- **Descriptor:** a paid, one-off review of 12 months of renewal and churn history. It ends in a ranked watchlist of at-risk renewals and a readout with the head of CS or RevOps. It leads to the Renewal Operations Build (play 04).
- **01 What it is:** a fixed-scope review of one customer segment. It is not software, a forecasting model, a CRM audit or a customer survey.
- **02 Who it's for:** heads of Customer Success or Revenue Operations at B2B subscription software companies of roughly 50 to 300 staff. A CS manager can sponsor, but the head must attend the readout.
  - **Qualifiers:** owns the renewal number, 100 or more paying customers, exports from a CRM and a billing system.
  - **Disqualifiers:** fewer than 100 paying customers, wants us to run renewals, head won't attend the readout.
- **03 Why they care:** they know which renewals to work first and which signals preceded churn in their own data.
- **Talking tracks:** Customer Success head, RevOps head, "is this just a dashboard?" (no, it's a one-off review with a named list of accounts), "will you call our customers?" (no).
- **04 Why we care:** it converts to play 04. It also shows us the state of the client's data before we quote the build.
- **05 Included:** intake call, one 12-month export analysis, ranked signal list, quarter watchlist, 60-minute readout, PDF report and spreadsheet.
- **06 Not included:**
  - Data cleanup or pipeline fixes: play 04.
  - Scoring inside their CRM: play 04.
  - A second segment: a separate review.
  - Customer outreach or save plays: not offered.
- **07 Delivery:** four steps. One analyst and one reviewer. Exports due within 5 working days of the intake call. The analysis time is marked as pending confirmation.
- **Callouts:** Positioning, and Open decisions.

#### Client handout (1 page, for prospects)

- **Headline:** Know which renewals to work first.
- **Subtitle:** See which accounts in your current renewal book look at risk, and which warning signs preceded churn in your own data.
- **Intro:** we review the last 12 months of renewals and churn for one customer segment. You receive a named list of accounts and a ranked list of signals from your own history. This is a one-off review, not software.
- **What you get:**
  - Risk-signal list, ranked by how often each signal preceded churn.
  - Account watchlist for this quarter.
  - 60-minute readout.
  - PDF report and spreadsheet.
- **Two columns:**
  - Who it's for.
  - What we need from you: a 12-month export from your CRM and billing system, plus usage or support data if you have it, sent within 5 working days of the intake call. This puts the data list up front, as the pilot calls asked.
- **Centre note:** one segment per review. A second segment is a separate review.
- **How it works:** intake call, analysis, a second-person check, and a 60-minute remote readout. We don't contact your customers, clean your data or build scoring in your CRM. Those are covered by the Renewal Operations Build.
- **Footer:** "Ready when you are." Contact reviews@example.com to begin.

The handout leaves out the internal "why we care" reasoning, the pipeline motive, the play 04 handoff logic and the disqualifier list.

#### Checks done by hand

- **Grounding:** every fact comes from the two input files. I added no price, duration, result or customer count beyond the notes.
- **Voice:** I read both documents for the house rules and found no em dashes and none of the listed sentence shapes. I did not run the prose checker, so this was a reading pass only.
- **Footer:** the offering is paid, so the footer is the neutral one, per the footer rule.
- **Not done:** no PDF render, no page-count check, no brand check, no manifest. I could not run these.

#### Files

- `out/spec.json`: the render source for both PDFs.
- `out/entry.md`: a condensed house-format record of the offering, with the five fact blocks, Tldr, Eli5 and both one-pager sections. Its internal one-pager points to `spec.json` for the longer prose. Fill those four sections from the spec if you want the catalog entry to stand alone.

skills.title: SOW quality
skills.description: Quality gate for client-facing Statements of Work and other contract-class deliverables (MSAs, Change Orders, proposals with contractual scope). Use to review, audit, de-slop, tighten, or finalize a SOW or contract, as the final authoring pass after a SOW is generated and before scope review, or to apply the Basis of Estimate framework to a new tier. It audits structure and language: structural de-slop, Basis of Estimate (source-backed quantity meanings and change triggers), and cross-reference discipline. It does not compute pricing (the Pricing System does) or author or render the SOW itself (that is sow).

guide.what: Review a statement of work and its obligations.
guide.when: A SOW or contractual scope needs a quality review.
guide.inputs: The draft agreement, confirmed scope, estimate, and controlling terms.
guide.outputs: Findings or revisions addressing ambiguity, duplication, and scope consistency.
guide.example: Review this SOW for ambiguous obligations and inconsistencies with the agreed scope.
guide.expect: It reads the whole SOW with its quote and template, runs a scan for repeated mechanics, then fixes structure and cross-references and re-scans. It flags numbers that do not trace to the pricing source instead of changing them, and the edited document stays unapproved.
guide.requires: The SOW as a .docx or text with its controlling quote, and Python 3 for the scan script.
guide.overview: It reads the whole SOW with its quote and template, runs a scan for repeated mechanics, then fixes structure and cross-references and re-scans. It flags numbers that do not trace to the pricing source instead of changing them, and the edited document stays unapproved.
guide.value: Find ambiguous obligations, repeated mechanics and inconsistencies between a SOW and the quote it should represent. It checks document structure and cross-references while retaining the agreed commercial basis.

preparation.where: Supply the complete SOW, its controlling quote and the approved template or terms. A Word file or full text works. The template is the agreement owner's baseline language, not a contract policy generated by this skill.
preparation.missing: Without the quote, numerical consistency cannot be verified. Unsupported figures are flagged rather than changed to fit. The review can repair the document but does not approve or sign the resulting agreement.

reuse.label: General use
reuse.reason: The method accepts the user’s project sources and takes private context as an explicit input.
reuse.basis: Source classification and automated reference scan; cross-environment execution has not been tested.

profile.setup: The SOW as a .docx or text with its controlling quote, and Python 3 for the scan script.
profile.expect: It reads the whole SOW with its quote and template, runs a scan for repeated mechanics, then fixes structure and cross-references and re-scans. It flags numbers that do not trace to the pricing source instead of changing them, and the edited document stays unapproved.

# Review contract scope

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`sow-proposal.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/sow-proposal.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

## Source authority and synthetic examples

Read the selected contract, confirmed quote and project review policy before editing.
Preserve roles, quantities, obligations, approval requirements and mandated wording.
The bundled examples are newly constructed editorial illustrations, not contract
terms. Use the actual agreement's structure, billing treatment, triggers and section
numbers. A fixed-scope cap must not become a nonbinding estimate; a fixed-fee
agreement must not acquire T&M billing. Raise contradictions as findings.

## Preserve the complete review contract

Read the complete document with its controlling quote, approved template and scope
baseline. Preserve parties, amounts, dates, approval state, obligations and required
disclosures. Distinguish an editorial correction from a commercial or legal decision.
Check that each deliverable has observable acceptance, each responsibility has an
owner, and each dependency is distinguished from a promise. Verify milestone totals,
dates, defined terms, attachments, exclusions and clause references against their
sources. Return edits and material unresolved decisions with exact document locations.
Remove duplication only when obligations and clause interactions remain intact. An
edited document stays unapproved until its authorized owner approves it.

## What this skill is for

This is the authoring-quality pass that runs on a client-facing SOW after pricing is set and before it goes to scope review. It does not write scope, compute hours, or set price. It makes a finished SOW read like a senior consultant wrote it: every mechanic stated once, in one place, with no AI tells and no internal reasoning leaking onto the page.

Three responsibilities, in priority order:

1. **Structural de-slop.** The worst AI tells in a contract are not word-level (those are checked by the internal diagnostics used by Writing Integrity). They are structural: the same clause restated three to five times, and rules followed by a sentence explaining why the rule exists. Fix these first. See `references/structural-deslop.md`.
2. **Basis of Estimate framework.** Review quantities (counts, code volume, catalog scale) against their agreed status as estimates, commitments or caps. Preserve the actual baseline and any distinction between volumetric (soft) and binary workstream (hard) triggers; do not invent either. See `references/basis-of-estimate.md`.
3. **Cross-reference discipline.** Each mechanic gets one authoritative home; every other mention points to it. See `references/section-ownership.md`.

## Boundaries (what this skill does NOT do)

- It does not compute or change pricing, hours, or staffing. Those values come from the confirmed quote or supplied commercial source; `scope-project` prepares authorized revisions. If a number looks wrong, flag it for the user; do not invent or adjust it.
- It does not generate the playbook artifact set (Overview, DDOC, Pricing Sheet, Proposal). That is the playbook system.
- Follow the selected project’s documented review and signoff process. Do not invent reviewers or treat an editing pass as contract approval. Keep assumptions specific to the actual engagement and its estimating basis.
- It does not reconcile to the pricing sheet by itself. Numbers in the SOW must trace to the authoritative pricing sheet; if they do not, that is a finding to surface, not a thing to fix silently.

## The workflow

Run these in order. Do not claim a section is clean without running the verification script against it.

### Step 1: Read the whole SOW first
Extract the complete document, including tables, and read it end to end before editing anything. The structural tells are only visible across sections. A single section can look fine while the document repeats one mechanic five times.

```bash
python3 scripts/slop_scan.py SOW.docx --text
```

### Step 2: Run the slop scan
The script reports repeated mechanics, justification-tail candidates, rule-of-three piles, em-dash and section-sign counts, and meta-commentary patterns. It finds candidates; you judge them. The bundled extractor uses Python’s standard library to read DOCX paragraphs, tables, headers, footers and notes; no external `extract-text` command is required. Read the rendered document separately for text in drawings or embedded objects and for layout. Corrupt or unsupported files fail explicitly.

```bash
python scripts/slop_scan.py SOW.docx
```

### Step 3: Apply the structural fixes
For each repeated mechanic, decide its one authoritative home (see `references/section-ownership.md` for mapping the actual agreement), state it fully there, and reduce every other instance to a one-sentence cross-reference or cut it. For each justification tail, cut the why unless it defends an exception or a stricter-than-default term (the exception rule is in `references/structural-deslop.md`).

If you are editing the generator (a `gen_*.js` docx-js script), edit the source and regenerate. If you are editing a delivered `.docx` with no generator, use tracked changes per the `docx` skill so the user sees every change.

### Step 4: Apply the word-level prose pass
Use `review-writing` to review meaning, voice and sentence construction during drafting. Its internal diagnostic tools check detectable wording patterns. Keep the SOW-specific structural review here; preserve the figure comparisons and required review receipt.

### Step 5: Verify before asserting
Re-run the scan. Confirm that authorized repetition repairs hold and every dollar/hour figure still traces to the commercial source. Review each remaining flag. Preserve exact quoted or mandated wording even when it contains flagged punctuation; record its source and required review disposition instead of editing an obligation to obtain a scanner pass. Report the actual counts and the remaining human review findings. A passing scan is a bounded diagnostic result; it does not prove semantic correctness or contract approval.

```bash
python scripts/slop_scan.py SOW.docx --verify
```

## Authored wording and preservation rules

- In authored cross-references, write "Section 4" in full. Preserve the source spelling in exact quotations or mandated language.
- Preserve the role names and responsibilities in the selected contract. Use Client Services Executive (CSE) only when that is the confirmed project role; never substitute it for an agreed Client Lead, Account Executive or other role.
- Apply the selected writing policy to authored headings and body. Retain exact quotations and mandated contract language; a diagnostic flag is not permission to change them.
- Never fill a gap with a plausible-sounding projection. If a number or fact is missing, flag it.
- If review reveals scope that the staffing cannot cover, surface the mismatch without adjusting price or scope.
- Bold defined-term lead-ins are contract register, not an AI tell. Keep them.

## Quick reference: the three structural tells

| Tell | What it looks like | Fix |
|------|--------------------|-----|
| Repetition-as-thoroughness | Same clause/mechanic stated 3 to 5 times across sections | One authoritative home, others cross-reference it |
| Clause-justification | A rule followed by a sentence explaining why the rule exists | Cut the why, UNLESS it defends an exception or stricter term |
| Rule-of-three + meta-commentary | Verb piles ("does not remediate, re-architect, or add"); sentences answering internal questions the client never asked | Collapse the pile; delete the meta-commentary |

See `references/examples.md` for newly constructed synthetic before/after pairs.

examples.title: Reviewing a draft helpdesk migration SOW against its quote
examples.markdown:
## Request

Can you review the attached draft SOW for our helpdesk migration against the quote summary before it goes to the client's procurement team? I want to know what's inconsistent, what's duplicated, and what needs a decision from someone else, without you changing any pricing.

## Inputs

Run of the built `write-statement-of-work` task package in its "contract scope and obligation review" mode. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### quote-summary.txt

QUOTE Q-2291 rev 3 (confirmed by pricing owner)
Pricing model: fixed fee. Total $91,400. 480 hours. 12 weeks from 2027-01-18.

Resources:
- Engagement Manager: 60 h x $200 = $12,000
- Solution Architect: 140 h x $220 = $30,800
- Senior Consultant: 220 h x $180 = $39,600
- Data Analyst: 60 h x $150 = $9,000

Scope items:
1. Case history migration. Volume estimate 38,000 cases (estimate from client export of 2026-10-12, not a cap).
2. Email templates: up to 40.
3. Automation rules: up to 12.
4. Cutover support and go-live readout.

Milestones: kickoff 25%, data load complete 45%, go-live 30%.
Exclusions: third-party integrations (including billing); custom reporting.
Acceptance: 10 business days per deliverable; final acceptance on go-live readout.
Client roles: Executive Sponsor, Data Owner (named by client), Engagement Manager approves deliverables for client.
Client dependency: admin access to the existing platform by 2027-01-18.

#### sow-draft.md

#### Statement of Work: Helpdesk Migration (DRAFT v2)
Provider: Tallow & Reed Consulting. Client: Harbourline Logistics. Quote ref: Q-2291 rev 3.

##### 1. Overview
Tallow & Reed will migrate Harbourline's support operation to the new helpdesk platform. Changes to scope follow the Change Order process in Section 7.

##### 2. Scope
The provider will migrate the full configuration of the existing platform, with functional parity on launch. The engagement runs 10 weeks from 18 January 2027.

##### 3. Deliverables and limits
3.1 Migration of case history (about 38,000 cases, a hard cap; any additional cases require a Change Order under Section 7).
3.2 Migration of up to 40 email templates and up to 12 automation rules.
3.3 Billing system sync for invoice-related cases.
3.4 Exclusions: integrations with third-party systems, including billing, are out of scope. Any change to scope requires a Change Order.

##### 4. Responsibilities
The provider will ensure Harbourline's administrator access is in place by 18 January 2027. The Client Lead approves each deliverable. Harbourline will supply a named data owner, so that data questions have a single point of contact.

##### 5. Fees
Fixed fee of $91,400. Overage is billed at the rates in the quote on a time-and-materials basis. Milestones: kickoff 25% ($22,850); data load complete 45% ($41,130); go-live 25% ($22,850).

##### 6. Acceptance
Harbourline has 5 business days to accept or reject each deliverable in writing. Silence is not acceptance. Final acceptance follows the go-live readout described in Section 9.

##### 7. Change control
Any change to scope, volume or timeline requires a written Change Order signed by both parties before work proceeds. A Change Order states the change, its fee and its schedule effect.

## Output

### Review of draft SOW v2 against quote Q-2291 rev 3

I read the full draft against the confirmed quote summary. I changed no figures and edited no text. Eight items need a decision from the pricing owner, the contract owner or you. Three are editorial and can be fixed once the decisions are made.

**Method note.** I could not run `slop_scan.py`, so I did its checks by hand: repeated mechanics, justification tails, verb piles and cross-reference checks. The counts below are my manual counts. The draft stays unapproved until its authorised owner signs off. This review is not legal approval.

#### 1. Decisions needed before it goes to procurement

| # | Location | Finding | Source | Who decides |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Section 5, milestones | The three milestones total 95%, or $86,830. The fixed fee is $91,400, so $4,570 is unbilled. The quote's go-live milestone is **30%** ($27,420). The draft says 25% ($22,850). | Quote milestones: 25/45/30 | Pricing owner confirms the split. I have not corrected it. |
| 2 | Section 5, "Overage is billed … time-and-materials" | This contradicts "Fixed fee". The quote is fixed fee and gives no T&M overage right. The sentence adds a billing model the quote does not contain. | Quote pricing model | Pricing owner and contract owner. Delete it, or confirm it is an agreed term. |
| 3 | Section 2, "10 weeks" | The quote says 12 weeks from 2027-01-18. | Quote header | Pricing owner. The date and the duration must match the quote. |
| 4 | Section 3.1, "a hard cap" | The quote calls 38,000 cases a volume **estimate** from the client's 2026-10-12 export, "not a cap". The draft turns an estimate into a cap, and Section 3.1 then sends extra cases to a Change Order. | Quote scope item 1 | Contract owner. Decide whether the number is an estimate or a cap, then say so once. If it is a cap, the quote needs a revision first. |
| 5 | Section 2, "full configuration … functional parity" against Section 3.2 | The parity promise conflicts with the caps of 40 templates and 12 rules. I have kept both until an authorised owner resolves it. As written, a client could claim parity for a 41st template. | Quote items 2 and 3 | Contract owner. Likely fix: tie scope to the Section 3 list and drop "full" and "parity". |
| 6 | Section 3.3 against Section 3.4 | 3.3 delivers a billing system sync. 3.4 excludes billing integrations. The quote excludes third-party integrations "including billing" and has no sync item. | Quote exclusions | Pricing owner. Either 3.3 is not in scope and should be removed, or the quote is missing an item. |
| 7 | Section 6, "5 business days" | The quote gives 10 business days per deliverable. | Quote acceptance | Contract owner. The shorter period favours the provider and departs from the quote. |
| 8 | Section 4, approver | The draft names "Client Lead" as approver. The quote's role is the Engagement Manager, who approves deliverables for the client. The quote lists no Client Lead. The quote lists an Executive Sponsor and a Data Owner. | Quote client roles | Engagement owner. I kept the quote's role names and did not substitute one for the other. |

#### 2. Obligation and dependency check

- **Admin access (Section 4).** The draft says the provider "will ensure" Harbourline's administrator access is in place by 18 January 2027. The quote lists this as a **client dependency**, not a provider promise. As written, the provider owns a client task. Reword to make Harbourline the owner. This is an owner correction, so I list it here for confirmation. It also needs a stated consequence if the date slips, and the quote gives none. That is an open gap.
- **Data owner (Section 4).** Harbourline supplies a named data owner. The name is not in the sources, so it needs a placeholder in the draft.
- **Final acceptance (Section 6).** It points to "Section 9", but the draft ends at Section 7. The quote ties final acceptance to the go-live readout. The reference is broken, and the readout is not described anywhere in the draft. Add the readout to the scope list, or point to the deliverable that holds it. The quote's scope item 4 (cutover support and go-live readout) has no matching deliverable in Section 3 either.
- **Custom reporting.** The quote excludes it. The draft's exclusions list leaves it out. Add it to Section 3.4 only if the contract owner agrees, since that is a scope-boundary decision.

#### 3. Quantities (Basis of Estimate)

| Quantity | Source | Status in quote | Status in draft | Owning section | Verification | Open decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ~38,000 cases | Client export, 2026-10-12 | Estimate | "Hard cap" | 3.1 | Mismatch | Finding 4 |
| 40 email templates | Quote item 2 | "Up to" limit | Same | 3.2 | Matches | Finding 5 (parity conflict) |
| 12 automation rules | Quote item 3 | "Up to" limit | Same | 3.2 | Matches | Finding 5 |
| 12 weeks | Quote header | Duration | 10 weeks | 2 | Mismatch | Finding 3 |
| 480 hours / $91,400 | Quote | Fixed fee | $91,400 (hours not shown) | 5 | Fee matches | Finding 2 |

The quote reconciles internally. The role hours sum to 60 + 140 + 220 + 60 = 480. The revenue sums to $12,000 + $30,800 + $39,600 + $9,000 = $91,400. Each role's hours times rate equals its stated revenue. The draft's $91,400 fee agrees with the quote. Only the milestone split fails.

The draft does not say when the case estimate is checked against actual inventory, or who accepts the result. That is an unresolved gate. I did not invent one.

#### 4. Structural de-slop (editorial, safe after the decisions above)

**Repeated change mechanic: five statements.** I found the change-order rule in Section 1, Section 3.1, Section 3.4, Section 5 (overage) and Section 7. Section 7 should own it. This follows the ownership map: the change process, trigger, approval and fee-and-schedule statement sit in one place.
- Section 1 already points to Section 7, so keep it.
- Section 3.1: replace the parenthetical with "Case volume changes follow Section 7", once Finding 4 is decided.
- Section 3.4: delete the last sentence ("Any change to scope requires a Change Order"). It restates Section 7.
- Section 5: the overage sentence is removed or confirmed under Finding 2.
- The Section 7 text stays complete. Note that it treats volume, scope and timeline alike. If the contract distinguishes volume changes from new workstreams, that is a contract-owner call. I have not invented a soft/hard split.

**Justification tails.** One candidate: Section 4, "so that data questions have a single point of contact." It repeats the purpose of naming a data owner and defends no exception. It may be cut, subject to the contract owner's approval of any change to an obligation. I would keep Section 6's "Silence is not acceptance". It is a stricter-than-default term, not a tail.

**Verb piles and commentary.** None found. "Functional parity" is a scope claim, not commentary, and is handled in Finding 5.

**Cross-references.** Sections 1, 3.1 and 3.4 point to Section 7, which exists and holds the rule. The Section 6 reference to Section 9 is broken (above).

Counts, by hand: repeated mechanic 1 (five locations), justification tails 1 candidate, broken references 1, meta-commentary 0. I have not re-scanned a revised document, because there is no revised document yet.

#### 5. Suggested next steps

1. Send Findings 1–3 and 6 to the pricing owner. They need a revised or reconfirmed quote.
2. Send Findings 4, 5 and 7 to the contract owner. Findings 4 and 5 together decide whether the scope is capped or estimated.
3. Confirm Finding 8 and the admin-access owner with the engagement owner.
4. After those decisions, I can apply the Section 4 edits as tracked changes and re-run the checks.

#### Gaps and assumptions

- I had only the SOW draft and the quote summary. There is no master agreement, template or approved decision deck, so clauses that would normally come from the agreement could not be checked. I did not assume them.
- The draft lacks signature, notice and miscellaneous terms. I treated it as a partial draft and did not judge that absence.
- No receipts from prose, brand or review-deliverable tooling exist. These checks need scripts I cannot run, and the document is not final.
- No `.docx` was produced, so nothing needed a visual or brand check.

#### Files

- `out/answer.md` (this review). Its key content is the eight findings above.

# Review deal economics

The Deal Desk readout answers one question for people who were not in the
scoping room: should Estate ship this offer, and on what terms. It is the
last internal gate before the client sees numbers, so its job is to make the
commercial reality legible, not attractive.

The cardinal rule: **surface everything, smooth nothing.** A reviewer who
approves a clean-looking packet with hidden problems is not protected; one
who approves a packet with explicit flags made a considered decision. Every
unconfirmed staffing role, every load-bearing assumption, every risk to
margin appears as a labeled flag with a named resolution path. Presenting a
clean deal that is not clean is the exact failure this artifact exists to
catch, and it is why the artifact registry lists "risk smoothed over" and
"real margin hidden behind point estimate" as hard fails.

Margin is the headline. A reviewer should reach the margin number, and its
position against the floor, in the first ten seconds. If the margin is
tight or provisional, that is the lead, not a footnote.

## Governance, delegated

- **evidence-core** runs first. Sales context, stakeholder
  postures, risks, and assumptions are load-bearing claims; build the ledger
  before the packet. If a load-bearing domain is Insufficient, produce the
  "Not ready for Deal Desk approval" memo and stop. A full packet after
  insufficient evidence is a hard fail.
- **The quote owns every number.** Hours, rates, fees, and durations come
  from the Q-number through the scoping MCP (`scoping_get_quote` and
  friends), never from memory or chat. Margin is computed from those inputs
  and printed with the computation, never asserted. Fixed fee or T&M, never
  both. If the quote and any other document disagree, the quote wins and the
  disagreement becomes a flag.
- **brand-renderer** owns the rendering and the visual, parity, and
  brand release gates. Never inline hex values or rebuild the token set.
- **review-writing** owns writing review; a confirmed profile supplies voice. Run its checker on the packet's prose. No em
  dashes, sentence-case headings, no AI vocabulary in the tagline or
  anywhere else.

If a governor is not installed on this surface, state the check it would
have run, do the best manual substitute, and say that is what happened.
Never skip silently.

## One mandatory human input

The delivery leadership cosign is asked for, never inferred. Ask the
delivery lead (or the user relaying them) whether delivery has cosigned
scope, hours, and assumptions, and record the answer verbatim. The
figures block field `delivery_cosign.status` takes exactly one of
`confirmed`, `conditional`, `pending`, or `declined`; the gate rejects
blank, `assumed`, `inferred`, and `tbd`. "Delivery cosign missing" is a
registry hard fail, and it means missing from the record, not missing
approval: `pending` with a named signer and a date is an honest, passing
answer. `confirmed` without a name and date fails.

Everything else in the packet can be harvested. This one field cannot.

## Workflow

**1. Orient.** Pin the opportunity, the Q-number, the deal desk meeting if
one is scheduled, and who reviews. Confirm the quote total and pricing model
through the scoping MCP before writing anything. Stamp the packet with the
Q-number and an as-of date; record IDs do not survive sandbox refreshes, so
the stamp is what makes the packet auditable later.

**2. Read current commercial policy.** Confirm the project's margin floor and
approval ladder from its named source. Record the verification date and the
selected values in the figures block. Read [margin policy](references/margin-approval-routing.md)
for the input contract. If policy is unavailable, prepare the supported economics
and identify the approval decision still needed. Never inherit a threshold from
an example or treat a valid figures record as approval.

**3. Harvest.** Internal first: the quote, the DDOC and its confirmed
option, the solution brief, the SOW draft if one exists, Salesforce
opportunity and contacts, transcripts read verbatim, Slack. Evidence-core
governs provenance: every claim carries a source and date, every inference
is labeled with a confidence band, conflicts show both sides.

**4. Build two ledgers, then the packet.** The commercial ledger: per-role
hours, rates, cost rates, fee, computed margin, staffing basis, sensitivity
scenarios with dollar impacts, levers with quantified effects. The risk
ledger: margin risks each paired with a protective clause by number or a
no-coverage flag (one or the other, never both, never neither), scope risks,
staffing prerequisites, load-bearing assumptions with quantified "if broken"
consequences. Then project the packet from the ledgers using
`references/section-catalog.md`. Every catalog section is always present;
an unfillable section becomes a named unknown with an owner, a resolve-by
date, and the gate it blocks, never a plausible projection.

**5. Route the asks.** Two to six asks, each with a direct recommendation,
formatted per `references/asks-and-decisions-log.md`. Compute which ladder
band the real margin lands in and route price-touching asks to that band's
approver or higher. The packet requests exactly one overall approval action:
approve, approve with conditions, reject, or not ready. More than one is a
hard fail. The decisions log ships empty; it is filled live in the meeting,
and pre-filling it fabricates approvals.

**6. Embed the figures block and run the gate.**

```bash
python3 scripts/deal_desk_gate.py packet.md
```

The block schema is in `references/margin-approval-routing.md`. The gate
recomputes internal cost from role hours and cost rates (and the fee too on
T&M), checks the stated margin against the recomputed one, checks the floor
comparison against the arithmetic, checks the approval route against the
ladder carried in the block, and rejects a blank or non-committal cosign.
Exit 0 or the packet does not ship. Fix the ledger and regenerate; never
hand-patch the rendered output, because the next regenerate drops the patch.

**7. Tie out every figure across the reviewed artifacts.** Export the quote's
figures (fee, per-role hours and rates, phase totals, verified percentages,
assumptions, scope lines) to JSON per the schema in
`scripts/quote_tieout_check.py`, then reconcile the packet prose and every
sibling artifact under review (SOW draft, ROM, proposal) against it:

```bash
python3 scripts/quote_tieout_check.py quote.json packet.md sow-draft.md rom.md
```

Any figure that traces to nothing in the quote fails, whether it is fabricated
or contradicts a quote value; the check prints the offending line and the
nearest quote value and resolves nothing. A quote figure, assumption, or scope
line no artifact carries is a warning to confirm. Fix conflicts at their
source (the quote through scope-project, or the artifact through its owning
skill) and rerun; this skill never edits a figure to make the tie-out pass.

**8. Render and gate the rendering.** Hand to brand-renderer for
the HTML (or docx backup for email and print). Margin is the visually
dominant figure, rendered against the floor; all economics in monospace.
Verify by rendering, then apply review-writing to the prose. Report counts per
gate, not adjectives, and write a one-line disposition per gate.

**9. Land and close the loop.** Deliver the file, commit it to the deal's
folder, write session memory pointing at the files. Close with the margin
verdict, the flags a reviewer must not miss, and your biggest judgment call
argued honestly from the other side. If the packet contains a real fork,
say so; never present it as settled.

## Durable output

Every run leaves a Markdown record per `_shared/output-contract.md`: the
packet itself on a build, or a review record with the gate and tie-out
results, the exceptions, and the remediation list on an audit. The decision
record lands in the engagement hub's `04-decisions-assumptions.md`, which
this skill owns for Deal Desk outcomes: what was asked, what the humans
decided, and what supersedes what. Deliver or link the file; never just say
it was written.

## If the margin does not survive

When the recomputed margin lands below the floor, or becomes a range whose
pessimistic end does, that is the headline and the packet still ships, with
the route escalated per the ladder and the levers section carrying real
options with quantified impacts. What never happens: adjusting hours or
rates to rescue the number. Pricing changes belong to scope-project against
the quote; this skill renders what the quote says and routes the
consequences.

## Boundaries

- Internal only. Nothing in this packet is client-facing; it carries margin,
  cost rates, and candid risk the client never sees.
- Does not price and does not touch the quote. scope-project owns scope and
  pricing changes; this skill renders and routes.
- Not the DDOC. The client-facing decision deck is build-deck; "Deal Desk
  document" as a client deck is a retired name for that artifact, and this
  skill is the internal readout only.
- Not the business case; that is write-business-case. Not SOW terms;
  that is write-statement-of-work, and the protective clauses' text lives in the SOW
  master, cited here by number only.
- Reviews and verdicts only. It never authors or silently rewrites the
  solution, the SOW, or any source evidence; a failed check produces a
  remediation list for the owning skill, never an edit.
- Does not approve. Humans clear the gate; the packet prepares it. The
  decisions log and sign-off table record what humans decided.
- Post-approval change detection (a material scope or margin change after
  Deal Desk requiring re-alignment before SOW) is deal governance, not this
  skill. It is a known gap: when a packet is being rebuilt after approval,
  flag the delta explicitly and say re-alignment is required.

## Running unattended

The cosign and the live decisions log need humans. On a scheduled or
headless run: build the ledgers, embed the figures block with
`delivery_cosign.status` set to `pending` and a named owner, run the gate,
and stop with findings. Say plainly that the cosign is outstanding. Never
record an answer nobody gave.

## When time is short

Cut in this order, and say what was cut: methodology detail, the staffing
Gantt (keep the allocation table), sales-context depth below the ROM and
deadline rows. Never cut: the figures block and its gate, the cosign ask,
the floor comparison, the assumptions table, sourcing, or the flags. A thin
honest packet clears review; a full smooth one is the failure mode.

## Files

- `references/section-catalog.md`: every packet section, its field sources
  (DS, SE, CA, PS), and the bar each must clear.
- `references/margin-approval-routing.md`: floor, ladder, protective
  clauses, re-verification rule, and the figures block schema.
- `references/asks-and-decisions-log.md`: ask format, live decisions log,
  action items, sign-off, and the cosign protocol.
- `scripts/deal_desk_gate.py`: the blocking gate. Python 3 stdlib only.
- `scripts/deal_desk_gate_selftest.py`: run it after any gate change;
  fixtures in `scripts/fixtures/`.
- `scripts/quote_tieout_check.py`: the deterministic tie-out. Reconciles
  every figure, assumption, and scope line in the reviewed artifacts against
  the quote export. Stdlib only; the quote JSON schema is in its docstring.
- `scripts/quote_tieout_check_selftest.py`: run it after any tie-out change;
  fixtures `tieout_quote.json`, `tieout_pass.md`, and `tieout_fail.md` in
  `scripts/fixtures/`.

9. Land and close the loop. Deliver the file, commit it to the deal's folder, write session memory pointing at the files. Close with the margin verdict, the flags a reviewer must not miss, and your biggest judgment call argued honestly from the other side. If the packet contains a real fork, say so; never present it as settled.

Durable output

Every run leaves a Markdown record per _shared/output-contract.md: the packet itself on a build, or a review record with the gate and tie-out results, the exceptions, and the remediation list on an audit. The decision record lands in the engagement hub's 04-decisions-assumptions.md, which this skill owns for Deal Desk outcomes: what was asked, what the humans decided, and what supersedes what. Deliver or link the file; never just say it was written.

If the margin does not survive

When the recomputed margin lands below the floor, or becomes a range whose pessimistic end does, that is the headline and the packet still ships, with the route escalated per the ladder and the levers section carrying real options with quantified impacts. What never happens: adjusting hours or rates to rescue the number. Pricing changes belong to scope-project against the quote; this skill renders what the quote says and routes the consequences.

Boundaries

  • Internal only. Nothing in this packet is client-facing; it carries margin,

cost rates, and candid risk the client never sees.

  • Does not price and does not touch the quote. scope-project owns scope and

pricing changes; this skill renders and routes.

  • Not the DDOC. The client-facing decision deck is build-deck; "Deal Desk

document" as a client deck is a retired name for that artifact, and this skill is the internal readout only.

  • Not the business case; that is write-business-case. Not SOW terms;

that is write-statement-of-work, and the protective clauses' text lives in the SOW master, cited here by number only.

  • Reviews and verdicts only. It never authors or silently rewrites the

solution, the SOW, or any source evidence; a failed check produces a remediation list for the owning skill, never an edit.

  • Does not approve. Humans clear the gate; the packet prepares it. The

decisions log and sign-off table record what humans decided.

  • Post-approval change detection (a material scope or margin change after

Deal Desk requiring re-alignment before SOW) is deal governance, not this skill. It is a known gap: when a packet is being rebuilt after approval, flag the delta explicitly and say re-alignment is required.

Running unattended

The cosign and the live decisions log need humans. On a scheduled or headless run: build the ledgers, embed the figures block with delivery_cosign.status set to pending and a named owner, run the gate, and stop with findings. Say plainly that the cosign is outstanding. Never record an answer nobody gave.

When time is short

Cut in this order, and say what was cut: methodology detail, the staffing Gantt (keep the allocation table), sales-context depth below the ROM and deadline rows. Never cut: the figures block and its gate, the cosign ask, the floor comparison, the assumptions table, sourcing, or the flags. A thin honest packet clears review; a full smooth one is the failure mode.

Files

  • references/section-catalog.md: every packet section, its field sources

(DS, SE, CA, PS), and the bar each must clear.

  • references/margin-approval-routing.md: floor, ladder, protective

clauses, re-verification rule, and the figures block schema.

  • references/asks-and-decisions-log.md: ask format, live decisions log,

action items, sign-off, and the cosign protocol.

  • scripts/deal_desk_gate.py: the blocking gate. Python 3 stdlib only.
  • scripts/deal_desk_gate_selftest.py: run it after any gate change;

fixtures in scripts/fixtures/.

  • scripts/quote_tieout_check.py: the deterministic tie-out. Reconciles

every figure, assumption, and scope line in the reviewed artifacts against the quote export. Stdlib only; the quote JSON schema is in its docstring.

  • scripts/quote_tieout_check_selftest.py: run it after any tie-out change;

fixtures tieout_quote.json, tieout_pass.md, and tieout_fail.md in scripts/fixtures/.
skills.excerptHtml:
The Deal Desk readout answers one question for people who were not in the scoping room: should Estate ship this offer, and on what terms. It is the last internal gate before the client sees numbers, so its job is to make the commercial reality legible, not attractive.

The cardinal rule: surface everything, smooth nothing. A reviewer who approves a clean-looking packet with hidden problems is not protected; one who approves a packet with explicit flags made a considered decision. Every unconfirmed staffing role, every load-bearing assumption, every risk to margin appears as a labeled flag with a named resolution path. Presenting a clean deal that is not clean is the exact failure this artifact exists to catch, and it is why the artifact registry lists "risk smoothed over" and "real margin hidden behind point estimate" as hard fails.

Margin is the headline. A reviewer should reach the margin number, and its position against the floor, in the first ten seconds. If the margin is tight or provisional, that is the lead, not a footnote.
