skills.markdown:
---
name: scope-project
description: Develop project scope and effort estimates from the user's brief, supplied models or configured pricing system. Support rough ranges and confirmed quote revisions. Produce usable local scope and calculations without requiring a CRM connection.
---

# Scope project

Build the requested scope from current project evidence. Use a supplied export
or the local model below when no pricing integration is configured. A rough
estimate does not require an existing quote. Keep accepted commitments separate
from draft scope and estimate assumptions.

## Select the work

| Request | Output |
| --- | --- |
| Define scope | Work items with supported boundaries and acceptance conditions |
| Estimate effort | Sourced role-hour ranges and their basis |
| Estimate cost | The effort model with an explicit rate source and currency |
| Plan staffing | Role capacity and a schedule constrained by dependencies |
| Revise a quote | A comparison against the confirmed quote revision; authorized changes only |

Read the supplied brief and existing decisions before asking a question. Find
the constraints affecting scope or price. Preserve contradictory evidence as
an unresolved decision. Ask only when a missing choice materially changes the
work; continue the supported parts while it is pending.

## Define the deliverable scope

Organize items around the behavior or deliverable being supplied. An item can
carry its requirements work through validation and deployment. Avoid counting
the same lifecycle effort again in a separate overhead row. A standalone test
or assessment engagement may have its own deliverable; follow the actual brief.

Give each item a stable ID and descriptive name. Explain its behavior and the
condition that bounds it. Link it to its source and acceptance check. Keep
dependencies and exclusions where they affect that item. Use the project's
capability taxonomy if one exists; a local draft needs no custom CRM taxonomy.

Distinguish explicitly requested work from a necessary implication. Keep an
inferred addition proposed until its scope owner accepts it. Do not turn an
unanswered question into a statement that documentation or access is absent.
An assumption is a proposed estimating condition, with its consequence if it
changes. It is never a substitute for a fact.

Read [the estimation method](references/methodology.md) for calibration and
staffing decisions. Use meaningful item names in cross-references; retain IDs
for traceability rather than making the reader decode abbreviations.

## Estimate with available sources

Use current scope decomposition or relevant comparables. Describe differences
in volume and complexity when adapting another engagement. A user-supplied
anchor can support an estimate when its working hours and scope are explicit.
Do not assume a working week, a phase split or a staffing ratio.

Keep a low and high bound around the expected effort where the source supports
a range. Explain which condition moves each bound. Do not invent a confidence
percentage or treat the expected value as a statistical median without data.
If effort remains unknown, retain the item as unestimated and identify the
discovery needed. Do not present a priced subset as the complete project cost.

Use the supplied rate card or confirmed quote for rates. Preserve its revision
and distinguish cost rates from client billing rates. Without rates, deliver
the effort estimate and the missing pricing input. Do not import old rates
from this estate or another engagement.

## Run the local calculator

The calculator requires Python 3 and no external service:

```bash
python3 scripts/estimate.py scope.json --output attempts/001/estimate.json
```

It writes the exact decimal calculations and a readable Markdown estimate.
Existing outputs are preserved. Use another attempt path after a revision.
The [fictional input](fixtures/estimate.example.json) shows the full contract.
Its rates and effort are test data, with no authority for a real project.

| Input | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | Reference and revision of the scope model |
| `currency` | Currency supplied for this estimate |
| `rates` | Role and rate, with the source of that rate |
| `items` | Unique ID and name; description and source; estimated items also need a basis and role allocations |
| `items[].status`, when used | `estimated` (the default) or `unestimated`; other values are refused |
| `items[].discovery_needed` | Required for an unestimated item; explain what must be learned before estimating it |
| `allocations[].hours` | Nonnegative `low`, `expected` and `high` values in that order |
| `capacity`, when used | Role count and weekly hours per person, with availability from 0 to 1 |
| `assumptions` and `exclusions` | Conditions and work boundaries preserved in the result |

The result includes item calculations and role-hour totals. It also gives the
aggregate hours and fee for each scenario. Amounts retain their decimal value;
the calculator applies no implicit commercial rounding or contingency uplift.
It records the input hash and calculator hash.

For work with no effort basis, set `status` to `unestimated`, retain its source
and description, and supply `discovery_needed`. Omit allocations or use an empty
list. The calculator rejects allocations on an unestimated item so hours cannot
be silently discarded.

Output format 2 retains every item. When any item is unestimated, the status is
`incomplete-estimate`, `totals_complete` is false, and full-project `totals` is
null. `estimated_subtotal` contains only the estimated work; it is null when no
item has an estimate. For fully estimated scope, `totals` keeps the scenario
calculations. Fees remain null without rates. Consumers must check completeness
before using totals. The Markdown shows item calculations, role hours, supplied
rate sources, and all three capacity scenarios. Capacity covers estimated work
only, so unknown work cannot acquire an implied delivery date.

Capacity produces a workload lower bound in weeks. Dependencies and waiting
time can extend the schedule. A capacity bound cannot establish a delivery date.
For a schedule, place the actual work against dependencies and agreed resource
availability. Preserve phase names and staffing increments from the project.

Inspect the generated estimate against the input. Recompute a representative
item and reconcile the totals. Check the range drivers and the meaning of each
assumption. Apply review-writing to the generated prose, including text
carried from a draft input. Calculation success does not establish scope quality.

## Use a configured CRM adapter

Read [CRM scoping](references/crm-scoping.md) only when the project uses the
documented custom integration. Inspect the tools actually available and confirm
the org before a write. Read [payloads](references/payloads.md) before preparing
a supported mutation. Use the target's actual metadata and schema version.

Create or update a record only within the user's authorized request. Show the
affected quote and scope before a material change. Never add team membership,
replace a tag catalog or activate a timeline merely to make local estimation
possible. Read back changed records and report what the system accepted.

## Deliver the result

Return the usable scope and requested calculations. Retain assumptions with the
estimate and name the conditions that would reopen it. Save actual generated
files and failed attempts. A hub update is optional and needs an available,
authorized project destination; local work remains usable without it.

Use compare-scope-options for a comparison or interactive proposal. Use the
write-statement-of-work workflow for the contract. A new estimate does not replace an
accepted quote, authorize a production operation or establish client approval.

examples.markdown:
## Request

Can you put together a rough estimate for the Northgate client portal? My call notes, our Q4 rate card and the dental-group project we'd use as a comparable are in the inputs folder. I need an hours and cost range for the partners' meeting on Friday.

## Inputs

Run of the built `scope-project` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Other files it produced, not shown here: `scope.json`.

#### call-notes.md

#### Northgate Veterinary Group: discovery call notes (2026-10-29)

Attendees: Priya Raman (operations manager, Northgate), our side: Tomas Eriksen.

##### What they want
A client portal in three parts:
1. Online appointment booking. Owners pick a clinic, a vet and a time slot, and can cancel or reschedule. Each clinic has its own opening hours and vet rosters. If no slot is free in the next 14 days, Priya wants the owner shown the earliest slot at any other clinic.
2. Appointment reminders by SMS and email, 48 hours and 4 hours before the visit.
3. Owner login with a read-only view of pet profiles, vaccination dates and past visit summaries.

Priya also wants old patient records moved from their legacy system (PawFile) into the new practice system so the portal can show history. She said "about 40,000 patients" and "some X-ray images". She does not know the PawFile export format, and nobody has looked at the images.

##### Clinics
The brief Priya emailed says 6 clinics. On the call she said a 7th opens in April and should be bookable from day one of the portal if possible.

##### Open items
- Deposits for surgery bookings: "maybe, the partners haven't decided". No payment gateway chosen.
- Target go-live: before the April opening.
- Practice system: the portal reads from a vendor API. Priya will ask the vendor for API documentation; not received yet.

##### Our delivery team (Tomas)
Developer 1 person, 32 h/week, 75% available. Business analyst 1 person, 16 h/week, 100%. QA 1 person, 24 h/week, 50%. Project manager 1 person, 8 h/week, 100%.

#### comparable-dental-portal.md

#### Comparable: Lakeside Dental booking portal (completed 2026-03)

Scope: online booking for 3 clinics, 9 dentists, cancel and reschedule, SMS and email reminders at 24 hours. One SMS vendor. No login, no record migration. Actual hours, time and materials.

| Part | BA | Dev | QA | PM | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Booking (3 clinics) | 30 | 120 | 40 | 10 | 200 |
| Reminders | 6 | 30 | 10 | 3 | 49 |

Notes: about 30% of booking development went to per-clinic hours and roster rules. A late request to add a second reminder time cost 8 extra developer hours. Reminders used the vendor's ready-made SMS library.

#### rate-card.md

#### Client billing rate card, 2026-Q4, revision v2

Currency: USD per hour. These are billing rates to clients, not cost rates.

| Role | Rate |
| --- | ---: |
| Project manager | 140 |
| Business analyst | 125 |
| Developer | 150 |
| QA engineer | 105 |

Approved by the finance lead on 2026-10-01. Time-and-materials engagements use these rates unchanged.

## Output

The portal work we can size comes to **411 to 652 hours, expected 501, or USD 56,240 to 89,200, expected 68,610**. That is not the full project cost. Legacy patient record migration has no effort basis yet, so I left it unestimated and have not given a project total.

#### Range

| Scenario | Hours | Fee (USD) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Low | 411 | 56,240 |
| Expected | 501 | 68,610 |
| High | 652 | 89,200 |

Fees use the 2026-Q4 v2 client billing rates (project manager 140, business analyst 125, developer 150, QA 105 per hour), unrounded and with no contingency added.

| Item | Low h | Expected h | High h | Expected USD |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Online appointment booking | 250 | 299 | 382 | 40,980 |
| Appointment reminders | 59 | 72 | 96 | 9,880 |
| Owner login and read-only pet records view | 102 | 130 | 174 | 17,750 |
| Legacy patient record migration | unestimated | | | |

By role (low / expected / high): developer 246 / 300 / 386, business analyst 64 / 78 / 102, QA 80 / 96 / 126, project manager 21 / 27 / 38. Project management is carried inside each item, so it is not counted twice.

#### How the numbers were built

- **Booking and reminders (Inferred).** Both come from the Lakeside Dental project: 200 hours for booking at 3 clinics and 49 for reminders. About 36 of the booking developer hours there went to per-clinic hours and roster rules, roughly 12 per clinic. Six clinics adds about 36, and the cross-clinic "earliest slot elsewhere" rule is new work. Northgate wants email as well as SMS, at two reminder times. Lakeside had SMS only, and adding a second time late cost it 8 developer hours.
- **Owner login and records view (Inferred, weaker).** The comparable has no login. I decomposed it by role from general knowledge of similar screens, so treat this line as the least anchored of the three.
- **What moves the high bound.** Booking reaches 382 hours if the seventh clinic (opening in April) must be bookable on day one, or if the vendor API is awkward. Reminders reach 96 if a different SMS vendor is needed. The low bound assumes the API documentation arrives and matches what the portal needs.

#### Items to confirm before Friday

| Dimension | Value assumed | Confidence | Confirmation action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clinics bookable at launch | 6 | Unknown | The emailed brief says 6; Priya said on the call a 7th opens in April and should be bookable from day one if possible. These conflict. Ask Priya whether the 7th is in launch scope. |
| Practice system vendor API: reading vet rosters and writing appointments | Supported | Unknown | Documentation has not arrived. Priya is requesting it from the vendor. I cannot say whether it exists or is adequate. |
| Reminder channels and times | SMS and email at 48 h and 4 h | Confirmed (call notes) | None needed. |
| SMS vendor | One vendor with a ready-made library | Unknown | Ask which vendor Northgate prefers. |
| Patient records to migrate | About 40,000 plus X-ray images (client's figure) | Unknown | Get a sample PawFile export, real patient and image counts, image sizes and the practice system's import options. |

The seventh clinic is a conflict between sources. The estimate stands on 6, and the 7-clinic case is covered only by the high bound.

#### Schedule

If the team is as described in your notes (developer 32 h/week at 75%, business analyst 16 h, QA 12 h effective, project manager 8 h), the developer sets the pace. The minimum is **10.25, 12.5 and 16.08 weeks** for the low, expected and high cases. That is a workload bound for the sized items only. It ignores client review time, waiting on the vendor API, and the migration. Counting back from the April opening is a separate exercise once the migration is sized.

#### Excluded

- Deposit payments for surgery bookings: the partners have not decided and no gateway is chosen. If included, this becomes a new item.
- Hosting, SMS and email usage fees, and practice system licences.
- Legacy record migration, until the discovery above is done.

#### What would reopen the estimate

- Seventh clinic needed at launch (resize booking).
- API documentation that lacks roster reads or appointment writes (resize booking and reminders).
- Deposits added (new item).
- Migration sized (adds to the total, and affects the schedule and the April target).
- A different SMS vendor (resize reminders).

#### Limits of this work

- This is a planning range. It is not a quote and does not replace any agreed commercial terms.
- I could not run the local calculator (`scripts/estimate.py`) here. I did its arithmetic by hand with its rules, and checked that the item totals add up to the role totals: 411, 501 and 652 hours both ways. The fees reconcile the same way. Rerun the calculator on `scope.json` to produce the hashed JSON output.
- The evidence, quality, brand and writing-diagnostics checkers were not available. I reviewed the confidence labels, calculations and wording by hand instead. The estimate is a plain Markdown file with no branded rendering.
- The ROM reconciliation gate applies to quote-anchored estimates, and there is no quote here.

#### Files

- `out/scope.json`: calculator input with items, bases, rates, capacity, assumptions and exclusions.
- `out/estimate.md`: the estimate tables above, with the role effort, capacity bound, assumptions and exclusions.
- `out/answer.md`: this summary.

skills.title: Simplify code
skills.description: Review and refine the current code change for reuse, clarity, maintainability, and efficiency without changing behavior. Use when a delivery workflow requires a simplify pass, when the user asks to simplify or clean up a diff, or before committing a non-trivial implementation. Scope work to the current branch diff or an explicit target, preserve public behavior and project conventions, apply only high-confidence edits, and verify the result with focused tests. In Claude Code, the built-in /simplify does the same job; prefer this skill when an estate workflow names its pass.

guide.when: A delivery workflow names a simplify pass, or a non-trivial diff needs cleanup before commit.
guide.inputs: The current branch diff or an explicit target, repository conventions and the relevant tests.
guide.outputs: High-confidence refinements with test evidence, plus behavior-changing candidates reported separately instead of applied.
guide.example: Review this diff for duplication and unnecessary complexity while preserving its behavior.
guide.expect: It works on the current branch diff or a target you name, reads the surrounding code and tests, and applies only high-confidence edits for reuse, clarity, maintainability and efficiency. It preserves behavior, stops if the diff base is ambiguous, and reports cleanups that would change behavior as recommendations rather than applying them.

skills.markdown:
---
name: simplify-code
description: 'Review and refine the current code change for reuse, clarity, maintainability, and efficiency without changing behavior. Use when a delivery workflow requires a simplify pass, when the user asks to simplify or clean up a diff, or before committing a non-trivial implementation. Scope work to the current branch diff or an explicit target, preserve public behavior and project conventions, apply only high-confidence edits, and verify the result with focused tests. In Claude Code, the built-in /simplify does the same job; prefer this skill when an estate workflow names its pass.'
---


# Simplify code

Make the current change easier to understand and maintain without changing what it does. This is
a judgment pass over code, not a formatter, prose rewrite, or license to redesign the feature.

## Scope

Use the explicit target when the caller supplies one. Otherwise inspect:

1. commits ahead of the branch's upstream or merge base;
2. staged and unstaged changes;
3. untracked source files that belong to the change.

Read the repository's `AGENTS.md`, nearby tests, and the surrounding implementation before editing.
Generated output, vendored code, lockfiles, snapshots, and unrelated pre-existing changes stay out
of scope unless the caller explicitly includes them.

## Review lenses

- **Reuse:** replace new duplication with an established local helper or pattern when the fit is
  exact and the result is clearer.
- **Clarity:** reduce needless nesting, indirection, branching, and naming ambiguity.
- **Maintainability:** keep responsibilities narrow, make invariants visible, and remove dead code
  introduced by the current change.
- **Efficiency:** remove repeated or unnecessary work when the improvement is evident and does not
  trade away readability or correctness.

Do not chase cleverness, minimum line count, or speculative abstraction. A slightly longer direct
implementation is better than a compressed one that hides behavior.

## Behavior boundary

Preserve public APIs, data shapes, permissions, ordering, error behavior, logging semantics,
user-facing strings, prompts, test expectations, and integration contracts. Do not weaken checks
or delete apparently redundant safeguards without proving why they are redundant. If a proposed
cleanup would change any of these, report it as a separate recommendation instead of applying it.

## Workflow

1. Establish the diff base and list the files in scope. Stop if the base is ambiguous or the
   repository has overlapping changes that cannot be separated safely.
2. Inspect the diff with enough surrounding code and tests to understand its behavior.
3. Record candidate improvements under the four review lenses. Reject speculative, cosmetic-only,
   or behavior-changing candidates.
4. Apply the smallest coherent set of high-confidence edits.
5. Run the narrowest relevant formatter, static checks, and focused tests. Run broader repository
   gates when its contract requires them.
6. Re-read the final diff against the original intent. Confirm that no unrelated file or protected
   behavior changed.
7. Report applied refinements, verification evidence, and worthwhile candidates deliberately left
   unapplied.

For a review-only request, stop after step 3 and return findings without editing.

## Host routing

OpenAI Codex agents run this skill directly. Current Claude Code can use
`/code-review medium --fix` for the corresponding review-and-apply step, then inspect its resulting
diff and run the repository's required tests. The delivery contract names both routes so it does
not depend on one vendor's built-in command vocabulary.

## Request

I'm about to commit the new overdue-notice code in inputs/overdue.py. Can you run a simplify pass on it, apply the safe edits, and tell me what you left alone? The project rules are in inputs/AGENTS.md and the tests are in inputs/test_overdue.py.

## Inputs

Run of the built `simplify-code` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Other files it produced, not shown here: `overdue.py`.

#### AGENTS.md

#### Project rules

- Python 3.11, standard library only.
- Money is always integer cents. Display text comes from `lib/money.py`:
  `format_cents(cents: int) -> str` returns `"$12.05"` for 1205 and `"$0.00"` for 0.
  Do not format money by hand.
- Notice dicts are consumed by the mailer service. Keys and value types are a contract:
  `member_id` (str), `title` (str), `days_overdue` (int), `fine_cents` (int), `fine_text` (str).
- Notices are sorted by fine, highest first, then by `member_id`.
- Run tests with `python -m pytest tests/test_overdue.py`.
- Code comments only for non-obvious reasons.

#### overdue.py

from datetime import date

from lib.money import format_cents

GRACE_DAYS = 3
FINE_PER_DAY_CENTS = 25
MAX_FINE_CENTS = 1000


def days_overdue(due, today):
    if today > due:
        return (today - due).days
    else:
        return 0


def calc_fine(loan, today):
    d = days_overdue(loan["due"], today)
    if d <= GRACE_DAYS:
        return 0
    else:
        fine = (d - GRACE_DAYS) * FINE_PER_DAY_CENTS
        if fine > MAX_FINE_CENTS:
            fine = MAX_FINE_CENTS
        return fine


def build_notices(loans, today):
    notices = []
    total = 0
    for loan in loans:
        if loan["returned"] is None:
            fine = calc_fine(loan, today)
            if fine > 0:
                days = days_overdue(loan["due"], today)
                text = "$" + str(fine // 100) + "." + str(fine % 100).zfill(2)
                notices.append({
                    "member_id": loan["member_id"],
                    "title": loan["title"],
                    "days_overdue": days,
                    "fine_cents": fine,
                    "fine_text": text,
                })
                total += fine
    notices.sort(key=lambda n: (-n["fine_cents"], n["member_id"]))
    return notices

#### test_overdue.py

from datetime import date

from overdue import build_notices, calc_fine

TODAY = date(2026, 11, 4)


def loan(member, due, returned=None):
    return {"member_id": member, "title": "T-" + member, "due": due, "returned": returned}


def test_grace_period_has_no_fine():
    assert calc_fine(loan("a", date(2026, 11, 1)), TODAY) == 0


def test_fine_after_grace():
    assert calc_fine(loan("a", date(2026, 10, 28)), TODAY) == 4 * 25


def test_fine_is_capped():
    assert calc_fine(loan("a", date(2026, 1, 1)), TODAY) == 1000


def test_returned_loans_skipped():
    assert build_notices([loan("a", date(2026, 1, 1), returned=date(2026, 2, 1))], TODAY) == []


def test_sorted_by_fine_then_member():
    loans = [loan("b", date(2026, 10, 20)), loan("a", date(2026, 10, 20)), loan("c", date(2026, 1, 1))]
    assert [n["member_id"] for n in build_notices(loans, TODAY)] == ["c", "a", "b"]

## Output

I simplified `overdue.py` and saved the result to `out/overdue.py`. I did not run the tests: nothing could be executed here, and `lib/money.py` was not supplied. I traced each of the five tests in `test_overdue.py` by hand against the new code and all five still hold. Please run `python -m pytest tests/test_overdue.py` before you commit.

#### Scope

The target was the one file you named, `overdue.py`. I read `AGENTS.md` and `test_overdue.py` first. There was no git history to diff, so the whole file counts as the change. `test_overdue.py` is unchanged.

#### Edits applied

1. **Hand-built money text replaced with `format_cents`.** `AGENTS.md` says money text must come from `lib/money.py`. The old line `"$" + str(fine // 100) + "." + str(fine % 100).zfill(2)` is what that rule rules out. For positive integer cents, `format_cents` returns the same string, for example `$10.00` for the 1000-cent cap and `$1.00` for 100. This rests on the `format_cents` contract in `AGENTS.md`, not on a run.
2. **Unused `total` removed.** It was summed inside the loop and never read or returned.
3. **Unused `from datetime import date` removed.** Nothing in the module referenced it.
4. **`days_overdue` reduced to `max((today - due).days, 0)`.** The old branch returned 0 whenever `today <= due`. In that case the day count is zero or negative, so `max` gives the same answer.
5. **`calc_fine` flattened.** It now computes billable days after the grace period, returns 0 if there are none, and otherwise returns `min(billable_days * FINE_PER_DAY_CENTS, MAX_FINE_CENTS)`. A loan 3 days overdue gives 0, 4 days gives 25, and 44 days or more gives the 1000 cap, as before. The vague name `d` is gone.
6. **Nesting in `build_notices` reduced.** Two nested `if` blocks became two `continue` guards. A returned loan and a zero fine are still skipped, and the order the notices are built in is unchanged.
7. **Single-use local variables inlined.** `days` and `text` were each used once, so they now sit in the dict.

#### Behavior check

- The notice keys (`member_id`, `title`, `days_overdue`, `fine_cents`, `fine_text`) and their types are the same, which matters because the mailer service consumes them.
- The sort is still highest fine first, then `member_id`.
- The function names, signatures and the three constants are unchanged.

#### Left alone

- **`days_overdue` is computed twice per overdue loan** (once inside `calc_fine`, once for the notice). Removing that means changing `calc_fine`'s signature, which the tests call directly. The cost is one date subtraction, so I kept the tested interface.
- **Renaming `calc_fine` or the `fine_cents` key** would read slightly better but changes either the public name or the mailer contract. Not applied.
- **No test asserts `fine_text`.** A case such as `build_notices([loan("c", date(2026, 1, 1))], TODAY)[0]["fine_text"] == "$10.00"` would pin edit 1. I left the test file alone because you asked for a pass on the module.

#### File

- `out/overdue.py`, the simplified module, 34 lines against 47 before.

```python
from lib.money import format_cents

GRACE_DAYS = 3
FINE_PER_DAY_CENTS = 25
MAX_FINE_CENTS = 1000


def days_overdue(due, today):
    return max((today - due).days, 0)


def calc_fine(loan, today):
    billable_days = days_overdue(loan["due"], today) - GRACE_DAYS
    if billable_days <= 0:
        return 0
    return min(billable_days * FINE_PER_DAY_CENTS, MAX_FINE_CENTS)


def build_notices(loans, today):
    notices = []
    for loan in loans:
        if loan["returned"] is not None:
            continue
        fine = calc_fine(loan, today)
        if fine == 0:
            continue
        notices.append({
            "member_id": loan["member_id"],
            "title": loan["title"],
            "days_overdue": days_overdue(loan["due"], today),
            "fine_cents": fine,
            "fine_text": format_cents(fine),
        })
    notices.sort(key=lambda n: (-n["fine_cents"], n["member_id"]))
    return notices
```

guide.outputs: A detailed specification with states, persistence, interfaces, and acceptance checks.

skills.markdown:
---
name: specify-implementation
description: Detailed UI, API and data-design reference used by write-feature-spec. Read for a requested implementation specification involving interfaces, persistence or interactive states. This module does not require a separate approval before an already authorized code change.
---

# Specify implementation

Use this reference with the product specification workflow. Select the sections
needed to explain the requested feature. An API-only change does not need a UI
mockup. A request to fix a defect does not automatically require a new product
specification, an HTML file or a separate approval interview.

## Inspect the existing implementation

Read the project instructions, brief, current decisions and relevant code before
proposing changes. Follow the affected imports, callers, routes and persistence
operations far enough to identify the regression surface. Record each important
finding with its file and behavior; a filename inventory is insufficient.

Check whether a function replaces records with DELETE and INSERT, whether an
upsert preserves their IDs, and whether uniqueness or foreign keys constrain the
proposed operation. Identify required context, such as a session ID, that may be
absent in the new entry point. Inspect interactive behavior in components that
appear read-only. Identify authentication helpers and existing patterns rather
than assuming a framework or replacing them during specification.

If these findings change the proposed design, explain the correction beside
the affected behavior. Preserve unrelated defects as follow-ups unless they
block the requested result. State any relevant source that could not be read.

## Describe the feature and its states

State the user's problem, the requested outcome and the supported behavior.
Separate accepted requirements from proposed choices and open decisions. Keep
material exclusions and dependencies visible where a reader could otherwise
misunderstand the scope. Do not invent an owner, date or metric to fill a field.

For an interactive feature, describe the applicable states:

| State | What the specification explains |
| --- | --- |
| Empty or first use | Explain how the user arrives and takes the first action. Show the initial content. |
| Loading or streaming | Progress, disabled or cancellable actions and repeated submission behavior |
| Populated | Show the available data and actions. Describe the result of an action. |
| Secondary surface | Explain how a modal or panel opens and closes. Identify the context it retains. |
| Error or rejection | Give the validation message and recovery path. Explain whether input survives rejection and which permissions apply. |
| Return visit | Explain how stored state reloads and who owns the record. |

An API-only implementation may still support an interactive task. When saved records, duplicate submission or connectivity loss affect users, specify retained input, an unknown commit outcome, authorized reload on return, and record ownership even when no UI mockup is needed. Session expiry does not establish deletion or loss of persisted records; describe the actual storage lifecycle only when sourced. If both context identifiers are supplied, resolve them to the same authorized canonical context or reject the conflict. A common owner alone does not make two contexts equivalent. A retry for an existing row must retain that row's established context. Do not offer dropping one identifier as permission to move or recreate that row in another context; a transfer is a separate operation requiring explicit authorization and a specified contract.

For each relevant state, name the trigger, visible result, permitted action and
next state. Add consequential alternatives such as missing dependencies,
duplicate submissions, cancellation or concurrent edits. Mark an inapplicable
state as such only when its absence matters to the reader.

For applicable UI behavior, specify keyboard operation, focus movement and restoration, accessible names and labels, and how validation or asynchronous status is announced. State the observable acceptance checks for those behaviors using the project's accessibility requirements. A visual mockup or contrast check alone does not verify them. An API-only change can identify this as an existing caller responsibility when that boundary is supported, rather than inventing a new interface.

Use a mockup when layout or interaction needs visual explanation. Show the
existing navigation and control states. Show the actual content shape.
Mark fictional data as examples. Use the project's confirmed design
tokens or the neutral brand profile. No palette, font, navigation shell or
company identity is prescribed by this module.

A static mockup demonstrates appearance and the states it depicts. It cannot
prove dynamic behavior, latency, accessibility or production fidelity. Reuse
actual components when the project makes that practical; verify implementation
separately. Do not promise a 1:1 translation from a drawing or HTML mockup.

## Specify persistence and interfaces

For a new table, give columns, types, defaults, nullability, keys and referenced
entities. For an existing table, identify each changed field and its migration.
State the access rules and read/write actors. Include row-level security or an
equivalent mechanism when the actual platform uses one. Explain unique keys,
upsert behavior and data backfill where they affect the feature.

Prefer an additive change when it meets the requirement. Identify a destructive
migration explicitly. Identify affected records and explain compatibility with
existing callers. Describe the recovery procedure.
Specification does not authorize executing it.

For each new endpoint, specify its method and path. Define authentication and
authorization. Give the request schema with successful and error responses.
Cover invalid inputs and missing resources. Explain what happens when a
dependency is unavailable. Describe idempotency,
ordering or retry behavior when the operation needs it.

For a changed endpoint, name the changed contract and the behavior it preserves.
For example, an optional conversation ID may be added alongside an existing
session ID. Explain how callers select the context and how an older caller
continues to work. Keep field names and required literals exact.

## Bound the implementation work

When implementation planning is requested, provide a file manifest with the
operation and actual path. Describe the proposed change and why it is needed:

| Operation | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| CREATE | A new file and its responsibility |
| UPDATE | The exact behavior changed in an existing file |
| DELETE | Identify what replaces the removed file and which consumers change. |
| READ | A source used for design that needs no implementation change |
| MIGRATION | A schema or data transition and its recovery conditions |
| CONFIG | A dependency, environment variable or service setting |

Include affected importers and callers when they need changes or regression
checks. A preliminary manifest is a plan, not a guarantee that investigation
cannot reveal another necessary file. Update it when the implementation scope
changes and surface a material decision. Preserve the user's existing approval
and release boundaries; a file count creates no additional approval gate.

## Persistence completion check

Before delivering a specification that saves records, explicitly state how a later authorized read reloads the durable record and how record ownership and context access are checked. Cover a fresh visit as well as recovery immediately after a timeout. If the existing read path or lifecycle is unknown, name it as an uninspected dependency and specify the observable readback requirement; do not invent a new endpoint or deletion policy as established behavior. Include an acceptance case for that later read, stable identity and denied access. This requirement describes data behavior and does not require a UI mockup.

## Make acceptance executable

For each criterion, name the initiating action and observable result. Specify
the exact verification method. State the expected behavior for the main path and material
failures. A screenshot can prove a rendered state; persistence needs a record
readback or an equivalent test. A schema check cannot prove a complete user task.

Select test and build commands from the current repository's documentation and
package scripts. Do not prescribe npm, TypeScript, Vitest or Next.js when the
project does not use them. Keep a planned verification distinct from a command
that actually ran and a result inspected at the intended destination.

Before delivering, check the specification against the supplied request and
the inspected code. Verify that states, interfaces, data changes, file scope
and criteria agree. Identify a material unresolved decision beside the section
it affects. Ask only for a decision that blocks useful work; continue the
supported portions. Never invent an approval or imply the specification was
implemented.

## Deliver in the requested form

Use the project's existing document or work-item format. A self-contained HTML
specification can embed its styles and assets with rendered mockups. A Markdown,
editable document or issue may suit the task better. Do not introduce a font
CDN or another network dependency into an otherwise self-contained artifact.

Retain supporting notes and evidence when needed for recovery or the user's
verification requirements. Run the applicable shared release checks, including
writing review and visual inspection for a designed document. Implementation
can proceed within the authorization already granted; request a remaining
approval only when the actual project or action requires one.

## Request

Can you write the detailed UI and API spec for the "save repair request as draft" feature described in inputs/brief.md? The code excerpt in inputs/current-code.md is everything I can share from the repo right now.

## Inputs

Run of the built `write-feature-spec` task package in its "detailed UI and API specification" mode. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### brief.md

#### Brief: save repair request as draft (Larchmont Homes resident portal)

Residents report repairs through a four-field form in the portal: category, room, description, preferred access window. Residents on mobile lose the form when the connection drops or the session times out (30 minutes idle). Support logged 41 complaints about this in September (fictional figure, from the support queue).

##### Requested outcome
- A "Save draft" button on the repair form. Saving keeps what the resident typed.
- When the resident comes back (new login, another device), the portal shows "You have a saved repair request" with Resume and Discard.
- Resume refills the form. Submitting the form turns the draft into a normal repair request.
- A resident has at most one draft per tenancy. Residents with two tenancies (e.g. a flat and a garage) can have one draft each.
- Only the resident who wrote the draft, and joint tenants on the same tenancy, may see it. Housing officers must not see drafts.

##### Decisions
- Confirmed: one draft per tenancy; officers cannot see drafts.
- Open: how long drafts are kept. Product owner (Priya Raman) to decide; not yet decided.
- Open: whether joint tenants can both edit at once. No decision.

##### Out of scope
- Photo attachments (separate project).
- Changing how submitted requests are triaged.

##### Note
The new mobile app will call the save endpoint using `tenancy_id` only. The web portal currently identifies the form by `portal_session_id`.

#### current-code.md

#### Code excerpt (Python / FastAPI, Postgres)

```python
# routes/forms.py
@router.post("/api/form-state")
async def save_form_state(body: FormStateIn, user=Depends(current_resident)):
    # body: portal_session_id (str, required), fields (dict)
    session = await sessions.get(body.portal_session_id)
    if session is None or session.resident_id != user.id:
        raise HTTPException(404)
    await db.execute("DELETE FROM form_state WHERE portal_session_id=$1", body.portal_session_id)
    await db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO form_state (id, portal_session_id, fields, updated_at) VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), $1, $2, now())",
        body.portal_session_id, json.dumps(body.fields))
    return {"ok": True}
```

```sql
-- form_state: id uuid pk, portal_session_id text not null, fields jsonb, updated_at timestamptz
-- repair_request: id uuid pk, tenancy_id uuid not null references tenancy(id), resident_id uuid, category text, room text, description text, access_window text, status text, created_at timestamptz
-- tenancy_member: tenancy_id uuid, resident_id uuid, primary key (tenancy_id, resident_id)
-- A cleanup job deletes sessions idle > 30 min; form_state has no FK to sessions.
```

Not supplied: the repair submit route, the current_resident helper, the front-end component, any test setup, and any existing read endpoint for form_state.

## Output

I wrote the specification for saving a repair request as a draft. It is ready for review but not ready to implement. Two decisions are open, and some files weren't supplied. Nothing has been implemented or run.

#### What the code excerpt changed

- **The existing save route can't hold drafts.** `POST /api/form-state` deletes the row and inserts a new one with a new id on every save. It is also keyed by `portal_session_id` with no foreign key, and the session cleanup job removes idle sessions. A draft stored there would become unreachable after the 30-minute timeout, which is the loss the feature must fix. The spec leaves that route untouched and adds a `repair_draft` table keyed by tenancy.
- **The mobile app and the web portal use different identifiers.** The app sends `tenancy_id` only, and the web form sends `portal_session_id`. The new routes take `tenancy_id` as the only context, so the web form must send the tenancy it is showing. A draft can't be moved to another tenancy.
- **Access follows the existing pattern.** A caller who isn't a `tenancy_member` gets 404, as `routes/forms.py` already does. This covers housing officers, who have no membership.

#### Open decisions

| Decision | Owner | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How long drafts are kept | Priya Raman | The spec sets no expiry and no cleanup job. Retention criteria are left out. |
| Whether joint tenants can edit at the same time | Not assigned | The spec proposes an optional `base_revision` check that returns 409 on a stale write. Without a decision, the last write wins. |

#### Gaps in what I could read

The repair submit route, the `current_resident` helper, the front-end component, test setup and any row-level security setup were not supplied. The submit change is therefore specified as behavior only. Submit must create the request and delete the draft in one transaction, and its request contract is left until that route is read. Two file paths in the manifest are marked unknown. I proposed a 2,000-character limit per field; the brief gave none.

#### Key content

**Endpoints** (all need an authenticated tenancy member):

| Method and path | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `PUT /api/tenancies/{tenancy_id}/repair-draft` | 201 on first save, 200 on replace with the same `id` and `revision` +1. 409 on stale `base_revision`, 422 on invalid input, 404 for a non-member, 503 if the database is down. A repeated identical request is safe. |
| `GET /api/tenancies/{tenancy_id}/repair-draft` | 200 with the draft, or `{"draft": null}`. This is the readback for return visits and for an unknown save outcome. |
| `DELETE /api/tenancies/{tenancy_id}/repair-draft` | 204 whether or not a draft existed. |

**Table** (additive): `repair_draft(id, tenancy_id NOT NULL REFERENCES tenancy, author_resident_id, fields jsonb, revision, created_at, updated_at)` with `UNIQUE (tenancy_id)`. Save is an upsert on `tenancy_id`, so the id survives. Rollback is dropping the table, which deletes unsubmitted drafts.

**UI states:** first use, saving, saved, return visit (banner with Resume and Discard), resume, discard confirmation, network failure, validation rejection, expired session and stale draft. After a timeout the UI says "We could not confirm the save. Your text is still here." and keeps the input. Retrying is safe. Status messages go in live regions, the Discard dialog traps focus and returns it to the Discard button, and field errors are tied to their fields.

**Acceptance criteria** (16 in the file). Examples:

- Saving twice gives one row and the same `id`.
- A draft saved before the idle timeout appears on another device after a fresh login, and Resume refills all four fields.
- A non-member and an officer both get 404, and the stored draft is unchanged.
- A resident with two tenancies holds two independent drafts.
- Submitting a resumed form creates the request, and the draft readback then returns null.
- A failed submit leaves the draft in place.
- A keyboard and screen-reader pass covers the save status and the discard dialog.

Retention checks are left out until the owner decides.

#### File

- `out/repair-draft-spec.md` is the full specification. It has the problem and confirmed requirements, code findings, UI states with a wireframe, API contracts, data definition, file manifest, acceptance table and assumptions.

### File: repair-draft-spec.md

#### Save repair request as draft: UI and API specification

Status: ready for review. Not ready to implement until the two open decisions below are settled and the uninspected routes are read.

##### 1. Problem and outcome

Residents filling in the repair form on mobile lose their input when the connection drops or the 30-minute idle session expires. Support logged 41 such complaints in September (figure from the brief, support queue).

Outcome: a resident can save the form, leave, and later resume it from any device, then submit it as a normal repair request.

###### Confirmed requirements (brief)

- A "Save draft" button on the repair form keeps the four fields: category, room, description, access window.
- On return, the portal offers Resume and Discard.
- Submitting a resumed form creates a normal repair request.
- One draft per tenancy. A resident with two tenancies can hold one draft in each.
- Visible only to the author and joint tenants of that tenancy. Housing officers cannot see drafts.

###### Open decisions

| Decision | Owner | Effect on this spec |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How long drafts are kept | Priya Raman (product owner) | Section 5 states no expiry and no cleanup job. Retention criteria stay blank until decided. |
| Whether two joint tenants may edit at the same time | Not assigned | Section 4 proposes a stale-write check. Treat it as a proposal. |

###### Out of scope

Photo attachments, and changes to how submitted requests are triaged.

##### 2. What the supplied code shows

| Finding | Consequence for the design |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/form-state` in `routes/forms.py` deletes the row for the session and inserts a new one with a new `gen_random_uuid()` id on every save. | A draft's id would change on each save, and a failure between the two statements loses the draft. The new feature uses an upsert on a unique key so the id is stable. |
| `form_state` is keyed by `portal_session_id` with no foreign key to sessions. The cleanup job deletes idle sessions. | A draft stored there would be unreachable once its session is gone, which is the exact loss the feature must fix. Drafts need a tenancy key. |
| The route checks `session.resident_id == user.id` and returns 404 otherwise. | The new routes follow this pattern: 404 for a tenancy the caller does not belong to, so existence is not revealed. |
| `tenancy_member (tenancy_id, resident_id)` has a composite primary key. | It is the membership check for author and joint tenants. |
| The mobile app sends `tenancy_id` only. The web portal sends `portal_session_id`. | The draft endpoints take `tenancy_id` as their only context. The web form must send the tenancy it is editing. |

Not supplied and therefore not inspected: the repair submit route, the `current_resident` helper, the front-end form component, test setup, any read path for `form_state`, and whether the database uses row-level security. Each is named where it matters. The existing `/api/form-state` route stays unchanged.

##### 3. UI behavior

Example wording below is illustrative.

###### Wireframe: repair form with a saved draft

```
Report a repair                         Tenancy: Flat 4, 12 Example Row
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| You have a saved repair request (saved 3 Nov, 18:42)         |
| [Resume]  [Discard]                                          |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
Category      [ Heating            v ]
Room          [ Kitchen              ]
Description   [ Radiator will not warm up...                   ]
Access window [ Weekday mornings     ]
              [Save draft]   [Submit request]
```

###### States

| State | Trigger | Visible result | Permitted actions | Next state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First use | Resident opens the form with no draft | Empty form, Save draft enabled once any field has content | Type, Save draft, Submit | Saving, or Submitting |
| Saving | Select Save draft | Button shows "Saving..." and is disabled. Typed input stays editable. | None on the button until the response | Saved, or Save failed |
| Saved | 200 or 201 response | Status line "Draft saved at 18:42", announced politely | Keep editing, Save again, Submit | Populated |
| Return visit | Resident opens the form on any device with a draft for that tenancy | Banner above the form with saved time, Resume, Discard. Form is empty until Resume. | Resume, Discard, or ignore | Populated, or First use |
| Resume | Select Resume | Fields filled from the draft, banner removed, focus moves to the first field | Edit, Save, Submit | Populated |
| Discard | Select Discard | Confirmation dialog "Discard this saved request?" with Discard and Keep. On confirm the draft is deleted and the banner disappears. | Confirm, Keep | First use |
| Save failed (network) | Timeout or no connection | Message "We could not confirm the save. Your text is still here. Try again." Form content stays. | Save draft (retry), Submit | Saving |
| Save rejected | 422 | Field-level messages below the offending fields | Fix and retry | Saving |
| Session expired | 401 | Sign-in prompt that returns to the form. Typed text is kept in the page until sign-in finishes. | Sign in, then Save | Saving |
| Stale draft (proposed) | 409 | Message "This draft was changed by someone else on your tenancy." with Load latest and Keep mine | Choose one | Populated |

Double activation of Save draft while Saving does nothing. If the connection fails after the request left the device, the outcome is unknown. The UI must not claim success or failure; it shows the "could not confirm" message, and a retry is safe because the save is idempotent (section 4). A later page load shows the true state through the return-visit banner.

###### Accessibility

- Save draft, Resume and Discard are native buttons, reachable by Tab in reading order, operable with Enter and Space.
- The saved and failed messages sit in a live region (`role="status"` for saved, `role="alert"` for failed or rejected).
- Field errors are linked to their fields with `aria-describedby`, and focus moves to the first invalid field after a 422.
- The Discard dialog traps focus, closes on Escape, starts focus on Keep, and returns focus to the Discard button on close. After a confirmed discard, focus moves to the Category field.
- The banner has the accessible name "Saved repair request".

The project's own accessibility standard was not supplied; the checks in section 7 apply until it is.

##### 4. API

All routes require an authenticated resident (existing `current_resident` helper, uninspected). Authorization for each: a `tenancy_member` row for (`tenancy_id`, caller). Otherwise 404. Officers hold no membership through their role, so they get 404.

###### `PUT /api/tenancies/{tenancy_id}/repair-draft`

Creates or replaces the draft for the tenancy. Repeating the same request gives the same result.

Request:

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "category": "Heating",
    "room": "Kitchen",
    "description": "Radiator will not warm up",
    "access_window": "Weekday mornings"
  },
  "base_revision": 3
}
```

- `fields`: required object. Each key is optional, string or null. At least one value must be non-empty. Unknown keys are rejected. Maximum length per value: 2,000 characters (proposed; no limit was supplied).
- `base_revision`: optional integer (proposed, covers the open concurrency decision). Omitted means last write wins. If present and not equal to the stored revision, respond 409.

| Status | Body | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 201 | draft object | First save for this tenancy |
| 200 | draft object | Replaced an existing draft. `id` unchanged, `revision` +1 |
| 401 | `{"error":"unauthenticated"}` | No valid session |
| 404 | `{"error":"not_found"}` | Caller is not a member of the tenancy, or the tenancy does not exist |
| 409 | `{"error":"stale_revision","current":<draft object>}` | `base_revision` mismatch |
| 422 | `{"error":"invalid","fields":{"description":"too_long"}}` | Empty, unknown key, or over length |
| 503 | `{"error":"unavailable"}` | Database unavailable. Nothing is partly written. |

Draft object: `{"id","tenancy_id","author_resident_id","fields","revision","updated_at"}`.

###### `GET /api/tenancies/{tenancy_id}/repair-draft`

200 with the draft object, or 200 with `{"draft": null}` when none exists. 401 and 404 as above. This is the readback used on every return visit and after an unknown save outcome.

###### `DELETE /api/tenancies/{tenancy_id}/repair-draft`

204 whether or not a draft existed. 401 and 404 as above.

###### Submit

---
name: start-delivery
description: 'Mobilize a signed engagement: the project charter, RAID and decision logs, internal and client kickoff decks and a Sprint 0 plan, built from the accepted sales-to-delivery handoff and signed SOW. Use when delivery is starting: kick off the project, mobilize the engagement, set up the RAID log, or "the handoff is accepted, what now". # Start delivery

Mobilization is the stage between an accepted handoff and real delivery work. It produces one
signed artifact (the Project Charter), one living system (the governance pack), and two meetings
(internal kickoff, then client kickoff). A weak start compounds: recovering lost efficiency in
weeks one and two can create later rework, so this stage is deliberate,
complete, and standardized rather than improvised per project.

One boundary carries the whole skill: **this skill drafts, humans sign.** It never signs the
charter, never commits the client to a cadence, never closes a handoff open question on its own,
and never provisions an environment. It prepares the artifacts the humans act on, and it tracks
what the humans did, truthfully.

## Project context required

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement, source records, private output location,
and intended audience. Map reference roles such as Program Lead, CSE, Solution Lead,
and Pursuit Lead to that project's authorized owners; these labels do not impose
an employer organization chart or signing authority. The executed agreement and
accepted project plan determine gates, commercial rules, and support obligations.
Keep account history, risk assessments, credentials, and client evidence outside
portable skill sources. A cached account, attached Project, or available connector
is not authorization to read, write, or publish.

## Phase 0: orient on the sources

Find the real objects before writing anything:

1. **The accepted handoff brief.** Its sections (team, stakeholder map with deal-versus-delivery
   mismatches, sell-cycle promises, scope and risks, open questions with owners) are this skill's
   raw material. If no accepted brief exists, stop: the handoff is not done, and that is
   prepare-delivery-handoff's job, not a gap to paper over.
2. **The signed SOW**, with its id and as-of date. The SOW is fixed input. Scope, phases, figures,
   and commercial structure come from it; this skill renders them and authors none of them. Any
   figure ultimately traces to the quote the SOW was built from, per the money rule.
3. **The delivery model.** Detect waterfall or agile from the SOW variant, then confirm with the
   Program Lead or CSE before building anything variant-specific. Detected is not confirmed;
   never assume. Record the confirmation (who, when) in the charter and as a decision log entry.
4. **The shared engagement record**, where one exists. Read what the handoff populated (meta,
   scope_baseline, stakeholders, team, open_questions, gates); write only this stage's sections
   (raid, decisions, artifacts, gates, confirmed team) and log every change.

Stamp everything generated with SOW id and as-of date. Record IDs do not survive sandbox
refreshes; the stamp is what makes an artifact auditable later.

## Phase 1: draft the Project Charter

Read `references/charter-spec.md`, then fill `assets/charter-template.md`. The two rules that
matter most:

- **Scope is the SOW scope restated, never renegotiated.** The charter is where the client
  re-accepts what they signed. When the handoff brief or a transcript shows the client expecting
  something the SOW does not say (or vice versa), that delta becomes a flagged item (F-###) with
  an owner and a resolve-by date before client kickoff. Neither write it into the baseline nor
  silently drop it. If it implies paid work, humans take it to a Change Order conversation.
- **Every section is always present.** A section the sources cannot fill carries a known unknown
  with an owner, a resolve-by date, and the gate it blocks. A blank is an open question, not an
  invitation to invent.

Gate the draft before any human reads it:

```bash
python3 scripts/charter_check.py CHARTER.md
```

It verifies required sections, the scope source stamp (SOW id plus as-of date), a fully assigned
RACI with exactly one Accountable per activity and every team role covered, no leftover
placeholder tokens, and no em dashes. Exit 0 passes. Report the printed counts, not an adjective.
Then run the review-writing checker over the charter prose. Fix the source and re-render; never
hand-patch output the next regeneration would lose.

The Program Lead secures the signature. Mark the charter DRAFT until they do. When the
signature lands, update the engagement's DELIVERY-STATE.md in the same session
(`charter_signed` with date, charter path, append-only dated log line) per
delivery-orchestrator's `references/delivery-state-spec.md`.

## Phase 2: stand up the governance pack

Read `references/governance-pack-spec.md`. Three artifacts from `assets/`: the RAID log, the
decision log, and the weekly status template. This skill creates and seeds them;
track-delivery stewards them from kickoff onward, which is why the ID conventions are a
contract, not a style: R/A/I/D-### for RAID items, DEC-### for decisions, zero-padded, permanent,
append-only. Downstream stewardship diffs these tables by ID; a renumbered log breaks every later
report.

Seeding is the substance: every handoff open question becomes an owned RAID item with a resolve-by
date (letting one vanish is the named failure mode of this stage), handoff risks become R items,
SOW basis-of-estimate assumptions become A items, and evidenced capability gaps from the
supplied project risk profile each get the agreed oversight and a sourced risk.
Every seeded item cites its source. Do not pad the log to look thorough.

Agree with the team where the pack lives before client kickoff, and log that location as a
decision. The decision log records only decisions humans actually made, with the human named.

## Phase 3: kickoff decks

Read `references/kickoff-deck-contracts.md` for what every slide must carry, per deck and per
variant. This skill owns the content contract only. Mechanics are delegated: build-deck runs
the stage-gated build, pptx owns the file format, brand-renderer owns brand tokens and
the visual, parity, and brand gates, review-writing reviews the copy. Do not inline hex values or
restate any of their rules.

Two decks, in order. The **internal kickoff** runs first, always: it is where the Program Lead
leads the risk and gap review off the seeded RAID log, and where the team agrees tools and the
note-keeping location, before the client sees anything. The **client kickoff** ends with explicit
agreement on cadence and the path to charter signature. Both decks are populated from this
engagement's record; a deck reusable on another client unchanged is a failed deck.

Build the confirmed variant only. If the SOW is ambiguous about the model, that is a flagged
delta and a human decision, not a hybrid deck.

## Phase 4: Sprint 0 plan, seeded backlog, research pack

Read `references/sprint0-backlog-seeding.md`. The Sprint 0 plan (mobilization plan on waterfall)
lists every item standing between the charter and productive Analyze work, each with an owner and
a date. The backlog seed is a projection of the SOW scope baseline: one E-### epic per
workstream, stories only where the SOW gives real basis, every item source-cited, no invented
scope, no sizing, no acceptance-criteria authoring (that is Analyze work, owned by
capture-requirements). The client research pack is a two-page sourced extension of the
handoff overview, not pursuit-grade research; a meeting-specific prep pack is prepare-sales-pursuit.
On agile engagements, Sprint 0 ends when `refine-backlog` has graded the first stories and
`plan-sprint` has planned Sprint 1 against measured capacity; both follow
`../_shared/planning-chain.md` and read the RAID log this phase seeds.

## Phase 5: track the operational setup

Sandbox provisioning and access grants are human or system actions. This skill records their
status per environment and per person (provisioned, requested, blocked, verified), flags blockers
as RAID items, and prompts the Program Lead on what is stuck. It never performs the setup and
never marks anything ready that nobody verified. Claiming unverified sandbox readiness is a named
failure mode; track real status only.

## Durable output

Every run leaves a Markdown record per `_shared/output-contract.md`. On a full
mobilization that record is the charter draft plus the seeded governance pack;
on a partial or headless run it is a run record carrying the gate counts, the
flagged deltas, and the human actions still outstanding. Deliver or link the
files; never just say they were written.

## Governance delegation

- **evidence-core** governs load-bearing factual claims (client context, stakeholder
  facts, sell-cycle promises). Run it before drafting where installed. If a load-bearing domain is
  insufficient, produce the readiness-gap memo and stop; a full charter on insufficient evidence
  is a hard fail.
- **brand-renderer** owns brand for every rendered artifact, applied during the build.
- **review-writing** owns writing review; run its bundled diagnostics on every prose deliverable, including the charter.
- **The quote and SOW own every number.** This skill renders figures and authors none.

Where a governor is not installed on the current surface, state the check it would have run, do
the best manual substitute, and say that is what happened. Never silently skip, never pretend.

## Running unattended

Phase 0's variant confirmation, the charter signature, cadence agreement, and both kickoff
meetings need humans. On a scheduled or headless run: draft the charter, run the gate, seed the
governance pack, and stop with findings and open items. Never record a confirmation, agreement,
or signature nobody gave.

## When time is short

Cut in this order, and say what was cut: (1) the client research pack, (2) the internal deck's
client-context depth, keep the risk and gap slide, (3) backlog stories, keep the epics. Never
cut: the charter gate, RAID seeding from handoff open questions, flagged deltas, source citations,
or the internal-before-client kickoff order.

## Boundaries

In the delivery chain (SOW, then prepare-delivery-handoff, then kickoff, then status, then
UAT, then manage-cutover-closeout), this skill's upstream producer is
prepare-delivery-handoff, whose accepted brief is the raw material, and its
downstream consumer is track-delivery, which stewards the logs this
stage seeds. Kickoff does not re-scope: the SOW baseline is restated, never
renegotiated, and every delta is a flag for humans.

- Does not run the handoff or write the handoff brief; that is prepare-delivery-handoff.
- Does not steward status, RAID, or decisions after kickoff; that is track-delivery,
  which takes over the exact files this skill seeds.
- Does not capture requirements or author acceptance criteria; that is
  capture-requirements, in Analyze.
- Does not scope, price, or amend scope. The SOW is fixed input; deltas are flags for humans.
- Does not sign, approve, or gate. It drafts what humans sign and tracks what humans did.
- Does not provision sandboxes or grant access; it tracks them.
- Does not build deck files itself; build-deck, pptx, and brand-renderer do.

## Files

- `references/charter-spec.md` charter section spec and the scope-restatement rules.
- `references/governance-pack-spec.md` governance templates, stable-ID contract, seeding rules.
- `references/kickoff-deck-contracts.md` slide-by-slide content contracts, both decks, both variants.
- `references/sprint0-backlog-seeding.md` Sprint 0 checklist, backlog seeding rules, research pack.
- `assets/charter-template.md`, `assets/raid-log-template.md`, `assets/decision-log-template.md`,
  `assets/status-report-template.md` the shells to fill; content, not structure.
- `scripts/charter_check.py` the charter gate. Stdlib only; exits nonzero on failure.
- `scripts/charter_check_selftest.py` runs the gate against `scripts/fixtures/` (one passing
  charter, five shipped failing ones, plus an em-dash case synthesized at runtime so the shipped
  tree itself stays em-dash free). Run it after any change to the gate.

skills.excerptHtml:
Mobilization is the stage between an accepted handoff and real delivery work. It produces one signed artifact (the Project Charter), one living system (the governance pack), and two meetings (internal kickoff, then client kickoff). A weak start compounds: recovering lost efficiency in weeks one and two can create later rework, so this stage is deliberate, complete, and standardized rather than improvised per project.

One boundary carries the whole skill: this skill drafts, humans sign. It never signs the charter, never commits the client to a cadence, never closes a handoff open question on its own, and never provisions an environment. It prepares the artifacts the humans act on, and it tracks what the humans did, truthfully.

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement, source records, private output location, and intended audience. Map reference roles such as Program Lead, CSE, Solution Lead, and Pursuit Lead to that project's authorized owners; these labels do not impose an employer organization chart or signing authority. The executed agreement and accepted project plan determine gates, commercial rules, and support obligations. Keep account history, risk assessments, credentials, and client evidence outside portable skill sources. A cached account, attached Project, or available connector is not authorization to read, write, or publish.
