examples.title: Mobilizing a housing repairs portal engagement from an accepted handoff
examples.markdown:
## Request

The handoff for the Brackenfield repairs portal has been accepted and the SOW is signed. Please mobilize the engagement: draft the project charter and seed the RAID and decision logs from the attached handoff brief and SOW extract. Internal kickoff is next week.

## Inputs

Run of the built `start-delivery` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### handoff-brief.md

#### Accepted handoff brief: Brackenfield Housing Association (accepted 2026-10-28)

**Company.** Brackenfield Housing Association manages about 6,800 social homes. Revenue is rent and service charges. Repairs are taken by phone and logged in a legacy spreadsheet-and-database tool; tenants complain they cannot see repair status.

**Team.** CSE Priya Raman (20%). Program Lead Tomas Weber (50%). Solution Lead Ines Okafor (60%).

**Stakeholders.** Executive sponsor Gareth Lindqvist (Chief Operating Officer) led the deal but will not attend delivery meetings; he delegated day-to-day to Hana Mbeki (Head of Customer Services, product owner). IT is one person, Sam Adeyemi (IT Manager), who also administers the Fieldline contractor scheduler.

**Sell-cycle promises.**
- Gareth, 2026-09-18 call: "Tenants will get text reminders before every repair visit."
- Priya to Hana, 2026-09-30 email: "Go-live before the January winter-repairs peak."

**Scope and risks.**
- Fieldline scheduler integration depends on a vendor API key that Sam has not yet requested.
- Sam is the only person who can grant Fieldline and legacy database access (single point of failure).
- Legacy repair data quality is unknown; Hana expects "some duplicates".

**Open questions.**
1. Who owns the legacy repair data and signs off the migration mapping? (Priya, raised in discovery; no date)
2. Has the Fieldline vendor confirmed API access on Brackenfield's licence tier? (Tomas)
3. Will Gareth attend steering committees, or does Hana hold his proxy? (Priya)
4. Where will project notes and documents live? (no owner)

**Risk profile note.** Brackenfield has not run a data migration or vendor API integration before (self-reported by Sam, discovery call 2026-09-22). Agreed oversight: Solution Lead reviews the mapping and API test results.

#### sow-extract.md

#### SOW extract: SOW-BHA-2026-014 (Waterfall variant), signed 2026-10-12

Client: Brackenfield Housing Association. Delivery: Cobalt Ridge Consulting. Engagement: Repairs Portal. Start 2026-11-16, 20 weeks, fixed fee.

##### 2. Scope
1. **Repairs case management.** Case records, triage rules and status workflow for repair requests. Tested by UAT scripts agreed in Analyze.
2. **Tenant self-service portal.** Tenants log in, report a repair and view its status. Tested by UAT scripts.
3. **Fieldline integration.** One integration that sends appointments to Fieldline and receives completion status. Tested by an end-to-end test in the sandbox.
4. **Data migration.** Repair history for the last 3 years (basis of estimate: about 42,000 records) loaded once. Tested by reconciliation counts signed by the client.

##### 4. Exclusions
4.1 Contractor mobile app. 4.2 Migration of records older than 3 years. 4.3 SMS or email notifications to tenants. 4.4 Integration with the rent accounts system. 4.5 Training beyond two sessions.

##### Exhibit A: basis of estimate
A1: legacy data is in one database with a documented schema. A2: Brackenfield provides Fieldline API credentials by Analyze week 1. A3: client reviewers return deliverables within 5 working days.

##### Phases (weeks)
Mobilize 1-2 (gate: Charter signed). Analyze 3-6 (Requirements co-signed). Design 7-9 (Design co-signed). Build 10-15 (Build complete in sandbox). Validate 16-18 (Go/no-go). Deploy 19-20 (Go-Live Acceptance).

## Output

### Repairs Portal: charter draft and governance pack ready for internal kickoff

I've drafted the Project Charter and seeded the RAID log and decision log from the accepted handoff brief (2026-10-28) and SOW-BHA-2026-014 (signed 2026-10-12). The charter is marked DRAFT. Nobody has signed it and nobody has confirmed anything, so the file records no confirmations.

#### Two things to settle before client kickoff

1. **F-001: text reminders.** Gareth Lindqvist told the team on 2026-09-18 that "tenants will get text reminders before every repair visit." SOW clause 4.3 excludes SMS and email notifications. I did not add it to the baseline or drop it. Priya Raman owns it, due 2026-11-12. If the client wants it, that is a Change Order conversation for the humans.
2. **F-002: go-live date.** Priya told Hana Mbeki on 2026-09-30 that go-live would come before the January winter peak. A 2026-11-16 start with 20 weeks puts Deploy in weeks 19 and 20, ending 2027-04-02. Same owner and date. R-006 is its companion risk.

#### What was produced

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `out/project-charter-DRAFT.md` | Nine-section charter, scope restated from the SOW with its source stamp, 2 flagged deltas, RACI, proposed cadence, phase plan |
| `out/raid-log.md` | 6 risks, 6 assumptions, 0 issues, 5 dependencies, each with owner, date, gate blocked and source |
| `out/decision-log.md` | Opened with no rows, because no named person has made a decision yet |
| `out/mobilization-plan-and-backlog-seed.md` | Nine-item mobilization plan with owners and dates, sandbox and access tracker, four epics and two discovery stories |

#### Charter key content

- **Engagement:** Brackenfield Housing Association, Repairs Portal, fixed fee, start 2026-11-16, 20 weeks, waterfall.
- **In scope:** repairs case management; tenant self-service portal; one Fieldline integration; one-time migration of 3 years of repair history (about 42,000 records).
- **Out of scope (clauses 4.1 to 4.5):** contractor mobile app; records older than 3 years; SMS or email notifications; rent accounts integration; training beyond two sessions.
- **Team:** Priya Raman (CSE, 20%), Tomas Weber (Program Lead, 50%), Ines Okafor (Solution Lead, 60%). Client side: Gareth Lindqvist (sponsor), Hana Mbeki (product owner), Sam Adeyemi (IT).
- **Phases:** Mobilize weeks 1-2, Analyze 3-6, Design 7-9, Build 10-15, Validate 16-18, Deploy 19-20, each with its SOW exit gate.
- **Cadence (proposed, not agreed):** weekly status on Thursdays, monthly steering, demo and gate review at each phase boundary.

#### RAID seeding

All four handoff open questions became owned items:

| Handoff open question | RAID item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Legacy data owner | D-003 | Priya Raman | 2026-11-12 (the brief gave no date) |
| 2. Fieldline API on the licence tier | D-001 | Tomas Weber | 2026-11-12 |
| 3. Sponsor attendance and proxy | R-001 | Priya Raman | 2026-11-12 |
| 4. Where documents live | A-001 | Tomas Weber (default, brief had no owner) | 2026-11-12 |

The rest came from the brief and SOW:
- **Handoff risks:** R-002 (Sam Adeyemi as single point of failure) and R-003 (unknown data quality).
- **Capability gap:** R-004, no prior migration or API integration experience, from the self-reported discovery call, with the agreed oversight of the Solution Lead reviewing the mapping and API tests.
- **Flagged deltas:** R-005 and R-006.
- **SOW basis of estimate:** A-003 to A-006.
- **Mobilization gaps:** D-002 (the API key has not been requested), D-004 (sandbox) and D-005 (charter signatory).

#### Gate results

`charter_check.py` can't run in this session, so I applied its six checks by hand against the saved file. This is a manual read, not a script run. Please run the script before anyone signs.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| required-sections | Pass: 9 of 9 present |
| scope-stamp | Pass: `Source: SOW SOW-BHA-2026-014, as of 2026-10-12` |
| raci-filled | Pass: 9 activities, every cell filled, one Accountable each |
| raci-coverage | Pass: CSE, Program Lead and Solution Lead all appear |
| placeholders | Pass: 0 template tokens, TBD or TODO |
| em-dash | Pass: 0 found |

The review-writing checker is also unavailable here. I did a manual read of the prose for filler and forced contrasts instead.

#### Assumptions and gaps

- **Delivery model not confirmed.** Waterfall comes from the SOW variant. The charter says so and A-002 tracks it. Tomas or Priya needs to confirm it, and the confirmation then goes into the decision log as DEC-001.
- **Evidence-core is not installed.** The manual substitute is that every charter fact traces to the two inputs, with the source in each row.
- **Dates are proposals.** The 2026-11-12 resolve-by date is my default of "before client kickoff", and the week-of-2026-11-09 internal kickoff is taken from your "next week". Week-start dates are plain calendar arithmetic with no holiday adjustment.
- **No signatory names.** Neither party's signatory appears in the inputs, so the sign-off blocks are empty and D-005 tracks the client's.
- **Sandbox and access are unverified.** The tracker marks nothing ready, because no source shows any provisioning.
- **Decks and research pack not built.** Both kickoff decks go through build-deck, and I have not made them. The content contract is ready: the internal deck should lead with R-001 to R-006 and F-001 and F-002. The client research pack was left out as the first item to cut. The client deck's risk slide should show the client-safe subset only.

#### Needs a human next

1. Tomas or Priya confirms the delivery model.
2. The team agrees the document location at internal kickoff.
3. Priya resolves F-001 and F-002 with the client before 2026-11-12.
4. Tomas secures the charter signature, targeted at the end of Mobilize week 2 (2026-11-27). Once it lands, `charter_signed` is recorded in DELIVERY-STATE.md.

### File: decision-log.md

#### Decision log: Repairs Portal (SOW-BHA-2026-014)

Opened at Mobilize by start-delivery, as of 2026-11-04.
Stewarded from here by track-delivery. IDs are permanent: never renumber, never reuse.

ID convention: DEC-### in creation order, zero-padded to three digits. DEC, not D, so decision IDs
never collide with the RAID log's dependency IDs.

A decision is logged when a human makes it, with the human named in Made by. This log records
decisions; it never contains a decision an agent made on the humans' behalf. A pending decision is
an open question in the RAID log (usually an A or D item), not a pre-filled row here.

Status values: Proposed, Decided, Superseded. A superseded decision keeps its row; the new row
names the old ID in Supersedes.

No decision has been made by a named person as of 2026-11-04. The three expected first entries are
tracked as open RAID items: delivery model confirmation (A-002), document location (A-001), and
cadence (proposed in the charter, agreed at client kickoff).

| ID | Decision | Date | Made by | Rationale | Options considered | Source | Status | Supersedes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### File: mobilization-plan-and-backlog-seed.md

#### Mobilization plan and backlog seed: Repairs Portal (SOW-BHA-2026-014, as of 2026-10-12)

Waterfall engagement, so Sprint 0 content is the mobilization plan. Dates are proposed; none is agreed.

##### Mobilization plan

| # | Item | Owner | Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm waterfall and record the confirmation as a DEC entry (A-002) | Tomas Weber | 2026-11-10 | Not started |
| 2 | Hold internal kickoff, with the risk and gap review off the RAID log | Tomas Weber | Week of 2026-11-09 | Not scheduled |
| 3 | Agree where documents live; log as a DEC entry (A-001) | Tomas Weber | 2026-11-12 | Not started |
| 4 | Disposition F-001 and F-002 with the client sponsor before client kickoff | Priya Raman | 2026-11-12 | Not started |
| 5 | Confirm sponsor proxy, data owner and charter signatory (R-001, D-003, D-005) | Priya Raman | 2026-11-12 | Not started |

guide.what: Turn discovery calls and interview notes into sourced research findings.

skills.markdown:
---
name: synthesize-discovery
description: 'Synthesize supplied discovery calls, interview notes, transcripts or Granola and Fathom exports into sourced findings: job statements, pain points with severity, exact verbatims, speaker-attributed insights, a TL;DR, open questions and next steps. Use when the user shares meeting content and asks what was learned, to pull insights from a transcript, map pain points or extract JTBDs. For the deal discovery record, ranked ledger or open questions, select the maintain pursuit findings mode and read maintain-discovery-record.'
---


# Synthesize discovery

## Caller context and source boundary

Use only the current task's supplied or explicitly authorized account, project sources and destinations. Resolve record names such as `client.profile` within that confirmed context; they are logical slots, not a default personal store. Connector availability alone does not authorize searching another account. Organization-specific pricing, capability catalogs, approval roles and policies must be supplied or confirmed; absent material context remains an explicit gap. Keep reusable package files immutable during a client task and save client records outside them. Never populate an example with private source material.


> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [`readout-brief.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/readout-brief.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

Turn discovery calls into sourced research findings for the current project. Use its industry, participants and terminology.

## Boundary with the discovery brief

This skill is the synthesis pass: raw call content in, sourced findings out. The
maintain pursuit findings mode uses [maintain-discovery-record](../maintain-discovery-record/SKILL.md),
which owns the deal's ranked two-column ledger, its open questions and the feed
into the pursuit brief. Select that complete workflow when the request is to
update the deal's structured record or ask what is still unknown about the
account. A synthesis can supply new findings to that ledger; it does not replace
it. The portable Discovery package embeds both workflows; no separate installation
is needed for the ledger mode.

## Supported input types

| Input type | How to handle |
|---|---|
| Pasted text or typed notes | Use directly |
| Uploaded .txt or .md | Read the file contents |
| Uploaded .docx | Use the `docx` skill to extract text first. Find it in your available skills; do not assume a path. |
| Uploaded .pdf | Use the `pdf` skill to extract text first. Find it in your available skills; do not assume a path. |
| Granola transcript | Pull it through the Granola MCP connector (`get_meeting_transcript`, `list_meetings`). There is no Granola skill. |
| Fathom transcript | Ask the user to paste or export the transcript |
| Audio or video file | Direct audio processing is not supported. Ask for a transcript or a Granola or Fathom export. |

## Workflow

1. Confirm the client, meeting type, who attended on each side and any known focus area. Infer what the content makes obvious and ask once for the rest. When the user wants speed, proceed and state the assumptions at the top.
2. Read the supplied content completely. A summary is secondary evidence and cannot become a verbatim transcript. Keep uncertain speaker labels uncertain.
3. Separate client voices from consulting-team voices. Client statements are the research signal; consultant questions are context.
4. Record each finding with its source location and speaker role. Keep one person's observation distinct from a pattern several people share, and retain meaningful dissent.
5. Rate severity from the source wording. Blocking, repeated or urgent statements are high. Frustration without a block is medium. A single vague mention is low. State the reason for each rating.
6. Write the output in the format and length the user asked for. Without a narrower request, cover the sections below in plain headings.
7. Run the release gate.

## What the synthesis covers

The TL;DR gives the core problem, the most urgent pain and the largest opportunity in two to four sentences, with the session details it draws on.

Job statements use *When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [outcome].* Write a job statement only where the source shows the outcome the client wants. Cite the signal and the speaker role for each one. `frame-jobs-to-be-done` holds the bar these statements must meet.

Pain points state what was said in plain language, with severity, frequency, evidence and speaker role. Describe the problem; recommendations belong elsewhere.

Opportunity areas are the team's inference from the pain points and job statements. Label them as proposed and link each one to the findings it rests on.

Verbatims are exact quotations from client speakers. Preserve the exact words and grammar of a quote with its speaker and timestamp or source location. Never invent a representative quote. Label a paraphrase as a paraphrase outside quotation marks. Select only useful quotes present in the source, even when there are few. Include a consultant quote only when it provoked a revealing client response.

Speaker-attributed insights describe each distinct client voice: apparent priorities, key concerns and influence signals, each tied to what the person said.

Open questions and next steps name what the session left unconfirmed, the follow-up that would answer it and the responsible project role when the source identifies one; otherwise leave ownership open. Send questions that belong to the deal record to the maintain pursuit findings mode.

Gaps and assumptions list information the analysis needed but the source did not contain. When the transcript is thin, say so instead of padding with weak inferences.

## Output delivery

Render the synthesis in Markdown in chat. Save a Markdown file in the project's existing output folder when files can be saved; otherwise provide the complete content in chat. When the user asks for a Word document, use the `docx` skill from your available skills and save it beside the Markdown file. Link saved files through the host's supported file-link mechanism.

A local save does not upload a file to NotebookLM or a Claude Project. Upload only to an authorized destination the user requests, and read back the saved record before claiming it is available there. When the project has a confirmed assessment framework, connect opportunity areas to it.

## Release gate (required)

Before you deliver, run the gate. This is a required step, not a suggestion. Full
spec in [`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md).

1. Apply review-writing to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For
   a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires.
2. Run review-deliverable before you call it final.

Do not present the artifact as finished until both checks have passed.

examples.title: Insurance claims intake: findings from two discovery calls
examples.markdown:
## Request

I've attached notes from two discovery calls with Fernbrook Mutual's claims team for our intake-redesign project. Can you synthesise them into findings for the steering readout on Friday? Keep any quotes exactly as spoken.

## Inputs

Run of the built `synthesize-discovery` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### call-1-claims-ops.md

#### Call 1: Claims operations lead (2026-10-20, 45 min, transcript excerpts)

Attendees: Priya Raman (Head of Claims Operations, Fernbrook Mutual); Dana Whitlock (consultant lead); Leo Marsh (consultant analyst).

[02:10] Dana: Walk us through what happens when a claim comes in.
[02:40] Priya: "Claims arrive by phone, the web form and email, and each one lands in a different queue. Somebody has to retype the email ones by hand."
[06:15] Priya: "We miss our own five-day first-contact target on about a third of claims. I'd have to pull the exact figure, but it's a third, give or take." (Priya's estimate; no report supplied.)
[11:30] Dana: What stops you fixing it?
[11:50] Priya: "The policy system is the blocker. Anything that touches it needs a change request, and the queue for those is months long."
[19:05] Priya: "I don't need a fancy portal. I need the adjusters to stop chasing missing photos."
[27:20] Priya: "Our fraud team would hate anything that auto-approves small claims. I'd want them in the room before we talk about it."
[38:00] Leo: Would a status page for customers help?
[38:20] Priya: "Maybe. Honestly the phone volume is the thing my director watches."

#### call-2-adjuster.md

#### Call 2: Senior adjuster (2026-10-22, 30 min, transcript excerpts)

Attendees: Tomas Okafor (Senior Claims Adjuster, Fernbrook Mutual); Leo Marsh (consultant analyst).

[01:45] Tomas: "Half my morning is emailing people for photos they already sent to a different address."
[05:10] Leo: How often do you have to re-request?
[05:25] Tomas: "Most water-damage claims. Maybe seven in ten. I haven't counted."
[09:40] Tomas: "The web form lets people submit with no photos at all. I raised it with IT last spring and was told it's tied to the policy system."
[14:00] Tomas: "I'd actually be fine with auto-approving the small ones. Under five hundred, the fraud rate is tiny." (Tomas's view; no fraud data supplied.)
[21:30] Tomas: "Customers ring me directly because the main line has no answers for them."
[26:00] Leo: Is there a shared view of claim status?
[26:10] Tomas: "No. I keep my own spreadsheet."

## Output

I've synthesised both calls into findings for Friday's steering readout. Pain points 1 and 2 are the strongest, because both people raised them. Every figure is a spoken estimate with no report behind it, so don't present them as measured.

**Assumptions:** the audience is the steering group. The inputs are transcript excerpts, so I treated anything outside them as unknown. Granola and Fathom were not used.

#### TL;DR

Claims arrive by phone, web form and email, and each channel feeds a separate queue. The web form accepts claims without photos, so adjusters spend their time asking for photos, and customers phone adjusters because the main line has no status to give. Priya Raman (Head of Claims Operations) says the policy system blocks changes. Tomas Okafor (Senior Claims Adjuster) was told the same about the web form. They disagree on auto-approving small claims.

#### Pain points

| # | Pain point | Severity | Frequency | Evidence | Speaker |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Adjusters chase missing or misrouted photos | High | Daily; about 7 in 10 water-damage claims (Tomas's estimate, not counted) | [19:05] call 1; [01:45], [05:25] call 2 | Ops lead and adjuster |
| 2 | Policy-system changes wait in a months-long queue | High | Ongoing | [11:50] call 1; [09:40] call 2 | Ops lead and adjuster |
| 3 | Three channels, separate queues, email claims retyped | Medium | Not stated | [02:40] call 1 | Ops lead |
| 4 | About a third of claims miss the five-day first-contact target | Medium | Priya's estimate; exact figure not pulled | [06:15] call 1 | Ops lead |
| 5 | No shared claim status; customers phone adjusters | Medium | Not stated | [21:30], [26:10] call 2 | Adjuster |

Reasons: 1 and 2 are high because two people raised them independently and the policy system is called a blocker. 3 is a stated frustration, not a block. 4 is an unverified estimate from one person. 5 comes from one speaker.

#### Job statement

Only one is supported by the sources: When a claim arrives without the photos needed to assess it, I want the missing items identified before an adjuster opens the file, so I can start assessment without a round of email requests. (Operations lead and adjuster, [19:05] call 1, [01:45] call 2.) No customer job is written, since no customer was interviewed.

#### Opportunity areas (proposed, not client requests)

1. Require photos at web-form submission for claim types that need them (pain point 1). Feasibility is unconfirmed because of the policy-system tie.
2. Route email and phone claims into one intake queue (pain point 3).
3. Give customers and the main line a claim status view (pain point 5). Priya was lukewarm, so it needs a link to phone volume.
4. Establish whether items 1 to 3 can avoid the policy system (pain point 2).

#### Verbatims

- "Claims arrive by phone, the web form and email, and each one lands in a different queue. Somebody has to retype the email ones by hand." Priya Raman, [02:40] call 1
- "We miss our own five-day first-contact target on about a third of claims. I'd have to pull the exact figure, but it's a third, give or take." Priya Raman, [06:15] call 1
- "The policy system is the blocker. Anything that touches it needs a change request, and the queue for those is months long." Priya Raman, [11:50] call 1
- "I don't need a fancy portal. I need the adjusters to stop chasing missing photos." Priya Raman, [19:05] call 1
- "Half my morning is emailing people for photos they already sent to a different address." Tomas Okafor, [01:45] call 2
- "The web form lets people submit with no photos at all. I raised it with IT last spring and was told it's tied to the policy system." Tomas Okafor, [09:40] call 2
- "Customers ring me directly because the main line has no answers for them." Tomas Okafor, [21:30] call 2

#### Speaker insights

**Priya Raman.** Priority is less adjuster rework, not a portal. She sees the policy system as the constraint, wants the fraud team involved before auto-approval is discussed, and says her director watches phone volume ([38:20]).

**Tomas Okafor.** Concerned with daily rework and direct customer calls. He keeps his own status spreadsheet ([26:10]) and has already tried to get the form changed through IT. He is open to auto-approving small claims.

#### Where they differ

Priya: "Our fraud team would hate anything that auto-approves small claims. I'd want them in the room before we talk about it." [27:20]. Tomas: "I'd actually be fine with auto-approving the small ones. Under five hundred, the fraud rate is tiny." [14:00]. His fraud-rate claim is a view without data. Her claim about the fraud team is an expectation, since that team wasn't interviewed.

#### Open questions and next steps

| Question | Follow-up | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Real first-contact miss rate? | Request the first-contact report | Open |
| Photo re-request rate by claim type? | Sample claim files or email logs | Open |
| Can the web form change without a policy-system change? | Ask IT what ties them and the queue length | Open |
| Fraud team view and fraud rate under 500? | Interview the fraud team before presenting options | Open |
| What does Priya's director measure? | Ask Priya for phone-volume figures and target | Priya Raman, if she agrees |

No project owners are named in the sources, so ownership is open. If you keep a pursuit ledger, I can pass these questions to the maintain-discovery-record workflow.

#### Gaps

- Both sources are excerpts; other speakers and unquoted moments are unknown.
- No customer, IT or fraud voices. Findings 2 and 5 rest on one or two internal speakers.
- "About a third" and "seven in ten" are spoken estimates.
- "Under five hundred" has no currency stated.

#### Checks and limits

I could not run the bundled scripts (brand preflight, prose and writing checks, quality gate). I did a manual reading pass for the writing standard and checked each quote against the source text. No receipt exists, so treat this as a draft for your review, not a gate-passed final. I used no brand profile and saved a Markdown file only; there is no Word version.

#### Files

- `out/synthesize-discovery.md`: the full synthesis above, with the fuller wording of the speaker insights and gaps.
- `out/answer.md`: this reply.

She is wary of the policy system as a constraint ([11:50]) and of the fraud team's reaction to auto-approval ([27:20]), which suggests she wants stakeholders involved before options are proposed. She names her director as the audience for phone volume ([38:20]), which signals who her measures of success answer to.

Tomas Okafor, Senior Claims Adjuster. He is concerned with daily rework and with customers calling him directly. He keeps his own status spreadsheet ([26:10]) and has already tried to get the form changed through IT. He is open to auto-approval of small claims ([14:00]) and speaks for adjusters only, not for fraud.

Where the speakers differ

Auto-approval of small claims is contested. Priya: "Our fraud team would hate anything that auto-approves small claims. I'd want them in the room before we talk about it." [27:20]. Tomas: "I'd actually be fine with auto-approving the small ones. Under five hundred, the fraud rate is tiny." [14:00]. Tomas's claim about the fraud rate is his view, and no fraud data was supplied. Priya's claim about the fraud team is her expectation, since the fraud team was not interviewed.

Open questions and next steps
QuestionFollow-upOwner
What is the real first-contact miss rate?Request the first-contact report Priya mentionedOpen
How often are photos re-requested, by claim type?Request a sample of claim files or email logs to check the "seven in ten" estimateOpen
Can the web form change without a policy-system change?Ask IT what ties the form to the policy system and what the current queue length isOpen
What does the fraud team think about small-claim auto-approval, and what is the fraud rate under 500?Interview the fraud team before any option is presentedOpen
What does Priya's director measure?Ask Priya for the phone-volume figures and targetPriya Raman, if she agrees

The source names no project owners, so ownership is left open.

Gaps and assumptions
  • Both sources are excerpts. Anything not in the excerpts is unknown, including other speakers and what was said between timestamps.
  • No customer, IT or fraud-team voices are included. Findings 2 and 5 rest on one or two internal speakers.
  • Every figure is a spoken estimate: "about a third" and "seven in ten". None has a report behind it. Do not show them in the readout as measured.
  • The meaning of "small claims" is Tomas's "under five hundred", with no currency given.
  • Assumed: the readout audience is the project steering group, and plain headings are acceptable.

skills.markdown:
---
name: tailor-resume
description: "Wording method for the candidate's tailored resume copy under prepare-job-application tailor: stated and estimated figures, rounding, posting keyword placement, bullet shape, ATS layout."
---


# Tailor resume

Use only the candidate identity, career records, thresholds, author profile and destinations explicitly supplied or authorized for this task. Record names below describe a suggested source map; resolve them under the confirmed career root or accept equivalent supplied records. None is a bundled personal default. Missing optional context does not block a bounded draft from supplied facts.

This skill supplies the wording method that `prepare-job-application` tailor step 11 leaves open. It does not choose the master, select programs or decide claims; those come from `00_Master/Career_Application_Operating_Context.md` and the role's `Role_Work_Record.md`, whose narrative translation table must be complete. If it is empty, stop and run `prepare-job-application tailor` first.

Before writing, load the operating context, the role work record, the master copy in the role folder, the live posting (if it is down, the record's posting snapshot, and say so), and `00_Master/Career_Narrative_Translation_Guide.md`. Claim authority starts with the candidate’s corrections and confirmed facts, then original evidence and the claim ledger, then detailed program records. The professional profile is a summary for navigation. Portfolio case studies are public copies and never a source for a resume figure.

Before combining facts in a bullet, verify that the source explicitly connects the actor, work, figure and period. Separate records for a team activity and a candidate's platform experience do not establish that the candidate led that activity or that it used that platform. An unnamed team's count stays off the candidate's bullet until ownership is supported.

Paths such as `00_Master/`, `03_Tracker/` and `06_System/` name records under the user's confirmed Career root; they are not relative to the installed skill directory. Resolve needed records to absolute paths from that confirmed root. The packaged checker is a separate executable resource, linked in the final step below.

## Two classes of figure

- Stated: an exact figure in the supplied professional profile, program record or evidence ledger. Preserve its unit, scope, period and precision. If the candidate requests rounding, document the convention and keep the exact source figure. Synthetic illustration: 78 completed test cases may be written as “about 80” only when that level of precision fits the claim.
- Estimate: a figure calculated from supplied inputs such as counts, frequencies, durations, deal sizes, before-and-after timings, totals and attributable share. Use an estimate only when the candidate wants it and the basis is defensible.

## Building an estimate

- Write the inputs and the arithmetic. Shapes: a range ("$1M–$2M deal values"), a bound ("20+ enterprise pursuits"), a share of a stated total ("about half of the synthetic $120K total"), frequency times period (5 workshops a month across 2025 → "about 60"), before and after with the baseline ("from about two weeks to half a day").
- Round to the nearest natural figure (nearest 5, 10, half or whole). When the arithmetic lands exactly between, keep the raw figure. Do not shade down for modesty or up for effect. For the chosen increment, calculate the adjacent lower and upper values and compare their distances from the raw figure. A supported 23 rounds to about 25 at an increment of five: distances are 3 and 2; the midpoint is 22.5. Keep the original unit and period. This changes presentation, not the source figure, and is not a new estimate.
- Signal the estimate with one word inside the number: about, roughly, ~, +, or a range.
- A ledger qualifier on a figure is handled first by replacement with the verified result (for example, replacing a forecast with the supplied confirmed result) and otherwise as one word inside the number ("a reported ~40%"). Never a clause, parenthetical or second sentence.
- Missing inputs: ask the candidate one question for that bullet ("roughly how many pursuits a quarter?") and leave the bullet unnumbered until the candidate answers.
- Record every estimate in the role work record under a new section `## Estimate basis`, placed after `## Resume source review`: bullet, figure, inputs, arithmetic, rounding. The readiness checker parses only the source review section, so the new section does not affect it. A figure reused on a second surface (LinkedIn, letter, interview) is promoted to the evidence ledger in a separate, explicit step; `draft-application-materials` reads estimates from this section and makes none of its own.

## What belongs on the resume

- In: scale and outcome figures — dollars, portfolio size, cycles, attendees, time saved, contract value, deals, pipeline.
- Exclude counts the candidate or rights ledger prohibits. Inventory counts can describe scale when they matter to the role, but must not stand in for a supported outcome.
- When people leadership is relevant, state responsibilities and headcount only when evidence and disclosure authority support them.
- Prefer the figures that explain scope and outcome. Do not invent a ratio merely to compress several unrelated counts.

## Keywords

Use supported language from the posting where it helps the hiring reader recognize relevant work.

- Extract in four groups: role identity (title nouns, function); platforms and methods (Salesforce Revenue Cloud, CPQ, Billing, quote-to-cash, Agentforce, integration, named AI tooling); outcomes the posting measures (adoption, cycle time, platform roadmap, budget); leadership verbs the posting repeats. A term is critical when it is in the title, the first three responsibilities, or repeated.
- Map each keyword to the evidence line where it is true. No evidence → a gap in the role work record for the letter or interview, and off the resume. Never add a tool, certification or title the candidate does not hold.
- Headline and profile: describe the supported work that fits the role. Include platform names where they help the reader understand that work; no platform count or leadership verb is required.
- Expertise line: the posting's exact phrasing for things the candidate has done.
- Bullets: the keyword that names the work, in the most recent instance; rewrite around it only when the sentence stays accurate.
- Use relevant posting terms naturally where supported. Review omissions and excess repetition; no keyword frequency is prescribed.
- Synonym precedence: the posting's term in the expertise line, the candidate’s term once elsewhere, never both in one line. "Managed managers and individual contributors" is permitted where the source says people leaders.
- Internal project names appear only with a plain description. Check exact phrases: "revenue recognition" is not matched by "rev rec"; "managing managers" is not matched by "leadership".

## Bullet shape

A bullet format cannot supply missing evidence. If the source establishes experience with API design but no ownership or leadership, retain that level of claim; do not add led, designed, built or managed. Record missing ownership, mechanism and outcome as gaps instead of presenting an invented achievement with placeholders.

When supported by evidence, a bullet names what the candidate decided or owned, the mechanism the candidate built or used, and the result. When those elements are absent, keep a bounded activity or experience statement and record the missing evidence separately. Use plain verbs (led, designed, built, priced, decided, managed, hired, coached). Vary the order. End at the fact; a consequence gets its own sentence. No trailing "resulting in" or "ensuring", no power verbs (spearheaded, orchestrated, championed), no builder constructions, no X-not-Y. Select client decisions, scaling mechanisms or other evidence when they demonstrate the role’s actual requirements. Titles and dates exactly as locked, month and year (for example, the synthetic span “Mar 2023–Jun 2024”).

## Layout and gate

Keep the master's typography; one or two pages as the router allows. ATS checks: standard section names, contact details in the body, no text boxes, images or content tables, standard fonts. Render to PDF and look at every page.

Apply `apply-author-style` with an explicitly supplied confirmed profile and the leadership-and-career section of `review-writing`. Where installed, run the bundled writing diagnostics and fix structure rather than swapping words; where not installed, check by reading and say no scan ran. Complete the resume source review receipt, resolve the [packaged readiness checker](../prepare-job-application/scripts/check_role_resume_readiness.py) from this workflow's location and run it with Python, passing the absolute path to `Role_Work_Record.md` as its single positional argument, update `03_Tracker/applications.md`, state `prepared locally`, and end with changed, verified, unchanged and the exact next action.

examples.title: Resume figures and keywords for a revenue operations director posting
examples.markdown:
## Request

Please rewrite the experience bullets on my tailored resume for the Director of Revenue Operations posting so the numbers are right and the posting's keywords show up where they're true. I'm fine with rounded or estimated figures if the basis holds up; my evidence notes and the posting are attached.

## Inputs

Run of the built `prepare-job-application` task package in its "resume figures and ATS wording" mode. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### evidence_notes.md

#### Evidence notes — Dana Whitlock (contact: dana.whitlock@example.com)

##### Locked titles and dates
- Senior Revenue Operations Manager, Harbor Analytics, Mar 2021–Present
- Sales Operations Manager, Brightfield Software, Jun 2017–Feb 2021

##### Ledger (claim authority)
1. Led the CPQ rollout on Salesforce for 140 sellers at Harbor. Quote turnaround went from 3 days to 4 hours. Source: program record, exact.
2. Billing automation at Harbor: forecast saving $1.8M a year (forecast, Jan 2023). Finance sign-off, Feb 2025: $1.3M realized in FY2024.
3. Deal desk at Harbor, which I run: reviewed non-standard quotes at an average of 23 a month through 2025. Set the discount approval matrix.
4. I manage 2 managers and 5 individual contributors in Revenue Operations (disclosure approved).
5. Brightfield: rebuilt the pipeline report used in the weekly forecast call; no figures recorded.
6. Forecast accuracy "improved" under my watch, no baseline or result in any record.

##### Other facts
- The Finance Systems team at Harbor (11 people) runs revenue recognition close. I work with them on handoffs; I don't manage them.
- Agentforce: I attended one vendor webinar. No hands-on work.
- Master resume headline: "Revenue operations leader".

#### posting.md

#### Director, Revenue Operations — Northvale Systems (posting, checked 2026-11-03)

Northvale sells subscription software to mid-market manufacturers. The Director owns revenue operations for a team of managers and individual contributors.

**Responsibilities**
- Own the quote-to-cash process from quote through invoice and revenue recognition handoff.
- Set the roadmap for Salesforce Revenue Cloud, including CPQ and Billing.
- Improve forecast accuracy and pipeline reporting with Sales and Finance.
- Manage managers and individual contributors across sales operations and deal desk.
- Run pricing and discount governance.

**Preferred**
- Hands-on exposure to Agentforce.
- Experience reducing quote cycle time.

## Output

I rewrote the experience bullets for the Northvale Director, Revenue Operations posting. I put in the figures your records support and the posting terms that are true for you. I left out four terms that aren't. The wording is a draft. I haven't produced a resume file or run the readiness check.

#### Bullets

**Headline:** Revenue Operations Leader

skills.markdown:
---
name: track-delivery
description: 'Continuous delivery documentation for Estate engagements: the weekly client status report, stewardship of the RAID and decision logs with stable IDs, and scope-drift detection against the SOW baseline that raises change-order candidates with an evidence trail. Use for a weekly or project status report, delivery update, what moved this week, logging a decision or risk from a meeting, updating the RAID log, or checking did we agree to that in scope. Do NOT use for authoring change orders or SOWs (write-statement-of-work), kickoff or charter (start-delivery), UAT tracking (validate-delivery), pricing (the Estate Pricing System), or sales pursuits (prepare-sales-pursuit).'
---


# Track delivery

> **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus
> [Writing Integrity review](../review-writing/references/detailed-review.md). Inputs, not a final pass.**

Keep the engagement record honest, week after week. Three jobs, always together: issue the status report from the record, steward the RAID and decision logs so nothing is re-litigated, and compare observed work against the SOW scope baseline so drift is flagged with evidence before it eats margin. Undocumented decisions cause the same conversation twice; unflagged drift becomes a change order handled reactively or, worse, absorbed silently.

Use the invocation actually configured for the engagement. A reporting cadence does not establish an automatic trigger; require configuration and run evidence before reporting that a scheduled or event-driven update occurred. Every run states exactly what period it covers and reconciles against the previous status file on disk, not against memory of a prior session.

## Project context required

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement, source records, private output location,
and intended audience. Map reference roles such as Program Lead, CSE, Solution Lead,
and Pursuit Lead to that project's authorized owners; these labels do not impose
an employer organization chart or signing authority. The executed agreement and
accepted project plan determine gates, commercial rules, and support obligations.
Keep account history, risk assessments, credentials, and client evidence outside
portable skill sources. A cached account, attached Project, or available connector
is not authorization to read, write, or publish.

## Inputs at a glance

| Input | Role | If missing |
|-------|------|------------|
| Meeting transcripts for the period | Evidence for log entries, drift, and quotes | Named gap in the report; ask the user what happened |
| RAID log and decision log | The record this skill stewards | Stop; offer to seed per `references/log-stewardship.md` |
| SOW scope baseline (scope body + Exhibit A) | The drift comparison target | Drift degrades to "no baseline on file", flagged |
| Previous status file | Reconciliation baseline | State this is the first status |
| Timesheet export or quote (Q-number) | The only legitimate burn source | Burn becomes a named gap, never an estimate |
| The user | Owner assignments, off-transcript events, decisions | Entries stay proposed, not written |

## Governance this skill delegates

- **evidence-core** owns provenance. Every log entry and every status claim carries a named source with a date. An absent fact is a named gap with an owner and a resolve-by date, never a blank or a plausible fill.
- **review-writing** owns writing review; a confirmed profile supplies voice. Run its checker on the finished status report. No em dashes, sentence-case headings, counts not adjectives.
- **brand-renderer** owns brand if the status ships as anything beyond markdown. The markdown report itself needs no brand pass.
- **The money rule.** Burn, remaining hours, and fee figures come from a timesheet export, the quote (Q-number), or an explicit user-supplied source. If no source is available this period, the figure is a named gap ("burn unavailable: no timesheet export provided, owner: Program Lead"). Never estimate burn silently. Never compute remaining from memory of last week's number.

Portability fallback: if a governor is not installed on the current surface, state the check it would have run, do the best manual substitute, and say that is what you did. Never silently skip.

## Phase 0: orient and pin the period

Pin all five before writing anything:

1. **The engagement.** Client, engagement name, SOW identifier. From the kickoff record or the user.
2. **The period.** Explicit start and end dates. Ask if ambiguous. The report header carries `Period: YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD`; the gate fails without it.
3. **The previous status file.** Find it in the engagement folder and read it. Open items, RAID counts, and last-reported burn come from that file. If none exists, say this is the first status of the engagement and that there is no prior baseline to reconcile against.
4. **The governance logs.** The RAID log and decision log seeded at kickoff by `start-delivery`, using the stable ID convention in `references/log-stewardship.md` (R-001, A-001, I-001, D-001 for RAID, where D is a dependency; DEC-001 for decisions). If the logs do not exist, stop and offer to seed them per that reference before producing any status.
5. **The SOW scope baseline.** The signed SOW's scope section and its Exhibit A Basis of Estimate where one exists. Without a baseline, scope-drift detection degrades to "no baseline on file" as a named gap, flagged in the report, not skipped.

## Phase 1: harvest the period's evidence

Read the meeting transcripts for the period verbatim, never summaries. A summary says "the client raised integration concerns"; the transcript says who asked for a second ERP integration and in which sentence. Pull direct quotes and attribute them by speaker and date; quotes are what make a drift flag or a decision entry defensible when it is challenged.

Also gather: the timesheet or burn source for the period, any artifact or gate movement (documents delivered, sign-offs obtained), and anything the user says happened off-transcript (record it as user-reported, with the user as the source).

Where transcripts live in Granola, Drive, or Slack, read what is actually there through the available integrations. Never substitute a similarly titled meeting for the one that was named.

## Phase 2: steward the logs

Rules in full in `references/log-stewardship.md`. The short version:

- **Append-only.** New entries get the next sequential ID. Existing entries are never renumbered, deleted, or rewritten; a correction is a new dated status line on the entry.
- **Every entry sourced.** Transcript quote with speaker and date, SOW clause, or a named person's statement. An unsourced item is proposed to the user, not written.
- **Every entry owned and dated.** Owner, status, resolve-by date, and the gate it blocks where applicable. Unowned actions evaporate.
- **Closure needs a sourced basis.** Never close a risk or mark a decision superseded because it stopped being mentioned. No source, stays open.
- Extract from each transcript: decisions made, new risks, new issues, new dependencies, assumptions stated as fact, and action items. Propose the batch to the user before appending when running interactively.

## Phase 3: detect scope drift

Protocol and evidence-trail format in `references/scope-drift-protocol.md`. The posture:

Compare every observed work item and client ask from the period against the SOW scope baseline. Classify using the Basis of Estimate trigger taxonomy in the contract scope and obligation review mode of `write-statement-of-work` (read `_runtime/review-contract-scope/references/basis-of-estimate.md` from that package; the selected agreement controls its applicability): **soft triggers** are volumetric, footprint materially exceeding Exhibit A; **hard triggers** are binary workstream additions such as a second integration or org, which trigger regardless of size.

When drift is found, raise a **change-order CANDIDATE**: the ask quoted verbatim with attribution, the baseline clause it exceeds cited by section, the trigger class, and the routing (Program Lead and CSE). That is the whole move. This skill never decides in-scope versus out-of-scope (a human call), never silently absorbs the work into status as if it were baseline, and never authors the change order itself; contractual review uses the contract scope and obligation review mode in `write-statement-of-work`, while authorized humans own contractual changes.

A period with no drift still gets a scope-drift section reading "None observed" with a one-line statement of what was compared. The gate requires the section either way; silence is not evidence of a check.

## Phase 4: write the status report

Fill `assets/weekly-status-template.md`. Section spec, ordering rules, and worked line examples in `references/status-report-spec.md`. The rules that carry it:

- **Outcome-first.** Lead with what the client can now do or decide, not with activity. "UAT entry criteria met" beats "the team worked on testing".
- **Counts, not adjectives.** "3 risks open, 1 new, 1 closed" rather than "good progress on risks". Every RAID and decision reference in the report uses its stable ID so the reader can find it in the log.
- **Red flags never buried.** Anything red or newly slipped goes in the flags section at the top of the report, stated plainly with its ID. A banner over a stale document body is not resolution: if a flag is cleared, the body lines that referenced it change too.
- **Every line about scope, hours, or dates carries a source.** Transcript, SOW clause, timesheet export, log entry ID, or a named gap.
- **Reconcile against the previous status.** Items reported open last period are either moved with a sourced basis or restated as still open. An item that vanishes between reports without explanation is the failure mode.

## Phase 5: gate before issuing

```bash
python3 scripts/status_check.py STATUS.md --raid-log RAID.md --decision-log DECISIONS.md
```

The gate is blocking. It verifies: the period is stated in the header; every stable ID referenced in the report exists in the corresponding log file; the scope-drift section is present and is either "None observed" or candidates each carrying at least one evidence citation; the hours-and-burn section names a source or a named gap; and no unfilled placeholders remain. Exit 0 passes; nonzero blocks issue. Report the counts it prints, not an adjective, and write a one-line disposition.

Review the report with `review-writing` and run its bundled internal `writing-diagnostics` diagnostics. If the diagnostics are unavailable, state the manual checks actually performed.

## Worked example, end to end

Input: a requirements-session transcript in which the client asks for a NetSuite integration; the SOW names a single integration (Workday). Correct output across the three jobs:

1. **Logs**: a dependency entry (D-0NN, client to confirm whether NetSuite is a requirement or a wish, owner and resolve-by date) and, if a human decided anything in the room, a decision entry. No decision entry for the ask itself; nobody decided anything yet.
2. **Drift**: a candidate block in the scope-drift section. Trigger class hard, the ask quoted verbatim with speaker and date, the SOW integration clause cited by section and quoted, at least one evidence line, routed to Program Lead and CSE.
3. **Status**: the candidate appears in the flags section as well as the scope-drift section, because it needs a decision. It reappears every period until a decision lands and gets a D-0NN.

The wrong outputs, for contrast: logging it as an action item for the team (silent absorption), deciding it is out of scope in the report (a human call), or drafting the change order (authorized humans own contractual changes; the contract scope and obligation review mode in `write-statement-of-work` reviews the resulting terms).

## State discipline

- Record IDs and quote totals are not durable anchors across sandbox refreshes. Stamp the report with its source objects and as-of dates: the SOW identifier and signed date, the timesheet export date, the transcript dates, the previous status filename.
- Truth hierarchy when sources disagree: signed SOW and its exhibits > governance logs > previous status file > chat context > memory. A conflict between them is flagged in the report, never silently resolved; show both and say which the report uses and why.
- Never hand-patch an issued report. Fix the log or the source, regenerate, and reissue with a new issue date; otherwise the next cadence run resurrects the error.

## Running unattended

Phases 2 and 3 normally propose before appending. On a scheduled or headless run: append log entries with a clearly marked `proposed` status, produce the report, run the gate, and state in the flags section that the proposed entries and any drift candidates await human review. Never record a decision nobody made, never close a RAID item unattended, and never issue the report to the client without a human in the loop; leave it as a draft for the Program Lead.

## Phase 6: land it

If any lifecycle gate moved this period, verify the engagement's DELIVERY-STATE.md reflects it (status, date, append-only log line) per delivery-orchestrator's `references/delivery-state-spec.md`; a stale state file is a flag in the report.

Deliver the report, and commit the report plus the updated logs to the engagement folder so the next cadence run can find them; the previous-status reconciliation in Phase 0 depends on this. Name the report with the period end date (`status-2026-08-08.md`) so ordering is unambiguous. Close with the user on: the flags, any change-order candidates raised, and the biggest judgment call of the period argued from both sides.

Status reports are issued, not signed. Drift flags are proposals for a human decision.

## Durable output

The status report is the run's durable Markdown record and follows `_shared/output-contract.md`: the period, the sources used, the counts, the flags, and the change-order candidates all live in the file, named by period end date and committed to the engagement folder. A run that stops before issuing still leaves a record of what was checked and what blocked it. Deliver or link the file; never just say it was written.

## When time is short

Cut in this order, and say what you cut: (1) the narrative accomplishments detail, keep the outcome bullets; (2) upcoming-period detail beyond the next gate; (3) artifact-register updates beyond what moved. Never cut: the period header, log stewardship for decisions and new risks, the scope-drift section, sourcing, or the gate.

## Boundaries

In the delivery chain (SOW, then prepare-delivery-handoff, then kickoff, then status, then UAT, then manage-cutover-closeout), this skill's upstream producer is start-delivery, which seeds the logs it stewards, and its downstream consumer is validate-delivery, which feeds it defects and test progress once Validate starts. Status does not re-plan: the plan, the baseline, and the gates stay where they were signed, and what this skill produces is the honest record of movement against them.

- Does not author change orders or scope language. Candidates route to authorized humans for a contractual decision; the contract scope and obligation review mode in `write-statement-of-work` reviews the resulting terms.

Keep the engagement record honest, week after week. Three jobs, always together: issue the status report from the record, steward the RAID and decision logs so nothing is re-litigated, and compare observed work against the SOW scope baseline so drift is flagged with evidence before it eats margin. Undocumented decisions cause the same conversation twice; unflagged drift becomes a change order handled reactively or, worse, absorbed silently.

Use the invocation actually configured for the engagement. A reporting cadence does not establish an automatic trigger; require configuration and run evidence before reporting that a scheduled or event-driven update occurred. Every run states exactly what period it covers and reconciles against the previous status file on disk, not against memory of a prior session.

Project context required

Use only the caller-confirmed engagement, source records, private output location, and intended audience. Map reference roles such as Program Lead, CSE, Solution Lead, and Pursuit Lead to that project's authorized owners; these labels do not impose an employer organization chart or signing authority. The executed agreement and accepted project plan determine gates, commercial rules, and support obligations. Keep account history, risk assessments, credentials, and client evidence outside portable skill sources. A cached account, attached Project, or available connector is not authorization to read, write, or publish.

Inputs at a glance

InputRoleIf missing
Meeting transcripts for the periodEvidence for log entries, drift, and quotesNamed gap in the report; ask the user what happened
RAID log and decision logThe record this skill stewardsStop; offer to seed per references/log-stewardship.md
SOW scope baseline (scope body + Exhibit A)The drift comparison targetDrift degrades to "no baseline on file", flagged
Previous status fileReconciliation baselineState this is the first status
Timesheet export or quote (Q-number)The only legitimate burn sourceBurn becomes a named gap, never an estimate
The userOwner assignments, off-transcript events, decisionsEntries stay proposed, not written

Governance this skill delegates

  • evidence-core owns provenance. Every log entry and every status claim carries a named source with a date. An absent fact is a named gap with an owner and a resolve-by date, never a blank or a plausible fill.
  • review-writing owns writing review; a confirmed profile supplies voice. Run its checker on the finished status report. No em dashes, sentence-case headings, counts not adjectives.
  • brand-renderer owns brand if the status ships as anything beyond markdown. The markdown report itself needs no brand pass.
  • The money rule. Burn, remaining hours, and fee figures come from a timesheet export, the quote (Q-number), or an explicit user-supplied source. If no source is available this period, the figure is a named gap ("burn unavailable: no timesheet export provided, owner: Program Lead"). Never estimate burn silently. Never compute remaining from memory of last week's number.

Portability fallback: if a governor is not installed on the current surface, state the check it would have run, do the best manual substitute, and say that is what you did. Never silently skip.

Phase 0: orient and pin the period

Pin all five before writing anything:

  1. The engagement. Client, engagement name, SOW identifier. From the kickoff record or the user.
  2. The period. Explicit start and end dates. Ask if ambiguous. The report header carries Period: YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD; the gate fails without it.
  3. The previous status file. Find it in the engagement folder and read it. Open items, RAID counts, and last-reported burn come from that file. If none exists, say this is the first status of the engagement and that there is no prior baseline to reconcile against.
  4. The governance logs. The RAID log and decision log seeded at kickoff by start-delivery, using the stable ID convention in references/log-stewardship.md (R-001, A-001, I-001, D-001 for RAID, where D is a dependency; DEC-001 for decisions). If the logs do not exist, stop and offer to seed them per that reference before producing any status.
  5. The SOW scope baseline. The signed SOW's scope section and its Exhibit A Basis of Estimate where one exists. Without a baseline, scope-drift detection degrades to "no baseline on file" as a named gap, flagged in the report, not skipped.

Phase 1: harvest the period's evidence

Read the meeting transcripts for the period verbatim, never summaries. A summary says "the client raised integration concerns"; the transcript says who asked for a second ERP integration and in which sentence. Pull direct quotes and attribute them by speaker and date; quotes are what make a drift flag or a decision entry defensible when it is challenged.

Also gather: the timesheet or burn source for the period, any artifact or gate movement (documents delivered, sign-offs obtained), and anything the user says happened off-transcript (record it as user-reported, with the user as the source).

Where transcripts live in Granola, Drive, or Slack, read what is actually there through the available integrations. Never substitute a similarly titled meeting for the one that was named.

Phase 2: steward the logs

Rules in full in references/log-stewardship.md. The short version:

  • Append-only. New entries get the next sequential ID. Existing entries are never renumbered, deleted, or rewritten; a correction is a new dated status line on the entry.
  • Every entry sourced. Transcript quote with speaker and date, SOW clause, or a named person's statement. An unsourced item is proposed to the user, not written.
  • Every entry owned and dated. Owner, status, resolve-by date, and the gate it blocks where applicable. Unowned actions evaporate.
  • Closure needs a sourced basis. Never close a risk or mark a decision superseded because it stopped being mentioned. No source, stays open.
  • Extract from each transcript: decisions made, new risks, new issues, new dependencies, assumptions stated as fact, and action items. Propose the batch to the user before appending when running interactively.

Phase 3: detect scope drift

Protocol and evidence-trail format in references/scope-drift-protocol.md. The posture:

Compare every observed work item and client ask from the period against the SOW scope baseline. Classify using the Basis of Estimate trigger taxonomy in the contract scope and obligation review mode of write-statement-of-work (read _runtime/review-contract-scope/references/basis-of-estimate.md from that package; the selected agreement controls its applicability): soft triggers are volumetric, footprint materially exceeding Exhibit A; hard triggers are binary workstream additions such as a second integration or org, which trigger regardless of size.

When drift is found, raise a change-order CANDIDATE: the ask quoted verbatim with attribution, the baseline clause it exceeds cited by section, the trigger class, and the routing (Program Lead and CSE). That is the whole move. This skill never decides in-scope versus out-of-scope (a human call), never silently absorbs the work into status as if it were baseline, and never authors the change order itself; contractual review uses the contract scope and obligation review mode in write-statement-of-work, while authorized humans own contractual changes.

A period with no drift still gets a scope-drift section reading "None observed" with a one-line statement of what was compared. The gate requires the section either way; silence is not evidence of a check.

Phase 4: write the status report

Fill assets/weekly-status-template.md. Section spec, ordering rules, and worked line examples in references/status-report-spec.md. The rules that carry it:

  • Outcome-first. Lead with what the client can now do or decide, not with activity. "UAT entry criteria met" beats "the team worked on testing".
  • Counts, not adjectives. "3 risks open, 1 new, 1 closed" rather than "good progress on risks". Every RAID and decision reference in the report uses its stable ID so the reader can find it in the log.
  • Red flags never buried. Anything red or newly slipped goes in the flags section at the top of the report, stated plainly with its ID. A banner over a stale document body is not resolution: if a flag is cleared, the body lines that referenced it change too.
  • Every line about scope, hours, or dates carries a source. Transcript, SOW clause, timesheet export, log entry ID, or a named gap.
  • Reconcile against the previous status. Items reported open last period are either moved with a sourced basis or restated as still open. An item that vanishes between reports without explanation is the failure mode.

Phase 5: gate before issuing

python3 scripts/status_check.py STATUS.md --raid-log RAID.md --decision-log DECISIONS.md

The gate is blocking. It verifies: the period is stated in the header; every stable ID referenced in the report exists in the corresponding log file; the scope-drift section is present and is either "None observed" or candidates each carrying at least one evidence citation; the hours-and-burn section names a source or a named gap; and no unfilled placeholders remain. Exit 0 passes; nonzero blocks issue. Report the counts it prints, not an adjective, and write a one-line disposition.

Review the report with review-writing and run its bundled internal writing-diagnostics diagnostics. If the diagnostics are unavailable, state the manual checks actually performed.

Worked example, end to end

Input: a requirements-session transcript in which the client asks for a NetSuite integration; the SOW names a single integration (Workday). Correct output across the three jobs:

  1. Logs: a dependency entry (D-0NN, client to confirm whether NetSuite is a requirement or a wish, owner and resolve-by date) and, if a human decided anything in the room, a decision entry. No decision entry for the ask itself; nobody decided anything yet.
  2. Drift: a candidate block in the scope-drift section. Trigger class hard, the ask quoted verbatim with speaker and date, the SOW integration clause cited by section and quoted, at least one evidence line, routed to Program Lead and CSE.
  3. Status: the candidate appears in the flags section as well as the scope-drift section, because it needs a decision. It reappears every period until a decision lands and gets a D-0NN.

The wrong outputs, for contrast: logging it as an action item for the team (silent absorption), deciding it is out of scope in the report (a human call), or drafting the change order (authorized humans own contractual changes; the contract scope and obligation review mode in write-statement-of-work reviews the resulting terms).

State discipline

  • Record IDs and quote totals are not durable anchors across sandbox refreshes. Stamp the report with its source objects and as-of dates: the SOW identifier and signed date, the timesheet export date, the transcript dates, the previous status filename.
  • Truth hierarchy when sources disagree: signed SOW and its exhibits > governance logs > previous status file > chat context > memory. A conflict between them is flagged in the report, never silently resolved; show both and say which the report uses and why.
  • Never hand-patch an issued report. Fix the log or the source, regenerate, and reissue with a new issue date; otherwise the next cadence run resurrects the error.

Running unattended

Phases 2 and 3 normally propose before appending. On a scheduled or headless run: append log entries with a clearly marked proposed status, produce the report, run the gate, and state in the flags section that the proposed entries and any drift candidates await human review. Never record a decision nobody made, never close a RAID item unattended, and never issue the report to the client without a human in the loop; leave it as a draft for the Program Lead.

Phase 6: land it

If any lifecycle gate moved this period, verify the engagement's DELIVERY-STATE.md reflects it (status, date, append-only log line) per delivery-orchestrator's references/delivery-state-spec.md; a stale state file is a flag in the report.

Deliver the report, and commit the report plus the updated logs to the engagement folder so the next cadence run can find them; the previous-status reconciliation in Phase 0 depends on this. Name the report with the period end date (status-2026-08-08.md) so ordering is unambiguous. Close with the user on: the flags, any change-order candidates raised, and the biggest judgment call of the period argued from both sides.

Status reports are issued, not signed. Drift flags are proposals for a human decision.

The status report is the run's durable Markdown record and follows _shared/output-contract.md: the period, the sources used, the counts, the flags, and the change-order candidates all live in the file, named by period end date and committed to the engagement folder. A run that stops before issuing still leaves a record of what was checked and what blocked it. Deliver or link the file; never just say it was written.

Cut in this order, and say what you cut: (1) the narrative accomplishments detail, keep the outcome bullets; (2) upcoming-period detail beyond the next gate; (3) artifact-register updates beyond what moved. Never cut: the period header, log stewardship for decisions and new risks, the scope-drift section, sourcing, or the gate.

## Request

Can you do the weekly status for Brightwater for the week of 26 to 30 October? The workshop transcript, our SOW excerpt with the RAID and decision logs, and the timesheet export are in the inputs folder.

## Inputs

Run of the built `track-delivery` task package. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### engagement-record.md

#### Brightwater customer portal: engagement record as of 2026-10-23

##### SOW-BW-2026-04 (signed 2026-08-14), excerpt

- Exhibit A, line 4: "Integrations: 1 (billing). Any additional integration is a Binary Workstream Addition and is handled by Change Order."
- Exhibit A, line 1: "Estimate: 320 hours."
- Gate: Requirements sign-off 2026-11-13.

##### RAID log

| R-003 | Billing API documentation is out of date | Sam Okoye | Open | 2026-11-06 | Requirements sign-off | Tomas Reyes, 2026-10-14 |
| A-001 | Portal serves residential customers only | Dana Whitlock | Open | 2026-11-13 | none | SOW section 2 |
| D-001 | Client IT delivers IdP metadata file | Tomas Reyes | Open | 2026-10-28 | Requirements sign-off | Kickoff 2026-10-07 |

##### Decision log

| DEC-001 | Weekly status goes out Fridays | 2026-10-07 | Priya Nandakumar | Matches client steering rhythm | Standing |
| DEC-002 | Portal launches with email notifications only | 2026-10-14 | Priya Nandakumar | SMS needs a separate carrier contract | Standing |

##### Previous status: status-2026-10-23.md

Reported 3 risks open, 0 issues, 2 dependencies open (D-001, D-002), 1 assumption open. Scope drift: none observed. Burn: 104 h to date of 320 h. Next gate: Requirements sign-off 2026-11-13.

#### timesheet-export-2026-10-30.txt

Timesheet export, SOW-BW-2026-04, exported 2026-10-30
Week 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30: 38.0 h
To date: 142.0 h

#### transcript-2026-10-28.md

#### Requirements workshop 2, 2026-10-28 (Brightwater customer portal)

Attendees: Priya Nandakumar (Brightwater product owner), Tomas Reyes (Brightwater IT), Dana Whitlock (Program Lead), Sam Okoye (CSE).

**Priya:** For sign-in, customers will use our existing identity provider. No separate portal passwords. That's decided.

**Dana:** Then we need the IdP metadata file to configure it.

**Tomas:** It's still with our security team. I can't promise it before 6 November.

**Priya:** When there's an outage, crews need to see it too. We'll need the portal to push outage notices into Fieldwise, our crew scheduling system. That's the same kind of thing as the billing connection, right?

**Sam:** That would be a second system on the integration side. I'll note it. I'm not saying yes or no.

**Tomas:** The billing API sandbox caps us at 60 calls a minute. Our nightly account sync might hit that.

**Priya:** We're assuming the billing account data is clean. It was cleaned in September.

**Dana:** Next session is 2026-11-04, notification templates.

## Output

The Brightwater status for 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30 is written and held as a draft for the Program Lead. It has 4 flags, 1 scope-drift candidate and 4 proposed log entries.

#### Flags

1. **Scope-drift candidate: Fieldwise integration (hard trigger).** On 2026-10-28 Priya Nandakumar said: "We'll need the portal to push outage notices into Fieldwise, our crew scheduling system." SOW-BW-2026-04 section 3.2 says: "The Services include one (1) integration, between the Portal and the Brightwater billing system." Exhibit A line 4 treats any additional integration as a Binary Workstream Addition handled by Change Order. Sam Okoye answered in the room: "I'm not saying yes or no." The candidate is routed to the Program Lead and CSE. I have not decided whether it is in scope and have not drafted a change order. It will stay in the report until a human decision is logged.
2. **D-001 (IdP metadata) is late.** It was due 2026-10-28. Tomas Reyes said he can't promise it before 2026-11-06. It blocks Requirements sign-off on 2026-11-13.
3. **Source conflict on D-002.** The previous status listed the billing sandbox credentials as open. The RAID log says they were delivered 2026-10-21. The report follows the log and shows both.
4. **Proposed entries need your confirmation.**

#### Log changes (appended, none renumbered)

| ID | Entry | Source |
|---|---|---|
| DEC-003 | Customers sign in through the client's existing identity provider, with no separate portal passwords. Made by Priya Nandakumar. | Priya, 2026-10-28: "That's decided." |
| R-004 | The billing API sandbox cap of 60 calls a minute may be hit by the nightly sync. | Tomas Reyes, 2026-10-28 |
| A-002 | Billing account data is clean. | Priya, 2026-10-28 |
| D-003 | The client confirms whether the Fieldwise push is a requirement or a wish. | Priya, 2026-10-28 |

No decision entry was written for the Fieldwise ask, because nobody decided it. D-001 got a dated history line; its original resolve-by date was left as it was.

#### Counts and burn

- Risks: 4 open (1 new), 0 closed. Issues: 0. Dependencies: 2 open (1 new), 1 delivered earlier. Assumptions: 2 open (1 new).
- Burn: 38.0 h this period, 142.0 h to date of 320 h (44.4%), 178.0 h remaining. Source: timesheet export 2026-10-30 and Exhibit A line 1. The previous status said 104 h, and 104 + 38.0 = 142.0, so the figures reconcile.

#### Gaps and assumptions

- **Plan file:** none was supplied, so on-track or off-track status per workstream is a named gap. Owner: Program Lead.
- **DELIVERY-STATE.md:** not supplied, so I couldn't check it. No gate moved this period. Owner: Program Lead.
- **Previous status:** I reconciled against the summary in the engagement record, not the `status-2026-10-23.md` file itself.
- **Proposed fields:** the owners for R-004 and D-003 and the 2026-11-06 resolve-by on D-003 are my proposals. The transcript gives no rationale for DEC-003, and the log says so.
- **Unattended run:** with no one to confirm, the new entries are marked proposed.

#### Checks

- **Gate:** I couldn't run `status_check.py`, so I applied its rules by hand. The `Period:` line is present. Every ID in the report (R-001 to R-004, A-001, A-002, D-001 to D-003, DEC-003) is in the logs. The scope-drift section holds 1 candidate with 2 `Evidence:` lines. The burn section names a source. No placeholders remain. Result: pass, 0 failures.
- **Writing:** the writing-diagnostics diagnostics were not run. I made a manual pass for em dashes, sentence-case headings, counts instead of adjectives and a source on every line about scope, hours or dates.
- **Brand renderer:** not run. The report is Markdown only.

#### Judgment call for you

Should the Fieldwise ask be raised with Brightwater now, before D-003 is answered?

- **Raise it now:** Requirements sign-off is 2026-11-13, and a new integration changes the requirements document. Waiting costs a week.
- **Wait for D-003:** Priya phrased it as a question, so it may be a wish. Raising a change order early could harden a casual remark into a commercial position.

I'd confirm D-003 with Priya at the 2026-11-04 session first, then decide. That is your decision and the CSE's.

#### Files

- `out/status-2026-10-30.md`: the weekly status. It is the full report, so the key content above is all in it.
- `out/RAID.md`: the updated RAID log (R-004, A-002 and D-003 added, a D-001 history line, and the earlier entries left as they were).
- `out/DECISIONS.md`: the updated decision log (DEC-003 added).

##### Flags

1. **Candidate: second integration (Fieldwise).** Priya Nandakumar asked for outage notices to be pushed into Fieldwise on 2026-10-28. The SOW names one integration, billing. This needs a decision from the Program Lead and CSE; see Scope drift and D-003.
