--- name: write-statement-of-work description: 'Generate Statements of Work (.docx) from a confirmed quote JSON and a selected contract profile, in Waterfall (fixed scope), Agile (adaptive scope), and Assess (advisory, readout-gated) variants. Use when asked to generate the SOW, draft the SOW from the quote, build the SOW for a Q-number, or turn a quote into a Statement of Work. The quote is the source of truth; this skill renders it, does not price (the Pricing System prices), and does not author scope language (scope-project does). It builds the .docx, resolves placeholders with an audit trail, verifies the required-clause gate, and hands off to the embedded contract review mode. For authoring quality review, select the embedded contract scope and obligation review mode; DDOC remains a deck workflow.' --- # Write statement of work > **Before writing: [`build-card.md`](../_shared/build-card.md) plus > [`sow-proposal.md`](../writing-diagnostics/references/registers/sow-proposal.md). Inputs, not a final pass.** Draft or generate the requested editable statement of work from the current quote, confirmed scope baseline, contracting entities, approved template and applicable agreement. The selected sources govern numbers, scope, acceptance and payment terms. This workflow does not invent pricing or scope commitments. ## Select a supported production route Build a source-to-document mapping for scope, deliverables, responsibilities, acceptance, timeline, pricing, payment milestones, assumptions, exclusions and change control. Resolve revisions and conflicting sources before asserting final terms. Use the available document tool with the supplied template for ordinary drafting, revisions, or agreements that do not fit this generator's input contract. Missing entity details or approved terms permit a clearly labeled draft with unresolved fields visible. Preserve contractual meaning and mandated wording, including its punctuation. Historical clauses and example profiles supply no approval. The optional generator below supports only its documented model and contract-profile shape. Use it when that shape faithfully represents the actual agreement. Its fixed variant structures, reconciliation requirements, upfront field or Exhibit A layout must not create a payment term, acceptance rule, scope cap or requirement for an existing CRM record. In particular, an independently sourced fixed fee may differ from hours times rate; this generator's per-role revenue equality cannot represent that model. Preserve the agreed fee and use the document-tool route for it. If other supplied terms cannot be represented faithfully, use the document-tool route; do not force the agreement into the generator or fill missing values from examples. For either route reconcile totals and milestones, inspect cross-references and placeholders, compare required clauses with the supplied template, then run the embedded contract review. Inspect every rendered page before finalizing. Creating a document does not approve, send or execute it. The following variant and CLI sections describe the optional generator. The selected agreement remains controlling; unsupported terms require the document-tool route. ## Variants Four, passed as the second CLI argument to `scripts/generate_sow.js`. One generator handles all four by branching internally; there is no separate builder file per variant. - **Letter of engagement** (`loe`), a short fixed-fee advisory engagement under the selected agreement. Carries scope, fee, timing, assumptions, selected agreement terms, acceptance, and signatures. It does not silently inherit the full SOW clause set. - **Waterfall** (`waterfall`), fixed-scope build. Phase-gated, Exhibit A basis of estimate, UAT gates production. The default. - **Agile** (`agile`), adaptive build. Sprint stages, backlog, same Exhibit A discipline. - **Assess** (`assess`), advisory engagement. Assessments and strategy plays. It differs structurally from the build variants and is not a tuning of them: - Delivery methodology is Discover, Assess, Recommend stages, not build phases. The stages describe analysis flow and carry no phase gates. - Deliverables are the actual scope items from the quote, not the fixed build artifact set. - Acceptance is **readout-gated**: the deliverables are accepted on completion of the executive readout. No defect severity, no UAT, no production gate. - Scope is fixed by the **Section 4 deliverable list**. There is **no Exhibit A**; an assessment is not sized by volumetrics like "up to N products". - Fee model is **fixed fee**. A conflicting T&M quote fails rather than being changed by the renderer. The contract shell is shared across every variant: parties and notice, Sections 1, 2, 6, 7, 11, the Miscellaneous Terms, and the signature block. Only the build-specific middle changes. ## Input: the quote model The generator reads one JSON file, the quote model. `fixtures/quote.example.json` is a runnable synthetic example; copy its shape and replace it with sourced engagement data. `fixtures/assessment.example.json` exercises the advisory variants. The models under `scripts/` are synthetic shape and missing-context regression examples. ```bash node scripts/generate_sow.js fixtures/quote.example.json waterfall \ --contract fixtures/contract.example.json --example --output output/example-sow.docx ``` **Required.** Structural or financial inconsistencies stop the build. Unresolved narrative fields also stop the build unless `--draft` was explicitly requested. A draft is visibly marked and cannot pass the contract verifier. | Path | Notes | |---|---| | `source.reference` | Confirmed quote identifier and revision, or a clearly synthetic fixture reference | | `projectContext` | `accountName`, `opportunityName`, `quoteName`, `businessNeed`, `businessDriver`, `psaEffectiveDate`, `clientAddress`, `clientContact`, `primaryContact`, `executiveSponsor`, `providerLead`, `accountsPayable`, `testScriptOwnership`, `returnBy` | | `pricingModel` | Explicit `tm` or `fixed`; assessment and letter variants require `fixed` | | `deliveryMethodology`, `scopeNote` | Confirmed method and supporting activities; do not turn a generic delivery template into scope | | `deliverables[]` | Confirmed `name`, `description`, `format`; required for build variants | | `projectSummary` | `totalValue`, `totalHours`, `durationWeeks`, `teamSize`, `totalScopeItems` | | `timeline.summary.blendedRate` | Printed against the calculated rate for comparison | | `timeline.bands[0]` | `startDate`, `endDate` | | `timeline.bands[0].phases[]` | `name`, `weeks`, `weekNumbers[]`, `purpose` | | `timeline.bands[0].resources[]` | `role`, `titleLevel`, `billRate`, `totalHours`, `totalRevenue`, `hoursByPhase{}`, `responsibility`; optional explicit `discountAmount` | | `scopeItemsByCapability[]` | `name`, `children[]`, `scopeItems[]` each with `name`, `description`, `assumptions` | `description` and `assumptions` accept HTML (`

`, `

  • `) or plain text with `-` bullets. **Optional.** Each of these replaces a mined or inferred value, and every substitution is logged. `platform`, `targetPlatform`, `sourceSystem`, `engagementType`, `engagementDriver`, `purposeNarrative`, `engagementBoundary`, `boundarySummary`, `exclusions[]`, `changeOrderTriggers[]`, `basisOfEstimate[{dimension, footprint}]`, `locBasisNote`, `exhibitA[{text, item}]`. **The three-way tie.** The generator reconciles before it renders, and prints PASS or FAIL. The model must satisfy all of: - every resource's `hoursByPhase` values sum to its own `totalHours`; offsetting errors in different roles do not cancel - each resource's hours times rate, less an explicit discount, equals its revenue - the sum of all `totalHours` equals `projectSummary.totalHours` - the sum of all `totalRevenue` equals `projectSummary.totalValue` A failure writes a diagnostic build record and produces no DOCX. Return the discrepancy to the quote owner; do not substitute a recomputed commercial commitment. The source blended rate and scope count must also reconcile. ### Build the model from the available quote source A local JSON export in the documented shape is sufficient. No proprietary scoping application or live connector is required. If the connected pricing system exposes the following tools, use its current export contract; these names describe an optional adapter, not tools this skill guarantees are installed. Confirm one quote revision and one selected band before filling gaps. | Tool | Returns | When | |---|---|---| | `scoping_get_sow_data` | `projectContext`, `projectSummary`, `scopeItemsByCapability`, and `timeline` with bands, phases, and resources | Always, first | | `scoping_get_scope_hierarchy` | Per-item hours and financials, with `includeHours:true` and `includeFinancials:true` | For the Section 9 fee tables | | `scoping_get_quote` | Quote-level resources and the rate-card grid | When the fee table needs the resource grid | | `scoping_manage_scope_items` | Write-back of a corrected description or assumption | On request, with confirmation, never silent | Given a Q-number rather than a record Id, resolve it first with a SOQL query on `Quote__c.Name`. **Read every rate from the quote.** Never hardcode a role rate; rates move in the live data, so memory is not a source. **Discrepancy handling.** Stop the build and retain the diagnostic record. Obtain a corrected source model from the owner. Never change an authorized figure to make the document reconcile. ## Workflow 1. **Read the quote** from its confirmed local export or available pricing-system adapter. Confirm the Q-number, the active timeline snapshot, the scope line items, and the total before rendering anything. 2. **Build the quote model** in the shape above. This is the step that turns the MCP response into `model.json`. 3. **Pick the variant** from the engagement shape, not from preference. Fixed deliverables with acceptance criteria is Waterfall. A backlog with a rate of delivery is Agile. Analysis with a readout is Assess. 4. **Render.** `node scripts/generate_sow.js model.json --contract contract.json --output output/sow.docx`. Add `--profile brand.md` for a selected brand. Writes the DOCX, a build record, and a resolution log. Existing outputs are preserved; use a new attempt path. 5. **Work the resolution log.** Every bracketed field is resolved before the document leaves the building. A missing source value is flagged, never filled. 6. **Verify the actual contract and quote.** `python3 scripts/verify_contract.py OUT.docx --contract contract.json --quote model.json --variant --output verification.json`. This compares selected clause text, identities, scope descriptions, quote values, and build hashes. It must pass. The older `verify_clauses.py` checks the reference clause table only and cannot approve a different contract profile. 7. **Read [the contract review workflow](../review-contract-scope/SKILL.md)**, embedded as the contract scope and obligation review mode, for the authoring pass: structural de-slop, the Basis of Estimate framework, and cross-reference discipline. 8. **Gate.** Parity, visual, prose. Written disposition each. ## Contract and brand inputs The `--contract` JSON is the canonical source for this engagement's provider identity, notice address, contact, clause text, and upfront percentage. It must include `status`, `source`, `provider`, `upfrontPercent`, and a complete `clauses` object with the same keys and shapes as `fixtures/contract.example.json`. Keep the confirmed profile and payment instructions in the private project. Reuse that profile across its SOWs. Do not copy bank details or contract approvals into this reusable skill. `status: confirmed` records the user's confirmed source. The example profile uses `status: example`; it runs only with `--example` and a model explicitly marked synthetic, and every generated example is labeled. Its clause markers are nonlegal test data and carry no approval for a real engagement. A passing text check proves that the selected wording survived rendering; it does not establish legal approval. The separate canonical brand profile owns colors, Office font, and optional logo. The neutral profile needs no proprietary files. A declared missing logo fails; a supplied raster logo preserves its aspect ratio. `--profile` or `SKILLS_BRAND_PROFILE` selects the profile, then the caller-supplied project brand profile, then the packaged neutral policy. ## What a clean run means Complete source inputs can produce zero unresolved fields. That is expected when the quote and contract profile supply the information. Missing information is never filled from remembered company conventions. `--draft` permits a marked working copy; the build record retains every unresolved field and the verifier fails it. Run the source-contract check, render the DOCX, inspect every page, and check the contents links, tables, signatures, and scoped assumptions. Retain each attempt, including failures and screenshots. A generated report does not replace the DOCX. ## Per option One SOW per option. A three-tier playbook carries three SOWs, not one with a tier table. Use a descriptive output path, for example: `10 - SOW - .docx`, for example `10 CPQ to RCA Migration - SOW - Remediate & Migrate.docx`. The real band name, never `Tier 2`; the code stays in the manifest, never in the filename. ## Rules - **The quote is the only source for a number.** No price, duration, or headcount that the quote does not ground. - Place volumetric assumptions and any change-control triggers where the selected agreement requires them. Preserve fixed scope caps and contractual rights; Exhibit A and the historical soft/hard taxonomy apply only when adopted by that agreement. - **One authoritative home per mechanic.** Exhibit A does not restate Change Order mechanics. Section 7.2 does not lead with consequences before establishing the rule. - **Preserve role names and responsibilities from the quote.** Use `roleAliases` only when an explicit mapping is part of the source. Do not silently turn an Account Executive into an engagement-delivery role. - Use the selected writing policy for authored wording. Preserve exact quotations and mandated clause punctuation; scanner flags never authorize changing contract terms. - Preserve supplied exclusions and their actual handling process. A proposed next step stays proposed; do not invent paid follow-on work. ## The assumptions in the SOW should already be familiar Where the project has an approved decision deck or prior scope record, compare its assumptions with the SOW and flag discrepancies. Preserve the actual approval state; neither an absent deck nor a generated document establishes client acceptance. Use the confirmed scope baseline when no deck exists. ## Clause coverage and files The selected contract profile is the authority for the actual build. `verify_contract.py` checks its wording, including the assessment and engagement-letter branches, against the generated document. Missing or changed text fails. It also checks input and artifact hashes so a changed quote cannot reuse an old passing build. - `scripts/generate_sow.js` renders all four variants, preserves scope paragraphs and bullets, mines assumptions and Change Order triggers, and reconciles the quote before rendering. - `scripts/input_contract.js` validates the inputs and performs per-role financial and phase reconciliation. - `scripts/approved_clauses.js` is a legacy filename for the synthetic reference clause structure. It supplies required keys; builds use the explicit profile's values. It is not a claim of approval. - `scripts/verify_contract.py` checks the actual selected contract and quote against the DOCX. - `scripts/verify_clauses.py` and `references/required-clauses.md` retain the reference anchor checker and its regression cases. - `fixtures/` contains runnable synthetic quote and contract examples. - `references/cpq-migration-exclusions.md` lists migration boundaries to resolve from the engagement sources. Select only exclusions supported by the actual engagement. ## Runtime Node.js with `docx` is required for generation. A declared logo also needs `image-size`; Python 3 runs the verifiers. Use the host's bundled dependencies when available. Otherwise run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` in this skill directory using its committed lockfile. The portable package includes its shared brand runtime and policy. It does not require a company drive or a neighboring skill checkout. ## Release gate (required) Before you deliver, run the gate. This is a required step, not a suggestion, and not something a reviewer does later. Full spec in [`release-gate.md`](../_shared/release-gate.md). 1. Apply review-writing to the prose. Use the bundled diagnostic tools to check saved writing. For a final artifact it emits a receipt the quality gate requires. 2. Run brand-renderer on the branded artifact: palette, borders, radii, logo, footer. 3. Run review-deliverable before you call it final. Do not present the artifact as finished until every check that applies has passed.

## Request

Draft the statement of work for the Brightwell Dental Partners intake portal from the confirmed scope, quote and contract profile in ./inputs/.

## Inputs

Run of the built `write-statement-of-work` task package. All inputs below are invented. The run had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so.

#### confirmed-scope.md

#### Brightwell Dental Partners — confirmed scope (fictional)

Client: Brightwell Dental Partners, LLC, a group of 11 dental offices in Ohio.
Provider: Harbor Lane Consulting, LLC (fictional consultancy).
Project: Online new-patient intake portal.

In scope:
1. Discovery and design: 2 workshops, intake form design for adult and pediatric patients, accessibility review to WCAG 2.2 AA.
2. Build: web intake form (responsive), insurance card photo upload, e-signature on consent forms, integration that pushes completed intake to the practice-management system "DentaCore" via its import API.
3. Testing: QA, one round of user acceptance testing with 2 pilot offices.
4. Launch: pilot in 2 offices, then rollout to all 11; staff training (2 remote sessions, recorded).
5. Hypercare: 30 days after full rollout.

Out of scope: appointment scheduling, payments, DentaCore configuration changes, translation beyond English and Spanish form text supplied by the client.

Client responsibilities: provide DentaCore API sandbox access by week 2; named product owner (Operations Director, Lena Ortiz); Spanish translations of form text; pilot office availability.

Assumptions: DentaCore import API supports the required fields; no PHI stored outside DentaCore and the HIPAA-eligible hosting the client already licenses.


#### contract-profile.md

#### Contract profile (fictional)

- Governing agreement: Master Services Agreement between the parties dated March 3, 2026 (assume standard MSA terms; this SOW should reference it, not restate it).
- Acceptance: deliverables deemed accepted 10 business days after delivery unless the client gives written notice of a material nonconformance.
- Business Associate Agreement: in place, dated March 3, 2026.


#### quote.md

#### Quote (fictional) — fixed fee by milestone

| Milestone | Amount (USD) |
|---|---|
| M1 Discovery and design accepted | 18,000 |
| M2 Build complete, QA passed | 46,000 |
| M3 UAT accepted, pilot live | 22,000 |
| M4 Full rollout and training complete | 14,000 |
| Total | 100,000 |

Hypercare included. Timeline: 14 weeks from kickoff. Change requests billed at $175/hour on approved change orders.
Payment terms: net 30 from milestone acceptance.

## Output

I've drafted the Brightwell intake portal SOW as a Markdown file with its gaps visible. It is not approved or sent, and I couldn't produce a DOCX or run any checks in this session.

#### Route and limits

- **Document route, not the generator.** The quote is a USD 100,000 fixed fee split by milestone, with no roles, rates or hours. The generator needs per-role hours times rate to equal revenue, so it can't represent this agreement. I wrote the draft by hand from the three inputs and kept the fee as quoted.
- **No scripts or document tool.** I couldn't run `generate_sow.js`, `verify_contract.py`, the slop scan or the release-gate checks. The Markdown file is the editable draft; it still needs conversion to the Word template, a rendered-page check and the review-writing, brand and quality gates.
- **Contract wording kept.** The SOW references the MSA dated March 3, 2026 rather than restating it. It uses the deemed-acceptance rule (10 business days unless written notice of a material nonconformance), net 30 from milestone acceptance, and $175/hour on approved change orders.
- **Writing review done by hand.** Each mechanic has one home. Acceptance is in Section 3, change control in Section 8, and the other sections point to them.

#### Figure check (by hand)

| Milestone | Amount (USD) |
|---|---|
| M1 Discovery and design accepted | 18,000 |
| M2 Build complete, QA passed | 46,000 |
| M3 UAT accepted, pilot live | 22,000 |
| M4 Full rollout and training complete | 14,000 |
| Sum | 100,000 (matches quote total) |

#### Open items, left as bracketed fields in the draft

1. **Timeline versus hypercare.** The quote says 14 weeks from kickoff and hypercare is 30 days after full rollout. The two only fit if rollout finishes by about week 10. Per-milestone target weeks were not supplied.
2. **Hypercare.** Its activities and response expectations are undefined. It is included in the fee but has no milestone, so the draft invoices the full fee by M4.
3. **Acceptance criteria.** Only the deemed-acceptance rule was supplied. The UAT pass standard and per-deliverable criteria need a decision.
4. **Late client dependencies.** Nothing says what happens to dates or fees if the DentaCore sandbox (due week 2), the Spanish text or pilot availability is late. I didn't invent a consequence.
5. **Missing party details.** The effective date, kickoff date, client address and notice contact, provider lead, accounts-payable contact, signatories, and MSA precedence wording are all absent.
6. **Contract profile.** It is marked as an assumption ("assume standard MSA terms"), so check the SOW against the actual MSA.

  2. Scope of services
  3. Deliverables and acceptance

##### 1. Purpose and agreement

This SOW is issued under the MSA. The MSA governs all terms not stated here, and this SOW does not restate them. If this SOW and the MSA conflict, [precedence rule: take from the MSA; not supplied].

Brightwell's new patients need an online way to complete intake before their visit. Harbor Lane will design, build, test and launch an intake portal that sends completed intake to Brightwell's practice-management system, DentaCore, through its import API.

##### 2. Scope of services

###### 2.1 Discovery and design
- Two workshops with Brightwell.
- Intake form design for adult and pediatric patients.
- Accessibility review of the design against WCAG 2.2 AA.

###### 2.2 Build
- A responsive web intake form.
- Insurance card photo upload.
- E-signature on consent forms.
- An integration that pushes each completed intake to DentaCore through its import API.
- Form text in English and Spanish. Brightwell supplies the Spanish text (Section 5).

###### 2.3 Testing
- QA by Harbor Lane.
- One round of user acceptance testing (UAT) with two pilot offices.

###### 2.4 Launch
- Pilot in two offices, then rollout to all 11 offices.
- Two remote staff training sessions, recorded.

###### 2.5 Hypercare
- 30 days of hypercare after full rollout, included in the fixed fee. [Hypercare activities and response expectations are not defined in the confirmed scope. Confirm before issue.]

##### 3. Deliverables and acceptance

| # | Deliverable | Milestone |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Workshop outputs, adult and pediatric intake form designs, WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility review | M1 |
| D2 | Built portal: responsive intake form, insurance card upload, e-signature, DentaCore integration; QA results | M2 |
| D3 | UAT with two pilot offices; pilot go-live | M3 |
| D4 | Rollout to all 11 offices; two recorded training sessions | M4 |

Acceptance follows the contract profile. Each deliverable is deemed accepted 10 business days after delivery unless Brightwell gives written notice of a material nonconformance within that period. Notice goes to [Provider notice contact; not supplied]. Brightwell's UAT in D3 is a single round.

Acceptance criteria for each deliverable beyond this rule were not supplied: [confirm whether D1–D4 need written criteria, for example the UAT pass standard].

##### 4. Timeline

The work runs 14 weeks from kickoff. [Per-milestone target weeks were not supplied. Confirm whether the 14 weeks include the 30-day hypercare period; 30 days after full rollout would extend past week 14 unless rollout completes by about week 10.]

##### 5. Client responsibilities and dependencies

Brightwell will:
1. Provide DentaCore API sandbox access by week 2.
2. Name a product owner. Lena Ortiz, Operations Director, is the named product owner.
3. Supply Spanish translations of form text.
4. Make the two pilot offices available for UAT and pilot.

The schedule depends on these items. [Effect of late delivery on dates or fees is not stated in the supplied terms; the MSA or Section 8 change control applies. Confirm.]

##### 6. Assumptions

- The DentaCore import API supports the required fields.
- No PHI is stored outside DentaCore and the HIPAA-eligible hosting Brightwell already licenses. The BAA dated March 3, 2026 applies.

If either assumption proves false, Harbor Lane will raise it with the product owner and handle any change in effort under Section 8.

##### 7. Exclusions

- Appointment scheduling.
- Payments.
- DentaCore configuration changes.
- Translation, except the English and Spanish form text Brightwell supplies.

##### 8. Change control

Work outside Sections 2 and 7, or a failed assumption in Section 6, proceeds only under a written change order approved by both parties. Approved change orders are billed at USD 175 per hour. No change order carries a fee until approved.

##### 9. Fees and payment

Fixed fee: USD 100,000. Hypercare is included.

| Milestone | Trigger | Amount (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Discovery and design accepted | 18,000 |
| M2 | Build complete, QA passed | 46,000 |
| M3 | UAT accepted, pilot live | 22,000 |
| M4 | Full rollout and training complete | 14,000 |
| **Total** | | **100,000** |

Each milestone is invoiced on acceptance under Section 3 and is payable net 30 from milestone acceptance. Invoices go to [accounts payable contact; not supplied]. Hypercare has no separate milestone; the full fee is invoiced by M4.

| Brightwell Dental Partners, LLC | Harbor Lane Consulting, LLC |
|---|---|

| Title: [not supplied] | Title: [not supplied] |

skills.markdown:
---
name: writing-diagnostics
description: Internal diagnostic and figure-preservation tools used by review-writing. This module supplies scanners and review records; it does not select an author voice or act as a second editor.
---

# Writing diagnostics

This internal runtime supplies scanners and review records for `review-writing`. Load it through that workflow.

Read [review-writing](../review-writing/SKILL.md) before using these tools.
That workflow owns writing review. A confirmed personal profile supplies the
author's voice. A visual brand profile controls appearance; it cannot select an
author voice or change a fact. These tools report detectable patterns; they do not rewrite
text or establish editorial quality.

Use the tools on every kind of authored prose, including instructions and
internal records. Keep exact source evidence and executable syntax unchanged.
Review the new wording around those spans. A file extension or audience label
does not exclude authored language from review.

## Review a saved file

```bash
python3 scripts/writing_check.py --config house.json FILE
python3 scripts/writing_check.py --config house.json --json FILE
```

The checker reads prose from supported document formats and structured text
fields. Exit 0 means it found no patterns, 1 means it found a pattern and 2 means
the check could not finish. Read its output and the complete document. Repair
the argument or sentence that caused a finding, then rerun the check.

`C24-formulaic-the-framing` reports recurring label and announcement shapes as
review candidates. It does not establish that a name or quotation is wrong.
Keep a justified match unchanged and record the reason when a review record is
required. A retained candidate still produces exit 1; do not claim a clean scan
or change a valid passage solely to obtain exit 0.
For a receipt, use `--retain-framing-reason "REASON" --retention-source "SOURCE"`
with `prose_receipt.py emit` after reading every candidate. The assessment is
bound to the artifact hash and applies only to C24; it cannot waive other rules.
C25–C27 add narrow review candidates for table readouts, action basis and repeated
reassurance. Read [contextual signals](references/context-signals.md) for their
observable conditions, format limits and rule-specific retention procedure.
These candidates cannot establish redundancy, unearned urgency or lack of evidence.
The validator checks the record. The reviewer remains responsible for the judgment.

Do not change the filename, label prose internal or put authored wording in a
quote to obtain a pass. A literal source span remains verbatim only when its
source and exact extent are identified in the internal review record. Keep
reviewing the surrounding authored text. Do not reclassify an invented claim
or an awkward sentence as captured evidence.

`prose_check.py` is a compatibility command for the same supported input path.
The older lexical engine also reports vocabulary and construction diagnostics.
Read [surface policy](references/surface-policy.md) for source-span handling.

## Review recurring patterns

Read [construction rules](references/construction-rules.md) and
[patterns](references/patterns.md) when investigating a recurring construction.
Use the applicable register for format-specific advice:

| Format | Reference |
| --- | --- |
| Slides | [Deck](references/registers/deck.md) |
| Contract or proposal | [SOW and proposal](references/registers/sow-proposal.md) |
| Report or brief | [Readout](references/registers/readout-brief.md) |
| Short message | [Email and Slack](references/registers/email-slack.md) |
| Other authored text | [General](references/registers/general.md) |

Registers supply examples and format checks under review-writing. Preserve
required terms and confirmed voice when a legacy example uses another style.
Read headings with their body text. Remove repeated explanations and subtitles
that repeat a title. A vocabulary substitution cannot repair an empty claim.

```bash
python3 scripts/scan.py audit docs "*.md"
python3 scripts/scan.py score draft.md --json
python3 scripts/scan.py --input FILE
```

The audit command includes supported structured files and returns an error for
unsupported input. The score command reports lexical density for comparison;
its success does not establish compliance. It strips some executable spans for
that measurement. Use the complete authored-language check for release review.

Vocabulary sources remain in `scripts/rewrite_scan.py`. The generated wordlists
come from `scripts/sync_wordlists.py`; preserve their synchronization check.
Weighted lists retain their existing weights. Changes to detection require
representative positive examples and valid prose examples, not a lower budget
chosen to pass a particular draft.

## Preserve figures and meaning

Before a substantive rewrite, retain the source version. Reconcile figures:

```bash
python3 scripts/rewrite_scan.py --tie-out SOURCE REWRITE
```

An added figure needs its source. A missing source figure requires checking
whether the omission was authorized. The writing pass cannot approve a price,
scope change or commercial commitment. Use the confirmed quote or versioned
estimate and preserve its assumptions. Keep client-stated figures attributed.

Compare the finished text with its source for changed ownership and conditions.
Retain factual uncertainty and meaningful author choices. Never add a number,
quotation or anecdote to make vague writing sound specific.

## Record a required review

When the producing workflow requires a narrative review record, use:

```bash
python3 scripts/prose_receipt.py emit FILE --out receipt.json \
    --before-file SOURCE \
    --protected "commercial figures from the supplied quote" \
    --change "replaced the generic claim with the supported action"
python3 scripts/prose_receipt.py validate receipt.json
```

The record binds the file hash to the checker result and declared edits. The
validator rechecks measurable assertions and figure changes. A no-change result
needs an actual reading assessment; arbitrary edits are unnecessary. A record
does not independently establish that an editor understood the document.

Brief replies receive writing review without a receipt. Captured transcripts
remain evidence and are never rewritten for style. Newly authored descriptions
in records still receive the same writing review as any other prose.

## Select configuration

The canonical baseline is `house.json`. An explicit configuration can add
checks; it cannot disable the maintained rules. The scripts and word data ship
together and need no neighboring installed skill. See
[configuration](references/house-overlay.md) and the [tellscan rule map](references/tellscan-rule-map.md) when maintaining the diagnostic
engine. Every supported artifact still needs a complete reading against its
facts and intended reader after the commands pass.

examples.title: Rewrite a stiff delay email to a facilities committee
examples.markdown:
## Request

Can you fix my draft email to the facilities committee about the pool roof delay? It reads stiff and I don't want it to sound machine-written. My project notes are in inputs/ and every figure has to stay as it is.

## Inputs

Run of the `writing-diagnostics` source module, which has no task package of its own. The recording session invented this scenario, the request and the inputs below before running the skill. It had no connectors, accounts or network access and could not execute scripts, so any scripted step was done by hand and the answer says so. Other files it produced, not shown here: `revised-email.txt`.

#### draft-email.txt

Subject: Exciting Update: Pool Reopening Timeline

Dear Committee Members,

I hope this email finds you well. I am thrilled to share a transformative update on the Alderbank Pool roof project. Navigating unforeseen challenges, our team has worked tirelessly to ensure a seamless path forward.

The reopening, originally planned for 3 March, is now expected on 14 April. This delay is not about quality, it's about safety. Inspectors found corroded steel in 6 of the 22 roof trusses, and replacing them adds $38,400 to the $212,000 contract. Fortunately, our contingency fund of $45,000 can absorb the cost, so no new money is needed.

Time is of the essence, as the steel quote expires soon. We will need your approval promptly to keep the project on track. Feel free to reach out with any questions, and thank you for your continued support and partnership.

Warm regards,
Tomasz Weber
Facilities Manager

#### project-notes.md

#### Alderbank Pool roof: notes, 3 November

- Old cladding came off the week of 20 October. Inspector (Dana Okafor, Ridgeway Structural) found corrosion in 6 of the 22 trusses.
- Contract with Calloway Roofing: $212,000. Change order for replacing the 6 trusses: $38,400, quote Q-2291.
- Quote Q-2291 holds until 25 November. After that the steel price is re-quoted.
- Contingency fund balance: $45,000. Change order needs committee approval because it is over the $25,000 delegated limit.
- Facilities committee meets 18 November.
- Original reopening: 3 March. New reopening: 14 April, only if the steel arrives within 5 weeks of the order.
- Swim club has been told the pool stays closed until the new date; they have asked for a written update.

## Output

I rewrote the email and saved it as `out/revised-email.txt`. Your original stays in `inputs/draft-email.txt`. The text is below.

```
Subject: Alderbank Pool roof: approval needed on 18 November for a 14 April reopening

Dear committee members,

The pool will reopen on 14 April instead of 3 March. After the old cladding came off, Dana Okafor of Ridgeway Structural inspected the roof and found corrosion in 6 of the 22 trusses.

Calloway Roofing quotes $38,400 to replace those six (Q-2291), on top of the $212,000 contract. The contingency fund holds $45,000, so the cost fits inside it. Because the change order is over the $25,000 limit delegated to me, it needs a committee vote.

The quote holds until 25 November, after which the steel is re-quoted. I am asking for approval at your 18 November meeting so the order goes in before the quote lapses. The 14 April date also depends on the steel arriving within 5 weeks of the order.

The swim club has asked for a written update. I would like to send it after your vote.

Tomasz Weber
Facilities Manager
```

#### What changed

- **Opening and subject.** The draft started with "I hope this email finds you well" and "thrilled to share a transformative update". The new version opens with the reopening date and puts the decision and its deadline in the subject.
- **Vague wording replaced with your notes.** "Unforeseen challenges", "worked tirelessly" and "expires soon" are gone. In their place are the inspector, the 6 of 22 trusses, the quote number and the 25 November lapse date.
- **Ask with a date.** "We will need your approval promptly" now reads "approval at your 18 November meeting". The notes explain why a vote is needed: the change order is over the $25,000 delegated limit.
- **Forced contrast removed.** "Not about quality, it's about safety" is deleted. Your notes don't say the delay was about safety, so that claim was not supported.
- **Dependency added.** The draft gave 14 April as firm. Your notes say it holds only if the steel arrives within 5 weeks of the order, so that condition is now in the email.
- **Closers removed.** "Feel free to reach out", "continued support and partnership" and "Warm regards" are cut. The email ends on the swim club item.
- **Ownership made explicit.** "The delegated limit" now says it is yours ("delegated to me"), and the approver is the committee.

#### Figures check

I did the tie-out by hand because I can't run `rewrite_scan.py --tie-out` here. Every figure and date in the revision matches your notes: 14 April, 3 March, 6 of 22 trusses, $38,400, $212,000, $45,000, $25,000, 25 November, 18 November, 5 weeks and Q-2291. I added no figures. Your draft said "no new money is needed"; I replaced it with "the cost fits inside" the contingency fund, which is the only claim the $45,000 balance supports. I did not compute a remaining balance, since your notes don't give one.

#### Checks I could not run

- I could not run `writing_check.py`, so there is no checker result. I read the text by hand against the construction rules instead: balanced clauses, antithesis, triads, stacked fragments, deference phrasing, chatbot closers and repeated phrases. I found none left, and I made a second pass to remove two sentences I had added without a source. This is a reading pass, not a scanner pass.
- No review receipt was produced, because this was a short message. The skill treats short messages as a quick pass without one.

#### Please confirm

- **Swim club line.** "I would like to send it after your vote" is my wording. Your notes say only that the club wants a written update. Change or delete it if you plan to send it sooner.
- **Dana Okafor's mention.** I named the inspector because your notes do. Remove the name if the committee doesn't need it.
- **Cladding timing.** I kept "after the old cladding came off" without a date. Your notes say the week of 20 October, so add it if you want.

Files:
- `out/revised-email.txt`: the revised email shown above.
